## D164 — the KO-CONDITION ANTECEDENT AS ITS OWN FAMILY: the CAUSE-CONDITIONED PRIZE REDUCTION, and PLACEMENT DISCHARGES A CONDITION ONLY FOR A CONSEQUENT THAT CAN LIVE AT THE PLACEMENT (engine 0.109.0 → 0.110.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 10)

> **⚠️ INTEGRATION NOTE.** D164 was built in an ISOLATED WORKTREE in parallel with
> D163 and was forbidden to touch `docs/`; its code was committed as `16fa8e8` while
> its doc-ritual content never landed anywhere at all — `decisions.md` ended at D163,
> this file's last section was D163, and `progress.md` did not mention it. **This
> section, the `decisions.md` row and the `progress.md` entries were integrated at
> D166**, off the commit message and the diff, which is the SAME REMEDY D163 applied
> to D162 one slice earlier (see §D162's note) — and the second time in three slices
> that a worktree slice's docs had to be recovered by a successor. Where the commit
> message and the code disagreed, the code won; **one commit-message number is
> corrected below** (`FIXTURE_POOL` is **291**, not the 290 the message claims).

### The printing

**Munkidori ex `sv06.5-037` / `-083` / `-091` — "Oh No You Don't"**, an **ABILITY**
(`abilities_json`, not `attacks_json`), printed verbatim:

> *"If this Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's
> Pokémon, and if you have any Pecharunt ex in play, your opponent takes 1 fewer
> Prize card."*

**Three printings, ONE body.** The D1 rows for `-037` (Double rare), `-083` (Ultra
Rare) and `-091` (Special illustration rare) are byte-identical on every column but
`rarity` — **verified by a single `count(distinct …)` over ELEVEN columns** (name, hp,
stage, types, retreat, abilities, attacks, weaknesses, resistances, reg mark,
legality) returning **1**, rather than by eye. D162 had already mapped the same three
ids onto ONE fixture for D154's per-attack lock on "Dirty Headbutt"; this registry row
**joins that program rather than replacing it**, so the card carries BOTH of its
printed sentences.

The antecedent census `LIKE '%Knocked Out by damage from an attack%'` returns **6
rows** — **confirming D158 and D162 a third time**, on the restored catalog (978 rows
/ 6 sets).

### ⚠️ LUCARIO `sv01-114` IS NOT THIS ANTECEDENT, AND EVERY LIST SINCE D158 SAID IT WAS

Printed: *"If any of your {F} Pokémon were Knocked Out by damage from an attack
**during your opponent's last turn**…"* — **retrospective** (it looks back at a turn
that has ended, not at the KO happening now), **board-wide** (any of your Pokémon,
not "this Pokémon"), **type-filtered** ({F}), and carrying **NO possessive clause** at
all. It is a different condition on a different reader.

**`conditionClause.test.ts` has held the correct account since D115.** So the OLDER
artefact was right and the NEWER census table was wrong: **recency is not authority.**

Two more inherited claims were off in the same place:

- **D158's own table renders Munkidori ex in the column Lucario's ATTACK sits in**,
  where it is an ABILITY on `abilities_json`.
- **`FIXTURE_POOL` is not 278**, the figure that header had carried for two slices.
  ⚠️ **And the commit message's correction is itself one short:** it says **290**;
  the literal counted at `16fa8e8` — and again at `HEAD` — is **291**. Two
  independent methods agree (a key sweep of the object literal and an import of
  `FIXTURE_POOL` at runtime), and D163's own "289" was one short in the same
  direction. **The second number of a two-number census, three handoffs running
  (§D163's lesson (3), still earning its line).**

### ⚠️ THE FINDING, AND IT IS ABOUT D158's OWN DESIGN: PLACEMENT DISCHARGES A CONDITION ONLY FOR A CONSEQUENT THAT CAN LIVE AT THE PLACEMENT

D158 read the **same printed antecedent** and paid nothing for it. It satisfied *"by
an attack"* **purely by WHERE it put its line** — `finishAttack`, which exactly ONE
path reaches; the Checkup and the mid-turn evolve sweep call `collectKnockOuts`
directly and never get there.

**This consequent modifies a PRIZE, and prizes are planned in `planPrizes` — INSIDE
`collectKnockOuts` — which ALL THREE paths reach.** So the identical printed clause
costs this printing a **threaded `attackerSeat?: Seat`** argument on
`collectKnockOuts` → `planPrizes`, passed at **exactly one call site** (`finishAttack`)
and deliberately omitted at the other two.

**The possessive is not free either.** `finishAttack` sweeps BOTH seats, so a holder
that died on the ATTACKER's own board (its own `damageSelf` recoil, its own confusion
self-hit, a defender's Rocky Helmet) is in the same batch — which makes
`attackerSeat === ref.seat` **load-bearing rather than decorative**.

The three clauses, each a separate refusal and each driven:

| printed clause | the refusal | what it rejects |
|---|---|---|
| *"by damage from an attack"* | `attackerSeat === undefined` | the Checkup KO and the mid-turn evolve/Ability sweep |
| *"from your OPPONENT'S Pokémon"* | `attackerSeat === ref.seat` | the holder dying on the attacker's own board |
| *"if you have any Pecharunt ex in play"* | a name scan of the KO'd body's OWN side | Active **and** Bench, by card **NAME** — the card has FOUR printings (`sv06.5-039`/`-085`/`-093`/`-095`) and no id would cover them |

### A SIBLING FIELD, NOT A UNION MEMBER — the standing rule, answered on THREE axes

`onKoPrizeReduction` sits BESIDE `onKoPrizeGuard` (Glimmora `sv02-126`) rather than
becoming a member of it, and the two **MUTUALLY REFUSE** each other's payment
(D155's rule, the same shape that forced `damageAttackerOnKo` apart from
`damageAttacker` at D158):

| | Glimmora's guard | this reduction |
|---|---|---|
| cause qualifier | **none** — "When this Pokémon is Knocked Out", so it must still deny the Prize at the Checkup | **named** — refused on every non-attack KO |
| effect | **ZEROES** ("can't take ANY Prize cards") | **DECREMENTS** ("1 FEWER" — on an ex, 2 → 1 and not 2 → 0) |
| coin | **flipped** | **none** |

One field carrying both would put an attack gate on Glimmora (breaking the Checkup KO
it is printed for) and a coin flip on this one. **The merge mutations fail 16 and 2**,
and both directions are driven on ONE board.

### The four ordering judgements, each pinned

1. **The plan is made on the PRE-KO state** — a Pecharunt ex dying in the SAME batch
   still counts. That is D158's one-simultaneous-batch model read one function later:
   the batch is a single instant, so nothing in it has left play while the plan is
   made.
2. **AHEAD of the §14 speculation** — reducing only on the real pass **fails 13**.
3. **PER BODY** — 2 holders give **2** reductions, not 4.
4. **`ABILITY_TRIGGERED` must precede `PRIZE_REDUCED`**, so the row that names the
   Ability lands above the row that states its consequence.

### VOICE — SYSTEM, but by a different route than D158's

`PRIZE_REDUCED` is a **new event**, and a **separate row from `PRIZE_PREVENTED`
although `PRIZE_PREVENTED` exists and is read**: *"no Prize card is taken"* is simply
**false when one is**, and on an ex this is 2 → 1. The row is SYSTEM-voiced for a
reason that is derived rather than inherited from its neighbour — this row's `seat`
owns the DYING Pokémon while the party the sentence acts on is that seat's OPPONENT,
so an active voice under `seat` describes the wrong player's loss and one under the
opponent credits them with their own penalty. The `ABILITY_TRIGGERED` row directly
above already names the Ability and its owner.

It carries **BOTH numbers** (`by` and `count`) because a decrement is only readable
against the face value: *"1 fewer"* alone leaves a player who does not know the card
is worth 2 unable to check the prize count they are about to see.

### ⚠️ ONE MUTATION RESULT WORTH THE SPACE: THE CLAMP NEEDED TWO CONSTRUCTED VALUES

`koPrizeReduction` clamps at 0 (`Math.max(0, baseCount - by)`). **A 1-Prize fixture
alone never reaches it**, because `1 − 1 = 0` whether or not the clamp exists — so
the guard **SURVIVED BEING "FIXED" ONCE**: a first pass deleted it and nothing failed,
including on a 1-Prize body.

The clamp fires only when the reduction **EXCEEDS** the face value, so the witness
pairs a **1-Prize body** with a **constructed `by: 2`** (`fix-koprize` / `FIX_KOPRIZE`
— 30 HP, no Rule Box, so `prizeValueOf` returns 1): `1 − 2 = −1`, clamped to 0. It is
the `fix-onko` pattern (a fixture proves machinery the printed cast cannot reach), and
the guard is KEPT rather than deleted because the field is DATA: the first printing
that reduces by more than one — or any printing of this Ability on a body without a
Rule Box — turns a silent negative Prize count into a real one.

**A test can look like it covers a branch and provably not.** That is the transferable
line, and it is the one D166 re-derived at a different boundary one slice later.

### Mutations — 23 run across three passes (18/21, 21/23, 23/23), including 7 ORDER mutations

**Two survivors, both fixed WITH WITNESSES rather than argued away:**

1. a **mid-turn Ability KO** reaches the opponent's board via
   `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts(…, SEATS, …)` — witnessed with Hawlucha `sv01-118`
   "Flying Entry", the only vehicle in the pool for a mid-turn KO on the OPPONENT's
   board, and without it the *"by an attack"* refusal is driven only for the Checkup;
2. **the clamp**, above.

### The structural questions

- **PARK? NO. PERSIST? NO** — `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **10**, pinned as an
  absence over the 16-key set. **The ninth consecutive control on D124's trigger.**
  (D165 broke the run one slice later, and for a reason this slice's field does not
  share: nothing here changes a stored TYPE.)
- **§11: nothing owed** — no op was added or removed.
- **Gates no action**; driven on both seats.

## D165 — REVIEW FIX, NOT A SLICE: `InPlayPokemon.lockedAttack` has ONE READER and TWO WRITERS, and neither merged (engine 0.110.0 → 0.111.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 10 → 11)

The **fourth** `/code-review` this branch has had and the **first to return a
correctness bug.** Scope `git diff origin/backend...HEAD` — **11 commits, D154–D164**
— run at D164 on the user's trigger. **Exactly ONE finding.** This is it.

### The defect

| | `preventAttackUse` (D154) | `lockDefenderAttack` (D157) |
|---|---|---|
| Holder | `ctx.seat`'s Active | the DEFENDER |
| Stamp | `state.turn + 2` | `state.turn + 1` |
| Field | `lockedAttack` | `lockedAttack` |
| Merge | bare overwrite | bare overwrite |
| Short-circuits when | `turn === turn && index === index` | `turn === turn && index === index` |

Both were **correct about themselves and silent about each other.** A self-side
re-install always stamps a later turn (an attack ends the turn, and the window is the
holder's own next one), and §5.3 forbids a second declaration inside one turn — so
neither op could ever land on its OWN live record. `preventAttackUse`'s doc block said
so out loud:

> …a differing index simply overwrites, **because a later install always stamps a
> later turn**.

True of the OP. **False of the FIELD.** `+ 2` from turn 3 and `+ 1` from turn 4 are
both **5**.

### The board — ordinary, played end to end, and it was written BEFORE anything moved

The repo's standing verify-before-you-fix rule, applied to a review finding for the
second time (D153 was the first, and there the review was UNDERSTATED). Here the
failing test was watched to fail for exactly the stated reason first:

```
turn 3 (P1) Skarmory sv03-142 uses "Slashing Steel" (idx 1)
            → lockedAttack = { turn: 5, attackIndex: 1 }
turn 4 (P2) Oranguru sv02-094 "Plotter's Command" parks chooseAttack on that
            Skarmory; P2 picks "Peck" (idx 0)
            → turn = 4 + 1 = 5, index differs → OVERWRITE
turn 5 (P1) the §8 gate refuses idx 0 … and ALLOWS idx 1
```

So **Skarmory uses "Slashing Steel" on the very turn its own printed drawback bars
it**, `redactedAttacksOf` and `GameHud` render the button LIVE, and the
`ATTACK_LOCKED` row promising otherwise is still standing in the log. Both families
are catalogued AND fielded and every intervening step is ordinary — the barred body
only has to stay Active, and retreat/switch/evolve would have cleared the lock under
§10 anyway.

### ⚠️ The finding is EXACT — the sweep was RUN, not assumed

D153's review account was understated (it named one wrong path and there were three),
so the writer/reader sweep was made rather than inherited. Result:

| field | writers | readers | collides? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lockedAttack` | **2** — `preventAttackUse` (`+ 2`), `lockDefenderAttack` (`+ 1`) | 1 — `lockedAttackIndex` (3 call sites) | **YES** |
| `boostedAttack` (D155) | **1** — `boostAttack` (`+ 2`) | 1 — `boostedAttackDamage` | no |
| `attackLockedTurn` (D143/D148) | 2 | 1 — `attackLocked` | no *address* to collide on |

The four `lockedAttack: null` literals are §10 CLEARS, not writers.

**`boostedAttack` is genuinely single-writer**, and its own "a different index
replaces" rule is unreachable as a deletion for exactly the reason
`preventAttackUse`'s was — which is why the premise is now ASSERTED rather than
assumed, and the trap written down: **the day a second writer of `boostedAttack`
lands (an opponent-side buff, or any op stamping `+ 1` where this one stamps `+ 2`)
it inherits this defect verbatim, and the fix is this one.**

### ⚠️ The irony, and the rule it leaves behind

D157 shared the field on the ground that

> `lockedAttackIndex` is the **ONLY READER** of `lockedAttack`, and it REFUSES the
> index whichever op wrote it.

Every word true, still true, and **not the question.** It never asked how many
WRITERS the slot has. And `types.ts`'s `LockedAttack` block refuses a *different*
merge — with D148's `attackLockedTurn` — on exactly this ground:

> It is refused because the two are **REACHABLE TOGETHER** and mean different things
> … and **one record could hold only the later write**.

**The repo had already written down the argument that condemned its own field, one
column to the left.** The rule:

> **The test is not "do these two records mean the same thing" but "how many WRITERS
> does this slot have, and can any two of them stamp the same turn".**

A reader count answers the question *"can these two facts share a consumer"*. It says
nothing at all about *"can these two facts share a SLOT"*, and D157 used the first as
though it settled the second.

### The shape: a LIST, and the ground is the READ SITES

`InPlayPokemon.lockedAttacks: LockedAttack[]` — `[]` means none (`markers`'s
convention rather than the six durated siblings' `=== null` one), newest last. The
record itself did not move a byte; the MULTIPLICITY did.

- **One shared merge rule**, `addLockedAttack` (interpreter.ts), used by both writers
  so the collision has exactly one answer in exactly one place a mutation can reach:
  **idempotent** on the `(turn, index)` pair (returns `null`, the caller suppresses
  the row), **appending** on a differing index, **pruning** entries whose turn is
  strictly behind. The prune is a GARBAGE rule and not an expiry rule — expiry is the
  reader's turn comparison — and it is what bounds the list by *bars stamped for
  turns not yet played* rather than by the length of the match.
- **One plural reader**, `lockedAttackIndexes(state, pokemon): number[]`. D154's shape
  argument survives verbatim: two of its three callers map over the whole `attacks`
  array, so a `(state, pokemon, index) => boolean` predicate would re-read one field
  N times. One read of the SET answers all three.
- **The rename is load-bearing.** `lockedAttack` → `lockedAttacks` and
  `lockedAttackIndex` → `lockedAttackIndexes` makes every one of the ~70 sites a
  COMPILE ERROR. Keeping the names would have left `expect(x.lockedAttack).toEqual({…})`
  compiling and failing at runtime — silent churn where the compiler could do the work.

### ⚠️ A second stamped field was priced and REFUSED, on a bound nothing proves

Option (a) — a `defenderLockedAttack` beside the self-installed one — fixes today's
collision and **pushes the same defect out by exactly one writer.** Nothing in the
type, in the op set or in the registry says a per-attack bar may have at most two
sources. The thing that LOOKS like a bound is a census (§D154's 8 rows / 6 names
self-side, §D157's 2 opponent-side, both CLOSED), and that is a fact about the
2026-08-03 catalog rather than about the shape. **D150's whole lesson is that this
repo does not accept an assumed bound.**

And (a) is not even cheaper where it counts: **both options cost the same
`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` bump** (a changed/added required key on `InPlayPokemon`) **and
the same enumeration at the read sites** (with two fields, the gate and both
projections must ask BOTH per row). (a) buys a smaller diff and nothing else.

### ⚠️ THE ENUMERATING CALLER, ARRIVING FROM THE DIRECTION NOBODY WATCHED

Four decisions forecast a trigger for a collection over the durated riders and four
declined it:

| | trigger | verdict | ground |
|---|---|---|---|
| §D147 | a fifth stamped field | decline | (counting) |
| §D152 | a member the read site must **DISPATCH** on | decline | retires counting |
| §D154 | an **ENUMERATING** caller | decline | *every reader knows which rider it wants before it looks* |
| §D157 | a prompt that must **LIST** something | decline | it lists a CARD's attacks, not a body's riders |

**All four were watching the rider KINDS, and that claim is still true** — nothing in
this fix dispatches on a member's kind, because every entry in the list means one
thing. What stopped being true, from D157's commit onward, is that one body could
carry only ONE of them. With two bars live, `redactedAttacksOf` and `GameHud` must
mark **every** barred index and neither knows in advance which, so both now ask
MEMBERSHIP of a set they receive whole.

> **A collection is earned by a MULTIPLICITY the read site must ENUMERATE just as
> much as by a UNION it must DISPATCH on — and only the second was ever being watched
> for.**

**The `attackBlock` union stays DECLINED.** Do not re-open it on this.

### ⚠️ D155's refusal is untouched and is SHARPENED

D155 kept `boostedAttack` out of this record because *its consumer PAYS the index this
one's REFUSES*. The list makes that a property of the **container**: every entry is an
address the §8 gate refuses, so an entry that had to be PAID would be exactly the
defect D155 declined to build. One field, one meaning, N addresses.

### The five structural questions

1. **PARK? NO — PERSIST? YES. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 10 → 11, the EIGHTH time on
   D124's trigger and the FIRST that is a CHANGED TYPE rather than a NEW KEY.** That
   is where the rule's own wording earns its keep: the test has never been *"did a
   required key appear"* but **"can the PREVIOUS deploy's RECORD hold the new TYPE"**
   — and a version-10 record carries `lockedAttack` on every body and no
   `lockedAttacks` at all (the reader `.filter`s an absent field and THROWS, so the
   landing is not even soft). No op was added or removed and neither writer parks;
   `preventChosenAttack`'s park and its `chooseAttack` prompt/choice shapes are
   untouched. **D156–D164 in between did NOT bump — nine consecutive controls.** And
   **no `@luminous/schema` diff**: `redactedAttacksOf` still folds the fact into the
   per-attack `playable` boolean, so the WIRE is byte-identical across the bump and
   only the DO's stored `GameState` moves.
2. **VOICE — NO ROW MOVED, AND THE ROW WAS ALREADY RIGHT WHILE THE ENGINE WAS WRONG.**
   An inversion this family has not had: D154 made `ATTACK_LOCKED` NAME the attack
   because *"can't attack next turn"* is FALSE on a body whose other attack is legal,
   and D162 found the inverse on a one-attack body. Here **both rows were honest and
   the FIELD threw one of the facts away** — the log promised a bar the state had
   deleted, so a player reading their own log was told the truth by the row and lied
   to by the engine. No new arm is owed and that is CHECKED rather than waved at: the
   two rows are installed on two different TURNS, so no row ever has to say "and
   also". **Rendered under both seats and READ**, including the both-locks-live case
   — and it fills **the cell D157 named as UNVERIFIED**, the first board where the
   actor-is-seat path (p1 barring p1) and the victim-side path (p2 barring p1) render
   side by side on ONE body. Both file under p1; the whole log is asserted verbatim
   and re-rendered with the seat NAMES SWAPPED to show it moves nothing.
3. **GUARD — SWEPT, and the §10 set takes a SHAPE change and NO new site.** All four
   literals become `[]`, each DRIVEN with TWO bars live (evolve, retreat,
   `switchInto`), because a list admits a failure a record did not: **a clear written
   as a FILTER** (shed what this body installed, keep what was imposed) **would leave
   the evolved card carrying an index off the card it came from** — and the evolve
   witness (`fix-skarm-stage1`, ONE attack) is the sharpest available shape for it.
   Three rules in three places, deliberately: §10 sheds the WHOLE list, the READER
   expires per entry, the WRITER prunes the past. **What the sweep does NOT traverse:
   it reads a body that has been through ONE clear, so a literal shedding the field on
   three routes and not the fourth is caught by the three per-route cases and not by
   the sweep** (D157's own blind spot, unchanged).
4. **MECHANISM — everything except the merge existed, and the merge is the fix.**
5. **IT GATES AN ACTION, so it owes BOTH payability projections — and they both take a
   diff for the first time since D154 built them.** `redactedAttacksOf` reads the set
   once outside its map and asks membership per row; `GameHud.tsx` the same. Pinned on
   both sides **with a CONTROL** (the same board with the list emptied offers both
   rows, so "both greyed" cannot pass because the panel was unpayable), plus a new
   jsdom case. **§11: NOTHING OWED** — no op added or removed, both verdicts
   (`preventAttackUse: "untouched"`, `preventChosenAttack: "blocked"`) unchanged and
   still driven by `preventBlock.test.ts`'s probe table.

### Cost

**1 field TYPE, 1 merge helper, 1 renamed reader, 1 §8 gate line, 2 projection lines,
4 §10 literals.** No new op, event, event field, log crumb, error code, prompt, park,
registry row, regex, fixture, deck, `@luminous/schema` diff or DB diff.
`lockedAttackMerge.test.ts` (**14 tests, SEED-FREE**, on the two predecessors' decks
one per seat — the collision needs a self-side barrer facing an opponent-side one, and

OVERWRITES"* both now assert APPEND, which is the defect's own pin at its own site.

## D166 — VERIFICATION FIX, NOT A SLICE: D165's INTERRUPTED MUTATION PASS FINISHED, and its own report of it was UNDERSTATED — FIVE survivors at ONE boundary, not two (engine UNCHANGED at 0.111.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` UNCHANGED at 11, **0 engine behaviour lines**)

Item **0** of D165's remainder list, and the first time this repo had committed a
slice with its own verification unfinished. Two halves: **finish the pass** (below),
and **recover D164's doc ritual** off `16fa8e8` (§D164 above).

### The pass, re-derived rather than trusted — and it moved the WRONG way

D165 recorded *"mutation-checked TWENTY-FOUR ways, 22 caught, two survivors at the
same boundary"*. The standing rule is that **a predecessor's own finding is on the
list of dangerous claims** and that a review is swept **in both directions** rather
than assumed to exaggerate. So the pass was rebuilt from the D165 diff rather than
from its list.

**31 mutants over the whole D165 surface** — `addLockedAttack`'s two lines,
`lockedAttackIndexes`, both writers' stamps AND their `now` arguments, the §8 gate,
both payability projections, all four §10 clears — against the **full** suite each
time (203 files), reverting with `git checkout` between runs.

| | claimed (D165) | re-derived (D166) |
|---|---|---|
| run | 24 | **31** |
| caught | 22 | **26** |
| survived | 2 | **5** |

**All five are the same boundary**, `addLockedAttack`'s prune
(`existing.filter((lock) => lock.turn >= now)`), written five different ways:

| # | mutation | why it survived |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `>= now` → `> now` | drops entries stamped for the turn being played |
| 2 | `>= now` → `>= now + 1` | the same off-by-one, written the other way |
| 3 | `>= now` → `>= turn` | prunes against the NEW stamp instead of the clock |
| 4 | `preventAttackUse` passes `turn` as `now` | #3 from the CALL SITE |
| 5 | `lockDefenderAttack` passes `turn` as `now` | #3 from the other CALL SITE |

⚠️ **THREE OF THE FIVE ARE MUTATIONS D165 NEVER GENERATED**, and two of those are
**call-site** mutations rather than mutations of the helper — which is why the count
went UP rather than down. **Re-running the mutants a predecessor listed is not
re-running its pass.**

### The verdict is WITNESS, not DELETE — and the argument is not taste

This repo's standard is that a guard no test can make fail is either witnessed or
deleted with its unreachability asserted: **D154 DELETED** one (it bought nothing),
**D159 / D161 / D163 KEPT** theirs (unreachability was assertable). **Neither applies
here.** An entry stamped for `now` is **LIVE NOW** — `lockedAttackIndexes` answers it
this very turn — so every one of the five mutants **deletes a bar that is still
biting**. That is **D165's own defect, relocated out of the merge rule and into the
garbage rule sitting one line below it**, and it is reachable on a played line. A
guard whose failure mode is the defect the slice exists to fix does not get argued
away.

### ⚠️ THE TWO WRITERS DO NOT REACH THE EQUAL CASE ALIKE, AND THE ARGUMENT IS PARITY

Both writers stamp the **holder's own next turn** — `preventAttackUse` `+ 2` from the
holder's turn, `lockDefenderAttack` `+ 1` from the opponent's — so **every entry on a
body carries that seat's turn parity**. Therefore:

- **`preventAttackUse` CAN meet `lock.turn === now`**, because it writes on its own
  Active during its own turn, and an opponent-imposed bar can be live on exactly that
  turn. **Driven as a PLAYED LINE.**
- **`lockDefenderAttack` CANNOT**, because it writes on the OPPONENT's Active during
  the actor's turn, so `now` is never one of the victim's turns. **Driven by
  SURGERY**, said rather than skipped — `addLockedAttack` is ONE function with ONE
  contract, and the parity it leans on is a fact about **today's two writers** rather
  than about the shape (D150's rule about assumed bounds, applied to a *reachability*
  claim instead of to a count).

### The played-line witness, and why the KO is deliberate

It differs from `collision()` in exactly one step — **P1 installs nothing on turn 2**
— so the board carries ONE bar rather than two:

| turn | seat | what happens | Skarmory's `lockedAttacks` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | P2 | Oranguru `sv02-094` "Plotter's Command" parks and picks **"Peck"** → `3 + 1` | `[{ turn: 4, idx: 0 }]` |
| 4 | P1 | Skarmory `sv03-142` declares **"Slashing Steel"** (still legal), whose own drawback writes `4 + 2` **while the imposed entry is LIVE** | `[{ turn: 4, idx: 0 }, { turn: 6, idx: 1 }]` |

**"Slashing Steel" deals exactly Oranguru's 120**, so the board stops at
`ko:takePrizes` with `state.turn` **still 4** — and the **READER** is asked there
(`lockedAttackIndexes` still returns `[0]`), rather than the record merely inspected.
Let the turn roll to 5 instead and the entry is dead by arithmetic, and only the
record's SHAPE would be observable. That choice is what makes this a behaviour pin.

### The boundary is now pinned from BOTH sides

`>= now - 1` — which would keep one already-dead turn — fails the predecessor's own
prune case. `> now` fails the new one. **32 run, 32 caught.**

### ⚠️ THE TRANSFERABLE LINE: A SLICE'S OWN REPORT OF ITS OWN PASS IS A CLAIM, NOT A RECORD

The dangerous-claims list already carried *a predecessor's own FINDING* (D153
understated, D165 exact) and *a predecessor's own CORRECTION*. This adds a tenth:
**a predecessor's own count of what it verified** — the only number on a handoff that
**nothing in the repo can contradict**, because no test fails when it is wrong; being
wrong is precisely the state of there being no test.

### The other half: D164's doc debt, and what recovering it corrected

§D164 above, the `decisions.md` row, a `progress.md` header at build **#148b** and a
session-log entry — all reconstructed off `16fa8e8`'s message and diff, the same
remedy D163 applied to D162 one slice earlier. **The SECOND worktree slice in three
whose ritual a successor had to adopt**, which makes it a pattern rather than an
accident: **a worktree slice's docs are not "deferred", they are UNOWNED until a
successor adopts them.** One inherited number was corrected in passing:
**`FIXTURE_POOL` is 291** — not D164's 290, not D163's 289 — measured two ways (an
object-literal key sweep at `16fa8e8` and at HEAD, and a runtime import). The SECOND
number of a two-number census, wrong three handoffs running.

### The structural questions

- **PARK? NO. PERSIST? NO** — `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **11**: no
  `InPlayPokemon` field added, removed or retyped, no `GameState` / `EffectContext`
  field moved, no op parks. **`engineVersion` stays 0.111.0** on D150's precedent for
  a test-only slice — the only production diff is doc-block prose — and no `index.ts`
  changelog block is added, because that block is the version string's own record.
- **VOICE? Nothing moved.** **GUARD? The guard IS the subject.** **§11? Nothing
  owed** — no op added or removed. **Gates no action.**

### Cost

**2 tests** (`lockedAttackMerge.test.ts` **14 → 16**) and **3 doc blocks amended**
(`addLockedAttack`'s prune bullet, `index.ts`'s D165 changelog entry, and the D165
mutation lines in `decisions.md` / this file). No op, event, prompt, regex, fixture,
deck, registry row, error code, web / DB / `@luminous/schema` diff.

## D167 — the `×`/MULTIPLY TWIN on the attacker's own damage counters: `This attack does {30|50} damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.` — the bare, no-adjective form, and the printing that proves this family splits by FOLD rather than by COUNT SOURCE (engine 0.111.0 → 0.112.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

**Item 1** of the remainder list, carried since D163 measured it, and the cheapest item
that page had held in twenty slices. **The pricing was inherited and it held exactly** —
which is worth saying, because the standing note is that structural claims usually do
not.

### The census — re-run, not inherited

`LIKE '%for each damage counter%'` over **all three text columns** of the local D1
(2026-08-03, **978 rows / 6 sets**) is **19 rows / 6 shapes**. Subtract the `more` twin
(7 printings, read since M2) and the `less` twin (5 printings, D163) and **exactly two
rows remain, both on `attacks_json`, both at index 1**:

| printing | attack | idx | cost | printed damage | per |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Drifloon `sv01-089` | Balloon Blast | **1** | {P}{P} | `"30×"` | **30** |
| Onix `swsh10.5-036` | Raging Swing | **1** | {F}{F}{C}{C} | `"50×"` | **50** |

**2 printings / 2 sentences**, spanned by **one `(\d+)` capture** — D121's
second-printing warrant met by the catalog rather than by an invented string. Both ids
re-queried per printing.

### ⚠️ THE FAMILY SPLITS BY FOLD, NOT BY COUNT SOURCE — and until this printing that was indistinguishable from a coincidence

`SELF_COUNTER_MULTIPLY` sits in `effects.ts` beside `SELF_COUNTER_SCALE` and
`SELF_COUNTER_PENALTY`, and it feeds **one new arm** in
`deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`. `count` is the **existing** `damageCountersOnSelf`
member; `scaledAttackDamage`'s arm for it has been live since **M2**.

**The three folds now share ONE count source, told apart by one word** — the sharpest
available statement that this family is partitioned by FOLD:

| adjective | reader | fold | reported through | printing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `more` | `deriveAttackDamageBonus` | base + `per × count` | `DAMAGE_DEALT.scaled` | Paldean Tauros `sv02-028` |
| *(none)* | `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier` | `per × count`, **base dropped** | `DAMAGE_DEALT.scaled`, `base 0` | Drifloon `sv01-089` |
| `less` | `deriveAttackDamagePenalty` | base − `per × count` | `DAMAGE_DEALT.debuff` | Cetitan `sv01-060` |

Until this slice **each fold happened to own a disjoint set of count sources**, and it
would have been easy to read that accident as the design. It is not: the interface
(`{per, count}`) and the count evaluator are shared **by fold**, and the source is free
to appear under any of them.

**`attack.ts` takes ZERO behaviour diff**, and that is the payout rather than a
coincidence — every site was already written against the READER instead of against the
`count` member:

- `scaling` is `damageBonus ?? damageMultiplier`;
- the base-drop rule keys on `damageMultiplier !== null`;
- `effectSimulated` and `modifierSimulated` are both written `scaling !== null || …`.

All four sites already subsumed the new arm, so both the `"×"` marker and the effect
string simply stop being flagged. **The contrast with D163 is the transferable part:
D163 needed a whole THIRD READER because its FOLD was new; this one needed none because
its fold was not.** *"Is this a new count source, or a new fold?"* is the question this
family is priced by, and the two answers differ by an order of magnitude.

`selfCounterMultiply.test.ts` drives **all three folds off ONE board at ONE counter
total** (3 counters → **40 / 90 / 140** against the same clean 340 HP defender), which
is the case no per-reader `toEqual` can make.

### ⚠️ The plan said "reuse a fixture" and there was NOTHING to reuse — the census that mattered was of `FIXTURE_POOL`, not of the catalog

**Five** bodies in the pool already print this exact count source — `sv02-028`,
`sv03-161` and `fix-attacker`'s "Rage"/"Fury" with `more`; `sv01-060`, `sv02-037` with
`less` — and **not one prints the bare form**. Neither `sv01-089` nor `swsh10.5-036` was
fielded anywhere in `packages/engine/src`.

So **both fixtures are authored fresh and transcribed off the catalog**, and the cheap
dodge was priced and REFUSED: bending a neighbour's effect string would have turned
*"one regex spans two REAL printed amounts"* into a claim about a string the test file
itself wrote. **That is D146's rule read from the FIXTURE side, and it is the exact
inverse of D163's payout** — there the pool sweep found the sentence already present,
verbatim and unread, and four of five printings needed no fixture at all. **Sweep the
pool either way; the answer is the slice's shape, not a formality.**

**Fixtures** (both carrying their whole printed attack list at its printed index, so
**no `INCOMPLETE` declaration is owed and 0 new entries appear in that table**):

- **`sv01-089` Drifloon** — 70 HP Psychic Basic, retreat 1, ×2 Darkness, −30 Fighting.
  The 70 HP is load-bearing: it is the smallest body in this family by a wide margin,
  so the counter ladder the suite drives (1, 3, 6) stays under its own HP while `30 ×`
  it produces **30 / 90 / 180** — three numbers a hard-coded `per` cannot fake. Index 0
  "Gust" ({C}{C}, 10) carries **no `effect` key at all**: the derives-to-nothing
  index-keyed negative.
- **`swsh10.5-036` Onix** — 120 HP Fighting Basic, retreat 4, ×2 Grass. Index 0 "Rock
  Tomb" is a **live `preventRetreat` op**, which makes the same negative **sharper**
  than Drifloon's: a sibling attack fully simulated by a DIFFERENT mechanism, so
  "index 1's clause does not leak" is asserted against something rather than against
  silence. The **fourteenth `swsh10.5` fixture**, and the second written after the
  re-ingest made the set checkable (D160/D162).

### Two second-order behaviours of the `×` fold, inherited and now DRIVEN

1. **Zero counters emits no `DAMAGE_DEALT` at all.** `scaledBase` and `scaledTotal` are
   both 0, so `attack.ts`'s `if (scaledBase + scaledTotal > 0)` skips the whole §8.5
   pipeline. That is **rules-correct** — the attack does 0 damage — **and the attack is
   still USED**, so the turn ends. Both halves are asserted, and the second is the one
   an early `return` would break.
2. **The crumb renders the WHOLE damage as ` · scaled +90` off a `base 0`**, e.g.
   *"dealt 180 damage to fix-psychic-weak · scaled +90 · weakness ×2"*, rendered under
   both seats and READ. That is how every existing member of this fold already reads
   (Pecharunt ex, Annihilape, Stoutland), so **no `log.ts` diff** — D159's *"does the
   row you need already exist?"* check, run and answered YES for the third slice
   running.

### The pin that went red was the one written to go red — RE-POINTED, not deleted

`selfScalingPenalty.test.ts`'s *"the UNREAD multiply twin on the same count source is
STILL LOUD"* asserted `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier(BALLOON_BLAST)` → `null`
**explicitly so that adding this regex — "the whole of that item's price" — would fail
there and be noticed.** It did. The assertion flips to the PRESENCE
(`{ per: 30, count: { kind: "damageCountersOnSelf" } }`) and names the reader that now
owns the sentence; its **three siblings are untouched and still true** (the additive
reader, the subtractive reader and the op deriver must all still refuse it), which is
what keeps *"at most one fold per printing"* checked from that side of the family too.

No other suite pinned these sentences — swept for `sv01-089` / `swsh10.5-036` /
"Balloon Blast" / "Raging Swing" across the whole package: **three hits, all in that one
file.** **An absence pinned deliberately is an item's price paid forward**, and the
correct response when it goes red is to re-point it, never to delete it.

### The structural questions

1. **PARK / PERSIST — NEITHER.** The clause is CATALOG text read at declaration by a
   pure function of the current state: no stamp, no op, no event type, no enum value,
   no union member. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **11** — the **TENTH** control on
   D124's trigger — pinned as an **ABSENCE** over the 16-key `InPlayPokemon` set.
   `engineVersion` **0.111.0 → 0.112.0** (minor, matching D161 0.107, D163 0.109,
   D164 0.110, D165 0.111). `packages/engine/package.json` is NOT bumped — it has sat
   at `0.3.0` since P3-M3 and the live figure every slice header quotes is
   `engineVersion`.
2. **VOICE — NO ROW MOVED**, and it was checked rather than assumed (above).
3. **GUARDS SWEPT, NOT LISTED** — the pool-wide "at most one reader answers any
   printed attack" sweep still holds, and it holds precisely because **it never named a
   count** (289 fixtures when D163 wrote it, 293 now).
4. **MECHANISM EXISTS — and this time ALL of it did**, which is the whole slice.
5. **GATES NO ACTION** — the attack must still be OFFERED on the board where it deals
   **0** (D163's negative form: the sharp case is the one where a player would expect a
   refusal and must not get one). **§11: nothing owed** — no op added. **No `redact.ts`
   and no `GameHud.tsx` diff.**

### ⚠️ The regenerated manifest contradicts D160's own account of the catalog

`bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts` changed **two** things: the two new `printed` rows
(this slice's) and

```diff
-    mtime: "2026-08-03T09:22:30.953Z",
+    mtime: "2026-07-26T20:43:16.258Z",
```

which is simply what `statSync` reports for the sqlite today. **ctime matches mtime**
(so the file has not been rewritten in place), it is **708,608 bytes** — byte-identical
to the committed figure — and it still holds **978 rows / 6 sets** on a re-query, so
**no census number moves and no test breaks.** Only the provenance stamp does.

But D160 recorded the sqlite as re-ingested and WAL-checkpointed on **2026-08-03**, and
the file on disk says it has not been written since **2026-07-26 with the restored set
already in it**. The likely explanation is that the `.wrangler` D1 was **replaced by a
`mv` of a same-filesystem backup** (a `mv` preserves both mtime and ctime; `cp -p` would
not have preserved ctime). **The measurement is kept and the contradiction is written
down rather than reconciled silently** — hand-editing a `DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` generated
file to preserve a stale stamp is exactly the copied-forward-number disease
`catalogManifest.ts` exists against (D156). If the episode is ever to be *recorded*
rather than merely noted, it belongs in `CATALOG_MANIFEST.history` **via the generator**,
never as a hand edit.

### Cost

**1 regex, 1 `if`.** No new op, event, event field, log crumb, error code, prompt, park,
field, registry row, redact arm or projection; no new `DamageCountSource`, evaluator
arm, reader or fold; **no branch in `attack.ts`**; and **no web / DB /
`@luminous/schema` diff**. `attack.ts` and `index.ts` take **comment and doc diffs only**
apart from the version string.

Plus **2 fixtures** (`sv01-089`, `swsh10.5-036` — both COMPLETE against the manifest),
**1 deck** (`SELF_COUNTER_MULTIPLY_DECK`, its own 60 so `SELF_SCALING_PENALTY_DECK`'s
and `SCALED_DAMAGE_DECK`'s boards stay byte-identical), `selfCounterMultiply.test.ts`
(**30 tests, SEED-FREE** — nothing in this family flips a coin and every Active is
placed by surgery), `selfScalingPenalty.test.ts`'s pin re-pointed, and
`catalogManifest.ts` REGENERATED (209 → **211** fixture rows, 0 absent).

**Mutation-checked NINE ways, 9 caught, 0 survivors:**

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | delete the new arm from `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier` | 17 failed / 2 files |
| M2 | `per >= 1` → `per >= 0` (a printed 0 admitted) | 1 failed |
| M3 | `per` hard-coded to 30 | 11 failed / 5 files |

## D168 — the OPPONENT-SIDE damage-counter count (`damageCountersOnOpponentActive`): `This attack does {10|30} more damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.` — the FIFTH `DamageCountSource`, and the first member that MIRRORS a member the union already had (engine 0.112.0 → 0.113.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

fold.** The two together are the same question asked from both sides, one slice apart.

### ⚠️ A `count` member where D163's one-word-different sentence was a whole new READER

The family splits by **FOLD** (D167's finding): `+` keeps the printed base, `×` drops it,
`−` keeps it and subtracts — three readers over ONE `{per, count}` interface and ONE
count evaluator. **D163's sentence changed the SIGN, so it bought a third reader. This
one carries "more", so its fold is byte-identical to the one `deriveAttackDamageBonus`
already performs**, and the only thing that varies is WHICH RESOURCE is tallied — which
is precisely what `DamageCountSource` is for.

**A fourth reader would have duplicated a fold to vary a count; a fifth member varies the
count and reuses the fold.** The inverse answer to the inverse question, on sentences
that differ by one word each time.

### ⚠️ The FIFTH member is the FIRST that MIRRORS an existing member

`damageCountersOnSelf` and `damageCountersOnOpponentActive` tally the **identical
resource** — `InPlayPokemon.damage ÷ 10` — off **two different bodies**.

**Two members rather than one member with a `side` field**, because every consumer of
this union dispatches on `kind` and nothing else: a `side` would have to be read by
`scaledAttackDamage` anyway, and the three members that have no side at all would then
carry a field they must ignore.

**The mirror is also the sharpest defect this slice can have**, so it is driven rather
than argued:

- a board with **9 counters on the ATTACKER and 3 on the DEFENDER** — reading self
  scores **270**, summing both scores **360**, and the right answer is **90**;
- **both census sweeps are asserted side by side** (the opponent-side producers and the
  self-side producers), so a reader that started answering both would collapse two lists
  into one — which no assertion on a single sentence can see.

### ⚠️ THE FINDING NOBODY SPECCED: a RESISTANCE cannot witness the pre-W/R fold order

Espeon's **−30 Fighting Resistance** looked like the natural order witness and is not one.
**Subtraction COMMUTES with the fold's addition:**

```
(100 + 30) − 30  =  100
(100 − 30) + 30  =  100
```

Both placements produce the same number, so that board cannot tell them apart. **Only a
MULTIPLY W/R separates them**, and the suite says so in its own words rather than
quietly using a better board.

The order is therefore driven on **Tyranitar ex `sv03-066`** (340 HP, ×2 Fighting).
Bloodmoon Ursaluna at **2 counters**, into a body already carrying 20:

| placement | arithmetic | result |
|---|---|---|
| **correct** (fold, then W/R) | `(100 + 60) × 2 = 320` | 20 + 320 = **exactly 340 — a KO** |
| reversed (W/R, then fold) | `100 × 2 + 60 = 260` | 20 + 260 = 280, **alive with 60 HP** |

**Two observables move together**, and the second is not a number a reader can talk
themselves into. A second case re-derives the oracle from the ROW's OWN fields
(`applyDamageModifier` over `base` and `scaled` in both orders) at one counter fewer, so
both placements are two live numbers rather than a KO and a number.

Espeon's Resistance is **kept for what it CAN show**: the scaled total carrying a
defender **past a subtractive term it survived a moment earlier** — 70 at zero counters,
100 at one, and 110 HP between them.

⚠️ **The transferable form is general and belongs to every ordering claim, not to this
family: an ordering claim needs a witness that does NOT COMMUTE, and a subtractive W/R
term can never be one.**

### The fixtures were the real cost, and one requirement no existing deck could meet

`FIXTURE_POOL` had **ZERO** coverage: none of the three cards, neither sentence, and **no
body whose damage had ever been read from the DEFENDING side**. All three fixtures are
**authored fresh and whole** — Espeon's idx-1 "Psy Bolt" and Bloodmoon Ursaluna's
unsimulated "Battle-Hardened" Ability are **carried rather than dropped**, so neither
owes an `INCOMPLETE` declaration.

And every number in this family is `base + per × (the DEFENDER's counters)`, so **the
defender must arrive PRE-DAMAGED and still SURVIVE**. Ursaluna's `100 + 30n` outruns
`fix-bigbody`'s 200 HP at **n = 4**, and `SCALED_DAMAGE_DECK`'s bodies well before that.
**A defender that dies is a defender whose arithmetic was never read.** Hence
**`OPPONENT_COUNTER_DECK` on its own 60**, fielding two 340 HP tanks:

- **`fix-titan`** (340 HP, NO attacks, no Weakness or Resistance) — the mulligan-free
  starter and the clean-number defender;
- **Tyranitar ex `sv03-066`** (340 HP, ×2 Fighting, no Ability, no registry row) — the
  ORDER witness above.

Its own 60, so no neighbouring suite's board moves.

### The structural questions

1. **PARK / PERSIST — NEITHER.** The clause is CATALOG text read at declaration by a pure
   function of the current state. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **11**, and this is
   **derived rather than inherited**: `DamageCountSource` is a **PARSE-TIME type in
   `effects.ts` that never reaches `GameState`**, so a new member of it cannot make a
   previously-stored record unreadable — which is exactly why it buys no bump where
   **D165's CHANGED `InPlayPokemon` field** did. Pinned as an **ABSENCE** over the 16-key
   set; the **ELEVENTH** control on D124's trigger. `engineVersion` **0.112.0 →
   0.113.0**; `packages/engine/package.json` stays `0.3.0`.
2. **VOICE — NO ROW MOVED**, and it was checked rather than assumed: the ` · scaled +N`
   crumb has rendered this field since 0.35.0, and is driven under **both** seats and
   READ (`dealt 190 damage to fix-titan · scaled +90`), plus the silent case — a pristine
   defender emits **no `scaled` at all**, because loudness is owed to UNREAD text (D140)
   and a fold that added nothing must not speak.
3. **GUARDS SWEPT, NOT LISTED** — the pool-wide "at most one reader answers any printed
   attack" sweep still holds, and the two count-source censuses are asserted **side by
   side** for the mirror reason above.
4. **MECHANISM EXISTS** — everything except the regex, the arm, the member and the
   evaluator arm did.
5. **GATES NO ACTION** — the attack must still be OFFERED against a **pristine** defender
   where the fold adds 0 (D163's negative form). **§11: nothing owed** — no op added.
   **No `redact.ts` and no `GameHud.tsx` diff.**

### ⚠️ A GENERATED FILE MUST BE REGENERATED, NEVER TEXT-MERGED

This slice and **D167** ran in **parallel worktrees** and both regenerated
`catalogManifest.ts` **independently from the same 209-row base**. D167 produced **211**;
this slice produced **212**. The true merged figure is **214**, and **no textual
resolution of the two diffs would ever have produced it** — a three-way merge of a
generated file resolves *cleanly* and is still wrong, because the file is a **FUNCTION of
inputs neither side had whole**.

The manifest was **regenerated after the merge** (`bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts`)
and this slice's own changelog line corrected from *"209 → 212"* to **"211 → 214"**.
**When two slices touch a generated file, the merge is a re-run, not a resolution** —
and the number a worktree handoff quotes for it is a number measured against a base that
no longer exists.

## D169 — the FIRST ATTACK-COST DISCOUNT and its SURCHARGE sibling: `This Pokémon's attacks cost Colorless less for each Prize card your opponent has taken.` / `As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, attacks used by your opponent's Active Pokémon cost {C} more.` — one mechanism, opposite signs, and an item whose real cost was the RENDER BYPASS (engine 0.113.0 → 0.114.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

**Item 3 of the remainder list**, priced at D162 with the code open — and **the first slice
of this batch that reaches outside `packages/engine`**: `packages/schema`,
`src/features/game` and `src/features/online` all move.

### Family: 3 printings / 3 distinct sentences — CLOSED at 3/3

Censused as its own question against the local D1 (**978 cards / 6 sets**, 2026-08-03,
all three text columns). `attacks_json` contributes nothing — **no attack in the pool
modifies a cost** — so both new rows are **Abilities**.

| card | sentence | shape |
|---|---|---|
| Pokémon League Headquarters `sv03-192` (Stadium) | "Attacks used by each **Basic** Pokémon in play (both yours and your opponent's) cost {C} more." | `StadiumEffects.basicAttackCostSurcharge` — **built since M4**, this slice's PRECEDENT rather than its work |
| Seismitoad `sv03-052` "Quaking Zone" | "As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, attacks used by your opponent's Active Pokémon cost {C} more." | `PassiveEffects.opponentActiveAttackCostSurcharge` → `continuous.ts opposingAttackCostSurcharge` |
| Radiant Charizard `swsh10.5-011` "Excited Heart" | "This Pokémon's attacks cost Colorless less for each Prize card your opponent has taken." | `PassiveEffects.attackCostDiscountPerOpponentPrize` → `continuous.ts selfAttackCostDiscount` |

Taken as **ONE slice rather than two**, on the ground that splitting would ship a seam
that handles one sign: **the discount forces the fold's SHAPE and the surcharge forces
the fold's STAGE answer.**

### The seam, and the fold restated

`continuous.ts effectiveAttackCost(state, pokemon, cost)` — still the one **payability**
derivation point, still with **three** consumers and no bypass: `attack.ts` §8.2 (its
only `attack.cost` read), `redact.ts redactedAttacksOf` (`playable`), `GameHud.tsx`
(`costMet`). **Its signature and all three call sites are UNTOUCHED**; both new sources
derive their seat internally, the aura-scan family's standard trick.

```
stadium = isBasic(top) ? stadium.basicAttackCostSurcharge : 0     // a per-TERM gate
added   = stadium + opposingAttackCostSurcharge(state, pokemon)   // stage-agnostic
net     = added - selfAttackCostDiscount(state, pokemon)
net === 0 → the caller's own array;  net > 0 → append net "Colorless";
net < 0   → remove up to -net "Colorless" FROM THE END (self-flooring)
```

**⚠️ THE ONE REAL ENGINE NOVELTY IS THE DISCOUNT DIRECTION, AND IT IS ABOUT TEN LINES.**
Everything the surcharge needs already existed, and so did the count: `takenPrizes` is
the function `attack.ts` already calls for the identical printed phrase (D144's
`opponentPrizesTaken` count kind).

**Both signs were expressible with NO type change.** The seam returns
`readonly string[]` of literal energy symbols with `"Colorless"` a distinguished member
— `costMet` buckets it by exactly that string compare (§6.4: any energy pays a Colorless
slot) — so a surcharge **appends** and a discount **removes**. A discount never touches
a typed symbol; the print says *"cost Colorless less"* and means it.

**⚠️ NO `Math.max(0, …)` IS OWED, AND THE REASON IS THE DATA STRUCTURE.** The array
**floors itself**: a removal loop can only remove symbols that are present, so a 6-Prize
discount against a printed `{W}{W}` leaves `{W}{W}`. Contrast `effectiveRetreatCost` one
screen up, whose cost is a **NUMBER** and which must clamp. **This seam owes no floor
because of its shape, not because someone remembered to write a check.**

**⚠️ THE TWO DIRECTIONS ARE SEPARATE FIELDS SUMMED INTO ONE NET DELTA — D163's trap,
named in advance and refused by construction.** The old body early-returned on
`surcharge <= 0`; a single field carrying both signs would have read a real discount as
*"nothing applies"*. The retreat seam already set the precedent with distinct
discount/surcharge fields (`stadiumRetreatDelta`'s `added - discount`). The netting is
**exact rather than convenient**: appending N Colorless and then removing M of them
leaves `max(0, printedColorless + N − M)`, which is what applying the net delta directly
produces — **no board separates the two orders**, and `effectiveAttackCost` returns the
**caller's own array** at net zero, which is both the cheap common path and the assertion
that `+1` and `−1` really cancelled.

### ⚠️ The defect NEITHER the recon NOR the brief found — a gate that belonged to ONE term

The body opened:

```ts
if (top === undefined || !isBasicPokemon(top)) return cost;
```

**That Basic gate belongs to League HQ's printed *"each BASIC Pokémon in play"* and to
NOTHING else.** Neither new sentence prints a stage, and **Seismitoad is itself a Stage
2** — so a surviving early return would have silently switched the new aura off against
**every Stage 1/2 Active it aims at**, on the one card whose own stage guarantees the
case comes up. The Basic test is now a **per-TERM gate**, `stadiumRetreatDelta`'s
precedent (*"a zero TERM, not the early return it used to be"*, made when the first
stage-agnostic aura reached the RETREAT seam). **This is the second time a Stadium's
stage clause has been mistaken for the seam's, and both times a cross-board Ability
exposed it.** It is also the mutant that kills **4** tests.

> **⚠️ THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH BELONGS TO EVERY WIDENING AND NOT TO THIS SEAM: A
> SHARED SEAM'S OPENING GUARD CAN BELONG TO ONLY ONE OF ITS TERMS, AND THE SECOND TERM
> INHERITS IT INVISIBLY.** When you widen a function that already serves one printing,
> read its EARLY RETURNS as the OLD term's preconditions rather than as the function's.
> Nothing in the type, the name or the existing tests says which.

### ⚠️ A better precedent than the one the brief supplied

The brief named **`opposingRetreatSurcharge`** (Spidops ex "Trap Territory") as
Seismitoad's near-verbatim twin. The truth is **`opposingAttackDebuff` (D151, Entei
"Pressure")**, which prints the *identical sentence* with exactly one predicate changed:

| | sentence |
|---|---|
| Entei `sv03-030` "Pressure" (D151) | "As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, attacks used by your opponent's Active Pokémon **do 20 less damage** (before applying Weakness and Resistance)." |
| Seismitoad `sv03-052` "Quaking Zone" (D169) | "As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, attacks used by your opponent's Active Pokémon **cost {C} more**." |

So **both Active clauses came free in one scan** — the SOURCE clause scoping the holder
to the Active Spot (a benched Seismitoad surcharges nothing; contrast
`opposingRetreatSurcharge`, whose print scopes only the TARGET) and the TARGET clause
scoping the victim to the opposing Active — and **nothing needed borrowing from
`opposingRetreatBlocked`**. `opposingAttackCostSurcharge` is `opposingAttackDebuff`'s
scan with one field name renamed: derived seat, both Active clauses enforced by the scan
rather than by an `activeOnly` field, the §9 gate through `disabledAbilityUids`, and
**no source loop** (the source clause is the opponent's Active ALONE, so a loop would
describe a board that cannot exist).

**The aura-scan family is now ELEVEN members**, in `continuous.ts` order:
`disabledAbilityUids` / `seatRemovesWeakness` / `hasFreeRetreatAura` /
`opposingRetreatSurcharge` / `opposingRetreatBlocked` / `hasFreeRetreatSelf` /
`opposingAttackDebuff` / `benchShieldedByActive` / the `installedAttackDebuffOf`-adjacent
scans / **`opposingAttackCostSurcharge`** (#10, cross-board, both Active clauses) /
**`selfAttackCostDiscount`** (#11, SELF-only but looks across the table —
`hasFreeRetreatSelf`'s shape, second instance).

### §9 suppression is FREE on both cards, and the two take DIFFERENT locks

`passivesOf` already suppresses the holder's own Ability, so the discount's §9 answer
cost nothing; Seismitoad gets its gate from the sibling scan's existing
`disabledAbilityUids` line.

- **Radiant Charizard is a BASIC**, so Klefki `sv01-096` "Mischievous Lock" really does
  silence Excited Heart and the printed `{R}{C}{C}{C}{C}` snaps back — **the family's
  third assertable §9 positive after D113's Snorlax and D114's Wimpod**.
- **Seismitoad is a STAGE 2, which no Klefki can reach** (D113's rule: reachability
  follows the SOURCE's stage), so its lock is **Ting-Lu ex `sv02-127` "Cursed Land"**
  against a **damaged** holder.

**Both boards are driven**, and the Klefki-cannot-reach-Seismitoad **negative** is driven
too, because it is the line that explains why the second lock is a different card.

### ⚠️ THE RENDER BYPASS — the item's true cost, which its original pricing missed entirely

`effectiveAttackCost` was the one **payability** seam and **not** the one **cost** seam:

- `redact.ts` published `cost: [...(attack.cost ?? [])]` — the **PRINTED** cost — on the
  line immediately above the one computing `playable` from the **EFFECTIVE** cost;
- `packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts` pinned that deliberately (*"`cost` is the
  PRINTED cost (for the energy dots)"*);
- both HUDs drew `<EnergyDots cost={attack.cost} />`, the local one with a comment saying
  so out loud.

**A shipped divergence.** **League HQ's surcharge has been invisible to players since it
shipped** — the button greys out and the dots do not say why — and a **discount** makes
it wrong in the **worse direction**: the attack button goes LIVE while the dots still
show the full cost the player has not paid.

### ⚠️ THE DECISION, AND IT IS THE SLICE'S REAL ONE: a SIBLING field, not a widened `cost`

`RedactedAttack` gains **`effectiveCost?: string[]`**, and **`cost` still means
PRINTED**. Four reasons, in the order they decided it:

1. **`cost`'s meaning as PRINTED is documented and depended on.** It is stated in the
   schema doc block and read by several call sites. Silently changing what an existing
   wire field means is the kind of reversal `conventions.md` requires a trail for —
   *"the only hard rule is don't reverse one silently"*. **A sibling is additive and
   reversible; a widened `cost` is neither.**
2. **The pair is strictly more informative than either field alone.** A client can render
   *"was 5, now 3"*, or tint the modified dots — which no single field can express, and
   which is exactly what a player staring at a greyed button needs.
3. **⚠️ The one candidate counter-argument was CHECKED and REJECTED.**
   `RedactedRetreat.cost` **does** publish the CONTINUOUS number under a plain name,
   which looks like an argument for widening — **but the printed retreat cost is not on
   the wire at all, so there was no second reading to preserve. Attacks carry BOTH
   readings; retreat carries one. The asymmetry is in the DATA, not in the taste.**
4. **Optional, and emitted ONLY when it differs from the print.** That mirrors
   `effectiveAttackCost`'s own contract (it returns the printed array itself when nothing
   applies) and keeps the frame byte-identical on every board with no cost modifier in
   play, so its *presence* MEANS *"this cost is modified"* — a fact a renderer could not
   otherwise derive. ⚠️ **The field means "DIFFERS FROM THE PRINT", not "a modifier
   exists": a `+1/−1` board and a discount with nothing left to remove both OMIT it, and
   both are pinned.**

**Render `effectiveCost ?? cost` wherever a player sees energy dots.** The online HUD does
exactly that; the local HUD needs no wire field at all and simply draws the array it
already computed (`EnergyDots`'s comment is re-pointed to say the cost handed in is the
EFFECTIVE one).

**No `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` consequence — 11 stands, DERIVED not inherited.** D124's test
is *"can the PREVIOUS deploy's RECORD hold the new TYPE"*, and `MatchRecord` persists
exactly `{version, seed, startedAt, names, state: GameState, log: SeatLogEntry[]}`.
**`RedactedAttack` is a wire projection, rebuilt every frame and persisted nowhere.**
Nothing was stamped onto `InPlayPokemon`: both prints are continuous ABILITIES re-read

field, no `BoardCondition` member, no op, no event, no error code (the §8 gate still
reuses `ATTACK_COST_UNMET`), no `EffectContinuation` inhabitant. `engineVersion`
**0.113.0 → 0.114.0**; `packages/engine/package.json` stays `0.3.0`.

## D170 — the BENCH-WIDE damage-counter count (`damageCountersOnYourBench`): `This attack does 10 damage for each damage counter on all of your Benched Pokémon.` — the SIXTH `DamageCountSource`, the FIRST that tallies over a ZONE rather than off a body, and the fourth corner of the fold × source square (engine 0.114.0 → 0.115.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

**Item 2's Family B** of the remainder list, and the last of the three items D167's
*"still unmapped"* section left standing **that is a scaling arm at all**. It was
deliberately sequenced AFTER D167, which put the multiply reader's third arm in the very
function body this slice edits.

### The family — 1 printing / 1 sentence, and it CLOSES at 1/1

Measured against the local D1 (2026-08-03, **978 cards / 6 sets**) across all three text
columns. `LIKE '%for each damage counter%'` is **19 rows** — the whole neighbourhood;
`LIKE '%on all of your Benched%'` is **exactly one**, and it is the same row:

| card | idx | attack | cost | printed | per |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tyranitar `swsh10.5-043` | **0** | Raging Crash | {C}{C} | `10×` | **10** |

The inherited catalog claim was **CONFIRMED in full** and **re-queried per printing rather
than recognised**. The printed stats were completed off the D1 rather than assumed:
**Stage 2 evolving from Pupitar, 180 HP, {C}{C}, Darkness, retreat 3, ×2 Grass, no
Resistance, no Ability, two attacks.**

⚠️ **ONE PRINTING MEANS THE `(\d+)` CAPTURE HAS NO SECOND WITNESS, AND THE SUITE SAYS
SO.** D121's second-printing warrant is met for this *family* by its three siblings
(self-`more` 7, self-`less` 5, self-bare 2, opponent-`more` 3), **never by this member**.
The capture is therefore driven on a rewritten amount that is **explicitly labelled
constructed text** — the inverse of D146's rule, applied so that a later reader cannot
mistake the assertion for a card.

### ⚠️ A NEW COUNT SOURCE ON AN OLD FOLD — D168's answer, on the multiply reader

The family splits by **FOLD** (D167's finding): `+` keeps the printed base, `×` drops it,
`−` keeps it and subtracts — three readers over one `{per, count}` interface and one count
evaluator. This sentence carries **no adjective**, so its fold is the `×` one
`deriveAttackDamageMultiplier` has performed since 0.35.0, and the only thing that varies
is **which resource is tallied** — which is precisely what `DamageCountSource` is for.

That completes a two-by-two the last three slices have been filling in one corner at a
time:

| | old fold | new fold |
|---|---|---|
| **old source** | (M2 baseline) | **D167** — bare `×` on `damageCountersOnSelf` |
| **new source** | **D168** (additive) / **D170** (multiply) | — |

**D167 was a new fold on an old source; D168 a new source on the ADDITIVE fold; D170 a new
source on the MULTIPLY fold.** The question this family is priced by is still *"is this a
new count source, or a new fold?"*, and the two answers still differ by an order of
magnitude.

### ⚠️ The FIRST member that tallies over a ZONE

`damageCountersOnSelf` reads the attacking Active, `damageCountersOnOpponentActive` (D168)
the defending one; this reads **neither Active** and **every body on the attacker's
Bench**. Consequences, each driven:

- **an EMPTY Bench and a pristine Bench are the same 0**, and the arm reaches that by
  summing an empty list rather than by a guard — a `bench[0]` implementation *throws* on
  the first and merely under-reads on the second;
- the floor is **per body, before the sum** (`Math.floor(p.damage / 10)` inside the
  `reduce`), so a stray non-multiple cannot round its way into a neighbour's slot: 25 + 25
  is 2 + 2 = **4**, not 50 ÷ 10 = 5. Driven, and mutated;
- the `p !== null` guard **mirrors `interpreter.ts`'s `yourBenchDamaged`** over the
  identical list. The type is non-nullable; the guard exists so the two walks over one zone
  read the same, **not** because a null is reachable.

### ⚠️ The SEAT is the whole defect surface — this member counts YOUR bench and hits THEIRS

D168's fifth member counts the **opponent's** Active; this one counts the **attacker's
own** Bench, and the attack that reads it damages the opponent. Count and target sit at
**opposite ends of one swing**, so a `defenderSeat` wiring is a mistake that survives every
symmetric board. The suite therefore drives a board with **all four zones damaged and all
four differently**:

| zone | counters | what a wrong arm would score |
|---|---|---|
| attacker's Active | 9 | 90 (`damageCountersOnSelf`) |
| **attacker's Bench** | **3** | **30 — the right answer** |
| defender's Active | 5 | 50 (`damageCountersOnOpponentActive`) |
| defender's Bench | 7 | 70 |

Every wrong zone, every pairwise sum (100 / 120 / 140 / 160 …) and the whole-board total of
240 are distinct from 30 and from each other, and the **mirror board driven from p2** makes
a seat mix-up fail on one side or the other rather than on neither.

`scaledAttackDamage` needed **no signature change** to reach it: `attackerSeat` has been in
scope since **0.66.0** for D115's `boardCondition` indicator, and this is the **second**
thing that argument buys.

### ⚠️ NO ORDER WITNESS EXISTS IN THIS FAMILY — the slice corrected its own brief

D168's transferable finding is that **an ordering claim needs a witness that does not
COMMUTE**, and this slice was dispatched to produce one. **It cannot exist here.** With the
printed base DROPPED, this fold has **exactly one term**, so

```
(0 + 60) × 2  =  0 × 2 + 60 × 2  =  120
```

agree **by distribution**, not by luck. There is no board in this family that separates the
two placements, and **the suite pins that as its own assertion** — beside the additive
contrast `(100 + 60) × 2 ≠ 100 × 2 + 60`, which is exactly why D168 could drive an order
and this slice cannot.

What the ×2 board **does** witness is the **base drop surviving a multiply**: Tyranitar is
a DARKNESS Pokémon into `fix-darkness-weak` (200 HP, ×2 Darkness) at 6 counters, so
`(0 + 60) × 2 = 120` stands against a leaked `(10 + 60) × 2 = 140`. The Weakness turns a
10 HP mistake into a 20 HP one, which is the only thing a multiply W/R can add to a
single-term fold.

⚠️ **THE TRANSFERABLE FORM IS D168's RULE'S CONVERSE, AND IT BELONGS TO EVERY ORDERING
CLAIM: WHERE A FOLD HAS ONE TERM, THE ORDERING QUESTION DOES NOT ARISE, AND A TEST THAT
CLAIMS TO WITNESS IT IS TESTING NOTHING. PIN THE ABSENCE.** D168 said an ordering claim
needs a non-commuting witness; the other half is that some families **cannot produce one**,
and the honest move there is an assertion that says so rather than a board that "looks
like" an order test.

| `BENCH_COUNTER_MULTIPLY` regex + doc block | `effects.ts`, **its own group after `OPPONENT_COUNTER_SCALE`** |
| reader arm | `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`, LAST, with its own `per >= 1` guard |
| `DamageCountSource` member | `damageCountersOnYourBench` |
| evaluator arm | `scaledAttackDamage` (`attack.ts`) — **no signature change** |

RIGHT ON THE SHAPE, for the SECOND slice running.** It omitted the reader arm (a regex with

on the additive reader one slice earlier, on the same remainder-list page**, which makes it
a **property of that page's pricing METHOD** rather than a one-off slip: *the list prices
the SENTENCE and the FOLD, and forgets that a new SOURCE is three edits, not one.* Any
future *"one regex + one evaluator arm"* costing on that page should be read as **at least

⚠️ **PLACEMENT: D168's lesson APPLIED, not re-learned.** The regex is grouped by **COUNT
SOURCE**, in its own block after the `OPPONENT_COUNTER_SCALE` line — not next to

whose opening sentence is *"THE SIGN-FLIPPED TWIN OF **THE LINE ABOVE**"*.

### ⚠️ First-match-wins verified in BOTH directions

There are now **four** patterns in `effects.ts` carrying the words "damage counter". All
are `^…$`-anchored with literal tails — `on this Pokémon.` (×2), `Active Pokémon.`,
`on all of your Benched Pokémon.` — so **no side needs a negative lookahead**. Driven both

**Both adjectived twins of THIS source are ABSENCES, not unread printings.** The D1 sweep

The near-misses are all **real catalog rows**: Oinkologne ex `sv01-158`/`-234` "Maddening

### The fixture was the real cost, and it drags in an ADMISSION

`FIXTURE_POOL` had **ZERO** coverage — `swsh10.5-043` was fielded nowhere in
`packages/engine/src`, and **no body in the pool had ever had its BENCH read for a
number**. The fixture is **authored fresh and transcribed off the catalog row**, whole and
COMPLETE against the manifest, so **no `INCOMPLETE` entry is owed**.

⚠️ **ITS INDEX-1 "Earthquake" IS UNSIMULATED, AND THE FIXTURE STATES THAT OUT LOUD.**
*"This attack also does 20 damage to each of your Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness
and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)"* — a **self-spread** no regex in `effects.ts` matches
(all four derivers return null, verified), so declaring it emits `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`
carrying the whole sentence. Carried whole for D156's reason (a dropped attack is wrong by
OMISSION and owes an `INCOMPLETE` declaration) and D169's convention (carrying it means the
fixture *states* a simplification rather than hiding it behind a card that looks fully
simulated). Krookodile `sv01-117` prints the same sentence at 30, so this is a **family
absence, not a one-card gap**.

It is also this slice's **skipped-sibling witness, and a better one than D168's**: Espeon's
"Psy Bolt" was a sibling the engine *does* read, where this is a sibling the engine openly
does not — so *"index 1 does not inherit index 0's clause"* and *"index 1 is still loud"*
are asserted on the **same board**, and together they separate *"the clause was read"* from
*"the card was recognised"*.

**A STAGE 2, placed by SURGERY** (`setActiveFromDeck`), so no Larvitar and no Pupitar are
carried — D168's precedent for Espeon (a Stage 1), **one stage deeper**. The alternative (a
Larvitar plus two played evolutions) would have bought nothing this family tests and made
every board three turns longer.

**`BENCH_COUNTER_DECK` on its own 60.** `CONDITION_CLAUSE_DECK` was **read first and
rejected** — it is the closest existing template, the one deck that fields a damaged Bench
at all (for `yourBenchDamaged`) — but it is **seed-pinned** by a suite with nothing to do
with this printing, and a `yourBenchDamaged` board needs only ONE damaged body where this
one needs a Bench whose **per-slot totals differ**. The fillers are `fix-titan` (340 HP, no
attacks, no W/R): a body that holds ten counters nowhere near a Knock Out, which is what
makes *"20 / 0 / 50 on three slots"* a readable board rather than a dying one — and the
same card plays starter, bench and clean defender because it is the one body that is both a
Basic and inert. `fix-darkness-weak` (200 HP, ×2 Darkness) is the §8.5 board. **The `×` fold
has no printed ceiling** — five slots at ten counters each is 500 — which is why the
defender is the largest body in the pool.

### Zero bench counters emit no `DAMAGE_DEALT` at all — DRIVEN, not discovered

`scaledBase` and `scaledTotal` are both 0, so `attack.ts`'s
`if (scaledBase + scaledTotal > 0)` skips the whole §8.5 pipeline. That is
**rules-correct** (the attack does 0 damage), **the attack is still USED** so the turn
passes to the opponent — the half an early `return` would break — and the printed text is
**still SIMULATED**, which is the distinction D140 draws. Exactly how D167's printings and
Stoutland's retreat-0 board already behave; inherited from the spec and asserted rather
than found later.

### The structural questions

1. **PARK / PERSIST — NEITHER.** The clause is CATALOG text read at declaration by a pure
   function of the current state: no stamp, no op, no event type, no event field, no state
   field. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **11**, and this is **DERIVED, not inherited from
   D168**: D124's test is *"can the previous deploy's RECORD hold the new TYPE"*, and
   `DamageCountSource` is a **PARSE-TIME type in `effects.ts` that never reaches
   `GameState`** — so a new member of it cannot make a previously-stored record unreadable,
   which is exactly why it buys no bump where **D165's CHANGED `InPlayPokemon` field** did.
   The reasoning transfers **because the shape of the change is identical**: a union member,
   a reader arm, an evaluator arm, and no stamp anywhere. Checked against this slice's own
   novelty too — **reading a new ZONE reads an EXISTING field off EXISTING bodies.** Pinned
   as an **ABSENCE** over the 16-key `InPlayPokemon` set, now on a **BENCHED** body as well
   as an Active (the first time that pin has been taken off the bench); the **THIRTEENTH**
   control on D124's trigger (D169 is the twelfth). `engineVersion` **0.114.0 → 0.115.0**;
   `packages/engine/package.json` stays `0.3.0`.
2. **VOICE — NO ROW MOVED**, checked rather than assumed: the ` · scaled +N` crumb off a
   `base 0` is how every member of the `×` fold already reads, driven under **both** seats
   and READ (`dealt 70 damage to fix-titan · scaled +70`), plus the silent case — a pristine
   Bench emits **no damage row at all**, so there is nothing to hang a crumb on.
3. **GUARDS SWEPT, NOT LISTED** — the pool-wide *"at most one reader answers any printed
   attack"* sweep still holds, and the bench-side and self-side multiply censuses are
   asserted **side by side**, because the two members share a READER and the sharpest
   available defect is one list absorbing the other.
4. **MECHANISM EXISTS** — everything except the regex, the arm, the member and the
   evaluator arm did.
5. **GATES NO ACTION** — the attack must still be OFFERED with an EMPTY Bench across from a
   full-health defender, where it deals **0** (D163's negative form: the sharp case is the
   one where a player would expect a refusal and must not get one). **§11: nothing owed** —
   no op added. **No `redact.ts` and no `GameHud.tsx` diff.**

Each mutant is *the mistake someone would actually make*, per the D169 lesson. Counts are
engine-package test FILES failed out of 114.

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | delete the reader arm (regex present, no arm — **the exact omission the pricing made**) | 1 file failed |

| M9 | `bench[0]` only (first slot) | 1 file failed |

⚠️ **NOT A MUTANT — A MEASUREMENT, AND THE TECHNIQUE IS WORTH THE LINE.** Moving the new
arm from LAST to FIRST inside `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier` and re-running the engine

mutually exclusive and the arm order carries no behaviour, where a mutation could only ever
have shown the absence of a failure. D157's rule (the comment says so rather than
pretending a test covers it) is now backed by a measurement rather than by an argument.
