## D171 — the TOOL-BORNE ON-KO TRIGGER: `When your Active Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, you may move a Basic Energy from that Pokémon to the Pokémon this card is attached to.` — Exp. Share `sv01-174`, the KO-antecedent family CLOSES, and the cost was a FOURTH DETECTION SITE nobody had priced (engine 0.115.0 → 0.116.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

The **last unread member** of D158's census, deferred at D164 with a price that a recon
pass then overturned **in both directions**. It is also the **first card in this engine
whose printed sentence is borne by a POKÉMON TOOL on a body OTHER than the one the
sentence is about** — the subject (*"your Active Pokémon"*) and the bearer (*"the Pokémon
this card is attached to"*) are two different Pokémon, and only one of them is dying.

### The inherited pricing was wrong in BOTH directions

D164 priced this as *"a `you may` choice that must PARK mid-sweep"*. That half was
**free**:

- `settleProgram`'s `resumeTail` is a **pure control-return flag that captures no KO
  state at all** — its whole contract is *"a PendingStage is sitting behind me"* — so the
  park needed **zero widening**;
- `TriggeredAbility.optional` **auto-fires**, so the printed *"you MAY"* buys no confirm
  arm;
- `moveEnergy` is **already declinable** — an empty pick is a legal answer
  (`validateChoice`) — so "may" is expressed by the ANSWER rather than by a branch.

**No confirm arm, no new prompt family, no new prompt kind, no new event type, no new log
arm.** The price was somewhere else entirely.

### ⚠️ THE SLICE'S REAL DECISION: A FOURTH DETECTION SITE

`triggers.ts koToolTriggersOf(state, seat, koedUid)` — *for each of my in-play Pokémon,
for each attached Tool, is there an `onAllyActiveKnockOut` program keyed on ANOTHER body's
KO* — with a new `TriggerTiming`, `onAllyActiveKnockOut`. **First of its kind in this
repo**, and each of the three existing sites fails for its own structural reason:

| site | what it reads | why it cannot see this card |
|---|---|---|
| `onKnockOutTrigger` | `cardIdByUid[uid]` of the **KO'd body's top card** | wrong body — the bearer SURVIVES — and it never looks at tools |
| `triggersOf` | `topCardOf(pokemon)` | a Tool is **never a stack top**, so this misses every Tool for **every** timing |
| `passivesOf` | **walks `pokemon.tools`** — the only pre-D171 site that does | folds `passive` into **NUMBERS**; no way to express a program, a park or a controller |

That third row is the whole economics of this family: **Vengeful Punch `sv03-197` was a
DATA ROW because its consequent is a number on a body that survives; this could not be,
because its consequent moves a CARD THE PLAYER CHOOSES off a body that does not.** Same
printed antecedent, same instant, opposite prices.

**Two deliberate refusals in the scan, each a line of the printed sentence:**

1. **THE KO'D BODY IS SKIPPED.** *"…move a Basic Energy from THAT Pokémon to THE POKÉMON
   THIS CARD IS ATTACHED TO"* names **two** Pokémon. A self-attached Exp. Share has no
   destination distinct from its source and is in the same discard-bound stack as the
   Energy, so it is not a holder here.
2. **NO §9 GATE.** `triggersOf` suppresses a locked Pokémon's triggered Abilities; this
   scan deliberately does not, because **a TOOL IS NOT AN ABILITY** — `passivesOf` states
   the same exemption for the same reason. A Klefki aura live over the holder leaves Exp.
   Share working, and **the negative is driven with the lock PROVED LIVE FIRST**
   (`disabledAbilityUids` really contains the holder's uid), so the positive cannot be
   vacuous. **An absence measured, not assumed.**

### ⚠️ THE SEAM: `koTrigger` IS A TEMPORAL IMPOSSIBILITY, NOT A WIDENING PROBLEM

`collectKnockOuts` queues its `koTrigger` stages **after** `knockOut` has run for every
ref in the batch, and `knockOut` does `discardFromStack(side, side.active, "all")`. By the
time any on-KO stage could look, **the Energy this sentence moves is in the discard
pile.** No amount of park support fixes that.

`koRecoilOf` **IS** a genuine before-`knockOut` hook — it is why Vengeful Punch works, and
it is deliberately placed ahead of the sweep — but it is **SYNCHRONOUS and cannot park**,
and this consequent is a player's choice. **Right point, wrong mechanism.**

The seam that fits is a **SIBLING OF `damagedTrigger`**:

```
attack.ts:  [ damagedTrigger? , koToolTrigger? , attackEpilogue ]
                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
           seeded on TOOL PRESENCE; runs under the DAMAGED, non-turn seat;
           settleProgram(..., { resumeTail: true })
```

It sits **BEHIND** `damagedTrigger` because *"damaged"* precedes *"Knocked Out"* in the
same instant, and because a reaction that heals or switches the defender should be able to
**unmake the KO this stage is conditioned on**. It sits **AHEAD** of `attackEpilogue`
because that is the only window that exists at all.

### ⚠️ THE STAGE CARRIES THE SEAT AND NOTHING ELSE

`{ kind: "koToolTrigger"; seat: Seat }` — the one member of `PendingStage` that names
**neither** the body that acts **nor** the body it is about. Both are re-read off the live
board when it runs:

- **"your ACTIVE Pokémon"** — whatever is in the spot NOW, which is what the present tense
  says.
- **"is Knocked Out"** — `isLethallyDamaged`, **the sweep's OWN predicate**, so "this will
  die" here cannot drift from what `collectKnockOuts` decides two stages later. That is
  `koRecoilOf`'s rule read one stage out.
- **"by damage from an attack from your OPPONENT'S Pokémon"** — discharged by
  **PLACEMENT**, exactly as D158 discharged it. Only `attack.ts` seeds this stage, and only
  for the DEFENDER's seat; the Checkup and the mid-turn sweep call `collectKnockOuts`
  directly and can never reach it.

⚠️ **AND THIS IS A CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, NOT A SAVING.** The recon specified a PAIR of
run-time re-checks — *"still lethal"* **and** *"still the same Active"* — with the uid
carried on the stage to support the second. **The pair collapsed to one**: re-reading the
subject off the live board is simpler and more honest than validating a remembered uid,
which would be a **second opinion that can disagree with the sweep**. `attackEpilogue`
already carries exactly one seat for the same reason. The general form is
`damagedByAttackAbility`'s *"re-derive the printed clause where it is answerable"* carried
far enough to **DELETE the remembered uid rather than re-validate it**.

⚠️ **COLLAPSING IT KILLED A FIXTURE THE BRIEF EXPECTED, AND BACKING OUT WAS THE RIGHT
CALL.** Driving a promotion between seed and run would have needed a `gust` on an attack,
which drags in an unrelated **§11 `preventBlock` ruling** the slice had no mandate to
make. The agent **backed out rather than half-land it** — a board that forces an
out-of-scope classification is not a cheap board.

### ⚠️ THE SEED GATE IS TOOL PRESENCE, NEVER `dealt > 0` — and the mutant that proved it

`damagedTrigger` is seeded inside the damage block on `dealt > 0`. **Copying that is the
mistake an author would make, and it SURVIVED THE FIRST MUTATION PASS**: every board in
the suite dealt main damage. The witness is **Mimikyu `sv02-097` "Ghost Eye"** ({P}{C},
**no printed `damage` field**, 7 damage counters on the opponent's Active) — the one
attacker in the pool whose §8.5 pipeline is skipped whole and whose **EFFECT PROGRAM still
kills**. **The printed condition is the KNOCK OUT, not the HIT.** Adding that board turned
the survivor into a kill.

⚠️ **THE TRANSFERABLE RULE, AND IT IS THE SECOND HALF OF D169's: A MUTANT THAT COPIES A
SIBLING'S REAL CODE NEEDS A BOARD THE SIBLING NEVER HAS.** D169 said a mutant must be the
mistake someone would actually make; the corollary is that such a mutant is **only as
sharp as the board that separates the two siblings**, and the sibling's own coverage will
never contain it.

### ⚠️ TWO GATES THAT BELONGED TO ONE TERM — D169's lesson, RECURRING ONE SLICE LATER

1. **`attachTool` tested `programFor(id)?.passive !== undefined`** for *"is this Tool
   simulated"*. Every authored Tool up to Vengeful Punch expressed its sentence as
   continuous NUMBERS, so *"has a passive"* and *"is simulated"* were the same predicate
   **by accident**. Exp. Share has a `triggered` program and **no passive**, so under the
   old gate the engine would have **refused to attach a card it fully simulates**, with
   *"not simulated yet"*. It is now a disjunction. ⚠️ **This is the SECOND SIGHTING of
   D169's finding, one slice after it was written down** — which is what turns it from an
   observation into a checklist item: *when widening a seam that already serves one
   printing, ENUMERATE ITS EARLY RETURNS AND ASK WHICH TERM EACH BELONGS TO.*
2. **`ENERGY_MOVED` named its source by SPOT**, under `LogContext`'s own doc guarantee
   that *"nothing it names has left play when the reduction settles"*. That guarantee held
   for Energy Switch and Poppy and **stopped holding here**: the source is Knocked Out
   later in the **same reduction**, and on a board that auto-promotes `{spot:"active"}`
   renders as the Pokémon that **REPLACED** it — a factually false row, persisted and
   broadcast. The event gained **`fromUid?`** (emitted always; optional only so the type
   stays additive) and the log arm prefers it, which is the route `KNOCKED_OUT` already
   uses and which the same doc block already names: *"KO'd names come off the event's own
   uid, not the state."* **The lesson: a log guarantee written for IN-PLAY subjects breaks
   the first time a subject LEAVES PLAY mid-reduction** — any future op that moves a card
   off a body the same reduction removes owes the same `…Uid` treatment.

### A THIRD `moveEnergy` ROUTE — the first pinned by UID

`koedActiveToToolHolder`: sources are the **ACTIVE alone**; the sole destination is the
Pokémon carrying `ctx.sourceUid`, which for a Tool-borne program is the **TOOL's own uid**.
This needed a new **`toolHolderRef`**, **not** `sourceRef`: *"the Pokémon this card is
attached to"* and *"this Pokémon"* are **two phrases with two readers**, and `sourceRef`
matches on the TOP card's uid, so it returns **EMPTY** for every Tool-borne program.

One decision survives (WHICH Energy), so the compound prompt, the wire validator and
`moveEnergyApply` are untouched, and the route is **invisible on the wire** — the client
sees Energy Switch's decision with a one-entry destination list.

`sourceUid` is **threaded into `moveEndpoints`** rather than read off `ctx`, because
`moveEnergyPlayable` (the `programPlayable` gate) has no context: it passes none, the route
then offers no destination, and a top-level Trainer authored with it is refused as a
would-only-whiff play — which is correct, since the route is reachable only from a Tool's
on-KO trigger. Pinned as a registry-wide guard.

### VOICE — NO announcement row, and that is the family's existing rule

A Tool emits **no `ABILITY_TRIGGERED`**: `log.ts` already says so at the neighbouring
recoil arm (*"it is a passive, and for a Tool there is no Ability to trigger"*). The
**prompt** — *"Move a Basic Energy from that Pokémon to the Pokémon this card is attached
to."*, the printed second half **verbatim** — and the `ENERGY_MOVED` row are the whole of
what a reader is told. Driven both ways.

### The structural questions

1. **PARK? YES. PERSIST? NO** — `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays **11**, **DERIVED**, and the
   recon's reason was **wrong even though its answer was right**. ⚠️ **`GameState.pending`
   IS persisted** — a park mid-attack is a live, reachable, stored position, so *"a stage
   kind is transient"* is factually false. The right answer comes from D124's test being
   **DIRECTIONAL**: *can the PREVIOUS deploy's RECORD hold the shape the new code
   expects?* An old record **cannot contain a `koToolTrigger`** (nothing wrote one) and
   every kind it can contain is still handled; the `route` change is a **WIDENED ENUM** on
   an op that *can* sit in `phase.cont`, which D124 explicitly excludes; **no REQUIRED
   field was added to anything persisted**; and `fromUid` rides `GameEvent`, which
   `MatchRecord` does not store (it stores the RENDERED log). ⚠️ **A new REQUIRED FIELD on
   an EXISTING `PendingStage` kind would NOT pass this test** — the additive kind does.
   `engineVersion` **0.115.0 → 0.116.0**; `packages/engine/package.json` stays `0.3.0`.
2. **VOICE** — no row moved except the one that had to: `ENERGY_MOVED` gained a uid so it
   could keep telling the truth. No new row, no new arm.
3. **§9: N/A BY DESIGN**, and **the negative is the assertion** (a Tool is not an Ability),
   driven with the lock proved live first.
4. **MECHANISM** — everything except the timing, the scan, the stage, the runner, the
   route, the ref helper, the event field and the widened `attachTool` gate already
   existed.
5. **GATES NO ACTION**; **no error code**; **§11: nothing owed** (no op added or removed).
   The only refusal surface is the pre-existing shared `moveEnergy` validator.

### The pin that went red was the one written to go red — RE-POINTED, not deleted

`ohNoYouDont.test.ts` pinned Exp. Share as an ABSENCE on **five** assertions, including
`programFor("sv01-174")?.triggered === undefined`. All five went red exactly as designed
and are **RE-POINTED** at what the slice built — plus **three new** assertions: the timing
is `onAllyActiveKnockOut` and explicitly **not** `onKnockOut` (an `onKnockOut` row would be
read by the KO sweep, which runs after `knockOut` has discarded the Energy), and **neither
Prize field is set**, so the partition test below it stays true. **A pin that goes red on
the slice it was written for is the pin working**, for the third batch running.

### ⚠️ A GUARD REMOVED BECAUSE A MUTANT COULD NOT KILL IT — and WHICH precedent that is

`moveEndpoints` first carried its own *"the holder must not BE the source"* test beside the
scan's skip. **Deleting it failed nothing** — the scan's skip means no board can arrive
there. Two precedents were available and they disagree: **D154 deleted** a guard nothing
could make fail; **D159 / D161 / D163 kept** theirs with the unreachability asserted.
**D154's was chosen**, and the reason is that those three kept a guard because it was the
FILE'S OWN IDIOM (three sibling calls that should read the same way) — here the two sibling
routes carry no such test, so the guard was an idiom of one. The rule now has exactly two
owners: the **SEMANTIC** one (`koToolTriggersOf` skips the KO'd body, because the printed
sentence names two Pokémon) and the **WIRE BELT** (`validateChoice`'s *"cannot move a
Pokémon's Energy onto itself"*). Removing the third made the scan-skip mutant kill **2**
tests instead of 1 — **the deletion SHARPENED a neighbouring mutant.**

### Mutation pass: 12 run, 12 caught — two as first-round SURVIVORS

Counts are engine test FILES failed. Every mutant is the neighbouring code's **real text**
— `damagedTrigger`'s `dealt > 0` gate, `triggersOf`'s §9 line, Energy Switch's `"all"`
scope, `sourceRef` in place of `toolHolderRef`.

| mutant | tests killed |
|---|---|
| queue `koToolTrigger` BEHIND `attackEpilogue` (i.e. the `koTrigger` placement) | **17** |
| forget to `popStage` before running the stage | **17** |
| `sourceRef` instead of `toolHolderRef` for the destination | **16** |
| seed the stage for the ATTACKER's seat (the possessive) | **16** |
| drop the LETHALITY re-check | 4 |
| filter `anyEnergy` instead of `basicEnergy` | 3 |
| don't skip the KO'd body in the scan | **2** (1 before the redundant guard was removed) |
| copy `triggersOf`'s §9 gate into the scan | 1 |
| route source `"all"` instead of `"active"` (Energy Switch's real code) | 1 |
| revert `attachTool`'s gate to `passive` alone | 1 |
| log falls back to the SPOT (drop `fromUid`) | 1 |
| **seed on `dealt > 0` inside the damage block** (`damagedTrigger`'s real code) | **SURVIVED — killed only once Mimikyu `sv02-097`'s 0-damage lethal board was added** |
| **`moveEndpoints`' own self-destination guard** | **UNKILLABLE — the guard was DELETED rather than witnessed (D154's precedent)** |

### The family — re-censused a FOURTH time, and CLOSED

`LIKE '%Knocked Out by damage from an attack%'` over **all three text columns** against the
local D1 (2026-08-03, **978 rows / 6 sets**) returns **6 printings / 4 distinct sentences**
— D158's figure, D162's re-run, D164's third confirmation, and now a fourth.

| card | column | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Vengeful Punch `sv03-197` (Tool) | `effect` | D158 — `passive.damageAttackerOnKo` |
| Munkidori ex `sv06.5-037`/`-083`/`-091` | `abilities_json` | D164 — `triggered.onKoPrizeReduction` |
| **Exp. Share `sv01-174` (Tool)** | `effect` | **D171 — `triggered.onAllyActiveKnockOut`** |
| Lucario `sv01-114` | `attacks_json` | **NOT this antecedent** (D164's correction) |

Excluding Lucario the family is **5 printings / 3 sentences**, and it is now **CLOSED at
3/3 sentences authored**, with the one deliberate abstention (`sv01-114`, the live
fall-through witness in `conditionClause.test.ts`) intact. **D158's KO-antecedent census is
fully mapped.**

### ⚠️ A SEVENTH ROW THE CENSUS PATTERN CANNOT SEE — NOW PINNED IN CODE

**Corviknight `sv02-148` "Accelerate"** (`attacks_json`): *"If your opponent's Pokémon is
Knocked Out by damage from **this attack**, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all
damage from and effects of attacks done to this Pokémon."* A **different antecedent
family** — the KO is *caused by* the attack being resolved rather than *suffered by* the
card's owner, and the consequent is a durated self-prevention. **No registry row, no
fixture.** Every run of this census since D158 has been blind to it, because the pattern
says *"from an attack"* and this row says *"from this attack"*.

⚠️ **THE DURABLE FIX, AND IT IS GENERAL: A ROW A CENSUS CANNOT SEE SHOULD BE PINNED IN
CODE, NOT RE-NOTED IN PROSE EACH TIME.** Corviknight has now been re-discovered by **three
separate passes**, each of which wrote it into a handoff and none of which stopped the
next. It is a **string in `expShare.test.ts`** now, asserted alongside `programFor` and
`FIXTURE_POOL` absences, so a fourth census cannot rediscover it as news.

### Cost

**1 `TriggerTiming` (`onAllyActiveKnockOut`), 1 board scan (`koToolTriggersOf`), 1
`PendingStage` kind + its `advance` arm, 1 flow runner (`runKoToolTrigger`), 1 `moveEnergy`
route + 1 ref helper (`toolHolderRef`) + 1 prompt arm, 1 optional event field
(`ENERGY_MOVED.fromUid`) + 1 log line, 1 widened `attachTool` gate, 1 registry row
(`EXP_SHARE`), 1 fixture (`sv01-174`, verbatim off the D1), 1 deck (`EXP_SHARE_DECK`,
**SEED-FREE** — no coin anywhere in the card).** Everything else was reused.

`expShare.test.ts` (**40 tests**, 8 groups: the printed datum, the board scan, the park,
the antecedent, the seam, the voice, the structural questions, the family after D171), plus
the re-pointed `ohNoYouDont.test.ts` pin. **No new event type, no new log arm, no error
code, no op, no prompt kind, no `@luminous/schema` diff, no DB diff, no web diff.**

15 files under `packages/engine/src` move (`registry.ts`, `types.ts`, `triggers.ts`,
`flow.ts`, `attack.ts`, `interpreter.ts`, `events.ts`, `log.ts`, `cardplay.ts`,
`effects.ts`, `testFixtures.ts`, `catalogManifest.ts`, `index.ts`, `ohNoYouDont.test.ts`
and the new `expShare.test.ts`) — **the widest engine diff of this batch by a distance.**

engine **0.115.0 → 0.116.0**; `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **UNCHANGED at 11**; manifest
**215 → 216** fixture rows, 0 absent; `bun run check` GREEN exit 0 — **210 files / 3761
tests** (was 209 / 3721).

### The KO-antecedent family after D171

**CLOSED at 3/3 sentences.** Three printings, three sites, and the sites differ **because
the consequents do** — which is this family's whole lesson across D158 / D164 / D171:

| sentence | consequent | site |
|---|---|---|
| Vengeful Punch | HP on a surviving body | `flow.ts koRecoilOf` — synchronous, before the sweep |
| Munkidori ex | a PRIZE | `flow.ts planPrizes` — inside the sweep |
| Exp. Share | a CARD the player chooses | `flow.ts runKoToolTrigger` — a parking stage before the sweep |

**Placement discharges a condition only for a consequent that can live at the placement**
(D164) — and D171 adds the other half: **a consequent that needs a DECISION cannot live at
a SYNCHRONOUS placement at all, however right that placement is.**

### What is left in this neighbourhood

- **`sv02-148` Corviknight is an OPEN, UNPRICED antecedent family of one** — *"Knocked Out
  by damage from **this** attack"* → a durated self-prevention. It needs a
  KO-CAUSED-BY-THIS-ATTACK read that nothing in the engine has, plus an `attackBlock`-shaped
  stamp that D142/D148 already built. **Probably cheap; nobody has looked.**
- **`onAllyActiveKnockOut` has ONE producer and the scan fires the FIRST match.** A second
  parking Tool trigger on one board is deferred, exactly as the board triggers defer
  chaining — same follow-up, now with a second caller wanting it.
- **The `LogContext` invariant is now CONDITIONAL.** Its doc still says every event it
  names is safe against the post-state; that is true only because `ENERGY_MOVED` was fixed.
  **Any future op that moves a card off a body the same reduction removes owes the same
  `…Uid` treatment.** Worth a sweep.

## D172 — the §12 STATUS IMMUNITY: `This Pokémon can't be {Burned | Paralyzed}.` — Dachsbun `sv01-099`'s OTHER clause plus Pachirisu `sv01-068`/`-208`, and the family's THIRD sentence deliberately left unbuilt (engine 0.116.0 → 0.117.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

Item 1 of D159's own remainder list, and the **first slice in this batch whose inherited
pricing was wrong in THREE separate places, all three STRUCTURAL**. The catalog figure —
*4 printings / 3 sentences* — was **EXACT** on both numbers when re-derived. Everything
the item said about the CODE was not.

**Scope decided before the build:** the two POKÉMON printings only. Therapeutic Energy
`sv02-193` is **deliberately not built** and is pinned as an absence with its price
written down (below, and on `EnergyProgram` in code).

### The census, re-run as its own question — and both numbers held

Local D1, **978 rows / 6 sets** (`sv01` 258, `sv02` 279, `sv03` 230, `sv06.5` 99,
`sve` 24, `swsh10.5` 88), 2026-08-03, over **ALL THREE** text columns:

```sql
WITH t AS (SELECT id, name,
             COALESCE(effect,'')         AS e,
             COALESCE(abilities_json,'') AS a,
             COALESCE(attacks_json,'')   AS k
           FROM cards)
SELECT id, name FROM t WHERE
     e|a|k LIKE '%an''t be Burned%'   OR ... Paralyzed / Asleep / Confused / Poisoned
  OR e|a|k LIKE '%affected by%Special Condition%';
```

→ **SIX rows. FOUR are the family; TWO are false positives, and both live in
`attacks_json`** — the column D159's own sweep (`abilities_json OR effect`) could not see
at all:

| id | column | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `sv01-099` Dachsbun "Well-Baked Body" | `abilities_json` | **clause 1 of 2** — D172 |
| `sv01-068` Pachirisu "Electricity Pouches" | `abilities_json` | **the whole Ability** — D172 |
| `sv01-208` Pachirisu (Illustration rare) | `abilities_json` | reprint, same program object |
| `sv02-193` Therapeutic Energy | **`effect`** | **NOT BUILT** — a Special Energy |
| `sv01-010` Vivillon "Miracle Powder" | `attacks_json` | false positive — APPLIES a chosen condition |
| `sv02-136` Sableye "Unseen Claw" | `attacks_json` | false positive — READS one |

⚠️ **THE THREE-COLUMN RULE PAID OUT TWICE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, IN ONE SLICE.** The two
false positives are in the column the old sweep missed, and **the family's own third
member is in `effect`** because it is an ENERGY and has no `abilities_json` at all. **A
sweep of any ONE column returns at most TWO of the four.** `FIXTURE_POOL` was swept as a
**SEPARATE** population (D156's rule) and held **ONE** of the four.

This is the strongest instance this repo has of the three-column rule, and it is worth
stating as a general one: **a single-column census can return at most half a family, and
it can return rows the family does not contain.** Read `.schema` before you read a
census.

### ⚠️ THE THREE INHERITED CLAIMS THAT WERE WRONG

1. **"It gates `applyStatus` AND the Checkup." — it gates `applyStatus` and NOTHING
   ELSE, and that is DERIVED.** `applyStatus` (interpreter.ts) is the engine's **only
   WRITER** of a §12 condition; every other site CLEARS (`flow.ts runCheckup`'s three
   recovery steps, and the three `noConditions()` sites on evolve / retreat / forced
   switch). **Gating the sole writer gates everything downstream**, so a body that
   cannot be *given* a status cannot arrive at the Checkup carrying one, and a Checkup
   gate would be **a second reading of one rule (D131's drift) that no board could ever
   make disagree with the first.** The one route that could have made it real — a §9
   lock live when the status lands and dead by the Checkup — is **unreachable**, and the
   proof is a counting argument over ACTIVE SPOTS (below). **Driven end to end rather
   than argued:** an immune body swung at with the condition it refuses takes **no burn
   tick and no cure flip** through a full §13, while the non-immune control on the
   identical declaration takes both.
2. **"All four clauses are carried VERBATIM on the fixtures and PINNED." — ONE was.**
   Dachsbun's. The other three lived in **PROSE**, in `registry.ts` and
   `attackerFilter.test.ts` comments. That is a failure mode D156 closed for whole
   Abilities and D159 closed for clauses, and it came back the moment the pinning was
   *described in a handoff* instead of *written in code*. Two are fixtures now; the
   third is a pinned absence.
3. **"One `PassiveEffects` field and one gate." — a FLOOR, exactly as the standing
   warning says, and short by TWO edits for the third time.** A gate that refuses in
   **silence** is D159's own headline finding wearing a §12 hat: without a row, a Burn
   aimed at Dachsbun reads *"Scovillain used Hot Bite · dealt 20 damage"* and nothing
   else — indistinguishable from an engine that forgot the clause. So the slice also
   owes **`STATUS_PREVENTED`** and its **log arm**. It is the **fifth** way this engine
   can null an effect and the **second in a row** to be found by RENDERING the row
   rather than by reading the code.

### ⚠️ "PINNED" IS A CLAIM ABOUT A TEST FILE, NEVER ABOUT A COMMENT

Three of this family's four clauses were described as *carried verbatim on the fixtures
and PINNED*. They were **mentioned**. **A COMMENT CANNOT GO RED** — it is not greppable
by any census that looks for behaviour, no `toEqual` consults it, and nothing fails when
the code it describes stops being true.

D171 wrote the neighbouring rule for a row a census could not SEE (Corviknight, pinned as
a string). **D172 found the same failure for rows a census could see perfectly well and
nothing asserted.** The transferable form: **a claim that something is pinned must name
the ASSERTION.** If you cannot name the `expect`, the thing is not pinned.

### The shape decision: a SCALAR on the interface, a LIST in the aggregation

`PassiveEffects.statusImmunity?: StatusName`, collected by `passivesOf` into
`statusImmunities: StatusName[]`. That is `preventDamageFromType` /
`preventDamageFromTypes`' shape **one field up on the same interface, written by D159 for
the same card** — and the reasoning is the repo's own rule applied literally (*the unit
of SHARING is decided by the READ site, the unit of STORAGE by the WRITE sites*):

- **count the WRITERS.** There are **two** — `WELL_BAKED_BODY` and
  `ELECTRICITY_POUCHES` — and each names exactly **one** condition. Nothing that exists
  needs to spell two.
- **the unit of SHARING is the READ site**, and the read site is one `.includes`. But the
  *aggregation* folds the holder's own passive **PLUS every attached Tool**, so two
  sources naming two conditions is a shape it must be able to report. A scalar fold could
  only ever be last-wins. **Hence the list lives there, not on the interface.**
- the list is **NOT de-duplicated**: the read is `.includes`, which cannot tell a repeated
  entry from a single one, and a `Set` would be a second collection type for one
  membership question (D131).
- ⚠️ **THE COUNTER-CASE IS REAL AND WAS NAMED RATHER THAN ABSORBED.** Therapeutic Energy
  names **THREE**. It is a SPECIAL ENERGY and writes **no `PassiveEffects` at all** —
  `passivesOf`'s `sources` are the TOP CARD and the TOOLS, and an attached Energy is
  neither — so widening this field to a list today would **pre-pay for a writer that
  cannot reach it**. Two adjacent fields on one interface with different shapes for the
  same reason would be the drift D131 warns about.

### ⚠️ §9 IS FREE, AND ITS LAST STEP IS UNDRIVEABLE — the ACTIVE-SPOT counting argument

Riding `passivesOf` buys the Ability-lock gate **with no line written**: the fold has
already dropped a locked holder's own printed passive and already kept every Tool's. The
mutant that matters is the one-line-shorter build —
`programFor(top.id)?.passive?.statusImmunity` read directly — which **survives Klefki**.
It is driven, and it dies.

The lock is DRIVEN LIVE over both printings, with `disabledAbilityUids` **proved to
contain the uid first** (D171's rule, so the positive cannot be vacuous): Klefki
"Mischievous Lock" over Pachirisu (Basic), Ting-Lu ex "Cursed Land" over a damaged
Dachsbun (the only lock in the registry that reaches a Stage 1), and the immunity comes
straight back when the lock's source leaves the Active Spot.

⚠️ **What CANNOT be driven is the lock letting a refused condition LAND**, and the reason
is structural rather than a gap in effort — **a counting argument over ACTIVE SPOTS**:

- every §12 status application in this engine comes from an **ATTACK** (the deriver's
  five arms) or from Armarouge's `activeOnly` Scorching Armor trigger — so the source
  occupies an Active Spot;
- every §9 lock in the registry is `requiresActive` **except** Spiritomb's, which narrows
  to Basic **V** — a suffix neither immune printing has;
- the immune body must itself be an Active, because `applyStatus` only ever resolves to
  `players[seat].active`.

**Three Active Spots wanted, two available.** This is D159's Thundurus finding recurring
on the other pipeline, and the assertion is written **on the pool** (which locks are
`requiresActive`, which suffix the bench-capable one narrows to) rather than left as a
comment, so a printing that makes it reachable goes red. **Asserted, not skipped.**

### The one board where the immune body is the ATTACKER

Scorching Armor is the engine's **only** route by which a status reaches a body that is
not the defender: the trigger runs under the DAMAGED Pokémon's seat, so
`applyStatus target: "defender"` resolves to the **ATTACKER's** Active. Dachsbun swings
its own "Headbutt Bounce" into Armarouge and refuses the Burn coming back. That is the
same gate asked through the **opposite seat resolution** — the one way the two arms of
`applyStatus` could have been built to disagree — and its control (Scovillain into the
same Armarouge) ends with **both** bodies Burned in one reduction, which is the sharpest
available statement that one call resolves two seats from two callers.

### PARALYSIS NEEDS A COIN, AND THE COIN BOUGHT A CLAIM

The local D1 prints **no single-sentence, non-flip Paralysis anywhere**: every plain
*"…is now Paralyzed."* row is either behind *"Flip a coin. If heads,"* (13 printings) or
behind a second sentence the deriver refuses (Weavile `sv06.5-014`'s energy discard,
Dudunsparce `sv02-157`'s self-shuffle, Cryogonal `sv03-055`'s go-second clause). So this
half can only be driven through a gate, and the suite picks its seeds by asking
`flipCoin` for the face it wants.

That turned out to buy a claim rather than cost one: **THE FLIP STILL HAPPENS ON AN
IMMUNE BODY.** The gate is inside `applyStatus`, downstream of `coinFlipGate`, so
`rngState` advances **identically** whether the target can be Paralyzed or not — asserted
by running the immune board and the control board off one seed and comparing the
post-`rngState`. A build that short-circuited earlier would consume a different number of
steps and **desynchronise every later flip in the match**.

And the tails case is its own claim: a tails flip never reaches `applyStatus`, so there is
**no** `STATUS_PREVENTED` row. *"Nothing happened"* has two causes here and they stay
distinguishable.

### VOICE — the row speaks the printed sentence

`STATUS_PREVENTED { seat, uid, status }`, rendered as **`"Dachsbun can't be Burned"`** —
the card's own text with the subject resolved. Filed under the seat that OWNS the refusing
Pokémon (the event family's contract), which for an attack-borne status is the
**DEFENDER's** chair — the opposite chair from `DAMAGE_DEALT`'s on the very same
declaration, because this row replaces `STATUS_APPLIED`, not the damage row. Both are
asserted on one swing.

⚠️ **IT CARRIES THE `status` AND NOT THE REASON, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE CALL FROM
`ATTACK_EFFECT_PREVENTED`, AND BOTH ARE RIGHT.** That row names no cause because five
different rules set one flag and it has never claimed to discriminate them. Here there is
exactly **one** rule, and the thing a reader cannot otherwise recover is **WHICH**
condition was refused — a body immune to one of several conditions an attack applies would
emit an uninterpretable row without it.

### The `applyStatus` early-return audit — D169's lesson, THIRD sighting and FIRST clean one

Three early returns sit ahead of the new gate:

| early return | which term it belongs to |
|---|---|
| `active === null` | **BOTH** — no body to status and no body to be immune |
| `uid === undefined` | **BOTH** — same |
| `attackEffectRefused(...)` | the **§11 ATTACK BLOCK alone** (D142) |

The new gate sits **BEHIND** the third, so a refused ATTACK keeps reporting itself as one.
⚠️ **The ordering is UNOBSERVABLE, and that is SAID rather than left as a coincidence:**
`preventDamage` installs only on the ATTACKER's own Active, an attack ends the turn
(§5.3), and **neither immune printing has an attack that installs a block** — so no legal
board reaches both gates. **Asserted over the fixtures' printed attack text and over
`attackBlock` being null on the board**, not left in a comment.

This is D169's lesson's **third** consecutive sighting (D169 `effectiveAttackCost`, D171
`attachTool`) and the **first time it came up CLEAN** — the shared seam's opening guards
genuinely belonged to both terms or to a term this slice does not touch. Which is the
point of a checklist item: **it has to be allowed to answer "nothing here".**

### The structural questions

1. **PARK? NO. PERSIST? NO — `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 11, DERIVED.** D124's test is
   DIRECTIONAL (D171). **Nothing this slice adds reaches `GameState` at all:**
   `statusImmunity` is a **CATALOG** field (registry.ts types), the aggregation is a pure
   function of the live board and is never stamped, and `STATUS_PREVENTED` rides
   `GameEvent`, which `MatchRecord` does not store (it stores the RENDERED log). No key
   moved on `InPlayPokemon`, no `PendingStage` kind was added, no required field landed on
   anything persisted. **The dodge was priced and REFUSED (D155):** a "cannot be Burned"
   flag cached on `InPlayPokemon` would go stale on an evolution, a promotion or a lock
   arriving, and would have bought a bump for nothing. Asserted by reading the in-play
   object's own keys.
2. **VOICE — one new event and one new log arm**, argued above.
3. **§9 — free by construction, DRIVEN live, and its last step proved impossible.**
4. **MECHANISM EXISTS** — `passivesOf`'s fold, its §9 drop, `applyStatus`'s three arms,
   `StatusName`, `STATUS_LABELS` and the whole deriver path all pre-existed. What did not
   exist was **a field for the sentence to land on**, which is precisely what D159
   declared when it left the clause LOUD.
5. **GATES NO ACTION** — checked, not assumed. The printed sentences never say "can't be
   used"; nothing touches cost, legality or the §4 turn-1 rule, and the field is invisible
   to `redactedAttacksOf`. **No `redact.ts` and no `GameHud.tsx` diff.** **§11
   CLASSIFICATION TABLE: NOTHING OWED** — that table is triggered by *an op the deriver
   can produce*, and this slice adds **no op at all**; `applyStatus`'s derived shape is
   byte-identical.

### The pins that went red were the ones written to go red

`attackerFilter.test.ts` pinned Dachsbun's immunity as an ABSENCE on two assertions
(`programFor("sv01-099")?.passive` `toEqual({ preventDamageFromType: "Fire" })`). Both went
red exactly as designed and are **RE-POINTED, not deleted**; the case is renamed to say
that ONE of its two LOUD clauses has since been built and the Stadium's has not. **A pin
that goes red on the slice it was written for is the pin working, for the fourth batch
running.**

### Mutation pass: 15 run, 14 caught, 1 deliberate survivor

Counts are engine test FILES failed. Every mutant is a real mistake an author would make,
and three are the neighbouring code's actual text.

| mutant | files killed |
|---|---|
| **M1** read the catalog row DIRECTLY, bypassing `passivesOf`'s §9 drop (survives Klefki) | 1 |
| **M2** drop the gate entirely | 1 |
| **M3** `.length > 0` instead of `.includes(op.status)` (immune to EVERY condition) | 1 |
| **M4** refuse but WRITE the condition anyway (drop the early return) | 1 |
| **M5** refuse SILENTLY (drop the `STATUS_PREVENTED` row) | 1 |
| **M6** file the row under the OTHER seat | 1 |
| **M7** gate ONLY the `burned` arm (the arm an author would remember) | 1 |
| **M8** place the gate AHEAD of `attackEffectRefused` | **SURVIVED — kept, unreachability ASSERTED** |
| **M9** drop the collect from `passivesOf`'s fold | 1 |
| **M10** Dachsbun's token is `asleep` instead of `burned` | **2** |
| **M11** drop the `sv01-208` reprint registry row | 1 |
| **M12** give the reprint an equal-but-DISTINCT object | 1 |
| **M13** drop the log arm (the event fires, nothing renders) | 1 |
| **M14** drop Dachsbun's unread-clause text from the fixture | **2** |
| **M15** drop Pachirisu's two unmapped attack clauses from both fixtures | 1 |

**⚠️ THE SURVIVOR IS AN ORDERING, NOT A GUARD, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS KEPT.** D154's
delete-the-free-guard precedent does not apply: **there is no redundant test to remove** —
the gate is required in *both* positions and only its POSITION is free. Both orderings
produce the identical board on every reachable input; only the log row would differ, and
the pair can never both be live. So the codebase's other standard applies —
**D159 / D161 / D163: keep, and turn the unreachability into an ASSERTION** rather than a
comment. `statusImmunity.test.ts` asserts it over the fixtures' printed attack text and
over `attackBlock` being null on the board.

**M10 and M14 killing TWO files each is the LOUD-fixture convention paying out**: the
wrong token and the dropped clause are caught by `attackerFilter.test.ts` as well, which
is the whole reason D159 wrote a pin it expected to outlive itself.

### Cost

**1 `PassiveEffects` field (`statusImmunity`), 1 `passivesOf` entry (`statusImmunities`),
1 gate at `applyStatus`, 1 event (`STATUS_PREVENTED`) + 1 log arm**, 1 new registry
program (`ELECTRICITY_POUCHES`) on 2 rows + 1 field added to `WELL_BAKED_BODY`, 2 fixtures
(`sv01-068`/`-208`, verbatim off the D1) and 1 deck (`STATUS_IMMUNITY_DECK`). **No op, no
error code, no prompt, no park, no `PendingStage`, no regex, no deriver arm, no redact

engine **0.116.0 → 0.117.0**; `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **UNCHANGED at 11**;

### ⚠️ THE DEFERRED PRICE (HISTORICAL — PAID AT D174) — Therapeutic Energy `sv02-193`, FOUR EDITS, THREE OF THEM OUTSIDE THIS FAMILY

⚠️ **WHAT THIS PRICE GOT RIGHT AND WRONG, MEASURED AT D174 AND SUMMARISED HERE SO A COLD READER
DOES NOT ACT ON IT.** **(a)** *"whichever it is, it is a LIST"* — **RIGHT**, and it went further:
the surface is the whole `passive?: PassiveEffects` interface and it is **TWO** lists, because the
recovery is a separate clause; the parenthetical *"`PassiveEffects.statusImmunity` staying a
SCALAR costs nothing — the Energy will not write that field"* is **the one claim that was
FALSE**, and the scalar widened. **(b)** *"expect this to be MOST OF THE SLICE"* — **EXACTLY
RIGHT**; what it could not know is that the audit is bounded to **ten of the twenty-two fields**
and that its result is **no behaviour change at all**. **(c)** the §9 exemption — **RIGHT, and
cheaper than it reads.** **(d)** the recovery — **right that it had NO PRECEDENT, WRONG about its
SHAPE**: it is *not* *"a new `EnergyOnAttach` arm"* (that fires per-card at attach and would have
missed `moveEnergy` / `attachFromDeck` / `attachFromTop`), it is a **board sweep at TWO NAMED
MOMENTS**. **(e)** *"re-answer the Checkup question FROM SCRATCH"* — **right to demand it**; the
re-answer changed the ARGUMENT and not the CONCLUSION. ⚠️ **And the armed tripwire below DID NOT
FIRE — it was armed in a COMMENT, and a comment cannot go red.** ⚠️ **Nothing in this price
contained the finding the slice actually produced: FOUR uncounted `%recovers from%` printings,
reachable by widening the PREDICATE rather than the columns.**

*"As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides {C} Energy. / The Pokémon
this card is attached to recovers from being Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed and can't be
affected by those Special Conditions."*

It is **not** "a third registry row". `EnergyProgram` today has exactly three fields
(`provides`, `demoteWithOtherSpecial`, `onAttach`) and **all three are read at ATTACH time
or at COST time** — nothing on it is read while the card merely sits attached.

1. **A continuous entry on `EnergyProgram`** — `passive?: PassiveEffects`, or a narrower
   `statusImmunities?: StatusName[]`. **Whichever it is, it is a LIST**: the printing names
   THREE conditions where every built member names one. (This is exactly why
   `PassiveEffects.statusImmunity` staying a scalar costs nothing — the Energy will not
   write that field.)
2. **A THIRD SOURCE CLASS in `continuous.ts passivesOf`.** Its `sources` array is
   `[the top card's passive, ...tools]` and has **NEVER walked attached Energy**. ⚠️ **This
   is the expensive edit and the one to price carefully: *every* field the fold already
   returns (`damageReductionAfterWR`, `hpBonus`, `damageAttacker`,
   `preventDamageFromTypes`, `statusImmunities`, …) silently gains an attached-Energy
   contributor, so each one owes a re-reading rather than a free ride. Expect this to be
   MOST OF THE SLICE.**
3. **The §9 answer stated the OTHER way round.** An Energy is not an Ability, so the new
   source must be **EXEMPT** from the `disabled` drop the holder's own passive takes —
   exactly as Tools already are — and the exemption must be *driven* with a lock proved
   live (D171's rule), not assumed.
4. **The RECOVERY half, which is a second MECHANISM and not a second field.** *"recovers
   from being…"* must **CLEAR** a condition already present: at attach time (a new
   `EnergyOnAttach` arm) and, because the immunity is continuous, on any board where the
   two could disagree. ⚠️ **Nothing in this engine currently clears a condition from a
   continuous effect** — every existing clear is a placement (`noConditions()`) or a
   Checkup step. **This is the part with NO PRECEDENT.**

⚠️ **AND IT REOPENS D172's CHECKUP FINDING — THE TRIPWIRE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ARMED.**
The whole reason no Checkup gate was built is that `applyStatus` is the only WRITER of a
condition. The recovery half of this card gives an immunity that can arrive on a body
**AFTER** the condition did (attach an Energy to an already-Paralyzed Pokémon), which is
precisely the shape §12 immunity has never had here. **Whoever builds this must re-answer
"does the Checkup need a gate?" FROM SCRATCH** — and `statusImmunity.test.ts`'s
**surgically-planted-condition case is written to be the FIRST THING THAT GOES RED** when
it does. That is not an accident of coverage; it is a tripwire, and it is armed.

Rough shape: **1 interface field + 1 source class + 1 §9 exemption + 1 new clear mechanism
+ 1 fixture + 1 registry row + a re-run of the Checkup question.** **Comparable to D172
itself, not smaller.**

## D173 — THE SIX WRONG-INDEX FIXTURES, FIXED RATHER THAN DECLARED: all six carry their whole printed attack list at PRINTED indices, `reindexed` empties and is PINNED empty, and the sweep that transcribed them turned up a WRONG VALUE on an axis no census recorded (engine **UNCHANGED at 0.117.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 11**, **0 engine behaviour lines**)

The item every remainder list has carried since D156 first counted five of them, and
the one D160 sharpened by finding the sixth **with the table it had just built**. It is
also the first item on that list whose whole content was **removing a declaration
rather than adding one**.

### What was wrong, and why it stayed green

Five fixtures (`sv06.5-026`, `sv01-124`, `sv01-079`, `sv01-032`, `swsh10.5-009`) each
dropped their printed **index-0** attack so the one their suite drives sat at 0; a sixth
(`sv01-096`) **substituted** another card's attack for the only one it prints. Nineteen
`{ type: "attack", index: 0 }` declarations across three files therefore named the
FIXTURE's number and not the CARD's.

⚠️ **AND ALL SIX WERE DECLARED, WHICH IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE MITIGATION.** Two
section comments in `testFixtures.ts` said, in as many words, *"a fixture's `index: 0` is
Slither Wing's and Koraidon's SECOND printed attack"*, and `catalogManifest.test.ts` held
six `reindexed: true` rows with reasons. The declaration is what let it live: it made a
wrong index **legible without making it wrong**, and a suite pinning `index: 0` stayed
green because the fixture had been bent to fit the pin. A declaration converts a defect
into a documented condition, and a documented condition has no pressure on it.

> **A DECLARATION IS NOT A FIX, AND THE TABLE THAT HOLDS ONE HAS TO BE ABLE TO EMPTY.**
> `catalogManifest.test.ts` did its job perfectly for four slices — it named the six, it
> proved no registry program keyed on one, it caught the sixth by measurement. What it
> could not do was make anybody remove one. **The cost of the entry was one line and the
> cost of the fix was one attack row, and the entry won for four slices running.**
> **When both are one line, fix it.**

### D160's six claims — all six CONFIRMED, none fixed incidentally

Verified against the fixture source before any edit. `sv06.5-026`, `sv01-124`,
`sv01-079`, `sv01-032` and `swsh10.5-009` each carried exactly one attack; `sv01-096`
carried `"Bite"`, a name the card does not print. **No seventh exists — and that is a
MEASUREMENT, not a sweep**: `(d)`'s `shifted` computation is total over `M.printed` and
now asserts `[]`, so a seventh would have gone red the moment the sixth was fixed.

### The wrong-index family after D173 — CLOSED at 6/6, table EMPTY and PINNED EMPTY

| card | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Slither Wing `sv06.5-026` | `["Smashing Wing"]` | `["Iron Smasher", "Smashing Wing"]` |
| Koraidon `sv01-124` | `["Rampaging Fang"]` | `["Claw Slash", "Rampaging Fang"]` |
| Kilowattrel `sv01-079` | `["Thunder Blast"]` | `["Skill Dive", "Thunder Blast"]` |
| Arcanine ex `sv01-032` | `["Bright Flame"]` | `["Raging Claws", "Bright Flame"]` |
| Klefki `sv01-096` | `["Bite"]` (INVENTED) | `["Joust"]` (printed) |
| Charmeleon `swsh10.5-009` | `["Flamethrower"]` | `["Scratch", "Flamethrower"]` |

**All six `INCOMPLETE` entries DISAPPEAR, and none remains with `reindexed: false`** —
no card has a genuinely unsimulated sibling that had to be carried and declared, because
an unread effect string is carried inert and costs nothing.

D163's note that `sv01-060` was authored COMPLETE *"precisely so its index-1 clause could
be driven"* is now the pool's rule rather than one card's exception: **a fixture carries
the whole printed attack list, and an omission is a failure rather than a table row.**

### The transcription was free; the SUBSTITUTION was the slice

Four of the six are pure transcription off the local D1 — a bare damage row (Koraidon's
"Claw Slash" `{C}{C}{C}` 70, Charmeleon's "Scratch" `{R}{C}` 30) or an effect string with
no reader (Slither Wing's "Iron Smasher" `{F}{C}` 20+, whose Future banner has no datum
anywhere — D146). Two carry sentences the engine **already reads**, so making the fixture
complete handed the pool two live programs it had been one attack short of:

- **Kilowattrel `sv01-079` index 0 "Skill Dive"** — the `anyTargetSnipe` sentence,
  derivable by an anchor unmoved since M3;
- **Arcanine ex `sv01-032` index 0 "Raging Claws"** — D163/D167's `+`-fold on the
  attacker's own damage counters.

### ⚠️ THE DECLARATION SITE NOBODY GREPPED — AND THE RULE IT COSTS

The nineteen re-pointed declarations split **`attackDiscards.test.ts` ×4**,
**`providesEnergy.test.ts` ×12** and **`src/features/game/GameHud.cardplay.dom.test.tsx`
×3** — and the third file is **outside `packages/` entirely**. An engine-scoped grep
found sixteen; the seventeenth through nineteenth were found by the suite going **RED**
on the first `bun run check` after the first card.

> **A FIXTURE LIVES IN THE ENGINE AND ITS INDICES ARE READ FROM THE WEB.** `FIXTURE_POOL`
> is imported by the HUD's DOM tests to build real boards, so any sweep for *"who names
> an index for this card"* that stops at `packages/engine/src` is short by construction.
> The brief for this slice said *"there may be more; grep per card rather than trusting
> the list"* and that was still not enough — **the missing axis was the DIRECTORY, not
> the card. A FIXTURE'S BLAST RADIUS CROSSES THE PACKAGE BOUNDARY.**

### ⚠️ FOUR POPULATION CENSUSES WENT RED, WHICH IS THE SLICE'S REAL PAYOUT

`selfCounterMultiply`, `selfScalingPenalty` and `opponentCounterScaling` each discover
their producers *from the population rather than from a list* — the design D167 and D168
were built on — and **all three had been sweeping a body that PRINTS their family's
sentence and seeing NOTHING**, because the fixture carried only its second attack. Each
gained **`sv01-032[0]`**. `clauseApostrophe`'s derivable-sentence census goes **64 → 65**
for the same reason (Kilowattrel's "Skill Dive"; the other three re-indexed siblings add
nothing — Koraidon's "Claw Slash" has no effect string at all, and neither "Iron Smasher"
nor "Raging Claws" carries an apostrophe). Every one was re-pointed, none deleted.

> **A TRUNCATED FIXTURE SILENTLY SHRINKS EVERY CENSUS THAT SWEEPS THE POOL.**
> *"Discovered from the population, not enumerated"* is the right design and it is **not
> self-validating**: its inputs were short, not its predicate, and nothing in the result
> said so. This is D156's scope rule pointed at the **FIXTURE POOL** instead of at the
> catalog.

### ⚠️ KLEFKI `sv01-096` WAS THE ODD ONE OUT, AND ITS SUBSTITUTION WAS LOAD-BEARING

Klefki prints **one** attack. The fixture carried `fix-attacker`'s Bite (`{C}`, 30) in
place of the printed "Joust" (`{C}`, 10) — the only entry in the table needing both an
`attacks` and an `invented` name — and the reason was stated: Klefki must be **Active** to
emit its aura, so it must be the attacker, and the lock-ON / lock-OFF pairs in
`abilityLock.test.ts` compared *"the SAME printed 30"* with Klefki in one arm and
`fix-attacker` in the other.

The substitution is gone and **the pairs are re-pointed rather than broken**. There is no
third board: no aura on either side can lock Bouffalant while something other than Klefki
attacks (Spiritomb reaches only Basic **V**; Ting-Lu ex and Klefki both require the Active
Spot, and the Active Spot is where the attacker is). So the shared literal is replaced by
a **DELTA**: each attacker carries its own no-passive baseline against `fix-bigbody`, and
what is asserted is what Bouffer **COSTS** each of them — **0** with the lock live, **20**
without it.

⚠️ **THE DELTA IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN THE LITERAL IT REPLACES, AND THAT IS THE GENERAL
POINT.** *"The same printed 30"* looked confound-free and was not: it fixed the number by
bending the FIXTURE, so the pair's premise was an artefact of the thing under test. Two
arms that each carry their own baseline need **no shared literal at all**. The mutant that
drops `passivesOf`'s §9 gate still dies here (`abilityLock` + 2 neighbours, **3 files**).

Joust's rider — *"Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's
Active Pokémon."* — is unsimulated, **MEASURED and not assumed**: all six `derive*`
readers return `null` on it. It rides as an inert string on a plain printed 10.

`expShare.test.ts`'s §9 negative needed the victim **pre-damaged to 20**: Bite's 30 used
to Knock Out a 30 HP `fix-victim` outright and Joust's 10 does not. 20 + 10 = 30 = HP
satisfies `isLethallyDamaged`, which is the predicate the stage re-reads.

With `reindexed` at zero, both cases in `(d)` would pass whatever the engine did — a
`for` over an empty table and a `toEqual` of two empty arrays. So:

1. the first case **pins the emptiness explicitly** (`expect(shifted).toEqual([])`), so a
   seventh shifted fixture is a FAILURE rather than a table entry;
2. the second is **widened from "the reindexed ones" to EVERY registry-authored attack
   index in the pool** — the invariant the narrow version was a proxy for, and one that
   only became checkable once nothing was allowed to be shifted.

⚠️ **THE EMPTINESS PIN IS UNKILLABLE ON ITS OWN AND IS KEPT ANYWAY** — nothing in the
pool is shifted, so deleting it fails nothing. It is **WITNESSED** instead of deleted: a
mutant that drops "Iron Smasher" *and re-declares it in the table* is caught by that line
and by nothing else (**3 files with the pin, 2 without**). This is D159/D161/D163's
precedent over D154's, and the discriminator is the one D171 named: **D154 deleted a guard
that was an idiom of one; this one is the file's own idiom** — `NO_CATALOG_ROW` is kept
empty for exactly the same reason, in exactly the same file, two hundred lines up. The
`reindexed` FIELD is kept for the same reason: **an omission this file cannot NAME is one
it cannot count.**

## D174 — THERAPEUTIC ENERGY `sv02-193`: the §12 family's THIRD SENTENCE, its only SPECIAL ENERGY, and the first CONTINUOUS clause this engine reads off an ATTACHED ENERGY — `passivesOf` gains a THIRD SOURCE CLASS, `PassiveEffects.statusImmunity` WIDENS to a list, and a CONTINUOUS CLEAR lands with no precedent (engine 0.117.0 → 0.118.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11)

⚠️ **THIS SECTION LANDED AFTER §D175, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS READ OUT OF ORDER.** D-numbers
were assigned at dispatch; §D175 already explains it and it is not re-explained here.

The last open member of the family D172 built two thirds of, and **the first item in this batch
whose inherited pricing was RIGHT** — four edits, three of them in code this family never
touches, all four real. What the pricing got wrong was only its ORDERING: *"expect the
`passivesOf` audit to be most of the slice"* was correct, and *"the recovery has NO
PRECEDENT"* was correct, but **the item did not know that the census itself still had a
finding left in it.**

> *"As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides {C} Energy.*
>
> *The Pokémon this card is attached to recovers from being Asleep, Confused, or Paralyzed and
> can't be affected by those Special Conditions."*

**The condition list is EXACTLY three — Asleep, Confused, Paralyzed — and it is load-bearing
twice**: it is why D172's scalar had to widen, and it is why the recovery is a second FIELD
rather than a flag.

⚠️ **AND THOSE THREE ARE EXACTLY `SpecialConditions.rotation`'s THREE NON-`none` VALUES, SO THE
ROTATION-SLOT SHORTCUT WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS REFUSED.** *"Clear the rotation slot"* is
behaviour-identical on this printing and **unspellable for a printing that names a SUBSET**
(*"recovers from being Asleep"* alone) — D118's rule: **a shape that happens to coincide with
the data is not the same as a shape that expresses the sentence.** The tokens are carried
per-condition and the clear is per-condition.

### The census held, and WIDENING IT BY ONE VERB FOUND A FAMILY NOBODY HAD COUNTED

Local D1, **978 rows / 6 sets** (`sv01` 258, `sv02` 279, `sv03` 230, `sv06.5` 99, `sve` 24,
`swsh10.5` 88), `.schema` read first, **all three text columns**, `FIXTURE_POOL` swept as a
separate population. D172's numbers re-derived **EXACT**: **4 printings / 3 sentences**, the
same six rows, the same two `attacks_json` false positives (Vivillon `sv01-010` APPLIES a
chosen condition; Sableye `sv02-136` READS one).

⚠️ **Then the pattern was widened by the card's OWN OTHER VERB — `%recovers from%` — and four
more printings fell out:**

| id | printing | shape | built? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sv01-086` / `-228` / `-245` | Gardevoir ex "Miracle Force" — *"This Pokémon recovers from all Special Conditions."* | an ATTACK → **DISCRETE** | ❌ |
| `sv01-145` | Blissey "Busybody Nurse" — *"Once during your turn… Your Active Pokémon recovers from all Special Conditions."* | an activated ABILITY → **DISCRETE** | ❌ |
| `sv02-193` | Therapeutic Energy | **CONTINUOUS** | ✅ D174 |

> ⚠️ **A CENSUS IS ONLY AS WIDE AS ITS VERBS.** D172 swept the IMMUNITY vocabulary (*"can't be
> X"*, *"affected by … Special Condition"*) and got the immunity family exactly right. **The
> card it was pricing has a SECOND clause with a SECOND verb, and nothing in a sweep for the
> first can see the second.** This is D172's three-column rule on a different axis: **the
> column was right and the PREDICATE was short.** The four new rows are all *"recovers from
> ALL"* and all fire at a MOMENT, so they want an op (`clearStatus`), not this slice's field —
> **recorded as a remainder rather than absorbed.**

`sv02-193` is the catalog's **only CONTINUOUS recovery**, which is exactly why it needed a
mechanism instead of a field.

### The shape decision: D172's SCALAR WIDENED, and the rule decided it

`PassiveEffects.statusImmunity?: StatusName` → **`statusImmunities?: StatusName[]`**, plus a new
**`statusRecovery: StatusName[]`**.

D172 chose the scalar by counting its writers — two, each naming one condition — and applied the
repo's rule correctly on the evidence it had: *the unit of SHARING is decided by the READ site,
the unit of STORAGE by the WRITE sites.* **D174 is the third writer and it names three, so the
scalar could no longer SPELL a writer.** The storage unit moved; the sharing unit never changed
(`applyStatus` was already asking `.includes` of a list).

⚠️ **D172 named this exact counter-case and declined the widening on ONE ground: the writer
*"cannot reach the field"*** — an Energy is neither a top card nor a Tool, so `passivesOf` could
not see it. **`EnergyProgram.passive` is what closed that gap, so THE REASON EXPIRED WITH IT.**
The alternative — leave the scalar and give the Energy its own plural field — would be **two
shapes for ONE reading on two interfaces feeding ONE fold**, which is the D131 drift D172 itself
warned about, and strictly worse than the widening it declined.

The Energy's surface is **`EnergyProgram.passive?: PassiveEffects`** and not a narrow §12-only
field, deliberately and at a price: reusing the interface makes the Energy the fold's third
source class *on equal terms*, and every field the fold returns gains an attached-Energy
contributor at once. **That price is the audit below.**

### ⚠️ THE `passivesOf` THIRD-SOURCE AUDIT — the biggest single item, and it came up CLEAN and it stayed ONE SLICE

`sources` had been `[the top card's printed passive, ...the Tools']` since M4. It is now
`[..., ...the attached Energy's]`. **Only the FIRST element takes the §9 `disabled` drop**, so
the new class is exempt by the same construction the Tools have always used.

**What bounds the audit to TEN fields and not twenty-two** is that `PassiveEffects` has 22 fields
and `passivesOf` folds only 10 of them. The other 12 (`disableAbilities`,
`seatDamageReductionAfterWR`, `removeWeakness`, `preventBenchDamageWhileActive`,
`noRetreatCostAura`, `noRetreatCostSelf`, `opponentActiveRetreatSurcharge`,
`preventOpponentActiveRetreat`, `opponentActiveAttackDebuff`,
`opponentActiveAttackCostSurcharge`, `attackCostDiscountPerOpponentPrize` and the aura cousins)
are read by **dedicated board scans off `programFor(top.id)?.passive`** and are **UNREACHABLE
from an Energy however the interface is typed.** That was **measured, not assumed**, and it is
the reason this stayed one slice.

| field | reachable from an Energy now? | correct reading? |

| `damageReductionAfterWR` | ✔ | ✔ — the §8.5 sites SUM sources; an Energy is a source. No writer in the pool. |

| `damageBonusBeforeWRIf` | ✔ | ✔ — collected RAW, evaluated at the read sites; a `BoardCondition` cannot see the source class. |
| `damageBonusBeforeWRIfTarget` | ✔ | ✔ — likewise, gated on the DEFENDER's suffix at the read sites. |

Right for *"the BASIC Pokémon this card is attached to"*, WRONG for an Energy printing that said only *"this Pokémon"* — such a printing needs a stage-free field. **No writer today.** |

`sv02-193` is the **only** card in the pool with an `energy.passive` at all, so every other
body's fold is byte-identical to what D173 shipped. It is **asserted over the whole pool**
(`therapeuticEnergy.test.ts`) rather than left in a comment, because a second Energy row added
without a re-reading is exactly the drift a comment cannot catch — **and the fold's KEY SET is
pinned too, so an eleventh folded field added without re-running this audit goes red.**

### §9 stated the OTHER way round, and the one board that shows both signs

D172 got Ability-lock suppression **free** by riding the fold: a Pokémon's printed passive IS an
Ability. **An Energy is not**, so the new source must be EXEMPT — the same seam, the opposite
verdict. It is exempt by construction (appended past the `disabled` term, like the Tools), and
because *construction* is what D172's three wrong claims were made of, it is **DRIVEN**:

- the lock is proved to contain the holder's uid FIRST (D171's rule, so the positive is not
  vacuous);
- the board is a Klefki-locked **Pachirisu holding a Therapeutic Energy** — one body, one
  `passivesOf` call, two sources, **two different §9 verdicts**: the printed Ability's
  `["paralyzed"]` disappears and the Energy's three survive. A build that got the exemption
  wrong in *either* direction fails there and nowhere else;
- the unlocked control on the same board reports **`["paralyzed", "asleep", "confused",
  "paralyzed"]`** — **the first board in this repo that WITNESSES D172's *"NOT de-duplicated"*
  design note**, previously a claim with no board.

⚠️ **Driving it to a LANDED condition is still impossible, for D172's counting argument over
ACTIVE SPOTS, re-derived rather than inherited** (a status source is an Active; every §9 lock but
Spiritomb's is `requiresActive` and Spiritomb narrows to Basic **V**; the target must be an
Active — **three wanted, two available**). Put a Klefki in the Active Spot and the attacker
becomes Klefki, whose only printed attack applies no condition. **Asserted over the pool.**

### ⚠️ THE RECOVERY: a WRITE, at NAMED MOMENTS — and why it is not another `applyStatus` gate

The card prints two clauses that **run in opposite directions in time**:

- *"…can't be affected by those Special Conditions"* is a refusal at the moment of application.
  That IS an `applyStatus` gate, it is `statusImmunities`, and **D172 already built it — the read
  site took a ZERO diff.**
- *"…recovers from being"* is about a condition that is **ALREADY THERE**, which no gate on the
  writer can ever see: by the time the Energy arrives, the write happened turns ago.

**And it is a WRITE, not a derived view.** The engine's idiom for a continuous effect is to
DERIVE at the read site (`effectiveMaxHp`, `effectiveRetreatCost`, `effectiveAttackCost`)
precisely so a cached value cannot go stale — D172 refused a cached "cannot be Burned" flag for
that reason. A derived `effectiveConditionsOf` would be **WRONG** here, and the printed word says
why: *"recovers"* is a **ONE-WAY change**. A Pokémon that recovered from Sleep is not Asleep
again when the Energy is discarded or moved away, but a subtraction at the read sites would bring
it straight back. So the condition really is removed — and staleness is impossible for the
opposite reason: **nothing is left to go stale.** Driven by stripping the Energy off the board
after the recovery.

`flow.ts recoverStatuses(state, events)` restores the invariant *no in-play body carries a
Special Condition a live continuous effect recovers it from*, at the **TWO NAMED MOMENTS** a
source can newly arrive:

1. **turn.ts `attachEnergy`** — the §6.2 manual attach, which is the card's printed use (attach
   it to your Paralyzed Active and attack this turn);
2. **flow.ts `settleProgram`** — the completion of ANY effect program, which covers
   `attachEnergyFrom`, `attachFromDeck`, `attachFromTop` and `moveEnergy` **in ONE line** where
   five separate interpreter call sites would have been an enumeration to keep up to date.

Naming the moments is **§8.1's own arrangement** (`collectKnockOuts` runs at three named moments,
not globally), and the sweep is idempotent, so a moment named twice costs a scan and nothing
else. **Both sites are driven off PRINTED cards**: the manual attach end to end with **no surgery
at all** (p2 Paralyzes p1's Active with a real attack, a real Checkup leaves it in place, p1
attaches, recovers, and can then attack), and the program site through **Poppy `sv03-193`** —
*"Move up to 2 Energy from 1 of your Pokémon to another of your Pokémon"* — **the pool's ONLY
program that can move a SPECIAL Energy** (every `attachEnergyFrom` route filters to
`energyType === "Normal"`).

**ACTIVE ONLY, and the bench premise is asserted rather than assumed**: `applyStatus` resolves
only to `players[seat].active` and every route off the Active Spot runs `noConditions()`, so a
benched body's conditions are the zero value on every reachable board and a bench arm would be a
branch no test could witness (D154's rule).

### ⚠️ D172's NO-CHECKUP-GATE CONCLUSION: SURVIVES. Its ARGUMENT: NARROWS. Its TRIPWIRE: DID NOT FIRE.

D172 concluded no Checkup gate was owed and gave two reasons:

| D172's reason | after D174 |
|---|---|
| (a) `applyStatus` is the engine's ONLY WRITER of a §12 condition, so gating the writer gates everything downstream | **STILL TRUE.** This slice adds a CLEAR and never a write; there is no board on which `recoverStatuses` can put a condition on anything. Asserted. |
| (b) *"no legal sequence puts an immunity onto a body that already carries the condition it refuses"* — proved by a counting argument plus the fact that evolution / retreat / forced switch all CLEAR | **FALSE.** Attaching Therapeutic Energy to a Paralyzed Active is exactly that sequence, and it is a printed play. |

**No gate is owed anyway**, and the ground is narrower and stated: **the only printing that can
OPEN the window also CLOSES it in the same instant**, because *"those Special Conditions"* makes
its recovery list equal to its immunity list. So a body still never reaches §13 carrying a
condition it is immune to.

⚠️ **THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH IT WOULD FALL IS NAMED AND MEASURED**: a **CONTINUOUS immunity
with NO recovery clause** — an Energy or a Tool printing only *"can't be Paralyzed"* — would open
the window and leave it open, and THAT is when the Checkup owes a gate. The catalog has no such
row: **all three immunity-without-recovery printings are Pokémon ABILITIES**, which arrive with
the body and cannot be attached to one. Asserted over the pool.

> ⚠️ **AND D172's ARMED TRIPWIRE DID NOT GO RED — WHICH IS THE FINDING, NOT A LUCKY ESCAPE.**
> `statusImmunity.test.ts`'s surgically-planted-condition case was written to be *"the FIRST
> THING THAT GOES RED when this lands"*. It is still green, and correctly so: its ASSERTION is
> that a planted Burn on Dachsbun still ticks, and that is still true — **an immunity, on its
> own, clears nothing.** What went false is the REASONING beside it, which said the board was
> unreachable. **The tripwire was armed in a COMMENT, and A COMMENT CANNOT GO RED — D172's own
> headline rule, caught on the very slice it was written for.** The case is **RE-POINTED, not
> deleted**: it keeps its assertion, gains the two lines that discriminate immunity from recovery
> (`statusImmunities === ["burned"]`, `statusRecovery === []`), and hands the reachable version
> to `therapeuticEnergy.test.ts`, where it is driven on both sides off a legal board.
>
> The transferable form: **a tripwire is a claim about an ASSERTION's future, so it has to BE an
> assertion.** If the thing that must break when a future slice lands is written in prose beside
> a passing `expect`, the future slice passes.

### VOICE — the row already existed, and shares its arm on purpose

`STATUS_CLEARED` gains a **sixth `reason`, `"recovered"`** — the first that is neither a
PLACEMENT (`benched`, `evolved`) nor a CHECKUP STEP (`wokeUp`, `burnCured`, `paralysisEnded`).
**No new EVENT**: same seat/uid contract, same list, same rendering verb, and a second event for
one reading is D131's drift. The log arm is **SHARED with `"benched"`** because the words are the
card's own — *"recovers from being…"* renders as **"fix-bigbody recovered from Paralyzed"** — and
the `reason` is what discriminates them for a consumer. The list carries a **SUBSET**: a Burned,
Poisoned, Asleep body attached to this Energy wakes up and keeps burning and keeps being
poisoned, and the row names only what came off. Because `log.ts`'s `default` arm narrows to
`never`, the new reason **could not be added without a case** — a type-level guarantee that a
widened event vocabulary cannot render silently.

### The structural questions

1. **PARK? NO. PERSIST? NO — `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` STAYS 11, DERIVED** on D124's DIRECTIONAL
   test. **Nothing reaches `GameState`**: both new fields are CATALOG (registry.ts types), the
   aggregation is a pure function of the live board and is never stamped, and the recovery
   **WRITES AN EXISTING FIELD** — `conditions` held `rotation` / `poisonDamage` / `burned` before
   this slice and holds exactly those three after it (asserted on the in-play object's own keys,

   emitted none.
2. **VOICE** — one widened reason, one shared log arm, argued above.
3. **§9** — the exemption stated the other way round, DRIVEN, with its last step proved

4. **MECHANISM DID NOT EXIST** — answered NO for the first time in a while. The immunity half is

5. **GATES NO ACTION** — the card's first paragraph is a plain {C} provision, so it makes attacks

## D175 — SPIRITOMB `sv02-089`'s TYPE DIVERGENCE AND THE `battler`-DEFAULT RULE: the LAST human-written wrong type gets its printed `["Psychic"]` and its printed "Fade Out" in ONE landing, `battler` DERIVES an unnamed `types` from the catalog manifest, and `TYPES_DIVERGE` empties to ZERO and is PINNED empty (engine **UNCHANGED at 0.117.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 11**, **0 engine behaviour lines**)

⚠️ **THE NUMBER IS OUT OF ORDER ON PURPOSE — THIS SECTION LANDED BEFORE §D174.** D-numbers
were assigned at dispatch, and **D174 (Therapeutic Energy `sv02-193`, §D172's priced
remainder) was still IN FLIGHT** in a concurrent worktree when this section was written,
taking `engineVersion` **0.118.0**. ✅ **It has since LANDED — see §D174 above.** D175 takes
neither a version nor any of the three files that slice owns, and **there is no lost decision.**

D173's thesis — *a declaration is not a fix, and when both cost one line, fix it* —
applied to the one remainder D173 itself created and could not take.

### ⚠️ The divergence was a wrong COLUMN, not a wrong ELEMENT

The local D1 row for `sv02-089` reads `types_json ["Psychic"]` and `weaknesses_json
[{"type":"Darkness","value":"×2"}]`. The fixture said `types: ["Darkness"]` — **the
Weakness value written into the type field, one column over.**

That is a sharper account than *"someone got it wrong"*, and it is **why** it read as
deliberate for as long as nothing checked the axis: `Darkness` is a real type, a plausible
one for a ghost, and **it agreed with the card** on the only line of the row anybody had
ever transcribed it from. It is D173's Klefki finding one turn further: *"Fairy"* survived
because it is a **retired** type; *"Darkness"* survived because it is **the adjacent
field's correct value**.

### It was not free, and the two halves landed together

Spiritomb's printed "Fade Out" was declared absent in `catalogManifest.test.ts`'s
`INCOMPLETE`, so correcting the type alone would have left a body right on one axis and
wrong on the other — the exact half-landing D173 exists to argue against. The attack is
carried verbatim off the same row and the `INCOMPLETE` entry is gone:

```json
{"cost":["Colorless"],"name":"Fade Out","effect":"Put this Pokémon and all attached cards into your hand.","damage":10}
```

**The declaration's stated reason was a claim about the SUITES, not about the CARD.** It
read *"the aura is the whole test and the body never attacks"*. Every other entry in that
cast omits an attack because the body only ever **DEFENDS**; Spiritomb never even did
that. **A reason that describes what the tests happen to do can never expire, because
nothing about the card can contradict it. That is the shape to distrust.**

#### "Fade Out" is INERT, and that is MEASURED

All six `derive*` readers — `deriveAttackRequirement`, `deriveAttackCoinFlip`,
`deriveAttackEffect`, `deriveAttackDamageBonus`, `deriveAttackDamagePenalty`,
`deriveAttackDamageMultiplier` — return `null` on the sentence, **run directly against
`effects.ts` rather than inferred**.

⚠️ **AND IT IS NOT A NEAR-MISS ON ANY FAMILY: THIS ENGINE HAS NO RETURN-TO-OWNER'S-HAND
`EffectOp` AT ALL.** A grep for `returnToHand` / `scoopUp` / *"attached cards into your
hand"* over `packages/engine/src` is empty outside this fixture. **Fade Out is a
SELF-BOUNCE — a MECHANISM with no op, rather than a SENTENCE with no regex.** Record the
distinction: an unread sentence in a built family is a pricing question about a regex; this
one is a pricing question about a whole op, and it is the useful part for whoever prices
the bounce family later. It rides as a plain printed 10 that would emit a loud
`ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` if anything ever drove it (D170's precedent) — nothing does.

### ⚠️ Breaking "an aura source that never attacks" disturbed NOTHING, and the reason matters

The remainder item warned that giving Spiritomb an attack might make boards reachable that
were not before. **Zero suites moved.** Every §9 counting argument that names Spiritomb
turns on the **registry program**, never on the fixture's attack list:

- `statusImmunity.test.ts`'s three-Actives-wanted-two-available proof reads
  `requiresActive === true` and `{ stage: "Basic", suffix: "V" }`;
- `abilityLock.test.ts` benches it and asserts the aura scan;
- D173's Klefki DELTA pair excluded it as an alternative attacker because it **reaches only
  Basic V** — a property of the program, not a consequence of having no attack.

The phrase *"a `disableAbilities` aura source that never attacks"* existed in exactly the
two declarations this slice deleted. **Nothing load-bearing ever believed it.**

### The rule: `battler` derives an unnamed `types` from the catalog manifest

```ts
function printedTypesOf(id: string): string[] {
  return CATALOG_MANIFEST.printed[id]?.types ?? ["Colorless"];
}
```

`battler`'s `types:` reads it, still **ABOVE `...overrides`**, so an explicit value always
wins. **Three pending edits became one rule**, and the fixture written the same way
tomorrow carries its print too.

⚠️ **IT DISSOLVES THE "DEFAULTED OR GENUINELY COLORLESS?" QUESTION RATHER THAN ADJUDICATING
IT.** `["Colorless"]` is a real printed value — Snorlax `swsh10.5-055` prints exactly that,
and now gets it — so any rule that treated the literal as a marker for *unset* would have to
tell two identical values apart and could not. **Here it never has to: for any id with a
catalog row the value IS the print**, so *defaulted* and *genuinely Colorless* produce the
same correct answer and stop being distinct cases. The literal survives only for the
SYNTHETIC `fix-*` ids, which make no claim about any printed card — and
`expect([...M.absent]).toEqual([])` already pins that *"no manifest row"* and *"not a real
printing"* are the same set.

**Rejected, with reasons:**

| candidate | why not |
|---|---|
| make the default **absent** so the sweep sees an omission | It does not shrink the table by **even one row**: `fixture.types ?? []` still fails the printed-types comparison, so all three stay declared — **a wrong VALUE is relabelled a MISSING one and nothing is fixed**. It also silently drops the `["Colorless"]` every synthetic body relies on (**measured: 1 file / 2 tests red**). |
| require `types` explicitly | **205 `battler` call sites**, nearly all synthetic. A broad reflow of `testFixtures.ts` — a file a concurrent slice is appending to — and it **re-opens hand-transcription at 205 sites, which is the EXACT failure mode that produced Klefki and Spiritomb**, instead of closing it. |

**What the rule does NOT do is make the sweep vacuous.** It removes the *defaulted* class
from it; every fixture that WRITES a `types` value is still checked against the print in
both directions, and the written ones were always the dangerous class.

### ⚠️ THE SLICE'S OWN FINDING: D173's CLASSIFICATION WAS WRONG — the rule fixed TWO of three

D173 split its five `TYPES_DIVERGE` rows into *two a human WROTE* and *three the `battler`
helper's `["Colorless"]` DEFAULT showing through*, and handed the second group forward as
wanting **a rule, not three edits**. The rule was built. It fixed **two** of them.

**Arboliva `sv01-023` is not a `battler` call.** It is a raw object literal — a Stage 1
with an `evolveFrom`, so it never went through the helper — and its `["Colorless"]` was
**WRITTEN**, copied from the helper's shape rather than from the card. It took the one
hand-edit after all (`["Grass"]`), and **only the sweep going red said so.**

> **A DEFECT FILED UNDER THE WRONG CLASS IS ONE A RULE AIMED AT THAT CLASS WILL MISS.**
> *"Fixture Colorless, print Grass"* is the **same OBSERVATION** for a defaulted value and
> for a hand-written one; the two are distinguishable only at the **CONSTRUCTION SITE**,
> and D173 inferred the cause from the **VALUE**. The written column was **3 of 5, not 2**
> — and it was the whole population. This is D173's own *"the missing axis was the
> DIRECTORY, not the card"* recurring one level in: **the missing axis was HOW THE FIXTURE
> WAS BUILT, not what it holds.** Its companion is the Spiritomb case above: **a wrong
> COLUMN looks exactly like a wrong ELEMENT.**

`blank` (the raw-literal base) and `battler` are two different construction sites, and only
one of them is reachable by a change to `battler`.
