## D177 — THE DISCRETE `recovers from all Special Conditions` FAMILY: one new op (`clearStatus`), TWO entry points, and the op-reuse question answered **NO** three times — plus the D173-class fixture that made a pool census blind to its own subject (engine 0.119.0 → 0.120.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 11**)

The family D174 found on its way past and could not build. Four printings, two sentences,
both **DISCRETE**, both unbuilt:

- **Gardevoir ex `sv01-086` / `-228` / `-245` "Miracle Force"** ({P}{P}{C}, 190, index 0) —
  *"This Pokémon recovers from all Special Conditions."* — an **ATTACK**.
- **Blissey `sv01-145` "Busybody Nurse"** — *"Once during your turn, you may use this Ability.
  Your Active Pokémon recovers from all Special Conditions."* — an activated **ABILITY**.

### The census — re-derived, and D174's numbers held EXACTLY

Local D1, **978 cards / 6 sets** (sv01 258 / sv02 279 / sv03 230 / sv06.5 99 / sve 24 /
swsh10.5 88), 2026-08-04, all three text columns:

```sql
select id, name from cards
 where lower(coalesce(effect,''))         like '%recovers from%'
    or lower(coalesce(abilities_json,'')) like '%recovers from%'
    or lower(coalesce(attacks_json,''))   like '%recovers from%';
-- sv01-086 / sv01-228 / sv01-245 Gardevoir ex | sv01-145 Blissey | sv02-193 Therapeutic Energy
```

**Five rows, four of them this family; the fifth is D174's own continuous, NAMED-set
recovery.** Eight other verb spellings — `is cured`, `cured of`, `removes all Special`,
`heal all Special`, `no longer affected`, `recovered from`, `is now cured` — return **zero**
new rows, and `%special condition%` adds only three unrelated readers. **The family is
CLOSED at 4 printings / 2 sentences on this catalog.** D174's list was right on every axis
it stated: names, ids, indices, costs, damage, and the DISCRETE/CONTINUOUS split.

### ⚠️ The wider verb found a FIFTH sentence nobody had counted — the NEGATIVE form

**Muk `sv01-127` "Poison Sacs":** *"Your opponent's Poisoned Pokémon don't recover from that
Special Condition when they evolve or devolve."* A modifier on **§10's evolution clear**
(turn.ts, `reason: "evolved"`) — no op, no moment of its own, and **DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT**:
it is a rule about a clear this op never performs. **Named** in `effects.ts`
(`SELF_RECOVERS_ALL`) and pinned as a string in `clearStatus.test.ts`, on D171's Corviknight
rule, so the next census counts it once instead of rediscovering it. This is the same lesson
D174 wrote paying out a second time: **a census is only as wide as its verbs.**

### ⚠️ THE OPEN QUESTION — can the discrete op reuse `recoverStatuses`? **NO**, three ways

The resume point flagged this as an open question and forbade assuming it. It was priced
against the function, and the answer is **clear the target directly**:

1. **THE DRIVER IS WRONG.** `recoverStatuses` is driven off `passivesOf(...).statusRecovery`
   — a **catalog** value contributed by a live **continuous** source. This op has no source;
   its warrant is that it ran. Reuse would mean writing a synthetic passive onto the board so
   a function could read it back off — a continuous effect impersonating an instant one.
   **Strip the `statusRecovery` read and there is no `recoverStatuses` left.**
2. **THE SCOPE IS WRONG.** That function is a **two-seat board sweep** restoring a board-wide
   invariant. This is **one body**, named by the printed subject, at one moment.
3. **THE SET IS WRONG.** Its per-condition filter (`recovers.includes(status)`) is exactly
   what makes a Therapeutic Energy wake a body and leave its Burn ticking. *"All Special
   Conditions"* names nothing to filter, so `noConditions()` is the whole clear — **the same
   call turn.ts's retreat and evolve clears already make**, not a fourth spelling.

**What IS shared is the VOCABULARY, and that is the part that mattered.** Both halves
announce `STATUS_CLEARED` with `reason: "recovered"` — the printed verb, **one log arm for
both** (log.ts already renders it, D174). A second reason would have been a second rendering
of the same word (D131). The reasoning is written at the interpreter arm, not only here.

### One op, NO FIELDS — D104's minimal shape, and here it is load-bearing

- **No `target`.** *"This Pokémon"* in an attack program and *"Your Active Pokémon"* in an
  Ability program are the **same expression** — `state.players[ctx.seat].active` — which is
  why the two halves are one op rather than D169's two. The only sentence a `target` would
  admit (*"your opponent's Active Pokémon recovers…"*) is one no card would print: recovery
  is upside.
- **No `statuses`.** *"All"* is the printed quantifier over the closed `StatusName` union.
  `PassiveEffects.statusRecovery` must carry a list because **its** printing names three.

### ⚠️ The two halves answer §9 DIFFERENTLY, on ONE body

Under a live Klefki "Mischievous Lock", the **same** Gardevoir ex is refused `Psychic Embrace`
(`ABILITY_DISABLED`) and **still recovers through `Miracle Force`**. An attack is not an
Ability, so the **suppression question belongs to the entry point** — and there is no §9 check
in `clearStatus` at all. Driven on one board, which is the sharpest form the claim has.

### ⚠️ The ATTACK half can NEVER reach two of the five conditions it names

Asleep and Paralyzed block **declaring** an attack (§8), so a Gardevoir carrying either never
runs its own recovery; the **ABILITY** half reaches all five, because `turnGate` does not read
conditions. That is the rulebook rather than a gap, and it is **asserted rather than
commented** — it is precisely the claim a later slice would "fix" by moving the clear to
declaration time. The tails branch of the confusion check pins the other half of it: a Confused
Gardevoir **cannot cure its own Confusion by trying**.

### ⚠️ THE D173-CLASS PREREQUISITE WAS REAL, AND IT IS THE FINDING TO KEEP

Gardevoir ex `sv01-086` sat in `FIXTURE_POOL` with an **empty `attacks` array**, declared in
`catalogManifest.test.ts`'s `INCOMPLETE` with the reason *"registry activated Ability … same
section comment"* — **a true statement about the SUITE that fielded the body and a false one
about the CARD**, which is the exact shape D175 struck out of that table. The consequence is
the sharpest one this table has produced:

> **For the length of that declaration, a `FIXTURE_POOL` census could not see its own subject
> while the catalog census could.** D174's own pool sweep reported *"the recovery half is 1 of
> 5"* and named the gap; it was the declaration, not the pool.

**Fixed, not re-declared** (the seventh entry struck out on the D173/D175 rule). The two
reprints `sv01-228` / `sv01-245` joined the pool at the same time, so *"all three printings
print the same bytes"* is now **driven** rather than pinned in prose — the deriver is
**TEXT-keyed**, so a reprint whose text drifted by one character would silently fall off the
derived path and nothing else in the repo could see it. `therapeuticEnergy.test.ts`'s pool
census is re-pointed from **1 of 5 → 4 of 5**; the residual fifth is Blissey, whose sentence
lives in the **registry** rather than on the card, which is the standing limit of any pool
sweep.

### The `programPlayable` whiff gate — deliberately NOT extended

*"Your Active carries no Special Condition"* is a public board fact of the Crushing
Hammer/Catcher shape, and `useAbility` refuses a program that could only whiff. The gate is
**not** widened to `clearStatus`: the engine's nearest precedent is `healChosen`, whose own doc
block refuses to filter to DAMAGED bodies because *"the printed sentence carries no damaged
restriction, so filtering would be a rule the card does not print"* (the Potion doctrine).
Busybody Nurse names no precondition either, and the op resolves **silently** on a clean body —
so a use that recovers nothing costs the player their once-per-turn and nothing else. Driven
as a case, so the choice is visible rather than absent.

### The structural questions

- **PARK? NO. PERSIST? NO. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 11.** ⚠️ **A new op usually owes a
  bump** — a parked program lives inside `GameState.phase`, so an op that can park changes what
  a record holds. This one **cannot park**: synchronous, field-free, single-step, and neither
  producer wraps it in anything that parks (the attack derives it alone; the Ability's program
  is exactly `[{ op: "clearStatus" }]`). No record written by the previous deploy can hold it
  and none this deploy writes can either. `conditions` still has its three M1 keys; the
  `reason` union did not even widen (`"recovered"` existed since D174).
- **§11:** not gated. `attackEffectRefused` refuses effects done **to** the body carrying a
  block; this op touches only the **attacker's own** Active, and `preventDamage` only ever
  installs on its own Active during its holder's opponent's turn — so the two **genuinely
  cannot meet**, which is stronger than every other `untouched` row in `preventBlock.test.ts`'s
  D150 table (they are careful to say that they *can*).
- **MECHANISM DID NOT EXIST — and the new thing is the ENTRY POINT, not the clear.** The engine
  could already clear conditions (three `noConditions()` placements, four Checkup steps) and
  already had a "recovered" row. What it had **never** had is a **program that clears**: every
  clear before this was a placement or a phase step, reachable only by moving a Pokémon or
  ending a turn.

## D180 — the reprint-alias gaps (Tier 0), and the catalog that was not there

**Engine 0.120.0 → 0.121.0. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11.**

Four printings whose byte-identical twin was already authored, on card ids the registry map
did not name — the backlog's whole Tier 0:

| Reprint | → program | Already-registered twin |
|---|---|---|
| `sv02-245` Copperajah ex "Bronze Body" | `COPPERAJAH_EX` | `sv02-150` |
| `swsh10.5-069` Rare Candy | `RARE_CANDY` | `sv01-191` / `sv01-256` |
| `swsh10.5-078` Professor's Research | `PROFESSORS_RESEARCH` | `sv01-189`/`-190`/`-240`/`-241` |
| `swsh10.5-084` Professor's Research | `PROFESSORS_RESEARCH` | (same) |

Four map rows onto three EXISTING `CardProgram` objects, in the idiom the map has used since
M4. No new op, field, program, event, park, fixture or deck.

### ⚠️ THE CATALOG IS ABSENT IN A FRESH CLONE, AND THIS SLICE RAN IN ONE

This is the durable finding and it outlives the four rows. `apps/api/.wrangler/` is
**gitignored dev state**. It is not in the repository, so a clone has no local D1 at all —
`find / -name '*.sqlite'` returned **zero rows**, and `bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts
--check` dies with `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` rather than reporting staleness. It cannot be rebuilt
either: `apps/api/scripts/ingest.ts` fetches `api.tcgdex.net`, and this environment's network
policy answers **403 to the CONNECT**, so neither the sqlite nor the live API is reachable.

**Consequence: no census in `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md` can be re-derived without
either the `.wrangler` state or network access to tcgdex.** The text-equality sweep behind the
Tier-0 claim was therefore *not re-run*; it is carried from the 2026-08-04 census and is the
sole warrant for these four rows. That provenance is recorded on the rows themselves, at the
top of `reprintAlias.test.ts`, and in the backlog doc.

The in-repo substitutes, in the order of authority this session used them: `FIXTURE_POOL`
(real fixtures carry verbatim printed text) → existing `*.test.ts` string literals →
`catalogManifest.ts` (names, types, attack/ability NAMES — **no effect text**) → the docs'
prose, which is exactly the class of claim the repo's own warnings say rots.

### What is pinned instead, and why no emptiness assertion was written

The repo prefers "pin the emptiness" to "enumerate the exceptions" — but an emptiness pin over
a population nobody measured is the worse failure: it goes green forever while asserting
something this session never checked. So `reprintAlias.test.ts` pins:

1. **the alias relation**, `toBe` on the SHARED program object rather than `toEqual` on a copy
   — the thing a future author breaks by pasting a second literal;
2. **the twins' printed text**, char-for-char off `FIXTURE_POOL`, so a re-ingest that moves the
   anchor voids the alias loudly rather than silently;
3. **the text-equality sweep RESTRICTED to `FIXTURE_POOL`** — which *is* runnable, *is* empty,
   and **states its own scope**: ~200 of the catalog's 978 rows, i.e. a FLOOR. It is blind to
   all four aliased ids, and must stay so: a fixture id naming a real printing needs a
   `CATALOG_MANIFEST.printed` row, and regenerating the manifest needs the sqlite.

⚠️ **The sweep's read predicate had to be made PER-COLUMN.** The first draft asked only "does
`programFor(id)` exist" and reported **two false positives** — Heracross `sv01-002` against
Spidops ex `sv01-019` (identical retreat-cost scaling attack text) and Scovillain `sv01-029`
against Armarouge `sv01-041` ("Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.") — because both
"authored" ids carry a registry program for their *Ability* while the shared sentence is an
*attack* the deriver reads on both sides. The right question is not "is this id registered"
but "is THIS COLUMN of this id read".

### Side finding

`packages/engine/package.json` carried `"version": "0.3.0"` — drifted since D132 while
`engineVersion` in `index.ts` moved to 0.120.0. Nothing reads either the file's version or
`engineVersion` outside `index.ts`, which is why it survived ~48 slices. Re-synced to 0.121.0.

## D181 — the Trainer-path ops printed as attack text, and one row's price re-derived

**Engine 0.121.0 → 0.122.0. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` unchanged at 11.**

Four anchors and four `return`s in `deriveAttackEffect`, for three families the engine has run
on the *Trainer* path since M4 and had no *attack* reader for:

| sentence | op | 6-set printings | **Standard-legal** |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `Draw a card.` | `drawCards 1` | 7 | **22** |
| `Draw 2 cards.` | `drawCards 2` | 5 | **9** |
| `Draw cards until you have 7 cards in your hand.` | `drawUntilHandSize 7` | 3 | **1** |
| `Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot.` | `gust` | 3 | **2** |
| …the same, behind `Flip a coin. If heads,` | `coinFlipGate{gust}` | 1 | *not measured* |
| **built total** | | **19** | **34** |

No new op, field, event, error code, prompt, park, `PendingStage`, log arm, redact arm,
projection, registry row, `@luminous/schema` diff, DB diff or web diff.

### The census re-derived exact — and two of its generalisations did not

Over `json_each(attacks_json)` at six-set scope, every backlog figure held: draw **12/2**,
draw-until **3/1**, self-switch **9/3**, gust **4/2**. What moved is the *wording*:

- the draw family's two sentences are `Draw a card.` (×7) and `Draw 2 cards.` (×5). The
  backlog's "Draw N cards." is a generalisation of one printed number;
- the draw-until N is **always 7**. Both arms stay parameterised anyway, because the Trainer
  path already prints other counts on the same ops (Nemona 3, Grusha 5).

### ⚠️ The self-switch family is NOT built, and that is the finding

The backlog priced `Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.` (9 printings, 3
sentences) at **one regex and one `return`**, on the ground that `switchActive` already exists.
It does. **The op is not the price.**

`finishAttack` addresses the Attacking Pokémon as `players[attackerSeat].active`. That is sound
only because nothing between the §8.5 hit and the epilogue can swap that seat's Active — and
`switchActive` is the one op that can, having lived in exactly one `trainer:` program (Switch
`sv01-194`) that no attack could invoke. Derive it from attack text and the §8.1 KO-conditioned
recoil (Vengeful Punch `sv03-197`) puts its counters on the body that was just **promoted**
rather than on the one that attacked.

**This is not a deduction.** `vengefulPunch.test.ts` sweeps it — *"no attack program — derived
OR authored — can move its own actor off the spot"* — and names the repair in advance: hand
`finishAttack` the attacker's uid, i.e. a **required field on the `attackEpilogue`
`PendingStage`**, which rides `GameState.pending`, is persisted, and therefore costs a
`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` bump. D181 is the first slice to turn that line red.
`preventBlock.test.ts`'s total op classification enforces the same claim independently.

The family's other 2 printings (`You may switch this Pokémon…`, **3 among Standard-legal
cards**) need an optional wrapper the vocabulary does not have: `switchActive` parks a
`choosePokemon`, a prompt with no `declinable`, and `parkOrForce` auto-applies at one candidate;
the only optional pick (`damageChosen.optional`) rides `choosePokemonMulti`, a different prompt
kind with a different answer shape; `TriggeredAbility.optional` governs whether a *trigger*
fires. Queued as **D186, the generic confirm-park**.

Both blockers are **pinned in code** against `fix-trainerops`, which fields all three unread
sentences and goes loud (`ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`) on each.

### ⚠️ A count needs a POPULATION *and* a LEGALITY — a second axis, new to this repo

Legality tracks the regulation mark exactly: Standard = marks **H** and **I**, plus Basic Energy
(no mark, always legal). 2,021 of the remote D1's 3,786 rows are Standard-legal — and **only 127
of the six-set 978 are** (`swsh10.5` is 0 of 88; sv01/sv02/sv03 contribute five Basic Energy
between them). **The whole D179 backlog ranks families over a population that is rotated out.**

A deriver arm survives that intact, because it is a *text parser* and printed sentences transfer
across sets. That is why this slice's clause table carries **both** counts on every row, and why
an unmeasured legal count is `null` rather than zero.

### Three fallout suites, each a real consequence

- **`preventBlock.test.ts`** — its TOTAL op classification demanded a §11 verdict *and* a driven
  probe for all three ops. `drawCards`/`drawUntilHandSize` are `untouched` (the **actor's** own
  deck and hand — no body for a block to protect). **`gust` is `untouched` too, and not as a
  judgement call**: this same file has driven Boss's Orders against a live block since D142, the
  gust lands, and the protection ends *because* the holder left the spot. A `blocked` verdict
  would contradict that case and make the clause's only reachable early clear unreachable.
- **`flipGatedOp.test.ts`** — D134 transcribed the gated gust **verbatim off the local D1** on
  2026-08-01 and listed it as a sentence "this reader has no op for". It was **re-pointed** per
  that file's own standing note, never deleted; three unmapped witnesses remain.
  ⚠️ **Unresolved:** D134 attributes that printing to **Bombirdier**, the backlog's gust row to
  **Tarountula `sv01-016` "String Haul"**. The sentence has exactly **one** printing, so one of
  the two attributions is wrong. Not resolved here.
- **`clauseApostrophe.test.ts`** — the U+2019 census moved 65 → 67, from a source no earlier
  entry on its list had: not a fixture, not a restore, but a **regex**.

### D180 follow-up — provenance discharged, and the legality footnote

All four D180 aliases were **measured** against the remote D1 (the six sets the local D1 holds
total exactly 978 rows) and **all four hold** byte-identically against their twins. The
as-shipped "asserted from a doc" paragraph is kept in `index.ts` rather than rewritten: how a
claim was warranted at the time is the thing this repo keeps losing (D178's rule).

⚠️ **All four ids are rotated out of Standard** — `swsh10.5` is regulation mark F (0 of 88
Standard-legal), `sv02` is mark G — so **D180 serves zero Standard-legal printings.** The four
map rows are correct and cost four lines; the lesson is the pricing rule they make visible:

> **A registry row and a deriver arm must never be priced on the same scale.** An arm is a TEXT
> PARSER and its sentences transfer across sets (D181's four anchors: 34 Standard-legal
> printings against 19 at six-set scope). A registry row is keyed by CARD ID and serves exactly
> the printings it names — so a row against a rotated set serves nobody in Standard.

⚠️ **The emptiness is still not pinned, and the reason changed from "could not" to "was not."**
The four rows are measured individually; the *sweep* that says there are no others has never
been re-run by anyone. `reprintAlias.test.ts` now carries the exact scoped SQL for it rather
than an assertion nobody earned.
## D184 — `matchesFilter` lifted from `interpreter.ts` to `cards.ts`: enabling work, a move and an `export` (engine 0.122.0 → **0.122.1**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 11**)

Not a card slice and not a behaviour slice. `matchesFilter(card, filter)` — the pure
card predicate behind every pile scan (`searchDeck` / `lookAtTopN` /
`discardPileRetrieval`) — was a **bare, unexported** function inside
`interpreter.ts`. It closes over nothing and never sees a `GameState`, so its
placement there was an accident of which module asked first. It now lives in
`cards.ts` beside `energyProvidesOf`, exported, with the body moved
**byte-for-byte**: the old and new bodies were extracted and `diff`ed, and the only
delta is the `export` keyword. All six dependencies (`isBasicPokemon`,
`evolveFromOf`, `isEnergyCard`, `isSpecialEnergy`, `hasRuleBox`,
`energyProvidesOf`) were already exported from `cards.ts` and already defined above
the insertion point, so nothing else moved with it.

All **8** call sites are unchanged — `:851`, `:885`, `:917`, `:3676`, `:3775`,
`:4150`, `:4212`, and `:4628` inside `matchesAttached` — and a grep confirmed the
count is exactly 8 with none outside `interpreter.ts`. Removing the definition left
`hasRuleBox` and `isSpecialEnergy` unused in `interpreter.ts`'s `./cards` import
(they had no other reader there), so those two specifiers were dropped and
`matchesFilter` added.

### `matchesAttached` stays, and the `providesEnergy` comment travels

`matchesAttached` is **not** moved. It takes `GameState` + `InPlayPokemon` and
answers the §6.5 while-ATTACHED question — what an Energy provides **on its host** —
which is a different question from the card-only one. It keeps deferring to
`matchesFilter` for every other filter kind, now across a module boundary.

The `providesEnergy` arm returns `false` **always and deliberately**, and its comment
moved with it. A card in a deck, hand or discard pile is attached to nothing and
provides nothing, so authoring that filter into a pile-scanning op yields an **empty
candidate set — a loud no-op, never a wrong card**, where guessing "a Basic Energy of
that type" would silently take the wrong print. That split is pinned by
`providesEnergy.test.ts` and referenced by name from `registry.ts` and `effects.ts`,
and the comment is the only thing in the code that says so; dropping it in the move
would have left the arm reading as a gap rather than a decision.

### Why now

A coming slice adds a damage-scaling count source that tallies **cards in your
discard pile matching a `CardFilter`** — 12 printings across 5 printed sentences,
including an attack-NAME predicate the filter vocabulary has never had. That consumer
lives in **`attack.ts`**, which must not import `interpreter.ts` just to ask a pure
question about a card. The repo forbids a second answer to an already-answered
question, so the choice was to move the answer or to grow a second one next to the
consumer. Doing it alone, ahead of the feature, means the behaviour slice lands
against an unmoved predicate and its diff is all feature.

### ⚠️ No import cycle — checked with the compiler, and the recon's *reason* was wrong

`cards.ts` gains `import type { CardFilter } from "./effects"`. The recon justified
this as "a type-only edge with **no reverse edge**". There **is** a reverse path:
`events.ts` imports `type { DamageModifier }` **back from `cards.ts`**, closing the
ring **cards → effects → events → cards** in the type graph. The verdict (no cycle)
survives, but for a different reason — **every edge of that ring is `import type` and
is erased wholesale**, so the ring has no runtime existence.

Verified rather than argued: the engine's full **21-module** graph was walked with the
**TypeScript compiler API**, counting only imports that survive type erasure (dropping
`import type` declarations and named clauses whose every specifier is `type X`, keeping
side-effect imports). Result: `cards`'s sole runtime dependency is `actions`, and
`effects` and `events` have **none at all**. The only runtime SCC in the package is the
**pre-existing `flow ↔ triggers` pair**, untouched here. A first hand-rolled regex pass
reported false edges — its non-greedy match ran across statement boundaries and
mis-attributed type-only-ness — which is recorded because the wrong answer looked
entirely plausible and only the compiler's own parser settled it. A **value** import
along any of the three ring edges would make the cycle real; a comment on the new
import in `cards.ts` says so.

### Not re-exported from `index.ts`

Decided, not defaulted. The sole future consumer (`attack.ts`) is **inside** the
package; a grep over `apps/`, `src/` and `packages/` found **no reference to
`matchesFilter` outside the engine** (the only mentions are comments in `registry.ts`,
`effects.ts` and `providesEnergy.test.ts`, plus docs); and nothing outside imports
`cards.ts` directly — every external consumer goes through `@luminous/engine`. The
public API is not widened on speculation. If a web or API caller ever needs it, that
slice adds the line.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

**A PATCH, from the repo's own split precedent.** D150's no-bump covers a **test-only**
slice, and the holds at 0.117.0 covered slices whose every production edit was a
**comment**. This is neither: real code moves between two shipped modules and the
package's internal export surface grows. So it takes the **0.103.0 → 0.103.1**
precedent, which chose a PATCH precisely because that slice touched shipped sources
rather than only a test file. `packages/engine/package.json` moved with `engineVersion`
— D180 re-synced the two after a long drift and they stay in step.

**`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 11 — derived, not declared.** A `MatchRecord` persists
`{version, seed, startedAt, state: GameState, log, names}`, so the gate moves when a
persisted **shape** moves: a `GameState` field, an `EffectOp` inhabitant (a parked
program lives in `GameState.phase`), an `EffectPrompt`/`EffectChoice`/
`EffectContinuation`, an event, or the wire. This slice moves a **function between
modules**. No `CardFilter` arm changed, no op was added or removed, nothing parks (the
predicate is synchronous and field-free), no `GameState` field, no event, no error
code, no `@luminous/schema` diff, no log label. A predicate is code and is never
serialized into a record — and because the body is byte-identical, a record written by
the previous deploy replays identically under this one.

### Cost

Two engine sources (`cards.ts`, `interpreter.ts`), `index.ts` (version + its note),
`packages/engine/package.json`, and two docs. **No test added**: a pure relocation with
a byte-identical body has nothing new to pin, and the existing pile-scan suites already
exercise every arm through the 8 unchanged call sites. `bun run check` **GREEN exit 0**
with counts **identical before and after — 214 files / 3910 tests** on both sides,
which is the evidence for the zero-behaviour-change claim.

Also corrected a doc the move staled: the 6-step recipe for adding a new `CardFilter`
kind said "add a `case` to `interpreter.ts matchesFilter`" and now names `cards.ts`.

### ⚠️ Process scar — the worktree was rooted on the wrong history

The session opened in a worktree branched from `origin/main` (`ffddded`), which is a
**disjoint history** from the work branch `claude/backend-dev-loop-12wbw3` (`f54abaf`):
`git merge-base` between them exits 1 with **no common ancestor**, and `origin/main`
carries **no `packages/` directory at all**. Caught by the first `ls`, not by a failing
build, and re-rooted onto the work branch before any edit. The documented worktree
hazard is about claiming a stale D-number; the sharper failure mode is a worktree whose
base is not an ancestor of the work at all, where every "file not found" reads as a
rotted structural claim rather than a wrong base.

## D190a — the STANDARD-LEGAL reprint-alias map (Tier 0): 22 printings for 9 map rows and no code

Tier 0 of `docs/reference/coverage-backlog-legal.md`, landed in `registry.ts` as 22
id→program rows onto **nine already-authored programs**, using the reprint idiom the
map has carried since M4 (`sv01-189`/`-190`/`-240`/`-241` share ONE
`PROFESSORS_RESEARCH`). No new op, no new field, no new program.

| Sentence | Anchor | Legal printings landed | Catalog printings |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| "…takes 30 less damage… (after applying W/R)" | `sv02-150` Copperajah ex | **8** | 14 |
| "…put 3 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon." | `sv01-005` Cacnea | **3** | 4 |
| "Draw 3 cards." (Supporter) | `sv01-180` Nemona | **3** | 6 |
| "…takes 20 less damage…" | `sv01-121` Stonjourner | **2** | 2 |
| Janine's Secret Art | `sv06.5-059` | **2** | 2 |
| "…the Attacking Pokémon is now Burned." | `sv03-044` Armarouge | **1** | 1 |
| "All of your Pokémon take 10 less damage…" | `sv02-113` Hariyama | **1** | 1 |
| Energy Retrieval | `sv01-171` | **1** | 1 |
| Pokégear 3.0 | `sv01-186` | **1** | 1 |
| **total** | — | **22** | **32** |

Two of the nine are the interesting ones. **"Draw 3 cards." lands on two card NAMES
that are neither of them Nemona** — Friends in Paldea (`sv08.5-109`/`-137`) and Cheren
(`sv10.5w-081`): the SENTENCE is the key, not the name, which is the whole content of
the reprint idiom stated at its limit. And **`sv06-123` Heatran** shares Armarouge's
`onDamagedByAttack` trigger, whose antecedent is byte-identical to Counterattack
Quills' — a passive — so the two are one skim apart and the only thing separating them
is the consequent.

### The sweep was RE-RUN, which is what `reprintAlias.test.ts` asked for by name

D180 shipped its byte-identity **asserted from a doc**, and its test file left the
exact query for the next session with the note that *"a pin claiming a measurement
nobody made is worse than no pin"*. That sweep ran here, against the **REMOTE D1
`luminous`** (`735f0fb5-cdc3-494d-8b97-74a8ade0124a`), on **3,786 rows / 20 sets**, of
which **2,021 carry `legal_standard = 1`**.

**The read predicate is PER COLUMN**, which is D180's own correction applied to the
catalog rather than to `FIXTURE_POOL`: the `abilities_json` join runs only against the
texts of ids whose program carries `abilities`/`passive`/`triggered`, and the `effect`
join only against ids carrying `trainer`/`stadium`/`rareCandy`/`energy`/`passive`/
`triggered`. Asking the cheaper question — *does `programFor(id)` exist* — is exactly
what produced D180's two false positives, where the shared sentence was an ATTACK the
deriver reads while the registry program belonged to an Ability.

**IT MATCHED THE CENSUS EXACTLY.** Nine sentences, 22 legal printings, and nothing else
in any of the three columns. The `attacks_json` sweep returns exactly **one** group —
Hail Blade's text on two `swsh10.5` rows — with **zero** legal printings, so the
census's "zero attack aliases exist" holds as well.

### ⚠️ Four correct aliases were SKIPPED for measuring ZERO legal printings

This is the part D180 could not have written, and it is the reason a registry row and a
deriver arm must never be priced on the same scale. Each of these is a real,
byte-identical, unbuilt reprint-alias gap in the playable catalog — and each buys
nothing in Standard:

* **`"Discard your hand and draw 7 cards."` — 11 unbuilt catalog printings, 0 legal.**
  The census's QUALIFIED addendum made concrete: the modern Professor's Research
  reprints sitting in **`sv08.5`, `sv09` and `sv10.5b`** all carry regulation mark
  **G**. The biggest alias group in the catalog is worth nothing here.
* **Mimikyu's Safeguard sentence** — 6 printings, 0 legal.
* **The very −30 sentence whose 8 legal printings landed above** — 6 MORE printings
  (`sv03.5-009`/`-184`/`-200`, `sv04-128`/`-209`, `sv07-030`), all mark G. One
  sentence, 14 catalog printings, 8 legal: the split runs *through* a family, not
  between families.
* **Tinkaton's "Gather Materials"** — 2 printings, 0 legal.

All four are asserted **as unbuilt** in `reprintAliasLegal.test.ts`, with their ids and
counts, so the decision is checkable and reversible rather than remembered. If a
re-ingest ever makes one legal, that test is where the call gets revisited.

### What is pinned, and the one thing it cannot pin

The 22 reprints **cannot be fielded**: a fixture id naming a real printing must appear
in `catalogManifest.ts` (`catalogManifest.test.ts` case (c)), that manifest is
GENERATED off the local sqlite — `bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts` dies
`SQLITE_CANTOPEN` in this clone — and the manifest it holds measures a **978-row /
6-set** catalog containing none of `sv05`…`sv10.5w`. So no real-card fixture was added
(it would only make the manifest stale), and the file pins instead:

1. the **alias relation** — every new id resolves to the SAME PROGRAM OBJECT as its
   twin (`toBe`, not `toEqual`), which is what a copy-pasted second literal breaks;
2. the **nine targets' shapes**, named, since a change to one now moves up to eight
   more cards than its author may have in mind;
3. **group membership including D180's four rows**, so an addition cannot silently
   become a re-pointing;
4. the **nine programs DRIVEN through the real engine** via their fixtured twins —
   damage reduction at 30 and at 20, the recoil, the Burn trigger, the seat-wide aura,
   the draw, and the three parking Trainers (`chooseCards` ×2, `attachCards`).

### Mutation check — four mutants, all killed

Each is the mistake an author actually makes in a 22-row block of near-identical lines,
written by copying a neighbouring row's real code: `sv06-002` pointed at `STONJOURNER`
(20 instead of 30) → **3 failures**; Cheren pointed at `PROFESSORS_RESEARCH` ("it's a
draw Supporter") → **2**; Heatran pointed at `COUNTERATTACK_QUILLS` (byte-identical
antecedent) → **3**; and landing one of the zero-legal skips → **1**. No survivors.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

**`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays where D189 leaves it — derived, not declared.** A
`MatchRecord` persists `{version, seed, startedAt, state, log, names}`, so the gate
moves when a persisted **shape** moves. A registry row is a map lookup keyed by card
id: no `GameState` field, no `EffectOp` inhabitant, no `EffectPrompt`/`EffectChoice`/
`EffectContinuation`, no event, no error code, no wire, no `@luminous/schema` diff.
Three of the nine programs **do** park, and a parked program lives in `GameState.phase`
— so that was checked rather than waved past: `EffectContinuation` is
`{pendingOp, rest, ctx, record}`, i.e. **the OPS themselves and never a card id**, and
every op involved has shipped for many versions. A record written by either deploy
replays identically under the other.

**No engine version bump, for a mechanical reason rather than a doctrinal one.**
`packages/engine/src/index.ts` and `packages/engine/package.json` were both being
edited by a concurrent slice (D189, the attack tail) while this landed, and the two must
move in step. The ascending changelog block for this slice is **owed at merge**, not
skipped.

## D190b — Tier 1's registry-only programs: three landed, FOUR DROPPED, and the drops are the product

`docs/reference/coverage-backlog-legal.md`'s Tier 1 names **seven registry-only
programs across 29 printings** as needing "no new engine code". Re-derived op by op
against the engine as it actually stands, **four of the seven do**. They were dropped
rather than approximated, and this section is mostly about them.

### What landed — 3 programs, 11 Standard-legal printings

| Program | Printings (legal / catalog) | Ops, all pre-existing |
|---|---:|---|
| **Poison Point** — Roselia `sv05-008`, Roserade `sv05-009`, Scolipede `sv10.5b-056`/`-134` | **4** / 4 | D99's `onDamagedByAttack` + `applyStatus` — Armarouge's program, one `StatusName` over |
| **"Trade"** — N's Zoroark ex `sv09-098`/`-175`/`-185`/`-189` | **4** / 4 | `payFromHand {to:"discard"}` + `drawCards 2` — the Tinkaton shape exactly |
| **"Metal Bridge"** — Archaludon `sv07-107`/`-155`, `sv08.5-070` | **3** / 3 | `noRetreatCostAura {requiresEnergyType:"Metal"}` — Clefable ex's Lunar Zone as pure data |

All three get a **separate const**, deliberately NOT the shared object the Tier-0 idiom
would suggest: these sentences are *near*-twins, not byte-identical, and sharing would
make a later edit to Armarouge or Tinkaton silently move a card that never printed the
same words. `registryOnlyPrograms.test.ts` asserts the non-sharing explicitly.

### ⚠️ THE DOCTRINE: *exact map or flag*

A registry row has **no deriver behind it** to refuse a sentence it cannot parse.
Whatever is authored **is** what the card does, forever. An unauthored Ability at least
surfaces loudly ("not simulated"); a wrong-but-plausible one does not — and every one
of the four failures below is a **silent NARROWING of a printed rule**, not a crash, so
nothing in the suite would have caught it.

### The four that were dropped, with the exact missing piece

1. **Carmine** (`sv06-145`/`-204`/`-217`, `sv08.5-103` — 4 legal). ✅ **BUILT at
   D223** — `CardProgram.trainerFirstTurnExempt`, read at the engine gate **and at
   both HUD row-lighting mirrors**; the row named the field and not its read sites,
   which is the second slice running (D222 was the first) where that was the whole
   cost. See `carmine.test.ts`. The paragraph below is kept as written (D178:
   provenance is annotated, never overwritten). **THE CENSUS IS
   FLATLY WRONG HERE, AND IT IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE CLAIM TO HAVE TRUSTED.** It states
   the printed *"If you go first, you may use this card during your first turn."* is
   *"inert — the engine has no going-first Supporter lock for it to lift"*. **The lock
   exists and has since M4**: `cardplay.ts`'s Supporter branch returns
   `FIRST_TURN_SUPPORTER` on `state.turn === 1`. Carmine's entire first sentence is an
   EXEMPTION from exactly that rule, so `trainer: [discardHand, drawCards 5]` would be
   REFUSED on the one turn the card is printed to be legal on — strictly worse than
   unbuilt. **Driven red in the test file with Nemona rather than argued in prose.**
   Price: a `CardProgram` flag read at that gate — a new FIELD, i.e. Tier 2.
2. **Teal Mask Ogerpon ex "Teal Dance"** (8 legal — the census's biggest Tier-1 row).
   Needs **two** new fields on `attachEnergyFrom`, both listed by the census as already
   existing and neither of which does: a **SELF target** (the op's riders are
   `targetType`/`basicOnly`, which pick out a CLASS of the controller's own Pokémon —
   with two {G} bodies in play `targetType:"Grass"` lets the player attach to the wrong
   one; "this Pokémon" is a UID question, the way `moveEnergy`'s
   `koedActiveToToolHolder` pins its destination), and a **`recordAs` slot** (the op
   records nothing today, so the §9.2 `recordGate` behind *"If you attached Energy to a
   Pokémon in this way, draw a card"* has nothing to read).
3. **Iono's Kilowattrel "Flashing Draw"** (3 legal). Needs a **`from: "self"`** member
   on `discardEnergy`. The existing ones are `opponentActive`/`opponentChosen`/
   `yourActive`/`yours` (+ the `opponentEach` sweep), and `yourActive` means "this
   Pokémon" only inside an ATTACK, where the actor IS the Active. This Ability carries
   **no** Active clause, so a benched Kilowattrel would pay the cost off whichever body
   happens to be Active — and would be USABLE on a board where the Kilowattrel itself
   holds no {L} at all. Adding `activeOnly: true` to make `yourActive` correct would be
   inventing a printed clause the card does not have.
4. **N's Plan** (3 legal). Needs a relaxation of `moveEnergy`'s **single-source**
   coupling — `cardplay.ts` enforces *"every Energy must come from the same Pokémon"*,
   correct for every authored member so far because they all print *"from 1 of your
   Pokémon"*. N's Plan prints *"from your Benched **Pokémon**"*, plural: one Energy off
   each of two benched bodies is a legal paper play and a rejected wire message here.

**18 of the census's 29 Tier-1 registry printings are therefore NOT buildable today** —
it over-priced its own tier by 62 % of printings. All 18 ids are asserted **as unbuilt**
in the test file, each row carrying its missing piece, so the table is a work order.

### The demonstrators live in the TEST FILE, and `testFixtures.ts` is untouched

The eleven printings cannot be fielded: a fixture id naming a real printing must appear
in `catalogManifest.ts` (`catalogManifest.test.ts` case (c)), that manifest is generated
off the LOCAL sqlite — `bun run scripts/catalog-manifest.ts` dies `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` here
— and it measures a **978-row / 6-set** catalog holding none of `sv05` / `sv07` /
`sv08.5` / `sv09` / `sv10.5b`. Adding a real-card fixture would only make the manifest
stale.

So three synthetic `fix-*` bodies are declared **inside `registryOnlyPrograms.test.ts`**
and handed to `createGame({..., cardPool})` — which takes its pool as a PARAMETER, the
one seam that lets a local pool stay local. `FIXTURE_POOL` is not touched at all;
`driveSetup` is re-scripted in ~20 lines because it closes over the shared pool. The
three ids are registered (`fix-poisonpoint`, `fix-trade`, `fix-metalbridge`) against the
**same program objects** the eleven printings resolve to, asserted with `toBe`, so what
the engine drives is literally the shipped program rather than a copy of it.

### Mutation check — seven mutants, all killed

Each written the way an author would actually get it wrong, by copying a neighbouring
program's real code: *copy Scorching Armor verbatim* (status `burned`) → **3**; *copy
Tinkaton verbatim* (`drawCards 3`) → **3**; *copy Lunar Zone verbatim* (`Psychic`) →
**4**; drop `activeOnly` → **1**; `oncePerTurn: false` → **2**; an unconditional aura
(no `requiresEnergyType`) → **3**; and landing one of the four drops → **1**. No
survivors.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

Both unchanged, on the same derivations as D190a. Three map lookups keyed by card id:
no `GameState` field, no `EffectOp` inhabitant, no prompt/choice/`EffectContinuation`
shape, no event, no wire, no `@luminous/schema` diff. "Trade" **parks** (a `chooseCards`
hand cost) and a parked program lives in `GameState.phase` — but `EffectContinuation`
carries `{pendingOp, rest, ctx, record}`, the ops themselves and never a card id, and
`payFromHand`/`drawCards` have shipped since M5. `index.ts` and
`packages/engine/package.json` were held by the concurrent D189 slice, so the ascending
changelog block is owed at merge.

## D193 — three `DamageCountSource` members that count BODIES and ENERGY, and a fourth built, measured and REVERTED

Engine **0.123.0 → 0.124.0**. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 12**. `apps/api`
untouched.

### The population, restated because it is what moved every number

The D1 (2026-08-04) holds **3,786 rows**, of which **2,021 are Standard-legal**
(`legal_standard = 1` ⇔ regulation mark H/I, plus unmarked Basic Energy). The six-set
census population this file's older sections were built on
(`sv01`,`sv02`,`sv03`,`sv06.5`,`sve`,`swsh10.5`) is **978 rows of which only 127 are
legal** — so a six-set count and a legal count are now describing almost disjoint
populations, and every figure below carries both.

| member | legal | six-set | folds MEASURED | edits predicted | edits ACTUAL |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `bothSidesBenchCount` | 5 | 0 | ADD only | 4 | **4** |
| `opponentBenchCount` | 6 | 4 | ADD (4) + MULTIPLY (2) | 6 | **6** |
| `energyOnOpponent` | 17 | 3 | ADD (8, active only) + MULTIPLY (3 active, 6 board) | 6 | **7** |
| `energyOnSelf` | 21 buildable | 3 | ADD (12) + MULTIPLY (9) | 6 | **DROPPED** |

### The price, re-derived — and the backlog is wrong for the THIRD time

A new count source is **not** "one regex + one evaluator arm". Verified against
`effects.ts`/`attack.ts`: it is **union member + evaluator arm + regex const + reader
arm**, and a BOTH-fold member is **two regex consts and two reader arms — six edits**.

`energyOnOpponent` came in at **seven**, and the seventh is worth naming: the optional
type token needs a resolver that tells "no filter printed" (`null` — count everything)
apart from "a filter I could not read" (`undefined` — stay LOUD), and collapsing those
two is the mistake that would make `for each {C} Energy…` quietly score the unfiltered
total. That is `attachedEnergyFilter`, shared by both reader arms.

**Plus one widening outside the family.** `countEnergyInPlay` (continuous.ts) had **no
`null` arm**, and the untyped board reading is really printed (3 legal), so it gained
one. Additive: every existing caller passes a concrete type or `"special"` and none can
observe the new arm.

### The fold is the printed adjective, and one of this file's own claims was stale

*"does N **more** damage for each…"* keeps the printed base (ADDITIVE); bare *"does N
damage for each…"* **drops** it (MULTIPLY). The `damage` column corroborates (`20+` vs
`30×`). Re-derived per sentence, never inferred from the attack name.

**⚠️ The correction is inside `effects.ts`.** D170's `BENCH_COUNTER_MULTIPLY` block names
Oinkologne ex sv01-158/-234 "Maddening Scent" and Tyranitar sv02-135/-222 "Rout"
printing *"This attack does 30 more damage for each of your opponent's Benched
Pokémon."* as the unread near-miss. That sentence is **9 printings and 0 legal** — it has
rotated out entirely, and the additive fold in the legal pool is carried by the `20
more` spelling (5 printings, 4 legal). The comment is left standing because it is still
true of the population it was measured on; the pattern is unaffected (one `(\d+)` spans
both), but the *pricing* was not.

**`bothSidesBenchCount` is ADD-only by ABSENCE, not by rarity.** The pool prints no
no-adjective twin in any text column; the only other row carrying the parenthetical
beside a "for each" draws cards. Pinned as an absence rather than left to be
rediscovered.

### The member that was DROPPED, and why that is the most useful line here

`energyOnSelf` ("…for each [{X}] Energy attached to this Pokémon.") is the **biggest** of
the four at 21 buildable legal printings, and it is **blocked, not unpriced**. Entei
sv03-030 "Blaze Ball" — *"This attack does 20 more damage for each {R} Energy attached to
this Pokémon."* — has been this engine's canonical **UNSIMULATED-"+" witness since
0.35.0**, and its sentence is exactly one of these printings. Building the member turns
**5 assertions across 4 test files red**: `scaledDamage.test.ts` (×2),
`perEnergyFlip.test.ts`, `log.test.ts`, `checkup.test.ts`. Measured by implementing the
member, running the suite, counting the failures and reverting — not estimated.

Those four files are outside this slice's ownership, so the member is handed forward
with its repair already found: the replacement witness is *"This attack does 30 more
damage for each Energy attached to **both Active Pokémon**."* — **10 printings / 8
legal**, ADD-only (its bare twin is 1 printing / 0 legal). That sentence is **also the
largest unbuilt member this slice measured**: a THIRD zone that spans the table, which
`OpponentEnergyZone` deliberately does not reach. Re-homing the witness and building
both is one slice.

**Two recon counts were the RAW sentence count, not the buildable one.** `energyOnSelf`'s
23 is **21**: one row is a two-sentence printing the whole-sentence anchor refuses, and
one filters on `Basic Energy` — a card **CATEGORY**, not a type, which resolves to
nothing and correctly stays LOUD. `energyOnOpponent`'s 17 **is** 17, because that
family's category row filters on `Special`, which `CLAUSE_ENERGY_TOKENS` already
resolves for free.

### The exclusions and the retired traps, all confirmed

- 3 legal **SNIPE** scales (*"…damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon for each Energy
  attached to this Pokémon."*) stay on `damageChosen` — asserted, both readers refuse.
- 3 legal counter-**PLACEMENT** scales (*"Put 2 damage counters … for each …"*) are not a
  damage clause at all — asserted.
- *"Flip a coin for each Energy attached to this Pokémon."* stays on
  `AttackFlipCount.attachedEnergy` (D128) — asserted.
- The *"each **extra** Metal Energy … can't add more than 120 damage in this way"* cap is
  **0 legal**. **No cap built.** Refused by the anchors, which is the correct answer.
- Spelled-out energy words (`Water Energy`, `Psychic Energy`, `Grass Energy`) are **0
  legal** — the legal pool is brace notation only. D118's dual-notation arms are **not
  deleted** (they are shared with the clause and coin families and cost these patterns
  nothing) and are recorded as **NOT load-bearing**.

### Ordering: one witness, three pinned absences

The additive fold gets a witness that **does not commute**: a Fire attacker into a
×2-Fire defender, where the pre-W/R fold reads `(20 + 60) × 2 = 160` and a post-W/R one
reads `20 × 2 + 60 = 100`. A subtractive term could never be the witness — it commutes
with the sum — which is why the multiplier is.

The `×` fold **cannot have one**, and that is pinned rather than papered over: it drops
the printed base, so the sum has **one term** and every ordering of a one-term sum
agrees. The absence is asserted through the row's own shape, which turned out sharper
than the arithmetic: `DAMAGE_DEALT` reports `base: 0` — not the printed 30, not the
folded 60 — with the whole term in `scaled`.

"Read at DECLARATION" is likewise unobservable for this family: no sentence in it removes
a body from a Bench or an Energy from a Pokémon, and none is a multi-sentence printing.
Pinned as an absence.

### Mirror witnesses, because three of these members mirror another

`opponentBenchCount` mirrors `bothSidesBenchCount`; the two `energyOnOpponent` zones
mirror each other and both mirror the attacker's own Energy. Each pair is driven on a
board where the sides **disagree**, so a reader that started answering both would
collapse them:

- **3 bodies on the attacker's Bench, 1 on the defender's** → both-sides **4**,
  opponent-only **1**, attacker-only (the mutant's answer) **3**. Three distinct numbers
  on one setup.
- **2 Energy on the defender's Active, 3 on its Bench, 1 on the attacker** → active zone
  **2**, board zone **5**, attacker's own **1**.

`board` is asserted to be a strict **superset** of `active` (§6.3 "in play" = Active +
Bench), because the plausible mistake is reading "all of your opponent's Pokémon" as the
Bench-only walk `damageCountersOnYourBench` performs.

### Mutants

**12 run, each copying a neighbouring arm's REAL code; 0 survived** the first round.
Seat drift on both body counts (from `damageCountersOnYourBench`), `benchBodies` counting
COUNTERS via that arm's verbatim `reduce` body, the active-Energy arm reading `attacker`
(from `damageCountersOnSelf`), board-zone seat drift, the type filter dropped, the zone
branch deleted, the two nullish filter answers collapsed to `?? null`, the `more`
discriminator dropped from a regex, D137's `['’]` class dropped, the zone capture
inverted, and the opponent-bench MULTIPLY arm moved onto the ADDITIVE fold.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

Engine **0.124.0**, ascending changelog block in `index.ts` and `package.json` in step.

`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 12**, derived rather than inherited. `DamageCountSource`
is a **PARSE-TIME** type: produced by the two readers from card TEXT at declaration and
consumed by `scaledAttackDamage` in the same tick. Swept — it appears in no `GameState`
field, no `PendingStage`, no `@luminous/schema` projection and no redaction, and
`scaledAttackDamage`'s switch is the repo's only dispatch over it. There is **no new
`EffectOp`**, which is D189's stated bump condition (a parked program lives in
`GameState.phase`). `countEnergyInPlay`'s widened parameter is a reachability widening —
D181's precedent — and a function signature rather than a record field in any case. A
version-12 record replayed against this engine reads every field it carries with the
same meaning.

### Fixtures

Two SYNTHETIC bodies (`fix-benchcount`, `fix-oppenergy`) and one deck
(`BENCH_BODY_DECK`). `FIXTURE_POOL` was swept as a **separate population** first and held
**zero** of the nine sentences — that sweep is now a test, so a later slice that adds one
of them elsewhere learns it immediately. Synthetic rather than transcribed because the
catalog manifest **cannot be regenerated** (`SQLITE_CANTOPEN`; the local `.wrangler` D1 is
absent), so a real-card fixture could not be diffed against its printing at all; `fix-*`
ids are skipped by `catalogManifest.test.ts` by construction.

### The census that moved, attributed rather than bumped

`clauseApostrophe.test.ts`'s discovered sweep — every apostrophe-bearing sentence the
FIXTURES print **that a reader resolves** — moved **67 → 74**. All seven rows are this
slice's: **3** from `fix-benchcount` (the three body-count sentences) and **4** from
`fix-oppenergy` (two zones × the folds each is printed with). Each is attributed in the
comment block above the assertion, per D181's precedent; a bare count with no attribution
is the "declaration is not a fix" pattern this repo has already paid for.

Two of the seven expose a slot shape no earlier row has: "Herd Charge"'s apostrophe is
followed by a **`)`** inside a parenthesised clause the pattern carries as ESCAPED
literals (every possessive row above it is followed by a space and a word), and the two
board-zone rows are the SAME regex with its optional type capture absent and present — so
the fold must survive a pattern whose capture length varies between two rows this census
counts separately. `fix-benchcount`'s FOURTH attack carries a real D154-class contraction
("Don't apply Weakness and Resistance…") and adds **none**, because the sweep admits only
sentences a reader RESOLVES and that self-spread is deliberately unsimulated — D170's
result, repeating.

Suite: **+37 tests in 1 new file** (`benchBodyScaling.test.ts`), plus the census
attribution in `clauseApostrophe.test.ts`. Repo: **220 files / 4029 tests** at the
baseline → **222 / 4080** green at commit (the other +1 file / +14 tests are a concurrent
`apps/api` slice's).

## D192 — MAIN-HIT DAMAGE-MODIFIER SUPPRESSION: `This attack's damage isn't affected by …` — THREE booleans, ONE shared read site, TWO stores, and the ordering witness that CANNOT exist for one of them (engine 0.124.0 → 0.125.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 12**)

The §8.5 pipeline's first printed sentence that removes **STEPS** rather than moving
numbers. `AttackDamageSuppression {weakness?, resistance?, targetEffects?}` — a FOURTH
deriver beside `deriveAttackDamageBonus`/`…Multiplier`/`…Penalty` — plus
`PassiveEffects.suppressTargetEffectsOnAttack`, the ABILITY half, meeting the attack half
at exactly one `||`.

### The population, re-measured

Remote D1 `luminous` (`735f0fb5-cdc3-494d-8b97-74a8ade0124a`), **3,786 rows / 20 sets**,
of which **2,021 carry `legal_standard = 1`** (⇔ mark H or I, plus unmarked Basic Energy),
queried 2026-08-04 over `attacks_json` and `abilities_json`.

| printed sentence | rows | legal | sets |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `…isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.` | 29 | **15** | T |
| `…isn't affected by Resistance.` | 17 | **9** | R |
| `…isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance, or by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.` | 10 | **8** | W+R+T |
| `…isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance.` | 2 | **2** | W+R |
| **total (attack)** | **58** | **34** | |
| ABILITY: `Damage from attacks used by this Pokémon isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.` | 6 | **6** | T |

The ability half is ONE sentence on ONE card: Walking Wake ex "Azure Seas"
(`sv05-050`/`-189`/`-205`/`-215`, `sv08.5-178`, `svp-127`).

### ⚠️ What turned out wrong

- **`suppressResistance` is 17 legal built, not 22.** 9 alone + 8 compound. The handoff's
  22 is reachable from no population: even adding all five deferred riders gives 20,
  because only 3 of the 5 name Resistance. `suppressWeakness`'s 15 is right *if* the
  riders are counted (10 built + 5); `suppressTargetEffects`' 23 (15 + 8) is exact.
- **The three-boolean ARGUMENT is half wrong, which matters more than the counts.** The
  scoping claim was "Weakness and Resistance each occur ALONE in the legal pool, so they
  cannot share a field". `resistance` alone is real and BUILT (9 legal). `weakness` alone
  is real in the legal pool but lives **entirely in the deferred riders** — inside the
  four sentences this slice builds, Weakness is only ever printed beside Resistance, so
  those two *could* have shared one field today. Three booleans still, on two structural
  grounds rather than the priced one: they are read at two DIFFERENT §8.5 steps (the
  Weakness ternary already had a null path, `seatRemovesWeakness`; Resistance had none),
  and the first rider to land would have to un-merge them.
- **The `FIXTURE_POOL` sweep found a carrier**, where four slices running found none.
  Bellibolt `sv03-078`/`-201` "Thunderous Edge" has printed sentence #1 verbatim since
  D159, where the fixture comment called it *"a live question this slice deliberately does
  not answer"*. It is answered with **no fixture edit** — and it was checked against D193's
  trap by running the full suite: Bellibolt is a DEFENDER in every case
  `attackerFilter.test.ts` drives, so nothing there moves.

### Four sites moved, not one — the clause's SCOPE, not its step

Beyond Weakness and Resistance, `targetEffects` reaches:

1. the post-W/R **reduction** — catalog and installed halves go, and the SEAT-WIDE aura
   drops to `"othersOnly"` rather than to zero (D161's reading inherited whole: an ACTIVE
   Hariyama loses its own 10, a BENCHED one keeps shielding its teammate — both driven);
2. the **ON-TARGET prevention trio**, with D159's OFF-TARGET pair left OUTSIDE the guard
   verbatim — and that half is now driven at the MAIN HIT, not only at the snipe arms
   (Neutralization Zone `sv06.5-060` nulls a fully-suppressed hit from a V attacker);
3. **the one the brief did not name** — the PRE-W/R `opposingAttackDebuff`, whose SOURCE
   *is* the opponent's Active (Entei `sv03-030` "Pressure"). `snipeActive`'s D151 split
   arriving at the main hit: the aura half of the `debuff` sum goes, the attacker-record
   stamp and this attack's own printed penalty stand.

### Sharing the READ SITE, not the STORAGE

One `||` into `suppressTargetEffects`; three §8.5 steps consult it and none can tell which
half answered. The stores stay apart because the attack half is a PARSE alive for one
declaration and immune to §9, and the ability half is a §9-SUPPRESSIBLE catalog aura.
Both signs driven on ONE board: under Spiritomb "Fettered in Misfortune" the ability half
reads the control's 90 and the attack half still reads 120.

The attacker-side read is **new to `attack.ts`**, which folded `passivesOf(next, defender)`
only. It arrives through `attackerSuppressesTargetEffects` (continuous.ts), the shape
`boostedAttackDamage` / `installedAttackDebuffOf` already use — and it is the FIRST of the
three that is a CATALOG fold rather than a stamp on the attacker's record, which is
exactly why it is the one §9 can switch off. Price: 1 `PassiveEffects` field, 1 fold key +
1 OR in `passivesOf`, 1 exported helper, 1 `||` at the site. `passivesOf`'s D174 Energy
audit is RE-READ for the thirteenth field rather than bumped.

**Not `damageChosen.ignoreWR`**, verified before concluding: ONE writer
(`CHOSEN_ANY_TARGET`'s group 2 — Umbreon "Feint Attack") and TWO read paths (`snipeActive`,
`placeSnipe`'s `deals` arm). It is a member of an OP and the main hit has no op, and it is
one boolean where three are needed. Asserted in both directions.

### Ordering: one witness, two pinned absences

The witness is a Fire 60 into a ×2-Fire / −30-after-W/R body: `60×2−30 = 90`, where
reduction-first reads `(60−30)×2 = 60`. The two suppressions then remove one operand each
for **four distinct numbers on one board — 90 / 120 / 30 / 60**.

`suppressResistance` alone **can have no order witness at all**, and it is PINNED rather
than faked: Resistance and the reduction are both subtractions under monotone floors and
`max(0, max(0,x−a)−b) === max(0, x−a−b)` for all a,b ≥ 0 (driven as arithmetic over the
range, not as a board that passes while asserting nothing); and ordering it against
WEAKNESS needs a card listing one type in BOTH columns — **0 of 3,786 rows**, measured —
so only the synthetic `fix-weak-tough` can, and it says so.

### Deferred: +5 legal rider-on-compound printings

`If your opponent's Active Pokémon isn't a Pokémon ex, this attack does nothing. …` (2),
`If you have 3 or more Energy in play, this attack does 70 more damage. …` (1),
`…for each damage counter on all of your Benched Cynthia's Pokémon. …` (1),
`Your opponent flips a coin for each of their Benched Pokémon. … for each tails. …` (1).
Every deriver here is fully anchored, so admitting them means a SENTENCE-SPLITTING seam,
not a looser regex — and 4 of the 5 are blocked on their own leading clause anyway. A
search-style pattern would silently claim the whole compound. Refusal asserted on the
printed text; `FIXTURE_POOL` already carries a sixth (Pachirisu `sv01-068`/`-208`,
3 catalog / **0 legal**) and it stays loud.

### Mutation pass — 13 mutants, **3 first-round survivors**, all three then killed

Each mutant copies a neighbouring arm's REAL code. Survivors and their repairs, reported
because a survivor is the finding:

- **M5** (the OFF-TARGET pair moved INSIDE the guard) survived: both off-target reads are
  FALSE by construction on the main-hit path, so no existing board could see the change.
  Killed by a Neutralization Zone board with a **V** attacker whose suppression comes from
  the Ability — the hardest-suppressed hit this engine can build, still nulled.
- **M7** (`installedAttackDebuffOf` nulled too) survived: no board carried an
  attacker-installed debuff. Killed by a local surgery stamping `attackDamageDebuff`, plus
  a board carrying BOTH sources where the clause takes exactly one.
- **M10** (`modifierSimulated` gaining the new reader) survived, and **could not be killed
  from the catalog**: all 34 legal printings sit on a FLAT printed damage. Killed by an
  index-5 PROBE attack (`60+` with the clause) asserting the row stays LOUD — D130's rule,
  `fix-attacker`'s base-0 "Fury" the precedent for a probe no printing licenses.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

Engine **0.125.0**, ascending changelog block in `index.ts` and `package.json` in step.
**D190's owed block is also written**, in ascending position between D189's 0.123.0 and
D193's 0.124.0 and carrying no version of its own — it moved none, because both files were
held by a concurrent slice when it finished.

`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 12**, derived. `AttackDamageSuppression` is a PARSE-TIME
value produced from card text and consumed in the same tick;
`PassiveEffects.suppressTargetEffectsOnAttack` is a **CATALOG** value read through
`passivesOf`, not persisted state. No `GameState` field, no `InPlayPokemon` key, no
`PendingStage`, no new `EffectOp` (D189's stated bump condition — nothing new can park),
no `EffectPrompt`/`EffectChoice`/`EffectContinuation`, no `@luminous/schema` diff, no
redaction change. `DAMAGE_DEALT` is unchanged: `weakness: null` and `resistance: null` are
already-supported inhabitants (`seatRemovesWeakness` and the snipe arms write both today)
and `reduction` is already optional. The widened `passivesOf` return is a reachability
widening — D181's precedent — and a function signature in any case. `apps/api` untouched.

### Fixtures and the suites that moved

Four SYNTHETIC bodies (`fix-suppressor`, `fix-azureseas`, `fix-suppresswall`,
`fix-resistwall`) and one deck (`DAMAGE_SUPPRESSION_DECK`). Synthetic because every real
carrier is in sv05–sv10.5w and `CATALOG_MANIFEST` measures a 978-row / 6-set catalog
holding none of them, and the generator cannot be re-run here (`SQLITE_CANTOPEN`). The 6
real Walking Wake ex ids get **registry rows and no fixture** — D190's Tier-1 idiom.

**Two suites outside this slice went red, both by design and both repaired rather than
bumped** — that is those guards working, not a chore:

- `therapeuticEnergy.test.ts`'s **eleven-key** `passivesOf` fold audit is now **twelve**,
  with the new key's Energy reading argued in place (it is the first key of that fold read
  off the **attacker**);
- `alwaysOnReduction.test.ts`'s `damageReductionAfterWR` census is **PARTITIONED** rather
  than extended — the real-card list is byte-unchanged and the two synthetic walls are

`clauseApostrophe.test.ts` **74 → 78**, attributed row by row: **3** from `fix-suppressor`
and **1 from a REGEX ALONE** — Bellibolt's sentence, in the pool since D159 and unread
until now. First time one slice has moved that census from both of its sources at once.
`fix-azureseas`' Ability adds **none**: the sweep enumerates `card.attacks` only.

Suite: **+35 tests in 1 new file** (`damageSuppression.test.ts`) plus 3 census repairs.

## D196 — the two Energy counts that were BLOCKED BY A FIXTURE, and the witness re-homed to unblock them

Engine **0.125.0 → 0.126.0**. `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 12**. `apps/api`
untouched.

### The slice in one line

D193 measured `energyOnSelf`, built it, watched five assertions in four suites it did not
own turn red, and **reverted**. The reason was not the member: it was that the member's
printed sentence is carried by `FIXTURE_POOL`'s Entei sv03-030, which had been the
engine's canonical **unsimulated-`+` witness since 0.35.0**. This slice re-homes that
witness first and then builds both members.

### The population, re-measured

D1 (2026-08-04): **3,786 rows**, **2,021 Standard-legal** (`legal_standard = 1` ⇔ mark
H/I plus unmarked Basic Energy). The six-set census population is 978 rows of which only
**127** are legal, so every figure below carries the legal count and the whole-catalog
count.

| member | legal | catalog | folds MEASURED | edits predicted | edits ACTUAL |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `energyOnSelf {energyType}` | **21** | 38 | ADD 12/26 + MULTIPLY 9/12 | 6 | **6** |
| `bothActivesEnergyCount` | **8** | 10 | ADD only | 4 | **4** |

`energyOnSelf` is the largest member this family has ever taken — bigger than D193's
three combined — and it was the last one built. `bothActivesEnergyCount` is one verbatim
sentence (`30+` on all ten rows), `attacks_json` only, no typed spelling anywhere.

**Every number D193 published was right.** 21 (not the earlier recon's 23), ADD 12,
MULTIPLY 9, both-Actives 10/8, its bare twin 1/0. The list of red assertions was right
too, verified by re-implementing the member and counting: `scaledDamage.test.ts` ×2,
`perEnergyFlip.test.ts`, `log.test.ts`, `checkup.test.ts` = **5 across 4**. A **sixth**
failure exists and could not have been on that list — `benchBodyScaling.test.ts`'s own
pinned absence for `bothActivesEnergyCount`, which only this slice's second member
touches. D193 wrote that pin deliberately and handed it forward; it is **flipped**, not
deleted.

### The re-homed witness, and why it is stronger than the one it replaces

**Pachirisu sv01-068 "Everyone Discharge"** ({L}{C}, `10+`):

> "This attack does 20 more damage for each of your Benched {L} Pokémon. This attack's
> damage isn't affected by Weakness."

It stays unread for **three independent reasons**, where Entei had exactly one:

1. **Two sentences.** Every reader in this family is whole-sentence anchored (`^…\.$`)
   and there is no composition path.
2. **An unbuilt count source.** "for each of your Benched {L} Pokémon" is a **typed**
   count of **bodies** on the attacker's own Bench. No `DamageCountSource` member counts
   bodies with a type filter: D193's two body counts are untyped, D196's two Energy
   counts are not bodies.
3. ⚠️ **The suppression half is refused alone too — and this is where the slice's own
   premise was WRONG.** The plan was that reason 1 would be sharpened by the second
   sentence being one D192's `deriveAttackDamageSuppression` already answers. It is not.
   *"This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness."* has **zero standalone printings**
   in the pool; the catalog prints that clause only as the **tail** of a two-sentence
   attack (3 rows, 2 of them legal, neither this card). That is exactly why D192's four
   anchored spellings have no Weakness-only member. So the composition has **no readable
   half at all**, and the expected corroboration turned out to be a third reason.

A slice that builds the typed bench count leaves reasons 1 and 3 standing; one that adds
sentence splitting leaves reason 2. That is the property Entei lacked, and precisely why
D193's revert had to happen. **The swap is also like-for-like on legality**: Entei's
sentence is 2 printings / 0 legal, Pachirisu's is 3 / 0 legal — no legal witness traded
away.

Entei does not leave the deck; it **changes sign**. It is now the family's only
**real-card positive** case, and specifically the one that pins the TYPE FILTER against a
real printing (`{per: 20, count: {kind: "energyOnSelf", energyType: "Fire"}}`).

### The price, verified against the file — and D193's formula held exactly

A single-fold member is **union member + evaluator arm + regex const + reader arm = 4**; a
both-fold member is **6** (two regex consts, two reader arms). Actual:
`bothActivesEnergyCount` **4**, `energyOnSelf` **6**, total **10**.

**No seventh edit, and no widened signature.** D193 paid a seventh for
`attachedEnergyFilter` — the resolver that tells "no filter printed" (`null`, count
everything) from "a filter I could not read" (`undefined`, stay LOUD). It already exists
and both new reader arms use it unchanged. Both evaluator arms call `countAttachedEnergy`
at the shape it already had, so unlike D193 this slice does not need even D181's
reachability-widening precedent.

### The two rows in the 23-vs-21 gap, both LEGAL

A raw sentence sweep is not a build estimate, and both rows prove it:

- *"This attack does 40 damage for each **Basic Energy** attached to this Pokémon."* (1
  legal) filters on a card **CATEGORY**. `Basic` is absent from `CLAUSE_ENERGY_TOKENS`,
  resolves to nothing, and the reader must stay LOUD. On a real board it deals its
  printed 40 with **no `scaled` field**, never the 3 × 40 an unfiltered count would give.
- *"…for each {W} Energy attached to this Pokémon. **Before doing damage, you may attach**
  any number of Basic {W} Energy cards from your hand to this Pokémon."* (1 legal) is a
  two-sentence printing. It is also **the one printing in the family that could make
  "read at DECLARATION" observable**, so the anchor's refusal is load-bearing rather than
  incidental.

### `bothActivesEnergyCount` — ADD-only by LEGALITY, which is the opposite of its neighbour

`bothSidesBenchCount` is ADD-only because the twin **does not exist**. This one's bare
twin **is printed** (*"This attack does 30 damage for each Energy attached to both Active
Pokémon."*) and is **0 legal** — so refusing it is a decision about the legal pool, not a
statement that the sentence is absent. Pinned as such. It takes **no type filter** either:
no typed spelling is printed in any column, so a capture would be a field no reader could
set — D193's zone-capture refusal, mirrored into the other axis.

Its near-miss is a coin row: *"Flip a coin for each Energy attached to both Active
Pokémon. This attack does 60 damage for each heads."* — **1 printing / 1 LEGAL**, unread
on **both** sides, and **not** `AttackFlipCount.attachedEnergy` either (that member reads
"attached to *this* Pokémon", one body). The pool's only legal both-Actives coin sentence
stays LOUD and is pinned for the next slice.

### The fixture sweep — five slices found zero, this one found ONE

`FIXTURE_POOL` was swept as a separate population **before** anything was written, and it
held `sv03-030` carrying `energyOnSelf`'s exact sentence. That single hit is this slice's
whole story: without the sweep it arrives as five red assertions in four unowned files,
which is exactly what happened to D193. The both-Actives half found the empty pool the
other five slices did. The sweep is a test.

### Ordering: two witnesses that do not commute, three pinned absences

The additive fold runs **pre-W/R** on both members, witnessed with a multiplier because a
subtractive term commutes with the sum and would assert nothing:

- Fire attacker, 1 Energy, into a ×2-Fire 210 HP body: `(30 + 50) × 2 = 160`, where
  post-W/R reads `30 × 2 + 50 = 110`. Both under 210, so no KO truncates it.
- The both-Actives twin: `(30 + 2 × 30) × 2 = 180` versus `120` — and here the
  **defender's own Energy is inside the number its own Weakness then doubles**, a shape no
  other member of this family has.

**Pinned absences:**

- The `×` fold **cannot have an ordering witness**: it drops the printed base, so the sum
  has ONE term. Asserted through `DAMAGE_DEALT`'s own shape — `base: 0`, not the printed
  30 and not the folded 60, whole term in `scaled` — which is sharper than the arithmetic
  and is D193's result repeating for structural reasons.
- **"Read at DECLARATION" is unobservable for ENERGY.** The only mutation of the attacker
  between `let next = state` and the fold is the confusion self-damage, which rebuilds the
  body through `withActive` and carries `energy` across untouched — and on tails the
  attack returns at `ATTACK_FAILED` without reaching the fold. Pinned rather than faked.
- The **board-wide spelling of the attacker's own Energy** ("…attached to all of your
  Pokémon") is unprinted, so `energyOnSelf` carries `energyType` and no `zone`.

### Mirror witnesses — eight distinct answers on ONE board

    attacker's Active   3 Energy (2 × {R}, 1 × {W})
    attacker's Bench    5 bodies, the first holding 1 × {R}
    defender's Active   5 Energy
    defender's Bench    1 body holding 2 Energy

`energyOnSelf` untyped **3** · `energyOnSelf {R}` **2** · the attacker's whole side **4** ·
`energyOnOpponent` active **5** · `energyOnOpponent` board **7** ·
`bothActivesEnergyCount` **8** · `opponentBenchCount` **1** · `bothSidesBenchCount` **6**.

`8 ≠ 7` is load-bearing: `bothActives = self + oppActive` and `board = oppActive +
oppBench` coincide exactly when the attacker holds as much as the opponent's Bench.

### Mutants — 13 run, ONE real survivor, ONE equivalent

Each copies a neighbouring arm's real code. **M4 survived the first round and was a
genuine gap**: `countEnergyInPlay(state, attackerSeat, …)` — the board-zone call
`energyOnOpponent` really makes one line up in the same `switch`, and therefore the
mistake an author writing this mirror would actually make. It passed because the mirror
board left the attacker's Bench **bare**, making "the Active" and "the whole side" the
same 3. One `{R}` on `bench[0]` separates them in **both** readings at once (3 vs 4
untyped, 2 vs 3 filtered) and kills it.

**M2 is EQUIVALENT and is recorded rather than dropped**: reading
`state.players[attackerSeat].active` instead of the declaration snapshot is unobservable
for this member, for the confusion reason above. For `damageCountersOnSelf` the same
mutation is real and already witnessed elsewhere — which is why the arm still takes the
snapshot.

The other eleven died: the defender's Active (from `damageCountersOnOpponentActive`), the
type filter dropped, both halves of the both-Actives sum deleted in turn, its second half
moved to the board zone, the two nullish filter answers collapsed to `?? null`, the `more`
discriminator dropped, the `^` anchor dropped, an unread type capture added to the
both-Actives pattern, the both-Actives arm moved onto the MULTIPLY fold, and the self-side
tail widened to any body.

### Suites outside this slice that moved

- **`benchBodyScaling.test.ts` (D193's, not on this slice's owned list).** Its pinned
  absence for `bothActivesEnergyCount` is the one D193 wrote to be closed. It is flipped
  in place — the reader now returns the member, and the pin is **kept** to assert the part
  that is still an absence (ADD-only by legality, bare twin refused).
- **`scaledDamage` / `perEnergyFlip` / `log` / `checkup`.** The four witness files, moved
  per the plan. `perEnergyFlip`'s assertion **inverted and got stronger**: it used to say
  Entei's sentence is null on both the coin and damage readers, which is equally
  consistent with two dead readers; it now says **live on damage, dead on coin**, which is
  the disjointness that file is actually about.

### Fixtures and the census

Two synthetic bodies (`fix-selfenergy` indices 0-3, `fix-bothactives` indices 0-2) and one
deck (`SELF_ENERGY_DECK`). Synthetic because the catalog manifest **cannot be regenerated**
(`SQLITE_CANTOPEN`), so a real-card fixture could not be diffed against its printing;
`fix-*` ids are skipped by `catalogManifest.test.ts` by construction. Every string is the
catalog's, char for char, with its real printed base. Two of the seven indices are
**refusals that are real legal printings**, which is unusual and deliberate.

`SCALED_DAMAGE_DECK` is re-homed in place at exactly 60 cards: `sv01-068` ×4 and
`fix-lightning-energy` ×8 are paid for out of `fix-basic-1` and `fix-fire-energy` rather
than added on top. Entei stays.

⚠️ **`clauseApostrophe.test.ts` does NOT move: 78 → 78, and that is a RESULT rather than an
omission.** Not one of the four newly-readable sentences carries an apostrophe — "attached
to this Pokémon" and "attached to both Active Pokémon" name no possessive at all, which
makes this the first Energy-count slice to take no diff there. Both new fixtures' other
indices add none either: the sweep admits only sentences a reader RESOLVES, and all three
of those are refusals.

### Version and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`

Engine **0.126.0**, ascending block in `index.ts` and `package.json` in step.
`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 12**, derived: `DamageCountSource` is a PARSE-TIME type
produced from card text at declaration and consumed by `scaledAttackDamage` in the same
tick — no `GameState` field, no `PendingStage`, no `@luminous/schema` projection, no
redaction, and no new `EffectOp` (D189's stated bump condition — a parked program lives in
`GameState.phase`, and a count source can never). No widened signature this time. The
re-homing moves TEST scaffolding only; no saved record names a fixture id.

Suite: **+33 tests in 1 new file** (`selfEnergyScaling.test.ts`), plus 5 repaired
assertions across 5 suites and 1 added handover case in `scaledDamage.test.ts`. Repo:
**223 files / 4120 tests** at baseline `de402a3` → **224 files / 4161 tests** green at
commit (D198 landed three `apps/api` + `src/` commits in between, which is where the
other +7 come from).

⚠️ **ONE SUITE IS RED AT COMMIT AND IT IS NOT THIS SLICE'S.** A concurrent engine slice
has `registry.ts` and a new `legalNonAttackPrograms.test.ts` **uncommitted** in the shared
tree; 8 of its 43 tests fail and `biome` reports one `noThenProperty` error in the same
