## D226 — N's Plan, and the coupling that had never been observable

`sv10.5b-083`/`-163`/`-170` — *"Move up to 2 Energy from your Benched Pokémon to
your Active Pokémon."* **3 Standard-legal printings**, regulation mark I, all
three byte-identical (remote D1 `luminous`, 2026-08-05). **The last of D190's
four `DROPPED` work orders; that table is now EMPTY at 18 printings and 4-for-4
to the field.**

### The field, and why it is not a `route`

`moveEnergy.anySource?: true`. A `route` fixes WHICH ENDPOINTS are offered;
`anySource` fixes HOW MANY of the offered sources ONE ANSWER may draw from. N's
Plan is `benchToActive` **plus** the rider: the endpoints are Armarouge's, and
only the coupling differs. Folding it into `route` would have made a third value
that means "the same endpoints, a different answer shape", which is two facts in
one field.

A three-column `json_each` census of the whole remote D1 (3,786 rows) finds
**exactly one** multi-source move sentence and it is this card's. Every other
member of the family — 13 printings of *"from this Pokémon"*, Poppy's *"from 1 of
your Pokémon"*, Exp. Share's *"from that Pokémon"* — couples.

### Four rules this slice adds or re-confirms

1. 🛑 **A COUPLING THAT NO PRINTED CARD CAN VIOLATE IS AN UNTESTED COUPLING.**
   Armarouge is the only other `benchToActive` printing and it is `max: 1`: one
   pick has one source however the rule reads. **Poppy (`max: 2`, free route) is
   the only printing in the catalog that can express a two-source answer**, which
   is why it is the control on every board in `nsPlan.test.ts` — Energy Switch
   (`max: 1`) would have been refused first by the COUNT rule, for a different
   reason, and would have made a **vacuous** control that read exactly like a
   real one. **Before using a card as a negative control, check it can produce
   the answer you want refused.**
2. ⚠️ **A `needs` STRING PRICES A FIELD; A SLICE PAYS FOR ITS READ SITES — AND
   THE ONLY WAY TO KNOW THEM IS TO GREP.** This row was the first of the four
   written after that lesson, and it named the `validateChoice` arm and both HUD
   previews correctly. The grep still found a **third client read site** it had
   not named: `projection.ts`'s wire→engine prompt rebuild, whose own doc
   promises the round-trip reproduces `phaseViewOf`'s decision EXACTLY. Five read
   sites for a four-line field. **D225's advice paid for itself the first time it
   was followed.**
3. ⚠️ **RELAXING A RULE IS WHERE ITS NEIGHBOURS GET DELETED.** The "cannot move a
   Pokémon's Energy onto itself" test rode on the single `source` the coupling
   produced. The cheap edit — delete the coupling — takes it with it, and both
   mutants are killed rows. The right shape is to make the coupling CONDITIONAL
   and GENERALISE the neighbour: per pick, which under the coupling is the same
   test, so the pinned message never moves.
4. ⚠️ **A DIALOG STAGE IS A FILTER, NOT DECORATION.** Both `MoveEnergyDialog`s
   staged by source, and that stage narrows the Energy list to one host. Keeping
   it under the rider would have left the card's printed answer **unbuildable
   from the UI while the engine accepted it** — afford-then-reject in its
   quietest direction, because a picker that never offers the second host reports
   nothing at all. **When you widen what an answer may contain, look at what
   narrows the offer.**

### The event, and the version

`ENERGY_MOVED` is emitted **one row per source**, not widened. Its own doc
promises every `uids` entry came off the one `from`, and `log.ts` renders that
literally — so one row naming a single bench body for two cards would be a false
sentence in the game log. Two honest rows cost no event-shape change and no
consumer change. **`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 12**, and it is DRIVEN: the op
PARKS, so its prompt is embedded in the persisted `GameState.phase` (D140's 2→3
position), and the test drives **Poppy** — an op that sets no rider — asserting
the park's `Object.keys` and the wire prompt are byte-identical to the pre-slice
shape. A widening, not a missing required field.

### An empty table is a vacuous table

`registryOnlyPrograms.test.ts`'s `DROPPED` checks were all `for` loops, and a
`for` over `[]` passes for free. Emptying the table without pinning
`DROPPED.length === 0` (and `PAID` totalling 18) would have replaced a real guard
with a green nothing — the exact class `conventions.md` names.

### Mutation — 9 mutants, 9 killed (61 s)

`D226-validator-deletes-coupling` (the cheap relaxation), `-drops-self-move` (its
collateral), `-prompt-drops-rider`, `-redact-drops-rider`,
`-projection-drops-rider`, `-local-hud-keeps-source-stage`,
`-online-hud-keeps-source-stage` (one per read site — the theme of the slice),
`-note-hardcodes-article` (the pre-slice line verbatim), and
`-one-event-for-every-source` (the pre-slice `uids: [...moved]` copied into the
new loop, so every row claims the whole move).

### Suite

**Re-measured, never inherited**: `bun run check` green end to end — `tsc -b`,

vitest **249 files / 4606 tests** (from 248 / 4593: +1 file, +13 tests). engine
`0.142.0` → **0.143.0**, `packages/engine/package.json` in the same commit.


## D228 — the damage rider on a promoted body, and the channel that already existed

*"This attack does {N} damage to the new Active Pokémon."* — **8 Standard-legal
printings across five sentences**: four "Drag Off"-family gust riders
(`sv05-112`/`sv10-091` 30, `sv10.5b-027`/`-111` 20, `sv08-153`/`-214` 40,
`sv06-127` 70 — **7 legal**) plus Grimmsnarl `sv07-096`'s 160 behind a printed
*"If you do"* (**1 legal**). Census re-derived against the remote D1 `luminous`
(3,786 rows / 20 sets, 2,021 `legal_standard = 1`) over `json_each(attacks_json)`
with `GLOB`, 2026-08-05. **D227's split-out backlog row counted this family
exactly; what it got wrong was the mechanism.**

### The finding: a missing channel that was not missing

D227 priced the family as *"a second §8.5 hit against a body that is not the
captured defender … the §8.5 pipeline lives in `attack.ts`, in FRONT of the
interpreter, with no channel for a program to re-enter it"*, and left the open
question **"is the fold re-entered per promoted body, or does the interpreter
gain an op `attack.ts` resolves?"**

**Neither.** `snipeActive` (interpreter.ts) has run the whole §8.5 pipeline from
INSIDE a program since D96 — Hail Blade's `damageDefender` routes into it — and it
addresses its target as `activeTop(state, otherSeat(ctx.seat))`, read off the
LIVE state at the moment the op runs. A body promoted by an earlier op in the
same program **is** that body, so *"the new Active Pokémon"* needs no addressing
machinery: Weakness, Resistance, the attacker's pre-W/R bonus and debuff, the
reduction passives, the §11 blocks and the §8.1 KO-survival clamp all arrive
unchanged.

⚠️ **The transferable rule: a price that names a MISSING CHANNEL must be checked
against the ops that already cross it.** D227's grep found the fold (in
`attack.ts`) and not its re-entry points (the interpreter's four damage sites),
and priced a slice at a new pipeline that was one union member.

### Why a second op rather than a widened `damageDefender`

D131's widen-don't-add test — *"is everything downstream of the field
byte-identical?"* — answers **YES** here (the same `snipeActive` call) and the
answer is still ADD, because the test has an **upstream** side. `attack.ts` reads
the op list BEFORE the program runs and DROPS the printed base when it finds a
`damageDefender` (`programDamage`), on the ground that Hail Blade's printed "60×"
IS the per-unit the op deals back. This clause is an **additional** number aimed
at a body the main hit never touched, so a printing carrying both would owe both.

All 8 printings print **no base damage at all** (every `damage` field absent —
measured), so `base` is 0 on every reachable board and the two readings agree.
Written from the rule rather than from what a test would notice (D130's
`programPerHeads` precedent) and recorded as a declared `unreachable-population`
mutant rather than tested around.

### The two printed shapes are two programs

| sentence | program | empty opponent Bench |
|---|---|---|
| `Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot. This attack does {N} damage to the new Active Pokémon.` | `[{gust}, {damageNewActive}]` | gust whiffs (§8.6), **damage lands on the unchanged Active** |
| `Switch out your opponent's Active Pokémon to the Bench. (…) If you do, this attack does {N} damage to the new Active Pokémon.` | `[{opponentSwitchOut, recordAs:"moved"}, {recordGate, slot:"moved", then:[{damageNewActive}]}]` | switch whiffs, slot empty, **nothing at all** |

On any board with a Bench to promote from the two are indistinguishable, which is
why the empty-Bench pair (same seed, same attacker, two indices) is the spine of
the suite. Merging them in either direction is a live mutant.

`opponentSwitchOut` grew the `recordAs` its own doc deferred *"until a printing
asks"* — at **both** arms. The RESUMED arm is the one a real Grimmsnarl board
takes (the opponent picks whenever they hold ≥2 benched bodies), so an omission
there empties the slot on exactly the boards the conditional is interesting on.

### Two provenance findings

🛑 **D227's Grimmsnarl fixture carried an invented `damage: 130`**, under a
comment reading *"Its printed 130 is the card's own base damage"*. `sv07-096`
prints no damage field (its 160 base belongs to the card's OTHER attack,
"Knuckle Sandwich"), and a green sibling case read that number as evidence *"the
attack works"*. ⚠️ **The provenance comment said "char-for-char" and meant the
EFFECT STRING** — the numeric fields beside it were never in the claim's scope,
which is how a fabricated byte survives a provenance note. **When a fixture names
a real printing, assert the fields it does NOT carry as well as the ones it does.**

⚠️ **Neither new anchor has a catalog witness for its own `$`.** Every printed
sentence that extends them joins at *"If you do"*, which fails the anchor on its
own bytes long before a tail matters — so the dropped-`$` mutant **survived** the
harness until a constructed tail (`… Draw a card.`) was added. The construction is
labelled as such in the suite rather than passed off as a census row.

### Mutation — 9 mutants, 8 killed, 1 declared survivor (30 s)

## D229 — the attacker's own Energy onto its own Bench, and an edit estimate that over-priced

*"Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon."* (**8 legal**),
*"Move 3 Energy …"* (**3**), *"Move a Basic Energy …"* (**2**) — **13
Standard-legal printings for TWO anchors and ONE `route` value.** Row 5 of
`coverage-backlog-legal.md`, and the **first derived arms the `moveEnergy` family
has ever had**: every printing before this one is a registry row (Energy Switch,
Poppy, Armarouge, Exp. Share, N's Plan), so the op had never had to survive a text
parser.

Census re-derived (never inherited) against the remote D1 `luminous` — 3,786 rows
/ 20 sets, 2,021 `legal_standard = 1` — on 2026-08-05 over `json_each(attacks_json)`
+ `json_extract(value,'$.effect')` with `GLOB`, swept over **all three text
columns**.

### The slice this session was handed, and why it moved

The resume point asked for the Samurott `sv10.5w-023`/`-107` ABILITY twin (2 legal)
**and** the `programPlayable` arm D227 declined to write speculatively — *"price it
against its read sites, and fall back to backlog row 5 if the arm turns out free."*

**The arm is free, and the measurement is three assertions rather than a
paragraph.** The Ability's program is `switchActive {recordAs: "moved"}` →
`recordGate {slot: "moved", then: [opponentSwitchOut]}`:

* `programPlayable` descends into **`coinFlipGate.then` and nothing else** — the
  argument for that descent is ruling/906's *"the flip is PROCEDURE, not effect"*,
  which a §9.2 record gate does not share (`switchActive`'s own comment already
  says the gate stays off the consequent, for Giovanni). So `opponentSwitchOut` is
  **never at top level** on any printing in the pool.
* The compound's **ANTECEDENT** is a `switchActive` the gate already refuses when
  the controller's Bench is empty — which is also the printed behaviour, since the
  consequent is gated on the antecedent having happened.
* **Both HUD row-lighting mirrors are therefore unaffected**, because they call the
  same predicate with the same arguments (`redact.ts`, `GameHud.tsx` line 245).

So the twin is 1 registry object for 2 legal printings and **zero engine code**,
and the arm stays unwritten: *a gate no printing reaches is a vacuous guard*. The
finding is pinned in `derivedSelfEnergyMove.test.ts` ("✅ NO NEW `programPlayable`
ARM WAS OWED"), including the positive case a speculative arm would have BROKEN —
Samurott with an own Bench and an EMPTY opponent Bench is still playable, because
the card does the first half of what it prints.

### 🛑 The finding: an edit estimate is a claim exactly as a count is

Row 5 read **"19 legal unbuilt printings · ~7 arms + 1 route value"**. Both halves
are wrong, and — for the first time on this page — in the **expensive** direction.

| Row 5 said | Measured |
|---|---|
| 19 legal printings | **16**, over five sentences. The 19 has no population behind it; a three-column sweep also returns **zero** ability and **zero** Trainer rows, so the whole family is attack text |
| ~7 arms | **2 anchors.** The numeric and article forms are ONE alternation (`ATTACK_DRAW`'s precedent — the absent capture group IS `max: 1`), and the two *"Move **all** Energy …"* sentences (3 legal) are not arms at all |
| "mirror of the built `benchToActive` route" | ✅ **exact** — and it is the whole implementation |

This branch has now re-derived four `needs` cells that under-priced (D199, D221,
D227, D228) and one that over-priced. **The rule is the same in both directions:
re-derive the `needs` column, not just the ids and counts** — and now, explicitly,
*write the anchors out before believing an arm count*.

`selfToBench` is `benchToActive` read backwards: sources are the attacker,
destinations are that seat's whole Bench, `needed: 1` (source and destination are

⚠️ **Its sources are THE ACTIVE and not `sourceRef`, and that is a claim about the

## D230 — the deck search onto your own Bench, and nine "arms" that were nine NOUNS

**Backlog row 6**, `coverage-backlog-legal.md`, priced at **22 legal printings /
~9 arms**. Re-derived and grouped BY SENTENCE before a line was written — which
is exactly what D229's resume point asked for — it is **25 legal printings over
12 distinct sentences for ONE anchor**.

```
Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench.
  Then, shuffle your deck.                                              7 legal
…up to 2 Basic Pokémon…                                                 7 legal
…up to 3 Basic Pokémon…                                                 2 legal
…up to 3 Charjabug… / …up to 2 Grubbin… / …up to 2 Froakie… / …a Pikachu… 4 legal
                                                            ─────────────────────
                                             20 legal printings, ONE anchor
```

`searchDeck {filter, dest:"bench", max}` + `shuffleDeck` — **Nest Ball's program,
byte for byte**, authored in the registry since M4. No new op, no new op field, no
new `CardFilter` member, and **no `interpreter.ts` / `registry.ts` / wire / schema
/ client / api diff at all**. The whole slice is a regex and an arm.

### 🛑 The finding: nine "arms" were nine NOUNS

The row's `~9 arms` counted the DISTINCT SENTENCES in its census and called each
one an edit. Grouped by sentence, all nine are **the same sentence**:

```
Search your deck for <QTY> <NOUN> and put <it|them> onto your Bench.
  Then, shuffle your deck.
```

`<QTY>` is the article or `up to N`; `<NOUN>` is `Basic Pokémon` or a name. So the
noun is two capture groups and the number is a third, and the article branch's
absent group **is** `max: 1` — `ATTACK_DRAW`'s reading for the third slice
running (D202, D229, here).

This is the **fifth** `needs` cell on this branch to misprice and the **second in
a row** to miss in both directions at once. The transferable form has not changed
since D229 wrote it: *write the anchors out before believing an arm count* — and
now also: **group the census by sentence first, because an arm count is a count of
SENTENCE SHAPES and not of strings.**

### ⚠️ And 25 was the SECOND figure this slice measured

The first sweep returned **24** and used `GLOB '*Search your deck*'` — CASE-
SENSITIVE on the opening verb — so it structurally could not see Lillie's Comfey
`sv09-068`, whose sentence begins *"**You may** search…"*. Nothing in the prose
caught it. What caught it was the **arithmetic row in `derivedBenchSearch.test.ts`
going red on its own author**: `20 read + 2 built + 1 disjunction + 1 §4 licence +
1 §9.2 tail` is 25, and the row said 24.

**A case-sensitive `GLOB` is a floor exactly as a single-column sweep is.** D200
learned the opposite failure (`LIKE` too WIDE: 95 rows where the truth was 6);
this is the same lesson from the narrow side. The durable repair is not "use a
different predicate" — it is that **a census written as an assertion can go red
and a census written as a paragraph cannot.**

### Both read sites the row named priced at ZERO — measured, not argued

D229's resume point asked for two things to be priced as read sites. Both came
out at zero engine code, and both are pinned as assertions rather than prose:

* **`programPlayable` owes no bench-space arm.** A deck search is *"playable
  enough"* because the deck is not public knowledge (Compendium ruling/284), and
  the bench-space question is already answered ONE LEVEL DOWN — the interpreter's
  `Math.min(op.max, benchSpace(state, ctx.seat))` clamps before anything leaves
  the deck, and `searchMove` clamps again on the way out. The suite drives a
  program with a **FULL Bench** as playable, beside a `gust` on an empty opponent
  Bench that is **not** — so the claim can go red in both directions.
* **Nothing in this family is a played Ability.** The three-column sweep returns
  exactly ONE ability row — Koffing `sv10-125`, a §9 TRIGGER over
  *"Pokémon that have \"Koffing\" in their name"*, a noun no `CardFilter` spells
  — and five TRAINER rows. A triggered program is never played, so the gate is not
  on the path at all. Pinned as a `FIXTURE_POOL` sweep that would go red the day a
  fixture prints the sentence as an Ability.

`preventBlock.test.ts`'s §11 table **did** go red for `searchDeck`/`shuffleDeck`,
exactly as the row predicted — **D181's shape for the fifth time**: an op the
Trainer path has run since M4 owes a §11 verdict the moment the DERIVER can emit
it. Both `untouched` (the only zones either op reaches are the actor's own deck
and own Bench), both driven, and both carrying `switchActive`'s disclaimer that
the SEAT is what that table does not cover.

### The noun is two captures and neither is a wildcard

D229's near miss was a real catalog row but **0 legal**. This family's are worse
and better at once — **three are legal and two are already BUILT**:

| printed noun | legal | why the anchor must refuse it |
|---|---:|---|
| `Basic Steven's Pokémon` (`sv10-083`) | 1 | owner subgroup — **registry-authored** |
| `Basic Lillie's Pokémon` (`sv09-068`) | 1 | owner subgroup + *"You may"* — **registry-authored** |
| `in any combination of Maushold and Maushold ex` (`sv08-158`) | 1 | a DISJUNCTION of two names |
| `Basic {G} Pokémon` | 0 | a TYPE filter — D229's `{D}` sibling one op over |
| `Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less` | 3 | an HP predicate (TRAINERS) |

🛑 **The two registry-authored rows are the sharp ones**, because `programFor`
wins over the deriver: a `(.+)` noun would have been **invisible on exactly the
two cards it was wrong about**, and would have fired on the next owner-prefixed
printing that arrived without a row — searching for *any* Basic Pokémon where the
card names a family. The literal alternative is therefore its own capture group so
the dispatch **never reads the matched text** (`DAMAGE_SUPPRESSION`'s rule), and
the NAME group is a **single capitalised word**: a hyphenated, spaced or
apostrophised name falls through to the loud `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` path rather
than being approximated.

Note why `sv08-158` is printed as a disjunction at all: **`byName` is exact in
paper too**. "Maushold ex" is a different card name from "Maushold", and the card
says so in so many words — which is corroboration for the filter's semantics from
outside the engine.

### What is deferred, and it is not this sentence

* **`sv06-009` Volbeat "Quick Sign"** (1 legal) — *"If you go first, you can use
  this attack during your first turn."* in front of the sentence. That is

D227, D228 and D229 each had to CONSTRUCT their `^`/`$` case — no printed member

`fix-charjabug` is the only body in `FIXTURE_POOL` whose `name` is a printed

## D369 — the CROSS-BOARD Pokémon Tool clause, and the EMPTY-SET BOUNDARY that is neither a shape nor a price (engine 0.273.0 → **0.274.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

⚠️ **THIS FILE HAS BEEN STALE SINCE D230**, and D369 is the first section added to
it in well over a hundred decisions. Everything between lives in
`docs/progress.md`'s session log (see the note at the foot of `decisions.md`). This
section exists because what it records is a **rule about the vocabulary**, which is
this file's subject rather than that one's.

### The member

`opponentActiveHasToolAttached` — *"If your opponent's Active Pokémon has a Pokémon
Tool attached, this attack does 80 more damage."*, **2 legal printings** in the
committed `legal_standard = 1` attack column. The cross-board twin of D122's
`yourActiveHasToolAttached`: the same `tools.length > 0` read on
`otherSeat(seat)`'s Active, `> 0` and never `=== 1` (§7.4's cap is an ATTACH gate
and Revavroom ex `sv03-156`'s "Tune-Up" raises it to 4), FALSE with an empty Active
Spot.

**A second flat member, not a `seat` field on the first.** The union is seat-NAMED
throughout — `yourActiveDamaged`/`opponentActiveDamaged`,
`yourActivePoisoned`/`opponentActivePoisoned`, and now this pair — and
parameterising a shipped member is a **RENAME**, priced by D362 at 31 sites across
7 files against 4 for the addition. **A WIDENING IS FREE; A RENAME IS NOT.**

**Its `conditionNote` is byte-identical to its clause KEY**, which the twin cannot
manage: the twin's printed subject is *"this Pokémon"* and D116 makes resolving that
pronoun the clause table's job. So the round trip
`If ${conditionNote(cond)}, this attack does N more damage.` re-derives to the same
member in ONE step — a property of this row, not of the family, and asserted as such.

### THE RULE THIS SLICE ADDS — three questions, not two

D368 established that a **SHAPE** question (*can this table hold it at all?*) is
cheaper than a **PRICE** question (*is it worth buying?*) and must go first. D369
adds a third, and it sits after both:

> **A SHAPE ASKS WHETHER THE TABLE CAN HOLD IT.
> A PRICE ASKS WHETHER IT IS WORTH BUYING.
> A BOUNDARY ASKS WHAT THE ROW WOULD *MEAN*.
> THE THIRD CAN FAIL WITH THE FIRST TWO BOTH GREEN.**

The candidate that produced it: *"all of your Benched Pokémon have at least 1 damage
counter on them"* (2 printings). Its shape is **fine** — a universal over the Bench
is a `(state, seat)` fact, and `noEnergyOnYourPokemon` has been a universal over the
in-play set since D111. Its price is the same 2.0 as everything else in the band. It
is blocked on what an **EMPTY BENCH** means, and that is worth **120 damage on a
board reached every game**.

**Both instruments that could settle it were run, and both came back empty:**

1. **The catalog.** The whole 640-sentence legal attack column prints **exactly ONE**
   universally-quantified antecedent. D368 settled its shape question by finding the
   same clause printed on two costs; there is no second printing here to compare
   against — no rider, no sibling amount, nothing.
2. **The union's own precedent** — and the reason it does not transfer is sharper
   than "the precedent is split". **Every empty-population member that reads FALSE is
   an EXISTENTIAL**, where falsity is FORCED by logic and no convention was ever
   chosen. The one prior **UNIVERSAL** (`noEnergyOnYourPokemon`) reads vacuously TRUE
   — on a board **§4 makes unreachable**, because a player always has an Active.
   **THE ONE PRECEDENT WITH THE RIGHT SHAPE WAS SET WHERE IT COULD NOT BE WRONG**, so
   it is a habit rather than a warrant.

So the row is **deferred with the question named**, per D190b/D199 — *a
wrong-but-plausible program is strictly worse than an unbuilt one* — and pinned two
ways: a tripwire in `opponentToolBonus.test.ts` §2 that fires the day a row is added
for it, and a mutant (`D369-deferred-universal-gets-the-existential-row`) that
installs the row a hurried slice would actually write, mapping the universal onto the
**existential** member whose printed nouns nearly match.

### Two corrections to inherited claims

- **A near-miss guard had asserted the wrong side.** `toolClause.test.ts` carried
  the cross-board rewrite in its list of CONSTRUCTED near-misses, annotated *"The
  pool does not print it, and if it ever does it is a different member reading the
  other board — not this row."* The pool prints it **twice**, and has since the
  corpus was committed at D274. The first half was false the day it was written; the
  second half was this slice's specification. **D136's finding a third time: a suite
  written by the session that wrote the code inherits its blind spot.**
- **The twin's own printing is not Standard-legal.** Greedent `sv01-152` "Enhanced
  Fang" — the card D122 was built for — has **zero** legal printings today. D122's
  row survives on a **different AMOUNT of the same clause** (*"40 more damage"*, 2
  legal printings), which it serves for free because the amount is captured by the
  **skeleton** and never by the row. **A ROW KEYED ON THE CLAUSE OUTLIVES THE
  PRINTING THAT MOTIVATED IT; A ROW KEYED ON THE SENTENCE WOULD NOT HAVE**, and this
  is the practical cash value of D187's "an arm transfers across sets".

### The tie-break set, re-derived

D368's handoff named *"the two largest remaining candidates"* at 2 printings each.
Measured over the same instrument, the residue's 2-printing band holds **NINE**
distinct clauses. After D369 the residue is **32 sentences / 42 printings** and the
band is **eight**, named and pinned in `opponentToolBonus.test.ts` §1 so the next
slice inherits the tie-break measured rather than re-running it. **THE QUESTION WAS
NEVER "2.0 VERSUS 2.0" — IT WAS WHICH OF NINE 2.0s COSTS LEAST TO GET RIGHT.**

### An environment constraint, recorded

This session's container had **no D1 credentials** (`wrangler d1 execute` reports
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` unset) and no local sqlite copy of the catalog. Every
id-level measurement the recent slices made off remote D1 was therefore
**unavailable**, and none was guessed. `censusAttackCorpus.ts` (the committed
`legal_standard = 1` attack column: 640 sentences / 1,732 printings / 60,467
characters) plus the live derivations in `censusAtHead.test.ts` carried the whole
measurement instead. **A READER IS KEYED ON THE PRINTED SENTENCE, so this slice was
buildable without the database — a REGISTRY ROW, keyed by card id, would not have
been.** That asymmetry is worth remembering the next time the database is
unreachable: it decides what kind of slice is available, not whether any is.


## D370 — the BENCH-SCOPED TYPE clause, and the check that must run before the price (engine 0.274.0 → **0.275.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

`yourBenchHasType { type }` — **1** new `BoardCondition` member, **2** reader arms,
**1** new anchored pattern (`YOUR_BENCH_TYPE_CLAUSE`), and **zero** new vocabulary,
maps, clause-table rows, ops, events, error codes, registry rows, state fields,
prompt kinds, choice kinds or `packages/schema` bytes. It serves *"If you have any
{M} Pokémon on your Bench, this attack does 80 more damage."*, **2 legal
printings**, and the other ten types the day one is printed.

### 1. The VOCABULARY check is cheap, and it is the one that decides whether a clause is buildable at all

D369 ordered it ahead of the build and it takes one line:
`POKEMON_TYPE_BY_CODE["M"]` is `"Metal"`, a real `Card.types` value. **The sentence
one token over fails the same check.** *"You have any **Tera** Pokémon on your
Bench"* is in the corpus at 1 legal printing, and `Tera` is not a `Card.types` value
anywhere — D207 measured every occurrence of that banner as DEMAND with the SUPPLY
side absent.

🛑 **SO THE SAME TEMPLATE MUST BUY THE ONE AND REFUSE THE OTHER, AND WHERE IT
REFUSES IS A DESIGN DECISION.** The capture is deliberately loose (`(.+)`), so the
pattern MATCHES the trap sentence and the lookup misses — the clause falls through
to null and stays on the loud `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` path. A
`(Grass|Fire|Water|…)` alternation would refuse it at the anchor instead: the same
answer today, and a hand-kept list that rots the day a type is added to the schema.
**THE MAP IS THE VOCABULARY, NOT THE REGEX** — which is `CLAUSE_ENERGY_TOKENS`'
rule from D118, and now the third clause in the family to follow it.

### 2. Two members can be adjacent to a third without either being widenable into it

D199 says re-derive the `needs` column. Two of the union's 33 members come close:

* `opponentActiveHasType` reads the same **FIELD** on the wrong body.
* `yourBenchHasNamed` reads the same **ZONE** on the wrong **FIELD**.

Neither widens. The first is a **RENAME** — two required fields added to a shipped
member with live authors, priced by D362 at 31 sites across 7 files — and its second
axis does not merely change the subject: **an Active Spot holds ONE body and a Bench
holds a VARIABLE-SIZE SET, so the predicate stops being a lookup and becomes a
quantifier.** The second is a category error: `name` is an OPEN vocabulary matched
exactly against the catalog, `types` is CLOSED at eleven schema-pinned values, and a
member taking either would have to decide which field an arbitrary string means —
turning the free `Tera` rejection into a name lookup that silently succeeds against
nothing.

**A MEMBER THAT IS THE PRODUCT OF TWO EXISTING ONES IS NOT A WIDENING OF EITHER.**

### 3. The narrow ZONE is worth the whole bonus, and the fixture is what proves it

Both legal printings of this sentence are on **METAL attackers**. So an
`[side.active, ...side.bench]` reading — the spread `yourNamedPokemonInPlay`
legitimately uses for a clause printed *"in play"* — would let the attacker satisfy
its own clause off its own type and turn a conditional **+80** into an
**unconditional** one on every board the card ever reaches. It is D279's Falinks
refutation with a TYPE where that one had a NAME.

⚠️ **AND IT IS ONLY REFUTABLE ON A BOARD IF THE FIXTURE IS BUILT FOR IT.**
`fix-benchtype` is deliberately `types: ["Metal"]`; a Colorless attacker would
answer identically under both readings and the whole file would have proved nothing.
Same principle one axis over: `fix-dualbody` is `["Water", "Metal"]`, because
**every single-typed body in the catalog scores identically under `.includes` and
under an equality on `types[0]`** — one board separates them and it has to be built.

### 4. A WIDENING can falsify a comment in a file it does not touch

`conditionNote`'s `opponentActiveHasType` arm said the note *"round-trips to the
printed clause … the type word is the same token the sentence carried in"*. That was
true when it was written. **D367's token-map widening falsified it three slices
later**, from a different file: `{P}` and `{D}` are printed on 3 legal printings and
the note answers "Psychic" / "Darkness". The right answer — a brace code is a
card-face glyph and a tooltip is prose (D118) — with a claim about it that had
quietly stopped being true.

🛑 **WHEN YOU WIDEN A VOCABULARY, GREP THE SITES THAT *DESCRIBE* IT, NOT ONLY THE
ONES THAT USE IT.** The using sites are found by the compiler; the describing ones
are found by nobody.

D370's own note has the corrected form of the property: it does **not** round-trip
to the printed bytes (it spells `Metal`, not `{M}`) and it **does** round-trip to
the same **MEMBER**, through the map's spelled-out half. That is the stronger claim
and it is the one this family only gained at D367.

### 5. Two guessed figures went red before they were trusted, and one of them found a slice

The suite was written with two numbers nobody measured: the sentence's byte length
(**78 guessed, 75 measured**) and the count of brace-coded printings under the
sibling template (**3 guessed, 5 measured**). Both reddened on the first run.

The second is the interesting one. The extra two printings are *"If your opponent's
Active Pokémon is a {N} Pokémon, it is now Paralyzed."* — **2 legal printings**,
refused by all nine readers, whose **ANTECEDENT** costs zero new vocabulary
(`OPPONENT_ACTIVE_TYPE_CLAUSE` has read it since D120; `{N}` → `Dragon` since D234)
and whose **CONSEQUENT** no skeleton in this family spells. **THE CONSEQUENT WAS NOT
PRICED**, and that is recorded rather than implied.

**A GUESS THAT GOES RED IS CHEAPER THAN A GUESS THAT GOES GREEN, AND A WIDENED
QUERY IS THE CHEAPEST PLACE TO FIND THE NEXT SLICE.**

### 6. A claim without a plausible mutant is DECLARED, not faked

Six mutation rows, one per claim: the ZONE (C1), the SEAT (C2), `.includes` over an
array (C3), the vocabulary map (C4 — the neighbouring branch's REAL code, which
agrees with the right one on `{M}` and disagrees on `{C}`, `{N}` and `"Special"`),
the NOTE (C5), and the `Tera` tripwire (C6). All six killed.

⚠️ A **SEVENTH** claim is driven and has **no row**: "the identity is the stack TOP
(§1.2)". The realistic wrong code — `cardOfUid(state, p.stack[0])` — needs an import
`interpreter.ts` does not carry, so it is **not a slip this file's author could make
in one edit**, and a mutant that added the import would be testing the harness
rather than the guard. Recorded in `mutants.ts` beside the six, so the absence is a
statement rather than an oversight.

## D371 — the OPPONENT-RESISTANCE clause: the same COLUMN the engine already read, asked a different question (engine 0.275.0 → **0.276.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

`opponentActiveHasResistance { type }` — **1** new `BoardCondition` member, **2**
reader arms, **1** new anchored pattern (`OPPONENT_ACTIVE_RESISTANCE_CLAUSE`), and
**zero** new vocabulary, maps, clause-table rows, ops, events, error codes, registry
rows, state fields, prompt kinds, choice kinds or `packages/schema` bytes. It serves
*"If your opponent's Active Pokémon has {F} Resistance, this attack does 50 more
damage."*, **2 legal printings**, and the other ten types the day one is printed.

### 1. THE SUPPLY CHECK IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE VOCABULARY CHECK, AND THIS SLICE OWED THE FIRST

D370 owed the vocabulary question (*"is the captured token a real `Card.types`
value?"*) and answered it. D371 owed D207's other one: **name the FIELD before you
design the predicate.** A predicate over a banner no column CLASSIFIES yields a
permanently empty candidate set and a card that can never be played — `Tera`'s
shape, where every occurrence is DEMAND and the SUPPLY side is absent.

✅ `Card.resistances` is a real ingested column (`{type, value?}[] | null`,
`packages/schema/src/catalog/card.ts`), populated, and read by the §8.5 pipeline
since 0.1.x. So this is **not** that shape.

⚠️ **AND THE ONLY POPULATION THIS CONTAINER CAN MEASURE IS A FLOOR ON A BIASED
SAMPLE.** `FIXTURE_POOL` held **24 of 444** bodies with a Resistance, **16** of them
Fighting, before this slice's fixtures landed. That is evidence the field is
populated; it is **not a denominator**. There are no D1 credentials here, so the
Standard-legal count is **UNMEASURED**, and a guessed figure would be worth less
than the absence (D183: a count with no population is a floor). Said, not promoted.

### 2. 🛑 THE SAME FIELD CAN ALREADY BE READ BY THE ENGINE AND STILL NEED A NEW MEMBER — BECAUSE THE QUESTION IS DIFFERENT

This is the slice's finding, and it is the one to carry forward.

`resistanceOf(attacker, defender)` (cards.ts) has read `Card.resistances` since the
engine's first weeks. It delegates to `weakResModifier`, which **skips every entry
whose `type` is not one of the ATTACKER's types**, because §8.5 asks *"does this
Resistance apply to THIS attack"*. The printed clause asks whether the defender
**HAS** `{F}` Resistance, **whoever is attacking**.

**THE SAME FIELD, TWO QUESTIONS.** So the member reads the column directly and is
deliberately NOT routed through the helper — and the difference is not arguable, it
is a board:

| board | clause | `resistanceOf` | dealt |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Metal** attacker vs Fighting-resistant defender | TRUE | **null** | 10 + 50 = **60** |
| **Fighting** attacker vs the same defender | TRUE | −30 | 10 + 50 − 30 = **30** |

The first row is the whole separation: a member routed through the helper pays
**10** there. `fix-oppresist` is Metal for exactly that reason and `fix-oppresist-f`
is the same attack on a Fighting body so the agreement case is driven too — without
it, "does not go through `resistanceOf`" would only ever be shown where the helper
is null, and a member that answered TRUE unconditionally would pass.

🛑 **BEFORE ADDING A MEMBER THAT READS A FIELD, GREP FOR WHAT ALREADY READS IT AND
ASK WHAT QUESTION THAT READER IS ASKING.** "The engine already reads this" is not
the same as "the engine already answers this", and the gap between them is where a
silent narrowing lives.

### 3. A predicate on `{type, value?}` reads `type` ALONE, and §8.5 says so in its own code

`WeakRes.value` is `z.string().optional()`. `weakResModifier` matches on `type`
**first** and only then parses `value` — falling back to the modern-era −30 when the
parse fails. **An entry the pipeline cannot PRICE is an entry it still HONOURS.** So
a predicate that also required a printed `value` would make a card with a garbled or
absent Resistance value stop *having* one, which no printed sentence says.

`fix-dualresist` is built for this and for the array reading at once:
`[{ type: "Grass", value: "-30" }, { type: "Fighting" }]` — the match is **SECOND**
(so `resistances[0]` misses it) and carries **no value** (so a `value`-requiring
predicate misses it too). One body, two readings separated.

### 4. The WEAKNESS column is one field over, and this repo has already made that mistake twice

`weaknesses` and `resistances` are the same shape in the same schema on adjacent
lines, and D173's Klefki and D175's Spiritomb both had their `types` transcribed out
of the wrong one. So `fix-fightweak` prints **Fighting Weakness and NO Resistance**:
an arm reading the wrong column flips there and nowhere else in the file.

⚠️ **AND THAT FALSE NEEDED AN ATTRIBUTION CONTROL** (D214). "The clause is false on
`fix-fightweak`" proves nothing if that fixture's weakness column were unreadable —
the board would answer the same under a broken schema. So a **Fighting** attacker
into the same body is driven: 10 × 2 = **20**, clause still false. Same body, same
column, opposite answer.

### 5. The apostrophe class is load-bearing on THIS template and was not on the last one

D136 gave the anchored patterns a `['’]` class so a catalog re-ingest normalising
punctuation could not silently un-derive their sentences. `YOUR_BENCH_TYPE_CLAUSE`
(D370) needed none — its sentence spells no apostrophe at all. This one does, and
the template pass is handed the **RAW** clause on purpose (`literalClauseRow`'s fold
is for TABLE keys), so the class in the pattern's own source is the **only**
mechanism on this path. It has a mutant row of its own, and that row is **green
against today's catalog** (0 of 978 rows carry U+2019) — which is what standing
insurance looks like.

### 6. Seven mutation rows, one per claim, and one claim DECLARED without a row

C1 the §8.5 routing, C2 the weakness column, C3 the seat, C4 `.some` over the array,
C5 the `value` half, C6 the vocabulary map, C7 the apostrophe class.

⚠️ **C1 IS A ONE-EDIT SLIP HERE IN A WAY D370's SEVENTH CLAIM WAS NOT.**
`resistanceOf` and `weaknessOf` are **already imported** by `interpreter.ts`, so
"reuse the helper we already have" costs an author nothing. D370's stack-top mutant
needed an import the file did not carry and was therefore declared rather than
written; this slice's equivalent — reading the stack BOTTOM — is declared for the
same reason, because `activeTop` is the only accessor the arm has.

**THE TEST FOR WHETHER A CLAIM DESERVES A ROW IS WHETHER THE WRONG CODE IS ONE EDIT
AWAY, AND THAT TEST IS ANSWERED BY THE FILE'S IMPORT BLOCK.**

## D374 — the FIRST printed CARD NAME read off an ATTACHED card, and D207's supply question asked of a candidate that was expected to FAIL it (engine 0.278.0 → **0.279.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

**Clause:** *"If this Pokémon has any Team Rocket's Energy attached, this attack does 60
more damage."* — Team Rocket's Zapdos `sv10-070` "Wicked Thunder", **1 sentence / 2 legal
printings**. D373's handoff, taken.

**Ships:** `yourActiveHasNamedEnergyAttached` (`name: string`), 1 LITERAL
`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, 2 reader arms, 1 new import (`cardOfUid` into
`interpreter.ts`). Zero new maps, templates, patterns, ops or events.

### D207's SUPPLY question — asked FIRST, and it PASSES

D373 flagged this candidate as **the first in the run that could actually fail D207's
supply question**, and budgeted a refusal for it. It does not fail. The chain is
`InPlayPokemon.energy` (uids) → `state.cardIdByUid` → `state.cardPool` → `Card.name`, an
INGESTED column `matchesFilter`'s `byName` member has read since M4. `FIXTURE_POOL` has
held a real `Team Rocket's Energy` since **D242** (`fix-tr-energy`), put there as the near
miss `ownerPokemon`'s `category === "Pokemon"` conjunct exists to refuse — so the fixture
cost of the supply half was **zero**, and `trEnergyBonus.test.ts` §2 reads the name back
off a live board rather than off the fixture table.

**The rule to carry forward:** D207's failure mode is a predicate over a **banner no
column CLASSIFIES** (`Tera` — 22 rows, every occurrence DEMAND; `Ancient`/`Future` the
same). A predicate over a **FIELD** is a different animal, however exotic the value looks.
Ask which one you have before pricing anything.

### The SHAPE question: ONE CARD NAME, not the `Team Rocket's ` prefix family

*"Team Rocket's Pokémon"* genuinely is a prefix family — `CardFilter.ownerPokemon` (D242)
and `yourPokemonKoedOnOpponentsLastTurn.owner` (D326) both exist for owner prefixes — so
the same three words in front of *Energy* read as a family at first glance.

**They are not one.** Exactly ONE Energy card carries the prefix: `Team Rocket's Energy`
`sv10-182`, reprinted `me2pt5-217`. ⚠️ The catalog could not answer this (no D1
credentials); it was answered on the **WEB**, D373's instrument — official card database,
Bulbapedia, the set lists — and the engine's own `cards.ts` already recorded the card by
id as `ownerPokemon`'s near miss.

**So the two readings are EXTENSIONALLY IDENTICAL on today's pool, and the choice is
about tomorrow.** It goes D373's way on D373's tie-break: a name equality never
over-serves, a prefix reading would silently pay +60 for a card the sentence may not name,
and an engine that must guess guesses toward not paying. **The falsifier is named** — a
printed `Team Rocket's ⟨X⟩ Energy`, or a ruling reading the clause as the family — and the
remedy is one member field and one arm.

✅ **AND IT CARRIES AN ATTRIBUTION CONTROL** (D214): the prefix reading is computed BESIDE
the member on every board the suite builds. They agree on seven real-pool attachments and
differ on exactly one — an **invented** `Team Rocket's Fix Energy`. A shape choice whose
only separating board holds a card nobody printed still has to be SHOWN.

### Why it is a LITERAL row and not a template (D118, read from the wrong end)

`SELF_ENERGY_ATTACHED_CLAUSE` — `^this Pokémon has any (.+) Energy attached$` — **already
matches this printed clause** and captures `Team Rocket's`; the only thing that keeps it
null is `CLAUSE_ENERGY_TOKENS` having no such token. D118's rule is that a template needs a
**closed vocabulary the lookup can FAIL against**. The energy codes have one, the Pokémon
types have one, **a printed card NAME has none** — so a template over it would answer
*"Fixmon's Energy"* with this member. Literals are pass one in `boardConditionForClause`,
so the row wins outright.

### D368's recorded TRAP, taken the way the trap said it had to be

`undamagedBonus.test.ts` §6 has carried this sentence as a **trap** since D368: *"'Team
Rocket's' is a SPECIAL Energy (`sv10-182`), so `energy: "special"` would also match
Reversal Energy — a widening the printing does not ask for."* D374 did not widen that
token map. It bought a member that reads a printed NAME, and the trap rung is updated in
place to say so rather than deleted. **A trap that is later taken correctly is a receipt,
not a stale note.**

### D154's fold, on a NEW kind of site

This is the union's **first parameter that is printed text carrying an apostrophe**.
`literalClauseRow` already folds U+2019 → U+0027 on a clause-table miss, so the KEY
survives a punctuation-normalising re-ingest — but such a re-ingest curls `Card.name` too,
and an ASCII parameter compared against a curled name is exactly D137's half-fix wearing a
proper noun. **The arm folds the CARD side** (`foldApostrophes`, whose other consumer is
`attackIndexByName` in the same file), the parameter is stored ASCII, and both halves are
driven on a curled board (`trEnergyBonus.test.ts` §6) rather than argued.

### Why it is NOT `yourActiveHasEnergyAttached` widened

That member reads by **PROVISION** (`hasAttachedEnergy`, continuous.ts): a wildcard
Luminous IS a `{R}` Energy while it provides every type, and stops being one when a second
Special demotes it. A **NAME** is the opposite reading — it does not move with the board
and has nothing to do with what pays a cost. One field meaning both would make one member
mean two things on the same card. They disagree on a real board (a plain Special satisfies
`energy: "special"` and not this) and agree on another (`Team Rocket's Energy` satisfies
both), and both are driven.

### Housekeeping a successor inherits

* The census moved in **fourteen** files this time (D373's page said eleven, D372's nine).
  **THE RUNG COUNT IS STILL NOT INHERITABLE.** The three grep-proof rungs are the same
  three: `BUILT.attack - 922`, `BUILT.attack - 922 - 252`, and a bare-literal OPERAND
  (`expect(497 - REGISTRY_ATTACKS.length - SPLIT_ATTACK_UNITS)`) — **eight slices running**.
* ⚠️ **AN OWNER-PREFIXED FIXTURE IS A CENSUS SUBJECT IN FOUR FILES, WHATEVER CATEGORY IT
  IS.** `switchSeam` / `inPlayTarget` / `ownerTargetOps` each enumerate every
  `/^[A-Z][A-Za-z' ]*'s /` name in `FIXTURE_POOL`, and this slice's two prefixed cards are
  **Energy**, not bodies. The list edit is the whole cost — but it is not in any price a
  slice writes for itself, and this is the fifth time it has been paid.
* The residue behind the bonus skeleton is now **26 sentences / 32 printings**, with
  **THREE** clauses left in the 2-printing band.

## D373 — the UNIVERSAL over the Bench: an EMPTY-SET boundary that had to be CHOSEN, because the two precedents turned out to be each other's negation (engine 0.277.0 → 0.278.0)

**Clause:** *"If all of your Benched Pokémon have at least 1 damage counter on them, this
attack does 120 more damage."* — Drampa `sv05-138`/`-184` "Raging Cannon" (JP SV5M 060),
**1 sentence / 2 legal printings**. D369's deferral, taken.

**Ships:** `yourBenchAllDamaged` (bare-tag `BoardCondition`), 1 LITERAL
`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, 2 reader arms. Zero new vocabulary, zero new imports.

### The build was four edits. The slice was the boundary.

`conditionHolds` reads `bench.length > 0 && bench.every((p) => p !== null && p.damage > 0)`.
**The `length > 0` is the slice.** An empty Bench is **FALSE** — a CHOICE, and the whole
argument, the four silent rules instruments and the falsifier live in
`docs/reference/ptcg-rules.md` **§15b**, which D373 wrote for exactly this reason. Read
that section before touching any quantified clause; do not re-derive it here.

### The finding that made it decidable

D369 named `noEnergyOnYourPokemon` (TRUE on an empty board) as a prior *chosen*
vacuous-universal convention. **It is not chosen.** Its printed sentence is *"none of your
Pokémon have any Energy attached"* — a NEGATED EXISTENTIAL — so its TRUE is forced by
exactly the logic that forces `yourBenchDamaged`'s FALSE. **The two are each other's
negation; neither is a convention, and together they say nothing about a positive
universal.** `yourBenchAllDamaged` is the first empty-set semantics this vocabulary has
ever actually chosen.

### The near miss, and how the two are kept apart

`yourBenchDamaged` (D116, `.some`) and `yourBenchAllDamaged` (`.every`) read the SAME
array on the SAME seat for the SAME field. The printed keys differ by five words and the
whole-sentence anchor is all that separates them. **The separating board is a PARTLY
damaged Bench** — two benched bodies, one damaged: the existential TRUE, the universal
FALSE. A suite that only fields an all-damaged and an all-undamaged Bench cannot tell the
two members apart, and that is what D373's C2 mutant exists to prove.

### The invariant, and the attribution control

With the guard, `yourBenchAllDamaged ⟹ yourBenchDamaged` on **every** board; without it,
the empty Bench is the one board where a TRUE universal sits above a FALSE existential.
`benchAllDamagedBonus.test.ts` §2 computes the member's own predicate **with the guard
removed** and compares it board for board: it differs on **exactly one board in the whole
game** and agrees on the other seven shapes swept. **That is what makes the guard shown
rather than asserted** (D214).

### Housekeeping a successor inherits

* `D369-deferred-universal-gets-the-existential-row` is **RETIRED**, not re-pointed: after
  the row landed its edit became a duplicate Map key above the real row, i.e. a no-op that
  would have reported a phantom SURVIVOR. Its claim is C3's now.
* The census moved in **ELEVEN** files (D372's page said nine). Three rungs are unreachable
  by grep. Run the suite.
* **The web is reachable in this container** (WebSearch/WebFetch) and it is the right
  instrument for a RULES question — it is how the printing was identified and how §15b's
  four instruments were checked. It is **not** a substitute for the catalog and cannot
  give a legal-printing count.


## D372 — the CROSS-BOARD EQUAL-ENERGY clause: the shape answer was already written down, in the helper's own doc block (engine 0.276.0 → **0.277.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

`activeEnergyCountsEqual` — **1** new `BoardCondition` member, **2** reader arms, **1**
LITERAL `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, **1** new import, and **zero** new vocabulary,
maps, templates, patterns, ops, events, error codes, registry rows, state fields, prompt
kinds, choice kinds or `packages/schema` bytes. It serves *"If this Pokémon and your
opponent's Active Pokémon have the same amount of Energy attached, this attack does 100
more damage."* **and the same clause at 120** — **1 legal printing each**, two printed
sentences, one row.

### 1. 🛑 THE SHAPE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED BY *FINDING* THE ANSWER, NOT BY CHOOSING ONE

*"The same amount of Energy attached"* reads as Energy **CARDS** or as the **UNITS** they
provide, and those disagree on any board holding a multi-unit Special. The handoff named
the question and forbade re-deciding it. The answer is in
`countAttachedEnergy(state, pokemon, null)`'s own doc block:

> *"CARDS not units, for the same reason `countEnergyInPlay` gives below: one Energy card
> is one Energy however many units it provides."*

So the member **delegates** and adds no counting code. That is what keeps the printed
noun from meaning one thing to this clause and another to the §6.3 readings beside it.

⚠️ **AND THE QUESTION WAS REAL RATHER THAN RHETORICAL — DRIVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:**

| board | by CARD | by UNIT | member |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 basics vs **one** `fix-blend` | 2 ≠ 1 | 2 = 2 | **FALSE** (dealt 10) |
| 2 basics vs **two** `fix-blend` | 2 = 2 | 2 ≠ 4 | **TRUE** (dealt 110) |

The second row is the attribution control: without it, "the member reads cards" would be
shown only where the unit reading answers TRUE, and anything that refused a `fix-blend`
board for any reason at all would pass.

### 2. "THE ENGINE ALREADY READS THIS FIELD" — and this time it also already ASKED THIS QUESTION

D371's lesson run forward. `attack.ts` sums `countAttachedEnergy(state, attacker, null)`
and the same call on the defender's Active for *"…for each Energy attached to both Active
Pokémon."* (**8 legal printings**). **THE SAME TWO OPERANDS, A SUM INSTEAD OF AN
EQUALITY.** So the grep D371 ordered came back cheap rather than dangerous — which is the
other outcome of that check, and worth recording beside the case where it found a trap.

### 3. 🛑 THE ZONE IS THE BODY, AND THE WRONG CODE WAS ALREADY IMPORTED

`countEnergyInPlay(state, seat, null)` has been in `interpreter.ts`'s import block since
D193 and reads **Active plus Bench**. The printed subjects are *"this Pokémon"* and
*"your opponent's Active Pokémon"* — two BODIES. D279's Falinks refutation at a third
shape.

**THE IMPORT BLOCK IS WHY THIS IS A MUTANT RATHER THAN A SENTENCE.** Reaching for the
helper already in scope costs an author nothing; reaching for a UNIT count does not,
because `providedEnergy` and `unitsProvidedBy` have never been imported here. Same rule,
opposite verdicts, one line of evidence — D371's test, applied a third time.

### 4. 🛑 SEAT-SYMMETRIC IN VALUE, ASYMMETRIC IN SPELLING — and the word had to be split before it could be used

`handSizesEqual` has said since D119 that it is *"the ONE member of this whole vocabulary
that is SEAT-SYMMETRIC"*. This is the second, and the first where the two senses part:

- the printed **SENTENCE** is asymmetric — D116's pronoun on one side, the full noun
  phrase on the other;
- the **TRUTH VALUE** commutes, because equality commutes over the two Active bodies.

Both are driven (`sameEnergyBonus.test.ts` §6), and the claim is corrected to **FIRST**
at three sites — `effects.ts`, `interpreter.ts`, and `publicCount.test.ts`'s **test
name**, a file the new member never touches. **A NEW MEMBER CAN FALSIFY A COMMENT IN A
FILE IT DOES NOT TOUCH** (D370, in the other direction) — and this time the falsification
was predicted in the handoff and collected in the same commit rather than found later.

### 5. ⚠️ THE CENSUS STEP IS 2 SENTENCES AND 2 PRINTINGS — the first 2:2 step in this run

D368 moved 1:3; D369, D370 and D371 each moved 1:2. One clause printed under **two**
sentences moves 2:2. The fifteen census rungs are keyed on **both** columns, so every
chain that re-derives an earlier head gains a `- 2` on the sentence side **and** a `- 2`
on the printing side. **A CLAUSE-KEYED BAND ENTRY IS NOT A SENTENCE COUNT** — the
2-printing band that named this candidate counts CLAUSES, and this clause is two
sentences at one printing each.

### 6. ✅ D207's SUPPLY question does not ARISE here, and saying so is the result

Every member this family has bought since D368 reads an **ingested card column**
(`tools`, `types`, `resistances`), so *"does a column CLASSIFY this?"* had to be asked
each time — `Tera` is what happens when the answer is no. This one reads
`InPlayPokemon.energy`: a **game-state** array the engine writes itself on every legal
attach. There is no catalog column to be empty, so the permanently-empty-candidate-set
failure is unreachable **by construction** rather than merely unobserved.

### 7. ⚠️ THE PRINTED NEAR MISS IS ONE OPERATOR AWAY AND IS LEFT REFUSED

*"If this Pokémon has more Energy attached than your opponent's Active Pokémon, this
attack does 160 more damage."* — **1 legal printing**, the same two operands under a
**strict inequality**, refused by all nine readers at this head.

Building it in the same slice would have made the `===` → `>` mutant green for the wrong
reason. It is measured, pinned as a tripwire (`sameEnergyBonus.test.ts` §3), given a
literal-row mutant of its own (C5 — the "one more printing for free" escape hatch), and
handed on **priced**: 1 member + 1 row + 2 arms, zero new vocabulary, for 1 printing.

### 8. Five mutation rows, one per claim, and one claim DECLARED without a row

C1 the ZONE, C2 the far SEAT, C3 the empty Active Spot read as zero, C4 the comparison,
C5 the literal-row escape hatch onto the strict-inequality sentence. **5 KILLED / 0 GAPs
/ 0 ERRORS.**

⚠️ **C3 IS THE ONE WHOSE KILLING BOARD HAD TO BE BUILT ON PURPOSE.** A `theirs === null ?
0 : count(…)` reading is invisible on every board where the attacker holds at least one
Energy — 1 ≠ 0 is FALSE under both readings. Only the ZERO-energy board separates them,
and that board is reachable only *before* the printed `{C}` is paid, so no attack can be
declared from it and the member has to be read directly. **A COMMITMENT NOTHING DRIVES IS
A COMMENT**, and the board that drives this one is not one a suite produces by accident.

## D375 — the CROSS-BOARD TYPE INTERSECTION: the union's first predicate over two VARIABLE-SIZE SETS, and a slice whose entire price was the SHAPE (engine 0.279.0 → **0.280.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

Serves *"If any of your Pokémon in play are the same type as any of your opponent's
Pokémon in play, this attack does 120 more damage."* — Enamorus `sv06-093` "Love
Resonance" (80+, **+120**) and its Illustration-rare reprint `sv06-180`, **1 sentence /
2 legal printings**. ONE `BoardCondition` member (`inPlayTypesIntersect`, **NULLARY**),
ONE literal `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, TWO reader arms, ZERO new imports.

### The transferable parts

**1. A SLICE WHOSE PRICE IS *ONLY* THE SHAPE IS RARE, AND IT IS WORTH RECOGNISING.**
D207's supply question has been the first question of every slice in this run, and here it
was never close: `Card.types` already has four readers in this union. When the answer is
that obvious the temptation is to skip straight to code — and this is exactly the slice
where that would have cost most, because **two different builds would have compiled, been
green, and been wrong.**

**2. THE *DANGEROUS* KIND OF WRONG IS NOT THE *VACUOUS* KIND, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT
BOARDS.** D370's bench-scoped type clause could not be widened to *"in play"* without
going unconditionally TRUE — the attacker was a Metal body reading a Metal clause — so the
wrong build broke LOUDLY and any board would have found it. **This clause is the opposite
case.** The printing is a **Psychic** Enamorus, and *"any of your Pokémon in play"*
genuinely includes the attacker, so narrowing either half to the Active Spot **still pays
correctly on most boards** and under-pays silently only when the shared type sits on a
Bench. A reading that is right most of the time cannot be found by a suite that writes
ordinary boards; it has to be hunted. `typeShareBonus.test.ts` §4 computes both narrowed
readings **beside** the member on five boards — they AGREE on two and DISAGREE on three,
and the two agreements are the attribution control (D214): *a wrong reading that is always
false proves nothing about the boards where it differs.*

**3. 🛑 THE CATALOG CANNOT ALWAYS SEPARATE TWO READINGS, AND WHEN IT CANNOT, THE FIXTURE
IS THE ONLY GUARD.** `Card.types` is an ARRAY, and *"the same type"* is satisfied by any
shared member — but **no Standard-legal Pokémon is dual-typed** (measured on the remote D1
at D238: `json_array_length(types_json) > 1` returns zero rows). So an ARRAY EQUALITY and
an INTERSECTION agree on **every board that can be built out of real cards**, and a suite
authored from real shapes is green on either. `fix-dualbody` (`["Water", "Metal"]`, D370)
is the separator. ⚠️ **AND ONE DUAL-TYPE BOARD IS NOT ENOUGH**: `["Water","Metal"]` against
a single `["Water"]` kills the equality reading and **leaves a `types[0]`-only reading
alive**, because they still meet at index 0. The second board is the same fixture against
a single `["Metal"]`, where the shared member sits second. **TWO WRONG READINGS, TWO
BOARDS** — this is D374's *"the only killing board holds a card nobody printed"* one field
over, and the general rule is: **when the printed population is degenerate on the axis you
are reading, the fixture pool is the only place a guard can go red.**

**4. THE EMPTY-SET BOUNDARY WAS *READ*, NOT ARGUED.** §15b of `reference/ptcg-rules.md`
(D373) already partitions these: `∃` FALSE and `¬∃` TRUE are **forced by logic**, and only
the positive universal is a **choice**. This clause is a positive existential — two of them
nested — so an empty side is FALSE by force. **Re-arguing a settled boundary is how D369's
error happened in the first place**, and D373 wrote §15b precisely so a successor would
look it up instead. This one did.

**5. THE NOTE IS VERBATIM, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT THIS SENTENCE RATHER THAN A RULE.**
The printed clause names no pronoun for D116 to resolve and no card-face glyph for D118 to
spell out, so `conditionNote` returns the clause exactly and round-trips **both** to the
printed bytes and — through `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` — back to the member. It is the
family's first cross-board note that does. Its two neighbours deliberately do NOT
(`activeEnergyCountsEqual` drops a pronoun, `yourBenchHasType` spells `{M}` as `Metal`),
and §3 asserts the difference in both directions **so a successor does not "fix" one into
the other.**

### Housekeeping a successor inherits

* ✅ **THE OWNER-PREFIX TOLL IS KEYED ON THE FIXTURE'S *NAME*, NOT ON ADDING A FIXTURE.**
  `switchSeam.test.ts`, `inPlayTarget.test.ts` and `ownerTargetOps.test.ts` each enumerate
  every `/^[A-Z][A-Za-z' ]*'s /` name in `FIXTURE_POOL`. Five slices running paid that toll
  and every one of them happened to add a possessive-named card, so nobody could tell the
  two rules apart. **D375 added two fixtures and paid nothing**, which settles it.
* ⚠️ **THE RED CENSUS RUN COMES IN WAVES.** An `expect` throws, so later assertions in the
  same `it` never execute — D375 needed **four** full `vitest` passes to reach green,
  because each pass revealed the next assertion inside an already-failing block. **Budget
  the passes, not the run.** Four of the thirteen reddened rungs are keyed on a DIFFERENCE
  or a bare literal OPERAND and no grep of the figures reaches them.
* ⚠️ **THE WEB IS THE INSTRUMENT FOR IDS, AND THE QUERY MATTERS.** A bare WebSearch on the
  printed sentence returned nothing, twice. `https://limitlesstcg.com/cards?q=text:"…"`
  answered instantly — the default `q=` is name-only, and the `text:` operator is the whole
  trick — and `https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>` confirmed each id. `api.pokemontcg.io`
  returns **403** to WebFetch. **THE WEB STILL CANNOT GIVE A LEGAL-PRINTING COUNT**; that
  is `legalAttackCorpus()`'s and nowhere else's.

## D376 — the FILTERED DISCARD-PILE THRESHOLD: the sibling one zone over, read the other way round

Serves *"If you have 10 or more Basic {R} Energy cards in your discard pile, this attack
does 100 more damage."* — Chandelure `sv10.5w-018` "Incendiary Pillar" ({R}, 50+, **+100**)
and its Illustration-rare reprint `sv10.5w-103`, whose rules text is byte-identical, **1
sentence / 2 legal printings**. ONE `BoardCondition` member
(`yourBasicEnergyInDiscardAtLeast`, carrying an `energy` and a `count`), ONE literal
`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, TWO reader arms, **ZERO new imports**.

Engine **0.280.0 → 0.281.0**; `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **22 unchanged**.

### D207's supply question, asked first — and it was never close on either half

`PlayerState.discard` is a `string[]` of uids the model has carried since M1 with a dozen
readers, and **`CardFilter` already spells the printed noun**: `{ kind: "basicEnergy",
energyType }`, authored for the *"Basic {L} Energy card"* SEARCH sentences. Neither the
zone nor the filter is new. **So the whole price was the SHAPE — the second slice running
for which that is literally true** (D375 was the first).

### The shape: an INVERSION of the member it sits beside, not a relocation of it

🛑 `yourEnergyInPlayAtLeast { energy, count }` is the same three words one zone over, and
**its own doc block says it reads PROVISION** (`countEnergyInPlay`, continuous.ts). That is
*correct there*: an Energy card **in play** pays for whatever it provides, so a wildcard
Luminous Energy `sv02-191` counts as `{D}` while it is alone on a Pokémon.

**A DISCARD PILE PROVIDES NOTHING.** A card in a pile is attached to nothing;
`energyProvidesOf` is a reading of an ATTACHED card; and the printed words name a card
**CLASS** (*Basic*) plus a printed **TYPE**. So the member reads the PRINTED CARD through
`matchesFilter` and never through the in-play counter — **§6.5's standing rule, already
stated twice in `effects.ts` for the pile-scanning ops** (*"it is about the PRINT
(`basicEnergy` + `energyType`), never `providesEnergy`"*), applied to a `BoardCondition`
for the first time.

⚠️ **The parameter is narrower than the sibling's, and that is the same inversion again.**
`energy` is `BasicEnergyType`, not `BasicEnergyType | "special"`. The sibling admits
`"special"` because provision folds the card class in as one more countable thing; here the
class is FIXED by the printed noun, so `"special"` would spell *"Basic Special Energy"* — a
card that cannot exist. The compiler is what keeps it narrow.

### 🛑 THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING: the pile a suite writes by accident separates NOTHING

A discard pile holding **ten Basic Fire Energy and nothing else** makes the member agree
with **all four** wrong readings at once:

| widening | what it drops | separating board |
|---|---|---|
| the **ZONE** | the pile; `countEnergyInPlay` instead | ten Basic {R} **attached**, empty pile |
| the **CARD CLASS** | the printed *Basic*; `anyEnergy` | 9 Fire + 1 Special |
| the **TYPE** | the printed `{R}`; `energyType` dropped | 9 Fire + 1 Basic {W} |
| the **FILTER** | everything; `discard.length` | 9 Fire + 1 Pokémon |

Three of the four separating boards are the **same shape** — nine Fire plus ONE tenth card —
and only the tenth card differs, which is what makes the three widenings visibly *nested*
rather than three unrelated mistakes. `basicEnergyDiscard.test.ts` computes all four
readings BESIDE the member on every board and reports them as one object, so a rung says
*which* reading it separates instead of merely that something differs.

✅ **And the agreeing board is asserted FIRST, as D214's attribution control** (all five
readings TRUE), with the empty pile beside it (all five FALSE). Without that pair, "the
member disagrees with the widening here" would be a claim about a predicate that might
simply be always-false.

⚠️ **The sharpest rung is the wildcard.** `sv02-191` Luminous Energy makes
`yourEnergyInPlayAtLeast` TRUE at `count: 1` when it is **in play**, and contributes nothing
to this member from the **pile**. One card, two zones, two answers — which is the whole
difference between the two members, driven rather than argued.

✅ **The zone is driven in BOTH directions**, deliberately: ten attached with an empty pile
(member FALSE, sibling TRUE) *and* ten in the pile with none in play (member TRUE, sibling
FALSE). A member that was simply always false would satisfy the first rung and fail the
second.

### The threshold

`>=`, because the printed words are *"10 or more"* — a FLOOR, the sibling's reading of *"at
least"*. Driven at **exactly 9** (false, 10 damage dealt) and **exactly 10** (true, 110
dealt) through the attack path, then over the whole ramp **0..11 in one loop**, so `>`,
`>=` and `===` are separated by a property of the predicate rather than by three counts a
case happened to pick. The `count` and `energy` PARAMETERS are pinned separately: the
catalog prints one threshold and one type, so a hard-coded pair would be green on every
board in the file — that is mutant C6, and it is killed by asking the same nine-card pile
at `count: 9`.

### Housekeeping a successor inherits

* ⚠️ **THE FIXTURE DECK IS THE SLICE'S REAL RISK WHEN THE PRINTED NUMBER IS BIG.**
  `count: 10` means ten matching cards must come OUT of a 60-card deck **after** setup has
  taken 7 to hand and 6 to prizes. A first cut of `BASIC_ENERGY_DISCARD_DECK` ran the second
  Fire print at 4 and one seed put a copy in a prize. `discardFromDeck` throws with the
  count it found, so the failure is LOUD — but **the fix is a MARGIN, not a seed**. Budget
  roughly 1.8× what the deepest board needs; the committed deck carries 18 + 6 Fire prints
  for a deepest board of eleven.
* ✅ **THE OWNER-PREFIX TOLL WAS NOT PAID AGAIN, WHICH CONFIRMS D375's RULE.**
  `fix-emberpillar` carries no possessive, so `switchSeam` / `inPlayTarget` /
  `ownerTargetOps` all stood still. Second slice running.
* ⚠️ **THE RED CENSUS RUN COMES IN WAVES — D376 NEEDED FOUR PASSES** (14 files → 5 → 3 → 2
  → 0). Every wave surfaced rungs the previous one hid, because an `expect` throws and the
  later assertions in an already-failing `it` never run. FOUR of the fourteen are keyed on a
  DIFFERENCE or a bare literal OPERAND and no grep of the figures reaches them.
* ⚠️ **THE APOSTROPHE PARTITION SWAPPED HALVES.** `clauseApostrophe.test.ts` splits the
  carried bonus clauses into apostrophe-bearing and apostrophe-free. D375's clause carried a
  possessive and moved the first half (15 → 16); **this one carries neither a possessive nor
  a contraction nor a `Pokémon`, so it is PURE ASCII and moves the second (20 → 21)** while
  the first stands still at 16. The suite asserts the sentence's ASCII-ness directly, so a
  successor reaching for `foldApostrophes` on this row learns it would be guarding nothing.
* ⚠️ **THE WEB IS STILL THE INSTRUMENT FOR IDS — AND `limitlesstcg` TOKENISES.** D375
  recorded that the `text:` operator is what makes `q=` a card-text search. **D376 adds the
  next trap: `text:` splits the phrase into words and `AND`s them, and there is no token for
  a brace code.** `text:"…Basic {R} Energy cards in your discard pile"` returns **0 cards**
  and says so in words (*"…includes ("basic" and "{r}" and …)"*); the same phrase with the
  glyph DROPPED returns 10. **DROP EVERY `{X}` FROM A LIMITLESS QUERY**, then confirm each
  id on `https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>`, which returns the printed effect text and
  is how the corpus line was checked byte-for-byte. `api.pokemontcg.io` still returns **403**
  to WebFetch, and the web still cannot give a LEGAL-PRINTING count.
