## D377 — the CROSS-BOARD STATUS PAIR: one closed printed vocabulary over THREE model shapes, and the token priced and DECLINED (engine 0.281.0 → **0.282.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

Serves **THREE** printed sentences at **1 legal printing each**:

* *"If your opponent's Active Pokémon is Burned, this attack does 40 more damage."* —
  Slugma `sv05-028` "Roasting Heat" ({R}, **10+**);
* *"If your opponent's Active Pokémon is Confused, this attack does 90 more damage."* —
  Tapu Lele `sv08-092` "Mental Crush" ({P}{C}{C}, **90+**);
* *"If your opponent's Active Pokémon **isn't** Burned, this attack does nothing."* —
  Centiskorch `sv05-037` "Charring Breath" ({R}{R}, **180**).

TWO **NULLARY** `BoardCondition` members (`opponentActiveBurned`, `opponentActiveConfused`),
FOUR reader arms, TWO literal `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` rows, ONE
`ATTACK_REQUIREMENT_CLAUSES` row. **ZERO new imports, maps, templates, patterns, ops,
events or `packages/schema` bytes.**

### The handoff said TWO printings. It came out at THREE, and that is a CENSUS lesson

D376 handed this over as a PAIR at 1 printing each — *"2 printings for one purchase"*. It
is three, and the third was found by applying D310/D311's standing rule to the handoff's
own sweep: **a census is as narrow as the literal it matches.** Asking for `is Burned`
returns one sentence; asking for **every conditional sentence carrying a status word at
all** returns the printed NEGATION under a different consequent. `ATTACK_REQUIREMENT_CLAUSES`'
polarity rule (*the skeleton owns the negation*) means that row hands back the POSITIVE
member and `attack.ts` cancels when it fails — so the third printing costs ONE row and ZERO
vocabulary. **D363's Sawk arrangement, one member over, and the first time both consequents
of a member were purchased in the same commit.**

### The SHAPE question, part A: the three model shapes are a RED HERRING

`SpecialConditions` (`types.ts`) is `{ rotation: "none" | "asleep" | "paralyzed" |
"confused"; poisonDamage: number; burned: boolean }` — **Poison is a COUNTER, Burn is a
BOOLEAN and Confusion is ONE VALUE OF AN ENUM**, one closed printed vocabulary of five
words over three different model shapes. That is real, and it is not the slice's problem,
because the three already meet in exactly one place: **`presentStatuses` projects all three
onto one closed `StatusName` list**, and `opponentActiveHasSpecialCondition` has consumed
that projection since D116 as `.length > 0`.

So both new arms are `presentStatuses(active.conditions).includes("burned" | "confused")`
and neither picks a field. What that buys is not brevity — it is that **both members are
provable NARROWINGS of the wide one on every board**, rather than agreeing readings of the
same three fields, which is D222's two-readers-of-one-fact defect closed by construction.
`crossBoardStatus.test.ts` §5 SWEEPS the implication over all ten condition sets the model
can hold, and counts the two boards (Asleep, Paralyzed) where the wide member is TRUE and
all three named ones are FALSE — which is what stops the sweep being vacuous.

### The SHAPE question, part B: the `status` TOKEN, priced from the catalog and declined

D118's rule — *a template is safe only when the varying token has a CLOSED vocabulary to
fail against* — **PASSES here for the first time in this corner**: §12 prints exactly five
status words. **It is the COUNT that refuses the token, not the safety.** Swept over
`legalAttackCorpus()` (640 sentences / 1,732 legal printings) for every `is` / `isn't`
status clause on BOTH seats:

| status | sentences | printings | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Poisoned | 4 | 8 | **already built**, as TWO NULLARY seat-named members (`opponentActivePoisoned` 3 s / 5 p, `yourActivePoisoned` 1 s / 3 p) |
| Burned | 2 | 2 | this slice, BOTH consequents |
| Confused | 1 | 1 | this slice |
| Asleep | 0 | 0 | — |
| Paralyzed | 0 | 0 | — |

Three of five values are READ at all; two of those three are already two nullary members,
and re-pointing a seat-named member at a token is a **RENAME until proven otherwise** (D365
recorded it, D366 reproduced it, D362 priced the analogous one at **31 sites across 7
files**). So a token serves **exactly the 3 printings two rows serve** and buys reachability
for two values nothing prints. ⚠️ **WHAT WOULD FLIP IT**, so a successor can: a printed
SAME-SEAT *"this Pokémon is Burned/Confused"* read, or any `is Asleep` / `is Paralyzed` read
at all. At that point the conversion is one deliberate rename slice, never a drive-by.

⚠️ **AND THE SETTER SIDE IS ENORMOUS BY COMPARISON**, which is why the vocabulary FEELS
bigger than the read population is: *"…is now Burned"* alone is 14 printings on one
sentence, *"…is now Confused"* is 31. That half is `applyStatus`'s and has been built since
M3. **A vocabulary's size is not its READ population.**

### The vacuity modes, named before the build and each driven on a board

1. **`isImmobilized` is the trap with Confusion's name on it.** It is `rotation ===
   "asleep" || rotation === "paralyzed"` and **deliberately excludes Confused** (§12 lets a
   Confused Pokémon attack and retreat), so an arm that reached for the nearest rotation
   predicate is FALSE on every board the clause is about and TRUE on two it is not. §5's
   ten-row table catches it three ways in one assertion.
2. **Both statuses clear on the same events**, so a board that never moves the Active
   cannot tell "reads the field" from "reads a constant". §3 and §4 drive an ARM and a
   DISARM apiece, both through the GAME.
3. **The two clauses must not reach each other.** §5 fields one board carrying BOTH statuses
   (where a swapped member is invisible) and two carrying exactly one each.

### 🛑 BURN IS CURED BY A COIN, AND CONFUSION IS NOT — so the two boards cost different things

§13.2: at every Checkup a Burned Pokémon takes 20 **and then flips a cure coin**. So an
in-game Burn read a turn later survives only on **two tails**, and the board is
**seed-dependent**. This is not worked around — the seed is pinned and the flips are
**ASSERTED off `CHECKUP_COIN_FLIP`**, so a moved RNG fails loudly instead of silently
turning the rung into the clean-Active case wearing a Burn's name. The HEADS seed beside it
is then the **game-driven DISARM**, for free.

Confusion has no cure flip and survives indefinitely; its disarm is §11's **retreat**, which
clears the whole status row — a real `retreat` action taken by the seat that owns the
condition, on that seat's own turn. **Two statuses, two clearing rules, four boards.**

### The cast, and why every member of it is also a setter

`CROSS_BOARD_STATUS_DECK` fields three attackers and each is a setter or a reader of
another's condition: `fix-charbreath` (Centiskorch — index-0 "Singe" is the suite's only
in-game Burn source, index-1 "Charring Breath" is the CANCEL consequent), `fix-roastheat`
(Slugma — the +40 BONUS consequent on the condition `fix-charbreath` sets), `fix-mindcrush`
(Tapu Lele — self-arming, index-0 Confuses and index-1 reads it). `fix-*` and not the real
ids, for D376's reason unchanged: a fixture id naming a real printing needs a
`CATALOG_MANIFEST.printed` row and this container has no D1.

⚠️ **FOUR COPIES OF EACH ATTACKER AND NOT THREE — D376's MARGIN LESSON, PAID FORWARD AND
MEASURED.** At three copies, seed 60 threw *"p1 deck has no fix-charbreath"*: setup takes 7
to hand and 6 to prizes before a single surgery runs. **The fix is a MARGIN, not a seed.**

### What the census actually cost — and it was EIGHTEEN files, not fourteen

Residue (bonus skeleton) **24 / 28 → 22 / 26** (a **2:2** step); the "does nothing"
skeleton's own residue **3 s / 5 p → 2 s / 4 p**; resolving sentences **354 → 357**; raw
**1,239 → 1,242**; `BUILT.attack` **1,268 → 1,271**; unbuilt remainder **493 → 490**; the
requirement table **7 rows / 6 reachable / 13 printings → 8 / 7 / 14**; the apostrophe-BEARING
bonus half **16 → 18** (both new keys spell a possessive, so the apostrophe-free half stands
still at 21); the apostrophe requirement list **6 → 7**; the fixture-census `derivable`
**115 → 118**; the `FIXTURE_POOL` floor **460 → 463**.

🛑 **THE MOVING SET WAS EIGHTEEN FILES AND THE HANDOFF PREDICTED FOURTEEN.** The four extra
are the REQUIREMENT family — `benchCountRequirement`, `requirementFloor`, `splitOrder`,
`sawkRequirementSplit` — and they moved because **this is the first slice in the run to touch
BOTH consequents**. **THE PREDICTED SET IS A PROPERTY OF WHICH TABLES A SLICE EDITS, NOT A
CONSTANT.** Five full `vitest` passes to green (18 files → 3 → 3 → 2 → 0), the wave shape
D375 and D376 both recorded.

⚠️ **AND TWO OF THOSE FILES HELD A RECORD THAT THIS SLICE FALSIFIED.** D365's `REFUSED` list
carried *"a BURNED member — the state field exists, no condition reads it"* in both
`requirementFloor.test.ts` and `benchCountRequirement.test.ts`. The rows were **MOVED into a
new `TAKEN_SINCE` array, not deleted** (D178: provenance is annotated, never overwritten),
the partitions are re-assembled from both arrays so they still sum to D365's 4 / 9, and the
assertion is **INVERTED rather than removed** — the sentence is now asserted to resolve, and
to resolve to the NARROW member rather than the wide one that case exists to refuse. **D365's
refusal was right and only its timing was wrong.**

### The IDs — a web measurement, the fifth slice running, with two false positives refuted

limitlesstcg's `text:` search tokenises and `AND`s the tokens, so *"Active Pokemon is
Burned, this attack does 40 more damage"* returns **8 cards** and only one of them prints the
sentence. All three ids were confirmed against `https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>`,
which returns the printed effect byte for byte, and the two SV-era false positives — Magcargo
ex `sv06-029`/`-191` and Ninetales ex `sv03.5-038`/`-186`, both printing *"is now Burned"* —
were refuted the same way. ⚠️ **THE WEB STILL CANNOT GIVE A LEGAL-PRINTING COUNT**; that is
`legalAttackCorpus()`'s alone.

## D387 — THE STAGE 1 CLAUSE: a SUBSET that is not a NARROWING, and a guard written to record the obvious that went red

Paldean Tauros `sv08-018` "Spirited Tackle" ({R}{C}{C}, `90+`, **+90**, index 1 of two — "Rear Kick"
({R}, 30, no effect text) is index 0): *"If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Stage 1 Pokémon, this
attack does 90 more damage."* — **1 sentence / 1 legal printing**, the FOURTH sibling of a shape this
union has built three times (`opponentActiveIsBasic`, `opponentActiveIsEvolution`,
`opponentActiveIsStage2`).

### 🛑 A SUBSET IS NOT A NARROWING — the distinction the whole slice turns on

D386's handoff flagged this candidate as *"a NARROWING of a live member"*, because every Stage 1
satisfies `opponentActiveIsEvolution`'s `evolveFromOf(top) !== null`. D362 prices that class of change
at **31 sites across 7 files**, so if the flag were right the row would cost ten times what its
handoff quoted.

**The set relation IS a subset. The build is NOT a narrowing. Those are different claims.**

A member is narrowed by changing what **its own arms read**. Nothing here changed:

* `opponentActiveIsEvolution` keeps `evolveFromOf(...) !== null`;
* it keeps its `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row — **four printed sentences worth nine legal
  printings**, every one of which spells the word *"Evolution"* and wants the wide reading;
* it keeps both of its exhaustive-`switch` arms.

So the third mechanism is free and the handed price stands: **1 printing / 3 mechanisms = 0.33**
(one `cards.ts` predicate, the member plus its two arms, the clause row). **ASK "WHAT DO I HAVE TO
EDIT", NOT "WHAT IS A SUBSET OF WHAT".** D296 wrote this paragraph one stage up as a warning and
D367's clause-row comment quoted it forward; D387 is the first slice to need it as an ANSWER.

### 🛑 …and the subset itself is a CATALOG COINCIDENCE, which the rung written to record it found

§1 was written to assert *"every Stage 1 in the pool is also an Evolution"* — a sentence that reads
like a rule of the game. **It went RED.** The two readings are facts about **two independent
columns**: `stage` is a printed word and `evolveFrom` is a chain datum, and nothing in the ingest or
the engine makes them agree. Swept over `FIXTURE_POOL`:

* **67** bodies carry `stage: "Stage1"`;
* **one of them has a NULL `evolveFrom`** — `fix-exstage1` ("Fixgrown ex"), written for another suite;
* **24** bodies are an Evolution by the chain datum and NOT a Stage 1 by the printed word.

So on this engine's own data the two readings disagree in **both** directions, and a build that had
reached for "any Evolution" would have been leaning on a coincidence rather than on a rule.
`fix-exstage1` is now a fifth ladder rung, driven on the predicate rather than on a board.
**WHEN A GUARD IS WRITTEN TO RECORD SOMETHING OBVIOUS, RUN IT BEFORE YOU BELIEVE IT.**

### The pricing, and the handoff's own ranking overturned

| candidate | printings | mechanisms | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|

| the STAGE 1 row | 1 | **3** | **0.33** |
| 🆕 the RETREAT-COST row (**not taken**) | 1 | **2** | **0.50** |

### The deck is the truth table of one printed word — a LADDER, not a pair

There are **two** wrong readings of "Stage 1" and a pair of boards can only refuse one:

| body | printed `stage` | member | refuses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fix-bigbody` (200 HP) | `Basic` | FALSE | — the FALSE arm |

The defenders are big on purpose: 90 + 90 = 180 and the pool's `fix-stage1` is 90 HP, so the printed

**This is the evolution case D386 declared it could not drive**, and it is the only rung where *"the
TOP card is the current identity"* (§1.2) is a line of play rather than surgery.

Maractus `sv10.5b-008`/`-093` "Lively Needles" ({G}, `20+`, index 0 of two): *"If this Pokémon was
healed during this turn, this attack does 100 more damage."* — **1 sentence / 2 legal printings**,
the LAST 2-printing clause in the bonus residue, deferred **seven** times.

| candidate | printings | mechanisms | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| the face-up PRIZE row | 2 | **9** | **0.22** |
| the HEALED-THIS-TURN row | 2 | **5** | **0.40** |

The healed row's five are: the field plus its initialiser, the stamp, the member plus its two arms,
the clause row, and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION`. **BOTH CANDIDATES OWE THE RECORD BUMP**, which is the
whole point — the ground seven slices deferred this row on had stopped separating anything by the
time D385 measured the Prize row's `needs` column. The four mechanisms the Prize row buys and this
one does not are the difference: a player CHOICE of Prize index (a park, a prompt, a choice kind,
the `preventBlock` pair, `programWalk` rows), an INDEX REMAP when a Prize is taken, a THIRD payoff
anchor for the trailing reminder parenthetical, and a WIRE shape plus a UI.

⚠️ **AND ON REACHABILITY, WHICH THE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT SHOW.** D385 measured the Prize gate's false
arm as needing the attack used six times. Both arms of this one are ordinary play: heal with a
Potion and attack (true), or just attack (false).

### 🛑 D385's compiler method has a DOMAIN, and this is its edge

The handoff ordered the shape question first and named D385's `prizes` measurement as the way to
settle it — that one separated **1 file / 1 site** from **17 / 22** and ended a four-slice argument
in four minutes. Run here on all three candidate spellings it separates **nothing**:

| spelling | files with errors | error sites |
|---|---|---|
| per-BODY turn stamp — `InPlayPokemon.healedTurn: number \| null` | **1** | **1** |
| per-SEAT boolean — `PlayerSide.healedThisTurn: boolean` | **1** | **1** |
| per-BODY uid set — `GameState.healedThisTurn: string[]` | **1** | **1** |

**A DEAD HEAT, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN ACCIDENTAL.** `tsc -b --force` prices the
CONSTRUCTION SITES a required field creates. `InPlayPokemon` has exactly one constructor
(`makeInPlay`), `PlayerSide` one (`setup.ts`) and `GameState` one — so every widening of any of them
costs one site. D385's measurement worked because it compared a WIDENING against a SHAPE CHANGE, and
a shape change reprices every READ. **THE METHOD ANSWERS "widen or reshape", NOT "which widening".**

What settled it instead, both of them things the compiler cannot see:

1. **THE PRINTED SUBJECT IS "this Pokémon".** A per-seat boolean answers *"did this SEAT heal
   anything this turn"*, and the two come apart on a board a player reaches by playing a Potion on
   their Bench and then attacking with an untouched Active. `healedThisTurn.test.ts` §5 drives that
   board and computes the per-seat reading BESIDE the member, asserting they DISAGREE (D214).
2. **THE CLOCK.** A boolean and a uid set both need a turn-boundary clear; a turn STAMP expires by
   arithmetic. That is D124's argument for `promotedTurn` verbatim, and this field sits beside it.

### The seven stamp sites, and one helper instead of seven edits

Seven sites in `interpreter.ts` file a `HEALED` event. All seven now write their body through
**`healedBody(pokemon, healed, turn)`**, called on the line after the push — so "was healed" has one
definition in this engine and the log and the clause cannot drift apart (D222's rule, pointed at a
WRITER pair rather than a reader pair).

⚠️ **THE SEVENTH IS A JUDGEMENT CALL, NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** `moveCountersFromBench` files a
`HEALED` row for its SOURCE body and has since D138. A reading on which moving counters is not
healing is defensible — but it would have to move the EVENT too, and the helper is exactly what
forces those two to move together. A mutant (`D386-counter-move-skips-the-stamp`) exists to make the
decision visible rather than to call the alternative wrong.

⚠️ **A WHIFF IS NOT A HEAL.** Every caller clamps to the body's own damage and returns early at
zero, so a Potion on an undamaged Active files no event and writes no stamp. §4 drives it from the
real card.

### 🛑 The 2-printing band is now EMPTY — D379's saturation shape, paid across twelve files

The bonus residue steps **20 / 24 → 19 / 22**, and the clause it removes was the last one in the

`expect(band.sort()).toEqual([<this sentence>])`, and rewriting them to `toEqual([])` would have left

`benchNamedBonus.test.ts`'s `LEFT` table names what takes its place — *"If your opponent's Active
Pokémon is a Stage 1 Pokémon, this attack does 90 more damage."* at 1 printing, the FOURTH sibling of
a shape already built three times — and records the finding the old row's cost string produced:
**A COST THAT NEVER CHANGES CAN STOP BEING A REASON, BECAUSE WHAT IT IS COMPARED AGAINST MOVES.**
⚠️ And it flags D262's question for whoever takes it: `opponentActiveIsEvolution` is
`evolveFromOf(top) !== null`, which a Stage 1 also satisfies, so that row is a **NARROWING** of a

## D385 — THE SECOND CONNECTIVE: a price wrong in both directions, a proof obligation on `cond`, and a guard whose premise died while it stayed green

`optionalCostBoost.test.ts` §1 has carried a rung since D381 saying **the family is EIGHT when the
connective is shortened, not seven** — `/^You may .*\. If /` finds a record `/^You may .*If you do,/`
cannot see — and D381 named that record, refused it, and said what for.

> **Veluza ex** `sv09-043` "Purging Strike" ({W}{W}{C}, `120+`, index 1 of two — confirmed by id
> against tcgdex, which returns "Razor Fin" ({W}, 30, no effect text) at index 0)
> *"You may discard your hand. If you discarded any cards in this way, this attack does 120 more
> damage."*
> **1 legal printing**

### The slice was a pricing question, and the face-up Prize row lost

| candidate | printings | mechanisms | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| the FACE-UP PRIZE row | 2 | **9** | 0.22 |
| the HAND-DISCARD row | 1 | **3** | **0.33** |

The Prize row's `needs` column **GREW** on contact rather than shrinking, which is the direction D199
warns is harder to see. Beyond the field, the record bump and the redaction the handoff named, it
also needs:

1. **A THIRD payoff anchor row.** The printed consequent is `this attack does 80 more damage. (That
   Prize card remains face up for the rest of the game.)`, and
   `OPTIONAL_COST_PAYOFF_MORE_DAMAGE` is `/^this attack does (\d+) more damage\.$/` — `$`-terminated.
   **The reader refuses that card at the PAYOFF as well as at the cost**, and nobody had said so.
   D381's C5 mutant is the standing proof: dropping that `$` is exactly what would silently claim
   this card at +80 with the Prize never turned over.
2. **A player CHOICE of which Prize.** *"turn **1 of** your face-down Prize cards face up"* is a
   pick over INDICES of cards the player cannot see — a park, a prompt and a choice kind, not a
   field-free op like `discardStadium`.
3. **An index REMAP when a Prize is taken.** `flow.ts` filters the prize array **by index**
   (`side.prizes.filter((_, index) => !picked.has(index))`), so every face-up index above a taken
   one shifts. Nothing else in this engine carries an index set beside an array it filters.

### The shape question, settled by MEASUREMENT — recorded so nobody re-derives it

D384 ordered *"price `prizesFaceUp: number[]` as a WIDENING against a shape change to `prizes` as a
RENAME **first**"*. Both spellings were applied to `packages/engine/src/types.ts` in turn and
`bunx tsc -b --force` was READ:

| spelling | files with errors | error sites | non-test files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prizesFaceUp: number[]` beside `prizes`, **REQUIRED** | **1** | **1** | `setup.ts` |
| `prizes: { uid: string; faceUp: boolean }[]` | **17** | **22** | `flow.ts`, `setup.ts` |

**THE WIDENING WINS BY SEVENTEEN FILES TO ONE.** ⚠️ **And the handoff's own figure was a red herring
in BOTH directions.** `prizes` is *named* in 113 files, but only **six** sites anywhere read an
ELEMENT of the array and only **two** of those are element-TYPED (`flow.ts`'s
`const uid = side.prizes[index]` and `testFixtures.ts`'s spread of the tail into the deck) —
everything else is `.length`, `.slice` or a bare index. So the shape change is far cheaper than
*"113 files"* suggests **and** still seventeen times the widening. **A NAME COUNT IS NOT A COST;
RUN THE COMPILER.** The whole measurement took four minutes and closed a question four slices old.

### The price D381 quoted was wrong in BOTH directions

D381 wrote: *"a HAND discard as an attack step **and** a consequent conditioned on the COST's own
effect (*if you discarded any*), which is a RECORD of what the cost did rather than a board fact read
before it… the price is whether `discardHand` can RECORD"*.

* **The discard was already built.** `discardHand` has been an `EffectOp` since Professor's Research
  — automatic, park-free, no fields. What was missing was only an ATTACK program that reaches it.
* **The record is not needed at all.** The handoff's question was answered both ways: **yes**, a
  `recordAs` on `discardHand` is a widening and costs ONE line (the op already builds
  `[...side.hand]` for `HAND_DISCARDED`, and every recording op's arm is one `recordMoved(record,
  op.recordAs, uids)` call) — **and no, it must not be built**, because the `recordGate` it would
  feed **could not fail**. `AttackOptionalCostBoost.cond` is not optional, and the cost's payability
  is the SAME predicate the printed *"if you discarded any cards in this way"* states one clause
  later. **A FIELD WHOSE ONLY CONSUMER IS A BRANCH NO BOARD CAN TAKE IS A FIELD WITH NO OBSERVABLE
  MEANING** (D205; `switchActive`'s own note, one op over).

### The two connectives are synonyms HERE and not in English — which is a proof obligation

*"If you do"* asks whether the offer was **ACCEPTED**. *"If you discarded any cards in this way"*
asks whether the accepted cost **MOVED** anything. They come apart exactly when a player can say yes
to a cost that whiffs — and this reading makes that unreachable, because every row of
`optionalCostOps` supplies its cost's **EXACT** payability:

| cost row | `cond` | exact? |
|---|---|---|
| `discard a Stadium in play` (D381) | `stadiumInPlay` | a Stadium in play is always discarded |
| `shuffle N Energy attached to this Pokémon into your deck` (D383) | `yourActiveEnergyAtLeast {count}` | N on the body are always shuffled |
| `discard your hand` (D385) | `yourHandNotEmpty` | a non-empty hand is always discarded |

**SO EVERY FUTURE COST ROW INHERITS THE OBLIGATION THAT ITS `cond` BE NECESSARY *AND* SUFFICIENT.**
A merely NECESSARY gate would pay the bonus out on a whiff. `purgingStrike.test.ts` §3 drives that
over all three rows rather than asserting it here, and D385's C5 mutant (the row keeping its ops and
taking the neighbour's `stadiumInPlay` gate) is the defect stated as data.

⚠️ **AN ALTERNATION, NOT A FOURTH DISPATCH TABLE**, and this is the one place D385 does not follow
D383's symmetry. The cost half and the payoff half are tables because each row carries **DATA** (ops
and a gate; a payoff shape). A connective carries none — both spellings produce the identical
reading — so a table over it would be a dispatch whose every arm returns the same thing. The claim
the widening makes lives on `cond`, and that is where it is stated and driven.

### The member is NULLARY, and the absent digit is the argument

`yourHandExactly` and `opponentHandAtMost` carry a `count` because the catalog prints one
(*"exactly 3"*, *"3 or fewer"*, *"5 or fewer"*). This cost names the **whole hand** and prints no
number, so a `count: 1` would be **INVENTED** where `yourActiveEnergyAtLeast`'s arity is **CAPTURED**
— D383's own guard read from the other side. Measured off `legalAttackCorpus()`: **no own-hand
THRESHOLD is printed anywhere in the legal attack column, at any value.** What would flip it is a
printed own-hand floor, not a second sentence discarding a hand.

⚠️ **AND IT IS NOT `yourHandExactly` NEGATED.** *"Not exactly 0"* is the truth condition, but this
union has no `not` combinator and `ATTACK_REQUIREMENT_CLAUSES`' polarity trick belongs to the
SKELETON, not the member — a `cond` on `conditionGate` is read positively and nothing inverts it.

### The first gate in this family whose FALSE arm the real printing can reach

| slice | gate | how its FALSE arm is reached |
|---|---|---|
| D381 | `stadiumInPlay` | an empty Stadium zone |
| D383 | `yourActiveEnergyAtLeast {3}` | **not reachable from its own printing at all** — the suite drives a SYNTHETIC 4-Energy cost |
| D385 | `yourHandNotEmpty` | **a player who has played their hand out and then attacks** |

That is ordinary play, not a corner case, so §6 drives the refusal from the **REAL** card. It is
also exactly the property the face-up Prize row's gate does **not** have: *"you have a face-down
Prize"* is true on every board a player can legally attack from unless all remaining Prizes are
already face up, which needs the attack used six times.

### 🛑 A GUARD CAN ROT THE WAY A MUTANT CAN — AND THE SUITE HAS NO `ERROR` VERDICT FOR IT

D384 found a **mutant** whose premise had died. D385 found a **guard** whose premise had died, and it
stayed **GREEN WHILE BEING FALSE**.

`exactHandSize.test.ts` (D379) kept a `SIZE_CEILING` list — *"every legal attack sentence that reads
a hand's SIZE and is still refused"* — with this sentence in it, and its §1 loop asserted
`resolvedByAnyReader(sentence) === false` for every entry. That file's hand-kept `READERS` array is
the **NINE**-reader instrument. It does not contain `deriveAttackOptionalCostBoost`. So when D385
built the sentence through the tenth reader, the rung went on claiming a refusal that had stopped
existing, and **nothing reddened**.

**THE MUTANT CORPUS HAS AN `ERROR` VERDICT FOR A DEAD ANCHOR. THE SUITE HAS NOTHING.** The rule is
therefore now two greps rather than one: when your slice builds something an earlier slice
deliberately left unbuilt, grep **`scripts/mutation/mutants.ts` AND `packages/engine/src/*.test.ts`
for the printed SENTENCE**, not for the key and not for the file.

⚠️ **THE FIX IS NOT TO WIDEN THE NINE-READER ARRAY.** Four suites share it and its figures
(**364 / 1,255**) correctly did **not** move for this slice, because this sentence resolves through
the tenth reader alone. What was wrong is that a **REFUSAL** claim was drawn from a **CENSUS**
instrument. **A CENSUS INSTRUMENT AND A REFUSAL ORACLE ARE NOT THE SAME OBJECT**: the sentence left
the list, and the rung now reads BOTH oracles side by side and asserts that they disagree, which is
what stops the next slice repeating it.

### `programWalk` moved though the assembler arm did not

D318's rule says to add a fixture to `FIXTURE_POOL` the moment you export an assembler or reach a
new branch of one. `fix-purging` reaches the **same** `moreDamage` branch of
`optionalCostBoostProgram` that `fix-crushpress` has reached since D381 — no new arm, no new export.
`programWalk.test.ts` gained **three rows anyway**, and the reason is the **OP**: `discardHand` had
only ever appeared in a FLAT `trainer` list, which the enumerated walk that file measures against
can see, and this is the first time it sits inside an `optional.then` NESTED IN a
`conditionGate.then`. **AN EXISTING OP AT A NEW *DEPTH* MOVES THAT FILE TOO.**

### 🛑 A `find` rots as easily by being WRITTEN A SECOND TIME as by being deleted

Found while writing D385's own resume point. That page names the eight mutant anchors it carries
(the corpus's only non-source rows, D318's), and the first draft **quoted four of them verbatim**
so a successor could see them. The post-docs `find` pass came back **`4 bad, distribution
{1: 1280, 2: 4}`**: each quoted anchor matched **TWICE**, which the harness reports as **`ERROR`**
— and the sweep would have come back with four errored rows for a page that says exactly the right
thing.

**THE EXACTLY-ONCE RULE HAS TWO FAILURE DIRECTIONS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS EVER DISCUSSED.** Zero
matches means the code moved; **two matches means somebody wrote the line again**, and the page most
likely to do that is the one that documents the anchors. D318 hit the same shape inside `effects.ts`
(a doc block that reproduced two de-duplicated lines at their own indentation took a row from `1×`
to `1×`-in-a-comment); this is that finding one file set over. **DESCRIBE AN ANCHOR, NEVER QUOTE
IT** — and if you need to enumerate them, read them out of `mutants.ts` with a script rather than
pasting them into prose.

### The moving set was fifteen, and the bonus-residue predictor held

D384 moved eighteen because its sentence left the `^If …, this attack does N more damage\.$` residue
and thirteen files carry that chain. D385's sentence is an optional-cost compound — the residue held
at **20 / 24** and not one of the thirteen moved. What did move: `censusAtHead` (**eight** rungs),
`precociousEvolution` (**three**), `legacyEnergy`, `opponentResistanceBonus` (the `FIXTURE_POOL`
floor **and** the front-edited `ids.length - 1 - …` chain), `moreEnergyBonus`, `optionalCostBoost`,
`exactHandSize`, `programWalk`. **FIVE of the eleven moved rungs were MASKED by an earlier failure
in the same `it`** and it took **five** full suite runs to converge — one more than D384.
`clauseApostrophe` stood still, because the fixture's sentence spells no `'`.

## D384 — THE STRICT-INEQUALITY TWIN: a price that survived twelve slices, a seat-asymmetric member, and the first mutant retired for a dead PREMISE

D372 built *"this Pokémon and your opponent's Active Pokémon have the same amount of Energy
attached"* and, in the same commit, wrote its own near miss into four files: the SAME two operands,
the SAME field, the SAME `countAttachedEnergy` call, and `>` where that row spells `=`.

> **Swalot** `sv07-092` "Devouring Mouth" ({D}, `10+`, index 0 of two — confirmed by id against
> tcgdex, which returns "Venomous Hit" at index 1)
> *"If this Pokémon has more Energy attached than your opponent's Active Pokémon, this attack does
> 160 more damage."*
> **1 legal printing**

### The price the handoff quoted was right to the line, and that is the result

D372 priced it at *"one nullary member, one literal row, two arms"*, **refused to build it** — the
stated reason being that building it in the same slice *"would have made the `===` → `>` mutant
green for the wrong reason"* — and pinned the refusal in `sameEnergyBonus.test.ts` §3 with a comment
saying *"the day a reader claims that sentence, it reddens here naming the clause"*.

Twelve slices later every term held: **ONE nullary `BoardCondition` member
(`moreActiveEnergyThanOpponent`), ONE literal `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, TWO
exhaustive-switch arms in `interpreter.ts`**, plus ONE fixture, ONE dedicated deck and ONE suite.
ZERO new readers, ops, events, prompts, choice kinds, registry rows or `packages/schema` bytes. The
mutant did not go green, because the two members are separate and the suite drives both boards.

🛑 **D199's RULE IS NEARLY ALWAYS INVOKED WHEN A `needs` COLUMN WAS WRONG. THIS IS THE RARER HALF,
AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING**: a price that survives twelve slices is evidence the pricing practice
works, and the only way anyone finds that out is if somebody writes it down when it happens.

### Two nullary members, not one parameterised member — the OPERATOR is the whole argument

The pair shares its two operands, its ZONE (the BODY, not the SIDE) and its
`countAttachedEnergy(state, active, null)` call — the unfiltered CARD count. So the
cards-versus-units question D372 settled **cannot drift between them**: there is one call and two
callers.

What they do not share is the operator, and **an operator is not a parameter here**. Folding the
pair needs a member carrying an operator UNION — a GENERALISATION that renames a shipped nullary
member on the way. D362 priced the analogous rename at **31 sites across 7 files**, D365 and D366
each refused it, and D383 refused it one member over. **A SECOND NULLARY MEMBER IS FREE; A RENAME IS
NOT.**

### The first cross-body member that is SEAT-ASYMMETRIC IN VALUE

| member | commutes? | can a one-seat suite tell it from a seat-blind build? |
|---|---|---|
| `handSizesEqual` (D118) | yes | no |
| `activeEnergyCountsEqual` (D372) | yes | no |
| `inPlayTypesIntersect` (D375) | yes | no |
| `moreActiveEnergyThanOpponent` (D384) | **NO** | **yes — one board, two DIFFERENT answers** |

`>` does not commute, so on a board where the attacker leads the member is TRUE from that seat and
FALSE from the other. Those are two DIFFERENT answers rather than one re-derived twice, and that
rung — `moreEnergyBonus.test.ts` §4 — is **the only thing that separates the member from its own
inverse**. D372's doc block had to split *"symmetric in value"* from *"symmetric in spelling"* to
describe itself; this is the member the split was for.

It also buys a mutant an equality member **cannot have**: swapping the operands of `===` is a no-op,
so D372's arm was immune to that edit by construction. C2 swaps them here and inverts the answer on
every unequal board while staying invisible on every equal one — `morePrizesThanOpponent`'s own
polarity warning, reached through two BODIES instead of two SIDES.

⚠️ **AND THE `?? 0` SLIP IS WORSE ON THIS OPERATOR THAN ON THE EQUALITY, WHICH CUTS BOTH WAYS.**
Reading a missing DEFENDER as zero arms this clause for an attacker holding a single card (1 > 0);
D372's member had to be fooled at exactly zero, which needed an unpaid board no legal action
reaches. **A LARGER BLAST RADIUS AND AN ORDINARY PAYING BOARD TO FIND IT ON.**

### 🛑 A MUTANT CAN ROT WITHOUT ITS `find` MOVING A CHARACTER

D372's C5 read: *"a second `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row maps 'this Pokémon has more Energy
attached than your opponent's Active Pokémon' onto `activeEnergyCountsEqual`"*. It was killed by
`sameEnergyBonus.test.ts` §3, which pinned that sentence as REFUSED.

D384 built the sentence. C5's `find` still matched **exactly once** and still applied cleanly — but:

- `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` is a `Map` built from an entry array, so the **LAST duplicate key
  wins**;
- D384's genuine row sits **AFTER** C5's insertion point.

So the mutation would have changed **nothing**, and reported a **false SURVIVOR** — not an ERROR,
not a `find` miss, just a green row asserting a guard that no longer exists.

🛑 **THE EXACTLY-ONCE RULE IS AN EXPIRY DATE ON THE *CODE* A ROW IS ANCHORED TO. IT SAYS NOTHING
ABOUT THE ROW'S *PREMISE*.** C5 is **RETIRED** — the corpus's first retirement for that reason — and
D384's C6 carries the identical defect by mutating D384's OWN row instead of adding a second one.

**THE STANDING RULE THIS ADDS: when your slice builds something an earlier slice deliberately left
unbuilt, `grep scripts/mutation/mutants.ts` for the PRINTED SENTENCE — not for the file, and not for
the line.** The adjacency rot is caught by the anchors; this one is not caught by anything
mechanical at all.

### The moving set was EIGHTEEN files, and it is structural

D381 moved six, D382 eleven, D383 ten, D384 **eighteen**. The reason is not that this slice was
bigger — it is the smallest reader-keyed step in the run (1 sentence / 1 printing, the family's
first 1:1). It is that **a slice which takes a sentence out of the BONUS RESIDUE touches every file
carrying the residue chain**, and thirteen do: `basicEnergyDiscard`, `benchAllDamagedBonus`,
`benchNamedBonus`, `benchTypeBonus`, `crossBoardStatus`, `exactHandSize`, `opponentResistanceBonus`,
`opponentToolBonus`, `sameEnergyBonus`, `stadiumDiscard`, `stadiumPresence`, `trEnergyBonus`,
`typeShareBonus`. D383's sentence was an optional-cost sentence and never entered that residue.

**BUDGET BY WHICH RESIDUE YOUR SENTENCE LEAVES, NOT BY THE LAST SLICE'S FILE COUNT.**

⚠️ **AND TWO DIFFERENCE-KEYED RUNGS WERE *MASKED*.** `censusAtHead.test.ts`'s `BUILT.attack - 922`
and `BUILT.attack - 922 - 252` sit in `it`s whose earlier assertions also moved, and vitest stops an
`it` at its first failure — so they stayed invisible until two rounds of fixes later. **FOUR full
suite runs to converge, and the last two each surfaced exactly one new rung. A CLEAN RUN AFTER A
ROUND OF FIXES IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE ROUND WAS COMPLETE; ONLY A GREEN RUN IS.**

### The two census instruments read different numbers, and neither is wrong

`sameEnergyBonus`, `exOnlyActive`, `sawkRequirementSplit` and `benchNamedBonus` run a **NINE**-entry
`READERS` array and read **364 / 1,255** resolving; `censusAtHead`, `torrentialPump` and
`moreEnergyBonus` run **TEN** (with `deriveAttackOptionalCostBoost`) and read **366 / 1,262**. A
slice that widens one of the nine moves both; a slice that widens only the tenth moves one. D384

Two were D384's own doing — the *"still refused at this head"* paragraphs in `effects.ts`, which

SOMEBODY FINALLY RE-READS THE ENUMERATION**, and the enumeration is what rots, not the count.

The face-up Prize row (**2 printings**) is the last member of the `You may … If you do,` family and

touches all of them and is a **RENAME** (D335's discriminator). **THAT CHOICE IS THE SLICE.**

## D383 — THE PAYOFF UNION: D381's reading widened at its CONSEQUENT, a price that was wrong in BOTH directions, and an adjacency rot that fired on a NARROWING (engine 0.287.0 → **0.288.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

D381 read *"You may {cost}. If you do, {payoff}"* with the payoff fixed at *"this attack does {N}
more damage."*. The catalog prints a SECOND payoff on the same skeleton, and it is not a bigger hit
but an ADDITIONAL one:

> **Wellspring Mask Ogerpon ex** `sv06-064` / `sv06-194` / `sv06-213` / `sv08.5-027` / `sv08.5-152`
> "Torrential Pump" ({W}{C}{C}, flat `100`, index 1 of two)
> *"You may shuffle 3 Energy attached to this Pokémon into your deck. If you do, this attack also
> does 120 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for
> Benched Pokémon.)"* — **5 legal printings**, one byte-identical record, and **the biggest single
> sentence left on the attack backlog at D382's head.**

### A WIDENED PAYOFF AND NOT AN ELEVENTH READER — AND THE ANCHOR DECIDED IT, NOT TASTE

D382 handed this over as an open shape question. The catalog answers it in one measurement:
`OPTIONAL_COST_BOOST` is `/^You may (.+)\. If you do, (.+)$/` and it **already matched this sentence
WHOLE** — only `optionalCostOps` and the payoff regex refused it.

🛑 **TWO READERS CANNOT SHARE AN ANCHOR.** Every reader in `effects.ts` is held to a disjointness
proof drawn from its LEADING WORDS, which is what lets `attack.ts` SUM its terms instead of choosing
between them. An eleventh reader of this sentence would have carried a byte-identical top-level
anchor to the tenth, so no leading word could ever have separated them and the sum would have had to
become a precedence. Both HALVES of the reading were already dispatch tables (D381's `retrieveNoun`
note), so the payoff becoming one is symmetry rather than generalisation.

⚠️ **AND THE PRICE DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** A new reader costs a read site in
`attack.ts` plus a disjunct in each of `scaledBase`, `effectSimulated` and `modifierSimulated` — three
insertions into chains that six mutation rows are anchored on. Widening inherits D381's wiring
instead. What it DOES owe is the narrowing of two of those three terms, and that toll is paid rather
than pretended away (see below).

### THE PRICE WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE — D199's LESSON, IN ONE ROW

D382 priced this row at three mechanisms. Two of them were the wrong size:

| D382 said | it actually is |
|---|---|
| *"a `to: "deck"` destination on `discardEnergy`"* | **ONE OPTIONAL VALUE** on a field D295 shipped |
| *"a Bench-snipe consequent"* | **ALREADY BUILT** — `damageChosen {target:"opponentBench", count:1, source:"attack", deals:true}` since 0.38.0 |
| *"a NEW `BoardCondition` for ≥3 Energy on this Pokémon"* | **exactly right, and the whole cost** |

🛑 **THE VICTIM IS THE ACTOR FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND D295's RULE HELD WITH NO BRANCH.** That field's
doc block says *"the destination is the VICTIM's zone, not the actor's, and that is why it is one
field and not a seat"* — written when every producer aimed at the OPPONENT, so victim and actor were
always opposite. Here `from: "yourActive"` makes them the SAME seat and the printed possessive is
*"your deck"*; `discardVictimSeat` returns the controller for that arm, so the rule needed no branch.
**A RULE WRITTEN WHERE IT COULD NOT BE WRONG HAS NOW BEEN TESTED ON THE CASE THAT COULD HAVE BROKEN
IT** — which is the mirror of D373's finding about `noEnergyOnYourPokemon`, one field over.

🛑 **AND THE PAYOFF ANCHOR SHARES A REGEX BODY WITH `ALSO_BENCHED_SNIPE`.** The printed clause is the
same clause `deriveAttackEffect` has read since 0.38.0, differing only in the CASE of the leading word
— because behind *"If you do, "* the sentence lowercases it (D246/D316's rule). So the body is a named
fragment now and the two anchors splice it with `^This ` and `^this `. That is D222's rule applied to
a printed clause: ONE reading of one sentence, so the two cannot drift, and widening the fragment
widens BOTH readers — which is the coupling both callers want.

### WHAT IT COST: ONE `BoardCondition` MEMBER, AND THE COMPARAND IS WHAT MAKES IT A NEW ONE

`yourActiveEnergyAtLeast { count }` — at least `count` Energy **CARDS**, **UNTYPED**, on the
**ACTOR'S OWN BODY**. All three siblings were priced first and each is wrong on exactly one axis:

* `yourActiveHasEnergyAttached` — right BODY, **TYPED and UNQUANTIFIED**;
* `yourEnergyInPlayAtLeast` — right QUANTIFIER, **whole SIDE and a type**; and its `energy` field is
  `BasicEnergyType | "special"`, which has **no `"Colorless"` member at all**, so it could not spell
  an untyped noun even with the zone narrowed;
* `yourBasicEnergyInDiscardAtLeast` — right quantifier, **wrong ZONE** and on the printed card class.

Adding a `count` to the first or narrowing the zone of the second is a RENAME of a shipped member with
live consumers, which D362 priced at 31 sites across 7 files and D365/D366 refused twice. **A WIDENING
IS FREE; A RENAME IS NOT.**

🛑 **AND IT IS SEPARATE FROM `activeEnergyCountsEqual` (D372), WHICH IS THE SECOND QUESTION THE RESUME
POINT ASKED.** Both count Energy on ONE body through the SAME call —
`countAttachedEnergy(state, pokemon, null)`, the unfiltered CARD count — so they share an
implementation and can never drift. What they do not share is the **COMPARAND**: this one measures a
body against a printed CONSTANT, that one against ANOTHER BODY. Folding them needs a member carrying
an operator and a comparand union — a GENERALISATION rather than a widening — and it would swallow a
shipped nullary member on the way. **ONE COUNTER, TWO COMPARANDS, TWO MEMBERS.** The catalog's third
reading of those same two operands (*"…has MORE Energy attached than your opponent's Active
Pokémon"*, 1 legal printing, still refused at this head) belongs with `activeEnergyCountsEqual` and
NOT here: it is that member with `===` replaced by `>`, which is one more argument for two members
rather than one — and it is now the cheapest row on the backlog.

### THE PRINTED BASE DOES NOT MOVE INSIDE THE GATE — AND THAT IS THE WHOLE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE

*"ALSO"* names a SECOND hit on a BENCHED body the main §8.5 hit never touches, so the flat `100` lands
in the pre-program pipeline whatever the player answers and the program carries only `[cost…, snipe]`.
Two consequences, and both invert D381:

1. **BOTH GATES CARRY NO `otherwise` AT ALL.** D381's two decline arms exist precisely because ITS
   payoff re-homes a printed base a decline must still deal (`140+`, not `+140`); here a decline and
   an unpayable cost genuinely buy nothing, so D135 makes the field ABSENT rather than `[]`.
2. **`scaledBase` AND `modifierSimulated` ARE NARROWED THROUGH ONE NAMED LOCAL**,
   `costBoostOwnsTheBase` — `coinExplainsModifier`'s idiom two blocks down, and for its reason: the
   reversed reading's two payoffs answer that question differently. Dropping the base for this payoff
   would silently delete a 100-damage attack on EVERY board including the declined one, which is
   D228's asymmetry reached through a reader instead of an op. `effectSimulated` needs no narrowing
   and gets none — the sentence is the whole printed effect under both payoffs, VERIFIED rather than
   copied.

⚠️ The `modifierSimulated` narrowing is **correctness in principle and not a live bug**: all five
printings carry a FLAT `100`, so no board in the catalog can tell the two answers apart. It is written
from D130's rule rather than from what a test would notice, exactly as D130 and D192 were, and it is
recorded in `mutants.ts` as a row deliberately NOT written.

### 🛑 THE ADJACENCY ROT FIRED A FOURTH TIME, ON A SHAPE IT HAD NOT FIRED ON BEFORE

D316, D317 and D381 were each broken by a slice **ADDING** a disjunct to one of those three chains.
D383 added nothing — it **NARROWED** an existing term to a named local — and **six multi-line `find`
strings died in exactly the same way, without a character of theirs being edited.**

**A MULTI-LINE `find` IS A CLAIM ABOUT ADJACENCY, AND A NARROWING FALSIFIES IT AS COMPLETELY AS AN
INSERTION DOES.** All six were re-transcribed in the same commit as the code and verified one decision
at a time (the flags do not accumulate — D382): D316 **15 killed / 0 errors**, D317 **16 killed + 1
declared survivor / 0 errors**, D381 **8 / 0**, D295 **4 / 0** (two rows now kill in two files), D275
**8 / 0** with the version anchor re-pointed at `0.288.0`.

### 🛑 AN UNREACHABLE-FALSE GATE IS A MEASUREMENT, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHAT BELONGS IN THE RECORD

`yourActiveEnergyAtLeast`'s gate **cannot be FALSE on any board the REAL printing can build in this
pool**. Torrential Pump costs {W}{C}{C} — three UNITS — and `countAttachedEnergy` counts **CARDS**, so
the two come apart only on a body holding a multi-unit Special. The two in this pool are Neo Upper
Energy (Stage 2 holders only) and Reversal Energy (Evolution, no Rule Box), and Wellspring Mask
Ogerpon ex is a **Basic WITH a Rule Box**.

The gate is kept anyway, for three reasons stated rather than assumed: D381's reading makes `cond`
**REQUIRED** because that is what the swap MEANS (inventing an always-true member would be strictly
worse); the anchor CAPTURES the digit, so the arity is not fixed at 3; and without the gate,
`discardEnergy`'s *"do as much as you can"* rule for a MANDATORY discard would shuffle whatever is
there and collect the whole printed 120.

Its false arm is therefore **DRIVEN FROM OUTSIDE THE POPULATION** — D379's own technique, applied to a
**BOARD** rather than to a reader: `torrentialPump.test.ts` §6 fields a LOCAL synthetic printing
differing on the ONE token the cost anchor captures (four instead of three), so the attack is declared
legally on three Energy cards and the offer cannot be paid. **WHEN A GATE LOOKS VACUOUS ON THE REAL
CARD, MEASURE WHY, SAY SO, AND DRIVE ITS FALSE ARM FROM OUTSIDE THE POPULATION.**

### The refusal list one file over had to move — D382's finding as a routine cost

`optionalCostBoost.test.ts`'s `STILL_OWED.energy` asserted this exact sentence REFUSED. The row is
moved into a `TAKEN_SINCE` that **ASSERTS IT RESOLVES**, so neither rung can go green by a successor
quietly shortening a refusal list — the repair D382 made to `stadiumPresence.test.ts`, arriving one
slice later as a cost that was expected rather than as a surprise. **A GUARD KEYED ON A REFUSAL HAS AN
EXPIRY DATE, AND WHOEVER EXPIRES IT OWNS THE REWRITE.**

**1** `BoardCondition` member, **1** optional VALUE on `discardEnergy.to` and on
`ENERGY_DISCARDED.to`, **1** cost row, **1** payoff row, **1** shared regex fragment, **1** assembler

**ZERO** new readers, ops, events, prompts, choice kinds, error codes, `GameState` fields, registry

`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 22**, asked rather than inherited and NOT trivially: `discardEnergy`

the RENAME counter-examples).

Census, **+1 sentence / +5 printings — the biggest single-sentence step this summand has taken since
D348**: resolving sentences 364 → **365**, raw 1,256 → **1,261**, `BUILT.attack` 1,285 → **1,290**,
unbuilt attack remainder 476 → **471**, whole-census `built` 1,686 → **1,691** and its residue 697 →
**692**, `FIXTURE_POOL` floor 470 → **471**.

⚠️ **THE MOVING SET WAS TEN FILES, AND A READER *WIDENING* MOVES A DIFFERENT SET THAN A READER

THAT REACHES A NEW BRANCH OF ONE** — D318's rule, third payment.

🆕 **AND A SEVENTH RUNG JOINED THE SET NO GREP REACHES**: the named-fraction ROUNDING in

## D382 — THE `. Then, ` JOIN: D317's shape with the printed comma changed, and a refusal guard whose instrument could not see the reader that expired it (engine 0.286.0 → **0.287.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

### The slice was CHOSEN by pricing three candidates against each other

D381's resume point named three and asked for a comparison rather than a pick. All three were
measured off `legalAttackCorpus()` before a line was written, and **the price moved in BOTH
directions**, which is the reason to write both halves down (D199: a `needs` column overstates as
easily as it understates).

|---|---|---|

✅ **AND THE 5-PRINTING ROW GOT CHEAPER IN ONE PLACE AT THE SAME TIME, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER
THAN LOST.** Its payoff op — `damageChosen {target:"opponentBench", amount:120, count:1,
source:"attack", deals:true}` — **already ships**. And because the payoff is a **SECOND HIT**
rather than a bigger one, the printed base need **NOT** move inside the gate at all: the extra
damage lands on a BENCHED body the main §8.5 hit never touches, so `boostedArms`, the `scaledBase`

The program is `optional{then:[cost…, damageChosen], otherwise:[]}` behind a payability gate.
**PRICE A PAYOFF BY WHAT IT HITS, NOT BY HOW BIG THE SENTENCE LOOKS.**

### The shape question: is `. Then, ` the same shape as `, and `?

Chi-Yu `sv06-039` "Ground Melter" ({R}{C}, `60+`, index 1 of two — confirmed by id against tcgdex,
which returns "Allure" ({C}, *"Draw 2 cards."*) at index 0) prints:

> *"If a Stadium is in play, this attack does 60 more damage. Then, discard that Stadium."*

**ONE legal printing**, and **all TEN readers returned null for it** at D381's head — measured, not
assumed. The catalog answered the shape question three ways:

1. **BOTH HALVES ARE ALREADY OWNED SEPARATELY.** The bare antecedent — *"If a Stadium is in play,
   this attack does 70 more damage."* — reads through `deriveAttackDamageBonus` into
   `{per, count: {boardCondition stadiumInPlay}}` and has since D378; the bare consequent's op is
   D380's `discardStadium`. **The JOIN is the only thing bought.**
2. **THE CONSEQUENT ATTACHES TO THE YES ARM UNDER EITHER JOIN.** *"Then,"* is a SEQUEL where
   *", and"* is a rider, and neither is reachable when the antecedent is false — so both fold into
   `boostedArms`'s `[damageDefender(base + bonus), ...ops]` with nothing to choose between them.
3. **A THIRD READER FOR A CHANGED COMMA IS THE DESIGN D317 REFUSED OUT LOUD** — *"a design under
   which two printings of one printed shape need two mechanisms is a design that has not found the
   shape."*

⚠️ **TWO NAMED ANCHORS AND NOT ONE ALTERNATION.** `(?:, and |\. Then, )` would have collapsed the
disjointness into a regex whose greed nobody can read off the page. Two constants keep the claim
**assertable**: one demands a literal `. ` where the other demands a literal `, ` at the same offset
in the same sentence, so no sentence can match both — asserted in BYTES and over the whole corpus —
and the `??` between them is an **ORDER-FREE FOLD** rather than a precedence. That is **DECLARED as
an equivalent mutant survivor rather than tested around**, and it is a live tripwire: widen either
anchor into the other's territory and the run reports `STALE-SURVIVOR`. Contrast the COIN/CONDITION
pair one line up, where the order IS load-bearing and D317 has a row saying so.

⚠️ **THE COIN FORM WAS NOT WIDENED**, and the catalog is why:
`/^Flip a coin\. If heads, this attack does (\d+) more damage\. Then, /` returns **ZERO** sentences
in the whole legal attack column. Writing that arm would be authoring a card (D190b: exact map or
flag). The zero is measured in the suite, not asserted in prose.

### The near miss is the CATALOG'S OWN, which is why nobody had to invent one

Ting-Lu `sv06-110` "Ground Crasher" prints the **SAME** antecedent, the **SAME** *"discard that
Stadium"* consequent **AND** the `, and ` join:

> *"If a Stadium is in play, this attack also does 30 damage to each of your opponent's Benched
> Pokémon, and discard that Stadium. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)"*

It is still **REFUSED**, because its middle clause is a **SECOND HIT** rather than a bonus. **A
reader widened at the JOIN rather than at the ANCHOR would have swallowed it.** The `discard that
Stadium` family is **2 sentences / 2 printings**; D382 claims **1 / 1** and leaves **1 / 1**, named
and driven (D381's rule: a reader slice is priced in refused sentences claimed, measured at BOTH
ends). **THE BEST ATTRIBUTION CONTROL IS THE ONE THE CATALOG ALREADY PRINTS.**

### The order was looked for and NOT found — and the failed search is the result

D381's rule says: when an order is *"obviously unobservable"*, go and look for the one card that
observes it. D382 looked. The only Stadium in `FIXTURE_POOL` whose presence moves a damage number is
Neutralization Zone `sv06.5-060`, which prevents damage only **from an attacking Pokémon ex** — and
Chi-Yu is a **Basic with no Rule Box**. Unlike D381, this suite drives the **REAL** printing, so
`isExOrV` cannot be talked into it by a fixture NAME the way `Fixceti ex` was. Beach Court moves a
retreat cost and Pokémon League Headquarters an attack COST, both settled before the program runs.

So the order (`[damageDefender(120), discardStadium]`, matching the printed *"does 60 more damage.
Then, discard"*) is claimed from the **PRINT** and pinned in the **ASSEMBLED PROGRAM** rather than
on a board — D130/D228's precedent, verbatim. **A LOOK THAT FINDS NOTHING IS STILL A RESULT:
RECORD IT, SO A PRINTING THAT *CAN* REACH IT IS A KNOWN COST RATHER THAN A SURPRISE.**

### 🛑 A refusal guard whose INSTRUMENT could not see the reader that expired it

This was not part of the slice; it was found by the slice reddening.

`stadiumPresence.test.ts` keeps a local `READERS` array and describes it as *"the nine live readers,
run as one — the same set `censusAtHead.test.ts` uses"*. It had **NINE** entries.
`deriveAttackOptionalCostBoost` shipped at **D381** and claims Cetitan ex's *"You may discard a
Stadium in play. If you do, this attack does 140 more damage."* — a sentence that file's
`DISCARD_OP` list **asserts is REFUSED**. For a whole slice the rung ran, passed, and was false.

The repair is three parts, all in one commit: the tenth reader is added; both residue lists are
re-partitioned; and a **`TAKEN_SINCE`** list holds the departed rows and **asserts them RESOLVED**,
so neither rung can go green by a successor quietly shortening a refusal list (D379's saturation
trap). The defect is re-installed as mutant `D382-refusal-instrument-loses-the-tenth-reader`.

**THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: WHEN YOU SHIP A READER, GREP FOR EVERY HAND-KEPT READER ARRAY IN THE SUITE,
NOT ONLY FOR THE CENSUS FIGURES.** `grep -rn "deriveAttackDamageSuppression," packages/engine/src/*.test.ts`
finds them all in one call, because every such array carries that entry. **A GUARD KEYED ON A
REFUSAL HAS AN EXPIRY DATE, AND WHOEVER EXPIRES IT OWNS THE REWRITE — INCLUDING THE INSTRUMENT THAT
MEASURES IT.**

### The `conditionGate` arm had never been reachable from `FIXTURE_POOL`

`grep -c "more damage, and " testFixtures.ts` returned **1** at D381's head, and that one hit is
`fix-bonusconsequent`'s **COIN** sentence. So `bonusConsequentProgram` has TWO arms — a
`coinFlipGate` for the coin decider and a `conditionGate` for the board-fact one — and for five
slices the second was reachable only from `bonusConsequent.test.ts`'s LOCAL pool, invisible to every
sweep that walks the shared pool. `fix-groundmelter` closes it: **D318's rule, paid one arm over.**
The suite measures the gap rather than asserting it, so it goes RED the day a second such card lands
— which is the correct moment for a successor to re-read the claim.

⚠️ **AND THE REAL ID CANNOT LIVE IN `FIXTURE_POOL`**: `catalogManifest.test.ts` diffs the `sv*` ids
in that pool against the 978-row / 6-set manifest, and `sv06` is in none of `sv01`, `sv02`, `sv03`,
`sv06.5`, `sve`, `swsh10.5`. **A real id outside those six belongs in a suite-LOCAL pool** (D275's
idiom) **and a demonstrator pays for the blind spot that buys.**

### What shipped, and what it cost

ONE anchor constant, ONE consequent row, ONE `FIXTURE_POOL` demonstrator, ONE 35-case suite.
**ZERO** new readers, `EffectOp` members, ops, events, prompt kinds, choice kinds, `BoardCondition`
members, `GameState` fields, error codes, registry rows or `packages/schema` bytes.
`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 22**, asked rather than inherited (D335's discriminator: no
`EffectOp` member at all, so every step the widened reading emits could already appear in a v22
record and no v22 byte string means anything different under this one).

Census step **+1 sentence / +1 printing**: raw 1,255 → **1,256**, `BUILT.attack` 1,284 → **1,285**,
resolving sentences 362 → **363**, unbuilt attack remainder 477 → **476**, whole-census `built`
1,685 → **1,686** and its residue 698 → **697**, `FIXTURE_POOL` floor 469 → **470**. Both
damage-clause residues stand still.

A DIFFERENT SET THAN A READER *ADDITION*.** D382 did NOT move `programWalk` (no new exported
assembler), `preventBlock` (no new `EffectOp` member) or `precociousEvolution`'s §2 reader-surface

a bare literal operand, and the three subtraction CHAINS all gain their new term at the **FRONT**.

✅ **AND NO MUTANT ROW ON `attack.ts`, WHICH IS A FACT ABOUT THE SLICE RATHER THAN AN OMISSION.**
This reading is D317's, already wired into `scaledBase`, `effectSimulated` and `modifierSimulated`,

## D381 — THE REVERSED OPTIONAL BOOST: D316's sentence with its two halves swapped, on *zero* new ops, and an order that exactly one Stadium in the pool can see (engine 0.285.0 → **0.286.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

D316 read *"You may do {N} more damage. If you do, {drawback}"* — the antecedent is the PAYOFF and
the consequent is the cost. This slice reads the same sentence the other way round: the antecedent is
the COST and the consequent is the extra damage it buys. **Cetitan ex `sv10-065`/`sv10-210` "Crushing
Press"** ({W}{W}{W}{C}, `140+`, the card's only attack, confirmed by id against tcgdex for both
printings) prints *"You may discard a Stadium in play. If you do, this attack does 140 more damage."*

### A READER SLICE IS PRICED IN REFUSED SENTENCES CLAIMED — MEASURE BOTH ENDS

Off `legalAttackCorpus()` with `/^You may .*If you do,/` the family is **7 sentences / 14 printings**,
of which **3 sentences / 9 printings were REFUSED at D380's head**. This reader claims **1 / 2** and
leaves **2 / 7**. That is the whole value of the slice and it is asserted at both ends in
`optionalCostBoost.test.ts` §1 — the "before" figure is re-derived by dropping this reader out of the
set rather than quoted from prose.

**Every mechanism the claimed sentence needs already shipped**: `discardStadium` is D380's,
`stadiumInPlay` is D378's, `optional` is D186's, `conditionGate` is older than all three. What the
slice buys is a READING, one exported assembler and one cost-table row.

### THE CATALOG DECIDED THAT IT IS A SEPARATE READER

The two shapes look like each other and are not. The family partitions by **which half is the cost**,
and the partition is TOTAL:

* all **four** forward sentences buy their bonus with a consequent that can ALWAYS be paid — shuffle
  yourself away, hurt yourself, forgo next turn's attack — so their reading needs no precondition and
  their `optional` needs no gate;
* all **three** reversed ones lead with a cost that can be **UNPAYABLE** — a Stadium to discard, three
  Energy to shuffle away, a face-down Prize to turn up.

**THE PRECONDITION IS NOT A FIELD ONE FAMILY HAPPENS TO WANT; IT IS WHAT THE SWAP MEANS.** So
`AttackOptionalCostBoost` carries a `cond` the forward reading would never populate, and the reversed
reading is the TENTH reader rather than a second anchor on the eighth.

### THE SATURATION TRAP, ARMED AND REFUSED

Both remaining printings carry a **trailing reminder parenthetical**, so a `\.$` anchor on the payoff
half would have refused them **BY ACCIDENT** — the suite would have read green while claiming nothing
about the mechanism, which is D379's saturation trap with the polarity flipped. The repair is to
**RE-PAIR EACH REFUSED HALF WITH A HALF THE READER DOES READ**, on synthetic sentences no card prints:

* `You may turn 1 of your face-down Prize cards face up. If you do, this attack does 140 more damage.`
  → null, so the refusal is the COST's (there is no face-up-Prize state on `PlayerState`);
* `You may discard a Stadium in play. If you do, this attack also does 120 damage to 1 of your
  opponent's Benched Pokémon.` → null, so the refusal is the PAYOFF's;
* …with a control that resolves, so a broken import cannot fake either.

### THE PRINTED ORDER IS OBSERVABLE, AND ONLY ONE STADIUM IN THE POOL CAN SEE IT

`boostedArms` emits `[damageDefender(base + bonus), ...ops]` — the hit first — because that is the
printed order for D316's sentence. This one prints discard-then-damage, and the difference is **not
cosmetic**: **Neutralization Zone `sv06.5-060`** (`preventDamageToNoRuleBoxFromExV`) prevents damage
to a Pokémon WITHOUT a Rule Box from an attacking Pokémon **ex** — and Cetitan ex is one. So on that
board the printed order deals **280** and the swapped order deals **0** and then discards the Stadium
that stopped it. **EVERY OTHER BOARD IN THE SUITE IS GREEN EITHER WAY.**

That is why the fixture is named **`Fixceti ex`** rather than defaulting to its id: `isExOrV` reads
the `Card.name`, and a fixture called `fix-crushpress` would have made the one discriminating board
unreachable and the order claim untestable. **WHEN AN ORDER LOOKS "OBVIOUSLY UNOBSERVABLE", GO LOOK
FOR THE ONE CARD THAT OBSERVES IT.**

⚠️ A vacated `hpDelta` Stadium moves a MAXIMUM between the two hits as well, but all three of those
printings are `sv08`/`sv10` and outside the six sets `CATALOG_MANIFEST` covers — so that half is
NAMED rather than driven (D205: a mutant for an unkillable claim is worse than no mutant).

### BOTH GATES CARRY AN `otherwise`, WHICH IS THE DIFFERENCE FROM D380

`optionalCostBoostProgram` builds `conditionGate(stadiumInPlay) → optional → [discardStadium,
damageDefender(base + 140)]`, with `damageDefender(base)` on the confirm's decline arm **and** on the
gate's empty-zone arm. D380's bare *"You may discard a Stadium in play."* has neither, correctly: its
whole printed content is the discard, so its field is ABSENT (D135). Crushing Press is `140+` and not
`+140`, so an absent arm on either gate silently deletes a 140-damage attack.

The `conditionGate` is also doing more work here than it did at D380: with no Stadium in play a bare
confirm offers a "yes" that discards NOTHING and still pays the printed **+140** — **a free 140**,
which is the stakeless-dialog defect with damage at stake.

### A PROGRAM THAT SHARES A BRANCH IS A DAG, AND EVERY AUDITOR HERE ASSUMES A TREE

The first draft handed **one** decline-arm array to both gates. Equal in value, correct at runtime,
green on every board in the new suite — and `programWalk.test.ts` went red by **exactly one**, because
that file accounts for the ops it reaches BY IDENTITY and a shared arm is *"already seen"* down the
outer path, so `structural − enumerated === missed.length` fails. The assembler now calls
`boostedArms` twice (spelled differently, so neither line is a mutation-`find` duplicate of the other)
and says why in its doc block. **AN INVARIANT THAT COUNTS OBJECTS IS AN INVARIANT ABOUT SHAPE, NOT
ABOUT VALUE.**

### ASK THE CENSUS TWICE — AND SHORTEN THE CONNECTIVE, NOT ONLY THE NOUN

D310/D311's rule is to re-run a census with the literal shortened to the part a PRONOUN cannot change.
The same rule applies to the JOINING WORDS. `/^You may .*If you do,/` returns **7 sentences / 14
printings**; `/^You may .*\. If /` returns **8 / 15**. The eighth is *"You may discard your hand. If
you discarded any cards in this way, this attack does 120 more damage."* (**1** printing) — the same
reversed shape with its consequent conditioned on the **COST's own effect** rather than on the answer,
which is a RECORD of what the cost did and not a board fact read before it. Refused, named and driven.

### THE TENTH READER IS GUARDED BY EXACTLY ONE RUNG, AND IT LIVES IN ANOTHER FILE

`censusAtHead.test.ts`'s `READERS` list is **hand-kept**, and nothing in that file notices a new
reader: a tenth reader that resolves printings would leave `BUILT.attack` undercounted and the whole
census green. The only thing between that and rot is `precociousEvolution.test.ts` §2, which builds
`EXPORTED_ATTACK_READERS` from the MODULE (`Object.entries(effects)`, `deriveAttack` prefix) and diffs
its own copy against it, then pins the COUNT. It fired at D316, D317 and now D381, and was re-pointed
rather than relaxed each time. Its stated limit is still real: **a reader added under a different name
is invisible to it.**

1 new reader, 1 exported assembler, 1 cost-table row, 1 fixture (`fix-crushpress` / `Fixceti ex`), 1
dedicated 60-card deck (`OPTIONAL_COST_BOOST_DECK`, six of EACH Stadium — a MARGIN, not a seed), 33
cases in `optionalCostBoost.test.ts`. **Zero** new `EffectOp` members, ops, events, prompts, choice
kinds, `BoardCondition` members, error codes or `packages/schema` bytes.

Census: raw 1,253 → **1,255**; `BUILT.attack` 1,282 → **1,284**; resolving sentences 362 → **363**;

**698**; `FIXTURE_POOL` floor 468 → **469**. **Both damage-clause residues UNMOVED.** Seven files

`bun run check`: **388 files / 8,098 tests, `CHECK_EXIT=0`**, measured twice. `--decision D381`:

## D380 — THE STADIUM-DISCARD OP: the first slice in this run that buys an `EffectOp` rather than a `BoardCondition`, and it is smaller than its name (engine 0.284.0 → **0.285.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

D379 saturated the *"…this attack does nothing."* skeleton and measured what was left. The
arithmetic — not a mood — ended the clause-row era in this corner: the bonus residue is **21
sentences / 25 printings** and FLAT, and it decomposes as **three non-singleton records carrying 7
printings** (D368's standing SHAPE refusal, printed at 100 and at 80 — *two* rows, which the handoff
prose did not say — plus the deferred HEALED flag) and **eighteen records carrying eighteen**. So
the best clause row still available is worth **ONE** printing. The Stadium-DISCARD family is worth
**ELEVEN**, and this slice takes **SIX** of them:

| printed sentence | printings | card |
|---|---|---|
| `Discard a Stadium in play.` | **4** | Hisuian Growlithe `sv06-099`/`sv06-181` "Blazing Destruction" (no cost, no damage), Skarmory `sv06-119` "Big Storm" ({C}{C}{C}, 90), Mow Rotom `sv10-009` "Trimming Mower" ({G}, 20) |
| `You may discard a Stadium in play.` | **2** | Wooloo `sv07-124` / Dubwool `sv07-125` "Knock Over" ({C}{C}, 30 and 70) |

### 🛑 An op priced against what the zone already does, not against its name

`playStadium` (cardplay.ts, §7.3) has written this whole transition since M4: the replaced Stadium
goes to its **OWNER's** discard pile, `STADIUM_DISCARDED` is emitted, and §8.1's mid-turn Knock-Out
sweep runs from the same site. `discardStadium` is that same move reached from the other direction,
so it adds **no event, no zone, no state key and no prompt** — `state.stadium` was already
`{uid, owner} | null` and the op writes the `null`. **THE TRANSFERABLE HALF: "a whole OP" read like
a milestone and cost less than D378's predicate. Read the zone's existing writer before you price
the reader.**

### The four SHAPE questions, answered from the catalog before anything was spelled

1. **`You may discard…` is neither a second op nor a flag — it is D186's `optional`, which already
   exists.** The printed sentence is the bare one with `You may ` in front and the verb lowercased.
   A field on the new op would have been a second confirm mechanism beside one that already owns a
   prompt kind, a choice kind and a dialog on both surfaces; and `optional`'s own doc names the test
   it passes — the wrapper is for an inner op with **no empty answer**, which a nullary discard is.
2. **An empty zone is THREE different things and the printed text says which.** Bare imperative → a
   silent no-op (§8.6). *"You may"* → a question that must **not be asked**, because `optional`
   parks unconditionally and a confirm whose two answers leave the identical board is a decision
   with no stake — hence a `conditionGate` on D378's `stadiumInPlay`, which costs a `cond` and
   nothing else. 🛑 *"…If you can't, this attack does nothing."* → a CANCEL, and **`stadiumInPlay`
   answers it on the BOARD FACT while the SKELETON still refuses it**: §7.3's zone is a singleton
   and nothing in this engine can make an occupied zone undiscardable, so *"you can't discard a
   Stadium in play"* IS *"the zone is empty"* — but `ATTACK_DOES_NOTHING` is anchored `^If` and
   Eternatus `sv08-141` "World Ender" prints its clause **TRAILING and ANAPHORIC**. **THE MEMBER WAS
   RIGHT AND THE READER WAS MISSING, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT REFUSAL FROM "NO VOCABULARY".**
3. **`discard that Stadium` needs no referent** — the singleton again: the antecedent tests the one
   Stadium and the tail discards the one Stadium, so the two remaining tail sentences will REUSE
   this op unchanged rather than widen it.
4. **The pile is the Stadium's OWNER's, not the actor's** — the same PRESENCE/OWNERSHIP line D378
   drew one union over, and the one that would have shipped green. An actor-routed op is correct on
   every board where the attacker played the Stadium and silently wrong on the boards this family is
   printed for. `stadiumDiscard.test.ts` §3 drives it with **P2** as owner and asserts P1's pile
   UNCHANGED, then drives the same op on a P1-owned Stadium so no hard-coded seat is green on both.

### ⚠️ The zone's departure is observed through a CONTINUOUS effect, not through a pile

An op that appended the uid and left the zone occupied — or nulled the zone and forgot the pile —
passes every uid assertion. Both halves are separate mutants (C2 and C3) because **neither claim
implies the other**. §3 therefore reads Beach Court's printed *"Basic Pokémon retreat cost {C}
less"* off a body that was already on the board: `effectiveRetreatCost` is 0 before the attack and
1 after.

### ⚠️ §8.1 is owed and is already paid by the caller — and it is NOT driven, which is said rather than skipped

Vacating the zone can LOWER a maximum (Lively Stadium `sv08-180`, +30 to every Basic in play), and
§8.1's Knock Out is a state check on `damage ≥ maximum` rather than an event of the thing that moved
the number — exactly why `playStadium` ends in `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts`. This op needs no sweep of
its own: an ATTACK is swept by `finishAttack`'s `collectKnockOuts` over BOTH seats, and every other
program folds through `settleProgram` → `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts`. **THE SWEEP IS A PROPERTY OF
PROGRAM COMPLETION, NOT OF AN OP** (D176's rule, one op over). ⚠️ **No board this pool can build
makes a vacated zone lethal**: all three `hpDelta` Stadiums are `sv08`/`sv10` and outside the six
sets `CATALOG_MANIFEST` covers, so `FIXTURE_POOL` cannot hold one and `hpAura.test.ts` reaches them
only through a LOCAL `cardPool`. A mutant row for that claim would be unkillable, which is worse
than no row (D205), so none was written.

raw 1,247 → **1,253**, `BUILT.attack` 1,276 → **1,282**, resolving sentences 360 → **362**, the

706 → **700**, the `FIXTURE_POOL` floor 466 → **468**. **Both residues stand still** — this slice

## D379 — THE EXACT HAND-SIZE READ: the last sentence behind the does-nothing skeleton, and the first member the bonus consequent did not pay for (engine 0.283.0 → **0.284.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 22**)

D378 handed this over as the ONE printed does-nothing opener no `ATTACK_REQUIREMENT_CLAUSES` row
carried, with the shape question already half-measured. The answer held: **ONE new PARAMETERISED
`BoardCondition` member, `yourHandExactly { count }`, ONE clause row, TWO reader arms, ZERO new
imports.**

| printed sentence | consequent | `BoardCondition` | card | printings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `If you don't have exactly 3 cards in your hand, this attack does nothing.` | CANCEL | `yourHandExactly { count: 3 }` | Alolan Dugtrio `sv08-123` / `sv08-208` "Trio-Cheehoo" (**no Energy cost**, 120) | 2 |

✅ **THE SKELETON IS EMPTY.** The requirement table goes 9 rows / 8 reachable / 16 printings →
**10 / 9 / 18**, and the unmapped remainder 1 sentence / 2 printings → **0 / 0**. Every
*"If <clause>, this attack does nothing."* opener the legal attack column prints is now read, so
the next move on that rung has to come from a **set rotation** rather than from a slice.

### Both consequents were asked again — and the bonus side is EMPTY, which is a first

D363 (Sawk), D365 (Iron Boulder), D377 (Centiskorch) and D378 (Fan Rotom) each bought a member
that BOTH clause tables read, and the last two turned on that. Measured over
`legalAttackCorpus()`: the column prints **no own-hand exact read under a "+N more damage"
consequent at all**, so all 2 printings arrive through the cancel table and `yourHandExactly` has
no `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` twin.

> **Reusable form:** asking both consequents is still right. The answer is sometimes ZERO, and a
> measured zero is a result — it is what says the member was bought by the half that pays for it,
> rather than that nobody looked at the other half.

### The shape question: a single `count`, and the CATALOG chose it

Both shapes were already in the union one family over — `opponentPrizesRemaining { counts }` is
**set membership** because the pool prints *"exactly 3 or 4 Prize cards"*; `opponentHandAtMost
{ count }` is a **threshold**. Asked of the hand column at this head:

* *"exactly 3"* is the **only** own-hand exact read in the whole legal attack column;
* there is **no own-hand disjunction** — every `exactly N or M` in the column is the Prize one;
* there is **no own-hand threshold** — every *"or fewer cards in …"* clause reads *their* hand.

So a single `count` is what the pool warrants, and a `counts` list would be reachability nobody
prints (D377's arithmetic). ⚠️ **WHAT WOULD FLIP IT IS A PRINTED OWN-HAND DISJUNCTION, NOT A
SECOND VALUE** — a second printing at *"exactly 5"* flips nothing, because that is the axis
`count` already varies on. That is D119's own reason for `opponentHandAtMost`'s parameter, and
the catalog vindicated it when Mienshao printed a second threshold.

### An ADDITION, not a widening, because the near miss is wrong TWICE

D365 recorded that `opponentHandAtMost` is the wrong **SEAT** *and* the wrong **COMPARATOR**, and
both halves are real: `players[otherSeat(seat)]` against `<=` where this needs `players[seat]`
against `===`. **No parameterisation of a threshold yields an equality, and no seat argument
makes one member answer both printed sentences** — so this is an addition and D366's open
seat-parameter question is not even reachable from here.

`exactHandSize.test.ts` §4 fields Trio-Cheehoo and Absol ex `sv03-135` "Cursed Slug" on **one
state** — P1 holding four cards, P2 holding three. Trio-Cheehoo **cancels**; Cursed Slug pays its
**+120** (100 → 220). Two printed sentences about a hand, two seats, two answers, one board.

### Strict equality is not the usual polarity in this corner — the boundary is a CURVE

The skeleton owns the printed *"don't"*, so the stored fact is *"you have exactly 3"*. `>=` is
green on a 3-card hand and wrong on a 4-card one; `<=` is green on a 3-card hand and wrong on a
2-card one. **Both are green on the only board a suite asked for "exactly 3" tends to build.**
§4 attacks with 2, 3 and 4 in hand and lands 120 on exactly one; §3 sweeps 0…7 and requires the
true set to be `[3]`.

> **Reusable form:** when a member's comparator is an equality, assert the WHOLE curve, not the
> true point. A suite that only drives the satisfying board cannot tell `===` from `>=` or `<=`.

D378 predicted that building this sentence would empty `splitOrder.test.ts` §4's `unmapped`

**THE TRADE IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** It costs the guards their catalog provenance — one
assertion literally inverts from *"the corpus prints this"* to *"the corpus does not"* — and it
buys a defect no printed sentence could express: `ATTACK_REQUIREMENT_CLAUSES` is keyed on a
**literal**, so a table "simplified" into a `\d+` pattern would MAP the near-miss and strip a
companion sentence nothing had answered. `attackRequirement.test.ts` has now been re-aimed **four
times in four slices**, and this is the last one: **a constructed near-miss has no expiry date,

Both `REFUSED` arrays (`requirementFloor.test.ts`, `benchCountRequirement.test.ts`) are now

With `unmapped` empty, a `deriveAttackRequirement` that answered **everything** would satisfy

> **Reusable form:** when a coverage rung reaches 100%, add the refusal in the same commit.
