|---|---|---|---|---|
| `If a Stadium is in play, this attack does 70 more damage.` | BONUS | `stadiumInPlay` | Probopass `sv10-098` "Mountain Drop" ({C}{C}{C}, 70+) | 1 |
| `If there is no Stadium in play, this attack does nothing.` | CANCEL | `stadiumInPlay` | Fan Rotom `sv07-118` / `sv08.5-085` "Assault Landing" ({C}, 70) | 2 |

✅ **THE CANCEL HALF IS THE BIGGER HALF, WHICH IS A FIRST.** D363 (Sawk), D365 (Iron Boulder)
and D377 (Centiskorch) each put one member in both clause tables with the BONUS consequent
carrying the weight. Here it is **1 printing under the bonus and 2 under the cancel** — and the
purchase empties all but ONE sentence from behind the *"…this attack does nothing."* skeleton.

### The shape question: `yourStadiumInPlay` was NOT widened, and the printed bytes settle it

`yourStadiumInPlay` reads §7.3 **OWNERSHIP** and has **two live consumers whose ownership is
load-bearing** — registry `FALKNER` and the positive `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row *"you have
a Stadium in play"* (Palossand `sv02-096` "Earthen Power", +80). **A widening is free exactly
when every existing consumer wants the wider reading** (D362); neither of these does, so
yours→any is a **RENAME**. This is the SECOND time that exact widening has been priced — D364
declined it in prose and shipped nothing; D378 declines it by **building the member it would
have been mistaken for**.

🛑 **AND IT IS SETTLED WITHOUT A JUDGEMENT CALL, BECAUSE THE POSSESSIVE IS PRINTED.** Palossand
says *"**you have** a Stadium in play"*; Probopass says *"**a** Stadium is in play"* and Fan
Rotom says *"there is **no** Stadium in play"*. Neither new sentence carries a possessive at all.
`stadiumPresence.test.ts` §4 fields Probopass and Palossand on **ONE state** with the Stadium
played by P2 and reports both numbers side by side: **+70 PRESENT, +80 ABSENT.**

> **Reusable form:** when a new sentence looks like an existing member with the qualifier
> removed, the question is never whether the member's NAME could stretch. It is whether every
> consumer of that member wants the wider answer — and the printed possessive usually decides it
> before you have to ask.

### ✅ The first Stadium member that does NOT widen the P4 gap

`BoardCondition`'s own invariant paragraph says the online projection *"does NOT carry the
Stadium's owner"*, which is what makes `yourStadiumInPlay` unevaluable on a remote client.
`RedactedBoard.stadium` (packages/schema) is a `redactedCardSchema.nullable()` — the CARD, public
to both viewers, with **no owner field anywhere on it** — so `stadiumInPlay` is literally
`board.stadium !== null` on the wire. **Presence is the half that survives redaction; ownership
is the half that does not.** Two members already carry that note the other way round
(`opponentPrizesRemaining`, `youGoSecond`); this is the third and the first in the §7.3 corner.

It is the **first member in the union whose answer is seat-INDEPENDENT**, because §7.3's zone is
a shared singleton: two seats can disagree about whose Stadium it is and never about whether one
is there. §3 sweeps all three zone states, requires the two seats to AGREE on presence, and
**counts the two boards where ownership disagrees** — which is what stops the sweep being a fact
about a suite that never filled the zone.

Two more legal sentences read this board fact and both carry a tail: *"…does 60 more damage.

## D388 — THE RETREAT-COST THRESHOLD: one printed noun phrase, two live readings, and the shape question settled before a line was written (engine 0.292.0 → **0.293.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **unchanged at 23**)

Talonflame `sv07-123` "Aero Chase" ({C}{C}, `110+`, **+110**, index 0 of ONE attack), **1 legal
printing**: *"If the Retreat Cost of your opponent's Active Pokémon is {C}{C} or more, this attack
does 110 more damage."*

D387 measured this as the cheapest thing in the whole residue (**1 printing / 2 mechanisms = 0.50**)
and **deliberately did not take it**, on D368's rule rather than on price: its SHAPE question was
open. Settling that question turned out to be the entire slice.

### The shape question: TWO live readings of ONE printed noun phrase, and they disagree on real boards

`retreatCostOf(card)` (cards.ts) is the printed {C} column — literally `card.retreat ?? 0`.
`effectiveRetreatCost(state, pokemon)` (continuous.ts, D322) is the board fold: printed **+**
`stadiumRetreatDelta` **+** `opposingRetreatSurcharge` **−** `alliedRetreatDiscount`, under ONE
`Math.max(0, …)`, with `hasFreeRetreatAura` / `hasFreeRetreatSelf` short-circuiting to 0.

**Both were already implemented and both already had consumers**, so this was never *"which do I
build"* but *"which does the sentence NAME"*. They disagree on every board carrying a retreat Stadium
or a retreat aura, and this pool holds four such levers (Calamitous Wasteland `sv02-175`, Beach Court
`sv01-167`, Spidops ex `sv01-019`, Clefable ex `sv03-082`).

**THE FOLD WAS TAKEN, ON THREE GROUNDS:**

1. 🛑 **THE ENGINE HAD ALREADY ANSWERED THIS EXACT NOUN PHRASE.**
   `DamageCountSource.opponentActiveRetreatCost` (D110) reads *"for each {C} in your opponent's
   Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost"* and attack.ts resolves it through `effectiveRetreatCost`, with a
   comment saying so: *"a Stadium that changes what it costs to retreat changes what these attacks
   hit for"*. **D159 forbids a second answer to a question the engine already answers**, and a
   printed reading here would have made one printed noun phrase mean two different things in two
   readers of one file. ⚠️ **THE GENERAL MOVE, AND IT COST ONE GREP**: before arguing a shape
   question from the rules, grep for the PHRASE and see whether this engine has already answered it.
2. **THE RULES MAKE RETREAT COST A CURRENT VALUE.** `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §11 defines the cost off
   the printed symbols and records that effects reduce it, but is **silent** on what a card TEXT
   naming *"the Retreat Cost"* reads — so this went to the web (D373's route). The official account
   states an **order of operations** over the value: increases apply first, then reductions, and a
   Pokémon left with no Retreat Cost by an effect overrides every increase. Both halves are already
   inside `effectiveRetreatCost`. **A printed constant would need no order of operations at all.**
3. 🛑 **AND IT IS THE READING WITH A FALSIFIER.** Flipping the arm to the printed column turns **FIVE
   cases RED, in BOTH directions** — measured by doing it before the build was trusted, and reverted
   by copy-back rather than by git (the tree-mutation rule).

### The disagreement is DRIVEN in both directions, and §3 alone would not have been enough

A guard that only exercises boards where the two readings AGREE is the vacuous guard this repo keeps
rediscovering (D200 → D214). So:

* **§3, the fold LARGER, on TWO different summands.** A printed-{C} defender under **Calamitous
  Wasteland** (the Stadium term) folds to {C}{C} and pays **220** where the printed column says 110;
  the same body under a **BENCHED Spidops ex** (the aura term — its printed sentence scopes only the
  TARGET, so a benched holder still imposes it) does the same **with no Stadium in play at all**.
  ⚠️ **THE SECOND RUNG IS WHAT KEEPS THE FINDING FROM BEING A FACT ABOUT THE SHARED STADIUM ZONE.**
* **§4, the MIRROR, and it is not decoration.** A printed-{C}{C} defender under **Beach Court** folds
  to {C} and pays **110** where the printed column says 220. **A wrong build reading `printed + 1` is
  green on all of §3 and red here.**
* **The sharpest single board:** the two Stadiums REPLACE each other in the shared zone, so ONE
  printed body answers TRUE → FALSE → TRUE across one game while `retreatCostOf` never moves. ⚠️ The
  engine refused the first draft with `STADIUM_ALREADY_PLAYED` (§7.3 allows one Stadium play per
  turn), so the swap costs two `endTurn`s — left as a line of play rather than surgeried around.

🛑 **AND EVERY DISAGREEMENT RUNG ASSERTS THE TWO READINGS RETURN DIFFERENT NUMBERS ON THAT BOARD
BEFORE IT READS ANY DAMAGE.** That is D214's **attribution control** applied to a pair of READINGS
rather than to a build artifact, and it is what stops a board where the two happen to agree posing as
a driven disagreement. **This is the transferable shape for any future two-reading clause.**

### A printing count inherited from a doc comment was wrong, and only the corpus saw it

`effects.ts` described the sibling retreat family as *"FOUR legal printings"*. `legalAttackCorpus()`
says the noun phrase *"…Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost"* is worth **SIX** legal printings across five
sentences, of which **TWO resolve** (both through the fold) and **three** are the SUBTRACTIVE twins
(*"30 less"* ×2, *"50 less"* ×1) sitting in a different residue. The comment was naming four **CARDS**
— Heracross, Spidops ex, Sharpedo, Stoutland — one of which has since **rotated** (`legal_standard =
0`). **A CARD LIST AND A PRINTING COUNT ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS, AND A DOC COMMENT AGES INTO THE WRONG
ONE SILENTLY.** Corrected in effects.ts, interpreter.ts and index.ts. This is D367's
perishable-uniqueness finding one field over: nothing in the suite was keyed on the four.

### `>=` and not a set, and the neighbour is not a precedent

`>=` is the printed *"or more"* — `yourBenchAtLeast`'s and `yourEnergyInPlayAtLeast`'s reading, **not**
`opponentPrizesRemaining`'s set membership. That member may enumerate because `prizes.length` is 0-6
and CLOSED (§3.8); a Retreat Cost has no such bound — printed values run to 5 and the Stadium/aura
terms are unbounded sums — so D365's warning runs the usual way: a member whose fold is
`counts.includes(…)` cannot be handed a threshold.

⚠️ **AND `opponentActiveHasResistance` (D371) ONE LINE UP IS NOT A PRECEDENT FOR READING THIS ONE
PRINTED.** That member reads `Card.resistances` directly — but this engine holds **no**
Resistance-modifying continuous effect at all (measured: continuous.ts carries `seatRemovesWeakness`
and no sibling for Resistance), so there is no fold there to decline. **The two members read the
opponent's Active's other printed columns and read them differently, and the reason is the CATALOG's,
not the code's.**

### The census — the moving set was TWENTY-TWO files, and SIX rungs were masked

Bonus residue **18 / 21 → 17 / 20** in sixteen suites; band `{1: 16, 5: 1}` → **`{1: 15, 5: 1}`**;
nine-reader **366 / 1,258 → 367 / 1,259** and ten-reader **369 / 1,266 → 370 / 1,267**;
`BUILT.attack` **1,295 → 1,296**; whole-census `built` **1,696 → 1,697**; apostrophe census
**43 → 44** (the BEARING half took the whole step, second slice running); fixture floor
**477 → 480**.

🛑 **SIX rungs were MASKED behind an earlier failure in the same `it`** and took four targeted
re-runs: `BUILT.attack - 922`, `- 922 - 252`, whole-census `built`, `units - built`, the leading
literal in the unbuilt-remainder chain, and `head - rawDelta - splitDelta`.

⚠️ **AND ONE MOVER WAS NOT ABOUT RETREAT AT ALL.** `stage1Bonus.test.ts` §1's *"Evolutions that are
not Stage 1"* population went **24 → 25**, because `fix-aerochase` is a **Stage 2 with a named
`evolveFrom`**. **That rung carries a fact about the WHOLE POOL, not about its own deck** — which is
exactly why it is derived live rather than frozen, and the only reason the cross-effect was visible.

### Two process traps, both cheap to avoid

1. **A VARIABLE NAME IS NOT A SCOPE.** A regex that bumped every `refused.length + N` across the
   residue files also moved THREE **CANCEL**-residue chains that had not moved at all — both rung
   kinds build a local named `refused`. The repair keyed on the const's own initialiser
   (`NOTHING.test` versus `BONUS.test`). **If you rewrite offset chains mechanically, key on what
   BUILDS the value, never on its name.**
2. **A MUTANT THAT CANNOT RUN IS NOT A MUTANT THAT WAS CAUGHT.** C1's first draft spelled the
   rejected reading as `retreatCostOf(spot.card)` — but interpreter.ts does not import it, so the
   mutant would have died on a **ReferenceError** before reaching a board, and **a KILLED verdict
   reads the exit code, not the failure message**. Re-spelled inline as `spot.card.retreat ?? 0`,
   which is that function's exact body. **Ask of every mutant: would this compile and run?**

### The IDs — a web measurement, the sixteenth slice running, with one tooling gotcha

A limitlesstcg `text:` search on the full clause **returned 0 cards**, because a `{C}{C}` glyph in the
query is split by the tokeniser. ⚠️ **DROP THE BRACES AND INTERSECT TWO SEARCHES INSTEAD**: `text:"If
the Retreat Cost of your opponent's Active Pokémon is"` returns 11 cards across a decade of sets and
`text:"or more, this attack does 110 more damage"` returns 16; **the intersection is exactly one —
Talonflame, SCR 123 (= `sv07-123`)**. `https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/sv07-123` then returned the
name, the 140 HP, the `Stage2` stage, the `Colorless` type, the {C}{C} cost, the `110+` base and the
effect text byte for byte, at **index 0 of ONE attack**. ⚠️ `compendium.pokegym.net` returns **403**
to WebFetch — its rulings are reachable only through search snippets and Bulbapedia, which is where
the order-of-operations statement came from. ⚠️ **THE WEB STILL CANNOT GIVE A LEGAL-PRINTING COUNT**;
that is `legalAttackCorpus()`'s alone.

## D389 — THE OPPONENT-SEAT BENCH COUNT: the seat-parameter question, settled on a re-measurement (engine 0.293.0 → **0.294.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 23**)

**BUILT.** Iron Crown `sv08-132` "Deleting Slash" ({M}{C}, `40+`, **+80**, index 0 of TWO),
**1 legal printing**: *"If your opponent has 3 or more Benched Pokémon, this attack does 80 more
damage."* ONE parameterised `BoardCondition` member (`opponentBenchAtLeast { count }`) with TWO
exhaustive-switch arms, ONE literal `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, ONE fixture
(`fix-deletingslash`), ONE dedicated 60 (`OPPONENT_BENCH_COUNT_DECK`) and ONE 24-case suite
(`opponentBenchCount.test.ts`). **ZERO new card predicates** — `bench` is a dense `InPlayPokemon[]`
and its `length` IS the count.

### 🛑 THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING: D388's §1 MOVE APPLIES TO A *SHAPE*, NOT ONLY TO A NOUN PHRASE

D388 settled a two-reading noun phrase by grepping for whether the engine had already answered it.
The same move settles a **SHAPE** question, and it settled the oldest one this run carried.

The question — a second `BoardCondition` member, or a `seat` parameter on `yourBenchAtLeast`? — had
been open since D362 and deferred for sixteen slices, and this candidate was the strongest case a
parameter had ever had here: it differs from the shipped member in the **SEAT ALONE**. (Contrast
D379's hand-size pair, which differed in the seat **AND** the comparator — two independent defects,
so an addition was forced and no judgement was needed.)

**ONE GREP ANSWERED IT.** `BoardCondition` holds **49 members and NOT ONE carries a seat field**, and
it holds **THREE pairs that differ in the seat alone**, each shipped as a second member:

  • `yourActiveDamaged` / `opponentActiveDamaged`
  • `yourActivePoisoned` / `opponentActivePoisoned`
  • `yourActiveHasToolAttached` / `opponentActiveHasToolAttached`  (D369)

D369's block on the last of those already argues the point in as many words: *"NOT written as a
recursive call on the twin with the seat flipped: `conditionHolds` is seat-RELATIVE, so 'the other
seat's own Active' is exactly what the twin would answer for a caller that passed the other seat —
and there is no caller that does."*

⚠️ **BEFORE ARGUING A SHAPE FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES, GREP FOR WHETHER THIS ENGINE HAS ALREADY CHOSEN
ONE.** A question a whole slice had been budgeted for had a precedent three deep.

### ⚠️ AND THE PRICE MUST BE RE-MEASURED IN *BOTH* DIRECTIONS

D387 caught a price quoted forward that had **shrunk** on contact (D362's 31 sites became three
mechanisms once the SET relation was distinguished from the BUILD relation). The handoff here was
explicit that D362's number might collapse again, because `yourBenchAtLeast` has ONE clause row and
TWO arms. **It did not.**

Measured at this head: **35 occurrences across 10 files, of which 22 are EXECUTABLE** — 20 `kind:`
literals and 2 exhaustive-switch arms — across **5 files** (`benchCountRequirement.test.ts` 14,
`benchTypeBonus.test.ts` 2, `effects.ts` 2, `interpreter.ts` 2, `scripts/mutation/mutants.ts` 2). The
remaining 13 are prose in doc blocks.

🆕 **THE INSTRUMENT, STATED SO THE NEXT SLICE DOES NOT INVENT ONE:**

```
grep -rn 'kind: "<member>"' --include=*.ts .   # the EXECUTABLE sites — what a rename costs
grep -rn '<member>' --include=*.ts .           # the total — what a rename READS LIKE
```

The two differ by a factor of ~1.6 here. **ONLY THE FIRST IS A PRICE.** A doc-block mention is a
paragraph to update, not a site that can break.

### 🛑 THE GROUND THAT ACTUALLY SETTLED IT: THE NOTE IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE PER SEAT

The arithmetic above says a parameter is expensive. It does **not** say it is wrong. What does:

`conditionNote` renders a **DIFFERENT PRINTED SENTENCE PER SEAT** — *"you have 3 or more Benched
Pokémon"* against *"your opponent has 3 or more Benched Pokémon"*. A `seat` field therefore does not
delete the second body; it moves two strings into a branch inside one arm, and pays the rename on
top. **THE SECOND MEMBER IS STRICTLY CHEAPER, NOT MERELY MORE CONVENTIONAL.**

⚠️ **AND THE NEW MEMBER'S NOTE IS A FULL ROUND TRIP** — byte-identical to its own
`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` key, which the twin's can never be, because D116 makes the table resolve
the printed pronoun and the two seats print different subjects. **WHEN A NOTE ROUND-TRIPS TO ITS OWN
KEY, ASSERT IT**: it is a free tripwire on the pair of tables and it names, in one line, why the seat
is not a field.

**GENERAL FORM:** *when deciding whether a distinction is a FIELD or a MEMBER, ask what the RENDERER
has to say. A field that the renderer must branch on anyway has bought nothing.*

### ⚠️ A RE-POINTING IS A RENAME UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE — SO PROVE IT EITHER WAY

D365 recorded that rule and D366 reproduced it, but **this run had never actually tested it**. A
refusal is only worth its evidence, so §1 drives **every live consumer of the shipped member on a
board**, even though nothing was re-pointed: its clause row still derives to
`{ kind: "yourBenchAtLeast", count: 5 }`, `conditionHolds` still answers on a five-body Bench,
`conditionNote` still returns its own sentence, and neither reaches this slice's key. Then the two
members are driven APART on one board.

### 🛑 THE SEAT DEFECT IS INVISIBLE ON A SYMMETRIC BOARD

The mistake an author actually makes is `state.players[seat].bench.length`, copied down verbatim from
the twin one case up (D190b: the real defect is always a neighbour's real code). It is **GREEN on
every board where the two Benches happen to match**, which is every symmetric board a suite tends to
build — D380's defect, one field over. The shape that refuses it:

  • **P1 FULL / P2 EMPTY** — the clause must be FALSE and the attack must deal the bare 40, while the
    twin says TRUE on the very same board and the very same seat;
  • **THE MIRROR (P1 EMPTY / P2 FULL)** — TRUE, 120, twin FALSE, so a build that read the seats
    backwards is red on one of the two rather than green on both;
  • **ONE BOARD, TWO SEATS** — `conditionHolds(state, "p1", …)` and `conditionHolds(state, "p2", …)`
    must DISAGREE, which is what `otherSeat(seat)` means and what a hard-coded `"p2"` fails;
  • **AND THE AGREEMENT BOARD, NAMED AS SUCH** (both Benches at 3) — so the case where the two
    members coincide is measured rather than absent.

## D390 — THE OPPONENT-SEAT IN-PLAY TYPE READ: an ANCHOR question, and a guard shipped one commit ahead of the thing it guards (engine 0.294.0 → **0.295.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **stays 23**)

**BUILT.** Electivire `sv05-054` "Short-Circuit Knuckle" ({C}{C}, `40+`, **+120**, index 0 of TWO),
**1 legal printing**: *"If your opponent has any {W} Pokémon in play, this attack does 120 more
damage."* ONE parameterised `BoardCondition` member (`opponentInPlayHasType { type }`) with TWO
exhaustive-switch arms and ONE anchored TEMPLATE (`OPPONENT_IN_PLAY_TYPE_CLAUSE`) reusing
`CLAUSE_POKEMON_TYPES` whole — the family's **FIFTH** parameterised clause and that map's **FIFTH**
consumer. ONE fixture (`fix-shortcircuit`), TWO bodies (`fix-waterbody`, `fix-inplaydual`), ONE
dedicated 60 (`IN_PLAY_TYPE_DECK`) and TWO suites (`clauseTemplateAnchors.test.ts`, 8 cases;
`inPlayTypeBonus.test.ts`, 23). **ZERO new vocabulary and ZERO new card predicates.**

### 🛑 THE TRANSFERABLE FINDING: WRITE THE GUARD IN THE COMMIT *BEFORE* THE THING IT GUARDS

`boardConditionForClause` consults the literal table and then **four anchored template patterns in
order**, and every one of the four carries a comment saying, in almost the same words, *"the patterns
are mutually exclusive at their anchors, so order decides nothing; appending keeps that true by
construction."*

That is a claim about the **whole set**, it was written four times, and **not one line of the suite
executed it**. It is exactly the shape `conventions.md`'s "A guard must be able to go RED" is about —
and worse than the usual case, because of *how* a fifth pattern falsifies it:

> **AN OVERLAPPING PATTERN IS INVISIBLE FROM OUTSIDE.** If pattern 5 can claim a clause pattern 2
> owns, nothing observable changes: pattern 2 still runs first, still matches, still returns the
> right member. The defect only surfaces when somebody reorders the chain, or when pattern 2 declines
> at its vocabulary and pattern 5 quietly answers instead — with a **different member** for a clause
> that had a correct one.

So the rung was written and **committed at the previous head**, with this slice's shape carried as a
row at `cond: null`. That ordering is not ceremony: **a guard written after the code can only ever be
fitted to it.** The file also became the tripwire that fires the day the shape is built, and it fired
on the very next commit.

**HOW THE CROSS PRODUCT IS DRIVEN.** Every pattern is `^<head><token><tail>$`, so the falsifiable
question is whether pattern *j*'s tail can be reached from pattern *i*'s head. The table carries each
pattern's head, token, tail, printed amount and printing count — so each row is authored from the
catalog (D183) and §1 re-derives the counts off `legalAttackCorpus()`. §2 builds all **N×(N−1) = 20**
hybrids and requires each to be REFUSED **and** to be absent from the corpus, so a refusal can never
be refusing something the catalog actually prints.

**THE RED WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED.** Loosening `YOUR_BENCH_TYPE_CLAUSE` from
`^you have any (.+) Pokémon on your Bench$` to `^you have any (.+) Pokémon` makes §2 fail on the exact
pair that overlapped; `effects.ts` was then restored by hand (never `git checkout`) and `git diff`
confirmed empty. D390's mutant **C6** is the same defect on the new pattern — its ` in play$` tail
dropped — and the cross-product rung is what kills it.

### ⚠️ AND THE FOUR COMMENTS OVERSTATED THEIR OWN SCOPE — THE CORRECTION IS THE HALF WORTH KEEPING

*"Order decides nothing"* is **true of the templates against each other** and **false of the resolver
as a whole**. The templates are not disjoint from the **literal table above them**:
*"your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Stage 1 Pokémon"* matches `OPPONENT_ACTIVE_TYPE_CLAUSE` (the
capture is "Stage 1", which reaches `CLAUSE_POKEMON_TYPES` and misses) **and** is a
`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row (D387) — and the row wins **only because the literal pass runs
first**. That is the resolver's one genuine ordering dependency, and it is now pinned in a rung of its
own, separate from the cross product, so a successor cannot read a true sentence about the templates
as a claim about the function.

### 🛑 THE ZONE IS THE MEMBER, AND IT IS WRONG IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS

* **Narrowing to the opponent's Active Spot** is D279's refutation with a TYPE. The printed words are
  "in play", so a {W} body on the opponent's **Bench** satisfies the clause — an Active-only reading
  agrees on every board where the {W} happens to be Active and silently **under-pays** on exactly the
  boards the card is for.
* **Widening to both seats** (`inPlayTypesIntersect`'s spread run twice) is the worse defect, because
  it lets the **attacker's own side** arm the clause.

⚠️ **AND THE PRINTED ATTACKER IS WHAT MAKES THE SECOND ONE VISIBLE AT ALL.** Electivire is
`Lightning` reading a `{W}` clause, so unlike D370's Metal-on-Metal printings — where an "in play"
misreading satisfies itself off the attacker and shows up immediately — this one needs a Water body
**deliberately fielded on the attacker's side** before anything moves. `inPlayTypeBonus.test.ts` §5
builds that board.

### 🆕 TWO TRANSFERABLE LESSONS ABOUT FIXTURES

**⑴ A FIXTURE DATUM CAN MOVE SOMEBODY ELSE'S FINDING, AND THE TIDY DEFAULT IS THE DANGEROUS ONE.**
`fix-shortcircuit` was first written with a NULL `evolveFrom` — the obvious choice for a synthetic
body that is seated with `setActiveFromDeck` and never evolved. But `stage1Bonus.test.ts` §1 sweeps
`FIXTURE_POOL` for Stage 1 bodies with a null chain and pins that set at **exactly ONE**
(`fix-exstage1`), because the disagreement between two independent printed columns (`stage` and
`evolveFrom`) is that file's whole finding. A second chainless Stage 1 invented here would have turned
an inherited measurement into an artefact of this slice, while every rung stayed green except a
length. The real card evolves from Electabuzz, so **D306's transcribe-don't-interpolate rule was the
fix as well as the diagnosis**. ⚠️ **ASK WHAT ELSE SWEEPS THE POOL FOR THE FIELD YOU ARE LEAVING
NULL**, not only for the one you are setting.

**⑵ A REUSED FIXTURE CAN SILENTLY UNDER-TEST, AND THE MUTANT IS WHERE IT SHOWS.** D370 cast
`fix-dualbody` as `["Water", "Metal"]` precisely to separate `types.includes(t)` from an equality on
`types[0]` — and **it cannot do that for a WATER clause at all**, because under `{W}` its Water sits
at index 0 and the wrong reading passes. Reusing it here would have left D390's **C4** mutant ALIVE
while the suite read as thorough. `fix-inplaydual` is `["Fire", "Water"]` for that one reason, and the
mutant row records the reason rather than only the body. **A fixture's discriminating power is
relative to the parameter under test, never a property of the fixture.**

### ⚠️ THE APOSTROPHE PARTITION MOVED, AND A TEMPLATE LANDED IN THE FREE HALF

`clauseApostrophe.test.ts` went **45 → 46** with the **apostrophe-FREE** half taking the whole step
(24 → 25) for a second consecutive slice, while the bearing half stood still at 21. 🆕 **And the
clause that landed there is TEMPLATE-owned, which only D370's bench-type key had ever been.** The two
apostrophe-bearing templates spell a POSSESSIVE and carry D136's `['’]` class in their own source;
this clause spells *"your opponent **has**"* and has nothing to class, so the new pattern carries no
class at all. **The character decides which half a clause lands in, not the partition.**

### THE ANSWER, AND THE RULE IT LEAVES BEHIND

**One OPTIONAL field**, `energy?: BasicEnergyType | "special"`, on the shipped
`yourActiveEnergyAtLeast` member (D383) — **not** a second member, which is the opposite of what
D389 decided one union axis over and of what nine consecutive slices had decided before it.

The measurements, all taken at this head rather than quoted forward:

  · **D389's strongest ground does not transfer.** Its seat parameter would have been **REQUIRED** —
    a rename across 22 executable sites — and would have saved no note body, because `conditionNote`
    prints a different SENTENCE per seat. `energy?` is **OPTIONAL**: `yourActiveEnergyAtLeast` has
    **11 executable sites across 4 files** (9 `kind:` literals + 2 exhaustive-switch arms) and the
    widening edits **ZERO** of them.
  · **The note gains a SLOT, not a sentence.** All three spellings — absent, `"special"`, a basic
    type — come out of one `return`, and the unnarrowed string is **byte-identical** to the one D383
    shipped, so no reject pill moved.
  · **The mechanism was already a parameter.** `countAttachedEnergy(state, pokemon, energy)` has
    taken `BasicEnergyType | "special" | null` since D128 and this arm already passed `null`, so
    `cond.energy ?? null` is the entire behavioural edit and the member is now isomorphic to the call
    it delegates to.
  · **It is D326's shape exactly — "ABSENT MEANS UNNARROWED".** The filtered set is a SUBSET of
    `pokemon.energy`, so the narrowed gate is TRUE on a strict subset of the boards the bare one is.
    ⚠️ D326's own settling argument (one card printing BOTH narrowings, which a union could not have
    spelled) does **not** transfer; this stands on the arithmetic instead, and the difference is
    stated rather than glossed.

🆕 **THE TRANSFERABLE RULE.** The member's own doc block already separates it from
`activeEnergyCountsEqual` by its COMPARAND (a printed constant versus another body).
**A COMPARAND IS A SHAPE AND TAKES A MEMBER; A FILTER THE DELEGATE ALREADY ACCEPTS IS A FIELD.**

⚠️ **AND THE PRICE OF A FIELD IS NAMED RATHER THAN WAVED AWAY.** An optional field is **invisible to
the compiler** at every site that ignores it — a new union member forces every exhaustive switch to
be updated, and a new optional field forces nothing. That is the one safety a second member gets for
free, and it is bought back in mutants: four of D391's six rows are exactly the defects the field
makes possible (the filter dropped, the row claiming the unquantified neighbour, the row authored
WITHOUT the new field, the note ignoring the filter it was handed).

### A LITERAL ROW, AND WHY A SIXTH TEMPLATE WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORST ONE

Two tokens vary in principle — the threshold and the energy code — so D118's one-token test fails and

That is the closest pair of anchors in the whole template set, so a sixth PATTERN would have entered

### THE COST AND THE CLAUSE NAME DIFFERENT TYPES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE GUARD

Frozen Wood costs **{W}{W}{W}{C}** and its clause counts **{G}** — a **Water** Pokémon reading a
**Grass** clause. With single-unit attachments, every board that can legally DECLARE the attack holds
four Energy cards, so the UNFILTERED reading at `count: 2` is TRUE on all of them.
**Dropping the filter does not make the printed bonus wrong somewhere; it makes it UNCONDITIONAL.**

That is why the FALSE case in `typedEnergyThreshold.test.ts` §3 is an ordinary paying board rather
than an unpayable one (D379's rule about driving a refusal from OUTSIDE a saturated population), and
why mutant **C6** mutates the FIXTURE's cost to `{G}{G}{G}{C}`: it arms the clause by paying and
deletes the FALSE case, breaking the EXPERIMENT rather than the engine. ⚠️ **A demonstrator whose cost
and clause named the same type could not have shown any of this.**

### CARDS, NOT UNITS — AND THE FIXTURE THAT CAN TELL THEM APART

The typed branch counts cards whose PROVISION includes the type (`providesEnergyType`, D118's rule),
so a Special providing `{G}{G}` counts **ONE** and the attack deals 120; two of them deal 240.

🛑 **`fix-blend` COULD NOT HAVE ASKED THIS QUESTION.** It provides `["Fire", "Water"]`, which
separates a CARD count from a UNIT count for an *unfiltered* tally and cannot do it for a `{G}` one —
it contributes one Grass card and one Grass unit, so both readings agree. `fix-grassdouble`
(`["Grass", "Grass"]`) is the first `EnergyProgram.provides` row in the repo to spell one type
**twice**; `providedEnergy` is a `flatMap`, so the duplicate survives and a units reading really would
see two. **A fixture's discriminating power is relative to the parameter under test** — D390's rule,
one member over, and this time it needed a new registry row rather than a new body.

⚠️ **AND `fix-frozenwood`'s `evolveFrom` IS THE PRINTED `"Snover"`** for D390's *other* fixture
lesson: `stage1Bonus.test.ts` §1 sweeps `FIXTURE_POOL` for Stage 1 bodies with a NULL chain and pins

### TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE INHERITED HANDOFF, BOTH FOUND BY ENUMERATING RATHER THAN READING

⑴ **THE RESIDUE HOLDS FOUR CLAUSES NO HANDOFF IN THIS RUN HAS EVER NAMED** — *"this Pokémon evolved
from Gimmighoul during this turn"*, *"…from Misty's Staryu…"*, *"this Pokémon used Form Ranks during
your last turn"* and *"…used Pervasive Gas…"*, one printing each, forming **two pairs that each share
one mechanism**. The evolve pair's price is measured rather than guessed: `InPlayPokemon` carries
`turnPlayed`, `promotedTurn` and `healedTurn` but **no evolution stamp**, and `evolvePokemon`
(types.ts) spreads `{...from}` so the evolved body inherits the pre-evolution `turnPlayed`. A required
`evolvedTurn: number | null` is **D386's exact shape** and owes `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 23 → 24.

⑵ **THE FACE-UP PRIZE ROW IS NOT IN THE BONUS RESIDUE AT ALL.** *"You may turn 1 of your face-down
Prize cards face up. If you do, this attack does 80 more damage."* does not match the
`If …, this attack does N more damage.` skeleton, so seven consecutive slices compared their candidate
against a figure the residue never contained. It is still the only multi-printing candidate in the
wider backlog and it is still refused, at 2 / 9 = 0.22 against 0.50.

**A HANDOFF TABLE IS A SAMPLE UNTIL SOMEBODY ENUMERATES THE RESIDUE.** Enumerate it.

### THE NEXT SHAPE QUESTION, AND IT IS THE FIRST TEST OF THE RULE ABOVE

The named next candidate is *"If a Pokémon that has \"Nidoking\" in its name is on your Bench, this
attack does 120 more damage."* (1 legal printing) — a **SUBSTRING** name read against
`yourBenchHasNamed { name }`'s **EQUALITY**.

⚠️ **THE RULE ABOVE PREDICTS A *MEMBER*, NOT A FIELD**: what changes is the COMPARISON OPERATOR, not a
filter the delegate already accepts, and no `nameMatches`-style predicate exists in `cards.ts` today.
**STATE THE PREDICTION AND THEN TRY TO FALSIFY IT** — price an optional `match?: "substring"` field
against a second member, count the executable sites BOTH ways at the head you find, and say which you
took and why. Four live clause rows read the equality member (`Falinks`, `Durant`, `Illumise`,
`Mightyena`, plus the `allOf` pair), so widening the member ITSELF is a rename with live consumers,
which is the D389 arithmetic rather than the D391 one. The refutation board is cheap: §4's naming rule
means "Dark Nidoking" and "Nidoking ex" satisfy the printed clause and fail the shipped one.

## D392 — THE SUBSTRING NAME READ, AND THE FIRST TEST OF D391's RULE

**Team Rocket's Nidoqueen `sv10-116` "Love Impact"** ({D}, `60+`, index **0** of TWO), *"If a Pokémon
that has \"Nidoking\" in its name is on your Bench, this attack does 120 more damage."*, **1 legal
printing**. Located with ONE brace-free limitlesstcg `text:` search on the printed tail *"in its name
is on your Bench"* — 30 hits, exactly ONE of them Standard — and confirmed field by field against
`https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/sv10-116`, which returns the 170 HP, the `Stage2`, the
`Team Rocket's Nidorina` chain, the Darkness type, the ×2 Fighting Weakness, retreat 3 and BOTH
printed attacks ("Mega Kick" {D}{D} 130 at index 1, the control).

### THE RULE D391 LEFT BEHIND WAS TESTED, AND IT HELD — FOR THE REASON IT NAMES

*A comparand is a shape and takes a MEMBER; a filter the delegate already accepts is a FIELD.* Here
what changes is the **comparison OPERATOR** (`===` → `.includes`), which is neither, so the rule
predicts a member. **It was priced BOTH ways anyway** — D391's own instruction — and every measurement
points the same way:

| | second MEMBER | optional `match?: "substring"` FIELD |
|---|---|---|
| sites of `yourBenchHasNamed` EDITED | **0** of 45 | **3** of 45 (the member line + both switch arms) |
| live consumers behind those edits | — | 8 `kind:` literals, 34 test assertions |
| `conditionNote` | a NEW arm, one sentence | a BRANCH inside one arm — a second **SENTENCE**, not a second **SLOT** |
| delegate already takes the parameter? | n/a | **no** — the comparison is INLINE, and `cards.ts` has no name-matching predicate |
| compiler safety | full: a mistyped `kind` is a type error | **none**: an optional field is invisible at every site that ignores it |

⚠️ **SO THE RULE IS ONE-FOR-ONE, NOT PROVEN.** What it has not met is a case where it and the
measurements DISAGREE — and D391's instruction still governs when it does: follow the measurements
and say so.

🛑 **THE PAYLOAD FIELD IS `fragment`, NOT `name`, AND THAT IS A COMPILER PROPERTY RATHER THAN A
NAMING TASTE.** With matching payloads the two members would differ by their `kind` token alone, so a
mistyped `kind` on any of the eight shipped `yourBenchHasNamed` literals would still typecheck and
would silently swap an exact read for a substring one. Differently-named fields make that swap a type
error in **both** directions.

### THE POSSESSIVE IS LOAD-BEARING, AND THE TOLL WAS PAID FOR IT

§4's naming rule makes the Standard satisfier **Team Rocket's Nidoking ex** — a name that CONTAINS
"Nidoking" and equals it nowhere. So the shipped equality member answers **FALSE on the board the card
was printed for**, and **so does a `startsWith` reading**, because the owner possessive puts the
fragment at offset 14. A tidy `Nidoking ex` fixture would have refuted the equality read and left the
prefix read alive; mutant **C7** installs exactly that rename on the FIXTURE — the engine untouched,
every substring rung green, and **C2 unkillable**. **THE PRICE OF A TIDY FIXTURE IS A MUTANT THAT
CANNOT DIE.**

That is why this slice pays the possessive fixture-name toll after **seventeen** slices of dodging it:
`switchSeam.test.ts`, `inPlayTarget.test.ts` and `ownerTargetOps.test.ts` enumerate every
`/^[A-Z][A-Za-z' ]*'s /` name in `FIXTURE_POOL`, and `ownerPrefix.test.ts` additionally matches both
new bodies through `ownerPokemon` — while the unprefixed `fix-nidoking` correctly lands in neither.
Four one-line list edits, all four designed to expire.

### THE POPULATION THE PRINTED PHRASE PICKS OUT IS NOT THE ONE THE ROW IS FOR

**3 legal sentences say "in its name", 2 of those quote a SINGLE name, and 1 of those is a board fact
under the bonus skeleton.** The other two are per-card SCALING reads — *"…20 damage for each Supporter
card that has \"Team Rocket\" in its name in your discard pile"* and *"…40 damage for each Pokémon in
play that has \"Koffing\" or \"Weezing\" in its name…"*, the second quoting **two** names in one clause,
which no single-fragment predicate can hold. **A LITERAL ROW AND EMPHATICALLY NOT A SIXTH TEMPLATE**:
the captured token is a card NAME, open-ended, with nothing to fail against, so a pattern would
resolve an unparseable fragment into a predicate that answers FALSE forever and silently. The printed
quotation marks make a template look SAFER than it is, which is why the rule is restated at the row.

⚠️ **THE QUOTATION MARKS ARE ASCII U+0022, CHECKED AGAINST THE COMMITTED CORPUS BYTE BY BYTE** — not
the curly pair — and `literalClauseRow`'s tolerance is the U+2019 **apostrophe** fold, which reaches
neither character. `clauseApostrophe.test.ts` moves **47 → 48** with the apostrophe-FREE half taking
the whole step for a FOURTH consecutive slice: **a key that LOOKS punctuated still has nothing to
class. THE CHARACTER DECIDES, NOT THE APPEARANCE.**

### THE CENSUS CASCADE TOOK SIX FULL VITEST RUNS

Rungs hide behind earlier assertions inside one `it`, so each run surfaced only the first failure per
case. Bonus residue **14 / 17 → 13 / 16**, distribution `{1: 12, 5: 1}` → `{1: 11, 5: 1}`; nine-reader
**370 / 1,262 → 371 / 1,263** and its residue **270 / 470 → 269 / 469**; ten-reader
**373 / 1,270 → 374 / 1,271**; `BUILT.attack` **1,299 → 1,300**; whole-census `built`
**1,700 → 1,701** and its residue **683 → 682**; unbuilt attack column **433 → 432**; unbuilt
remainder **462 → 461**; `BUILT.attack - 922` **377 → 378** and `- 922 - 252` **125 → 126**;
`head - rawDelta - splitDelta` **1,293 → 1,294**. Every earlier head is re-derived as an OFFSET from
the new one rather than frozen, so each of those chains gained one term **at the FRONT**.

⚠️ **AND TWO MORE CENSUSES NOBODY EXPECTS A *NAME* TO MOVE**: the `FIXTURE_POOL` floor
**486 → 489**, and `stage1Bonus.test.ts`'s non-Stage-1 evolution sweep **25 → 26**, because

## D393 — THE EVOLVE PAIR, AND THE FALSIFIER THAT FIRED WITHOUT ITS INFERENCE HOLDING

**Gholdengo `sv08-131` "Strike It Rich"** ({M}, `30+`, index **0** of TWO), *"If this Pokémon evolved
from Gimmighoul during this turn, this attack does 90 more damage."*, **1 legal printing**, and
**Misty's Starmie `sv10-047` "Abrupt Flash"** ({W}, `60+`, index 0 of ONE), *"If this Pokémon evolved
from Misty's Staryu during this turn, this attack does 80 more damage."*, **1 legal printing**. Each
located with ONE brace-free limitlesstcg `text:` search on the printed clause tail — each returning
exactly one card — and confirmed field by field against `https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>`,
which returned the HP, the `Stage1`, the printed `evolveFrom` chain, the types, the weaknesses (and
Gholdengo's Grass −30 Resistance), the retreat and every printed attack.

### PRICING A PAIR AS A PAIR IS NOT BOOKKEEPING — IT BUYS A REFUTATION

The two clauses differ only in the card they name, so **one member and one `InPlayPokemon` field
serve both**. Either printing alone would have bought exactly the same state for half the printings.
The part that is not arithmetic: **an arm that reads only the turn stamp and ignores `cond.name`
passes every test either card could write by itself.** The board that kills it is a Gholdengo that
evolved this turn being asked *Misty's Starmie's* clause — which does not exist until both printings
are on the table. A singleton slice would have shipped the same code with the name test unrefuted.

### THE STATE-SHAPE QUESTION, AND A FALSIFIER THAT FIRED WITHOUT ITS INFERENCE HOLDING

D392's handoff attached a falsifiable prediction — a per-body `evolvedTurn: number | null` (D386's
shape) rather than a per-seat `GameState` record (D326's) — and named two falsifiers.

**Falsifier (a) FIRED.** It read: *"if the placement turns out to have a single call site that
already knows the turn, a seat record may be cheaper to WRITE than a field is to thread"*. That site
exists: `evolveOnto` (types.ts) is the engine's ONE evolution placement — `placeEvolution` reaches it
from both hand routes (`evolve`, `rareCandy`), and all four `evolveFromDeck*` ops call it directly —
and it already writes `turnPlayed: state.turn`. **The antecedent held and the consequent did not**,
because a seat record would have been written at that same single site and bought nothing: the cost
of a per-body stamp was never the threading.

> ⚠️ **A FALSIFIER IS A PREDICTION ABOUT THE WORLD, NOT A PROOF SCHEMA. Its antecedent can hold while
> its inference does not — so check the inference, not only the fact.**

**Falsifier (b) did NOT fire.** `redactedInPlayOf` (redact.ts) names its output fields one at a time
rather than spreading the body, and `packages/schema` has never carried `InPlayPokemon` at all. Both
take **ZERO** bytes, so D386's precedent transfers whole.

**And the compiler tied the two shapes, exactly as it tied D386's three.** Each candidate was added
REQUIRED and initialised nowhere, then measured under `tsc -b --force`:

| shape | files with errors | sites |
|---|---|---|
| `InPlayPokemon.evolvedTurn: number \| null` | 1 (`types.ts`) | 1 (`makeInPlay`) |
| `GameState.evolvedFromThisTurn: Record<Seat, …>` | 1 (`setup.ts`) | 1 (the state literal) |

🛑 **SO THE PRINTED SUBJECT SETTLED IT, AND IT WAS DRIVEN ON A BOARD RATHER THAN ARGUED.**
*"this Pokémon"* is one BODY. `evolvedFromBonus.test.ts` §4 fields a Misty's Starmie placed straight
into play as the Active and evolves a **BENCHED** Misty's Staryu on the same turn. A per-seat record
answers *"did this SEAT evolve something from Misty's Staryu this turn"* → TRUE and pays the Active a
+80 it did not earn; the per-body stamp answers FALSE and the attack does its printed 60. §4's second
case is the one a `Record<Seat, number>` cannot express at all: two bodies evolving in one turn from
two different cards, where only one of them is the attacker.

### ONE FIELD, NOT TWO — THE NAME IS ALREADY ON THE STACK

`evolveOnto` APPENDS (`stack: [...from.stack, evolutionUid]`), so the card a body evolved FROM is
always the entry **one below the stack top** — §1.2's identity rule read one position down. Storing
the name beside the turn would be a second spelling of a fact the stack already holds, and the two
could disagree (D222). `conditionHolds` reads the stack; mutant **C4** installs the `- 1` off-by-one,
which is the slip this address invites because every other name read in the engine
(`yourBenchHasNamed`, `yourBenchHasNameContaining`, `yourNamedPokemonInPlay`) goes through
`topCardOf` and this is the only one that must not.

### 🛑 A REQUIRED FIELD IS NO COMPILER GUARANTEE THAT ANYBODY SET IT

`evolveOnto` builds its body as `{...from, …}`. **Deleting the `evolvedTurn: state.turn` line still
typechecks** — the spread supplies the pre-evolution body's value — and the clause then silently
never holds. That is the one safety a REQUIRED per-body field does *not* buy, and it is bought in
mutants instead: **C3** installs `from.evolvedTurn`, which is precisely what `promotedTurn` and
`healedTurn` correctly do one line up (§10 spreads them through, because evolving does not un-move or
un-heal a Pokémon). **Any future `InPlayPokemon` field written inside a spread owes this mutant.**

### `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 23 → 24, AND WHY IT IS SHARPER THAN D386's

A v23 record's in-play Pokémon carry no `evolvedTurn` at all, so a resumed match reads
`undefined === state.turn` **FALSE**. It does not throw. It does not look wrong. It silently withholds
the printed +90 from the player who evolved into the attacker on the very turn the match was
interrupted — the one turn the whole card is about. The record is refused instead.

### THE PREMISE THAT DIED WITHOUT ITS `find` MOVING (D384's class, fired for real)

D312 built Gholdengo's **index 1** ("Surf Back") as a registry row and pinned index 0 as *"an
evolved-this-turn conditional this engine does not read"* — in `registry.ts`'s doc block, in
`surfBack.test.ts`'s header and §1 comment, and inside the mutant
`D312-surf-back-authors-the-wrong-attack-index`'s `what`. **D393 built that sentence, and not one
character of the `find` moved.** `git grep` finds the quoted line; `precheck.ts` reports it matching
exactly once; only a reader who knows to grep the SENTENCE rather than the KEY finds it. All three
sites were re-transcribed in the build commit. The mutant is still KILLED and now kills for a
**second** reason: `programFor(id)?.attack` beats `deriveAttackEffect`, so an index slip MASKS the
+90 as well as unsimulating "Surf Back".

🆕 **Gholdengo is now the engine's FIRST card with a REGISTRY attack at one index and a DERIVED one at
another**, which makes `censusAtHead.test.ts`'s index-precision rung load-bearing in both directions
for the first time.

### THE POSSESSIVE TOLL, PAID AGAIN AND NOT BY CHOICE

The arm compares the pre-evolution card's `name` to the clause key **byte for byte**, so
`fix-mistystaryu` must be named *"Misty's Staryu"* or the demonstrator matches no printed sentence at
all — D183's defect wearing a proper noun. Mutant **C8** installs the tidy `"Staryu"` rename.
`switchSeam.test.ts`, `inPlayTarget.test.ts` and `ownerTargetOps.test.ts` each gained two ids, and
`ownerPrefix.test.ts` gained `fix-abruptflash/Misty` and `fix-mistystaryu/Misty` — **the first second
owner that predicate has ever been shown**, which turns four rows about Team Rocket into evidence
that `ownerPokemon` reads the PREFIX rather than a fixed list. D392 chose to pay this toll; D393
could not avoid it.

### ONE ROW OF THE FAMILY IS DELIBERATELY NOT BOUGHT

The legal attack column prints *"evolved from"* **three** times. The third is *"Your opponent discards
a card from their hand. If this Pokémon evolved from Salandit during this turn, your opponent
discards 2 more cards."* (**1 printing**) — the same board fact under a **DISCARD** consequent, so the
bonus skeleton refuses it before `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` is consulted. `yourActiveEvolvedFromThisTurn`
would serve it unchanged; what it needs is a THIRD consequent skeleton, which is a different and
bigger slice. §1 asserts it is present in the corpus and refused by every reader, so the claim cannot
rot into a silent widening.

### THE CENSUS CASCADE — THE OFFSET-CHAIN WARNING, SHARPENED

D392 recorded *"grep the offset chains up front"*. That is necessary and not sufficient, because
**the chains are written in TWO syntaxes and a regex over one misses the other**:
`benchNamedBonus.test.ts` spells its chain across twenty-two LINES (`resolved.length -\n  1 -\n …`)
while every other file writes it inline, so a sweep for `resolved.length - 1` reported **zero matches
in the one file that had two chains**.

⚠️ **AND ONE FULL `vitest run` CAPTURED TO A FILE OUTSIDE THE CHECKOUT IS WORTH ITS 100 SECONDS.** It
listed all 52 failures with file:line in a single pass, which is what collapsed the rest into targeted
edits. The harness's own background task-output file is **TAIL-ONLY** and will under-report the
failure list — at D393 it showed 3 of 52.

## D394 — THE USED-ATTACK PAIR: WHOSE CLOCK, AND WHICH COMES FIRST — THE READ OR THE WRITE

**Falinks `sv07-088` "All-Out Attack"** ({C}{C}, `30+`, index **1** of TWO), *"If this Pokémon used
Form Ranks during your last turn, this attack does 90 more damage."*, **1 legal printing**, and
**Weezing `sv09-092` "Crazy Blast"** ({D}{C}, `50+`, index 1 of TWO), *"If this Pokémon used
Pervasive Gas during your last turn, this attack does 120 more damage."*, **1 legal printing**. Each
located with ONE brace-free limitlesstcg `text:` search on the printed clause tail (`SCR 88`,
`JTG 92`) — each returning exactly one card — and confirmed field by field against
`https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>`, **including the attack at index 0 that each clause NAMES**,
which is the half a card-name search does not give you. 🆕 **A CLAUSE THAT QUOTES AN ATTACK NAME HAS
A TAIL SEARCH JUST AS A CLAUSE THAT QUOTES A CARD NAME DOES.**

### 🛑 THE CLOCK WAS A GUESS AND IT WAS MEASURED ACROSS A KO PARK

`state.turn` is a GLOBAL counter, so *"your last turn"* is two counter steps back **only if nothing
inserts or skips a step**. A Knock Out is the interrupt that could: it parks the tail on a player
decision for an unbounded time. Both park shapes were built and driven rather than argued off
`turnTail`:

| board | what the counter did |
|---|---|
| **ATTACK-EPILOGUE KO** — Pervasive Gas's printed 30 is exactly lethal on a 30 HP defender | declared at `turn = 3`; `pending` = `takePrizes, promote, endTurn, checkup, startTurn`, and **both** ko:\* phases park at `turn = 3`; settles at 4; P1's next turn is **5**. **Δ = 2** |
| **CHECKUP KO** — a lethal poison tick between the turns | parks at the ENDING turn's value with `pending` = `takePrizes, promote, startTurn`; two consecutive parks give 1 → 3. **Δ = 2** |

The mechanism is that **`turnTail` queues exactly ONE `startTurn` and every KO stage is spliced in
FRONT of it**. So `state.turn - 2` is D143's `state.turn + 2` reflected — the same claim
(*"declaring an attack ENDS the turn, so the turn after this one is the opponent's"*) read backwards.
A `- 1` is the OPPONENT's clock and compares against a turn number no body of this seat can carry.

### 🆕 THE PARITY DOES THE SEAT CHECK FOR FREE

`state.turn - 2` shares the current turn's parity, and a body is only ever stamped on a turn its own
controller held (the §8 gate refuses an attack from the seat that does not hold `turn:action`). So
the arm evaluated OFF-TURN for the non-turn seat compares against a turn number that seat's bodies
cannot carry and gets an **honest FALSE rather than a borrowed TRUE** — `yourFirstTurn`'s property
arrived at a third way, by arithmetic instead of by operand choice, with no `phaseViewOf` guard to
forget. It is a false NEGATIVE off-turn, which is stated in the arm rather than hidden; no printed
sentence asks this member off-turn.

### 🛑 THE OTHER HALF OF THE SLICE IS AN *ORDERING*, AND NO EARLIER STAMP HAD TO ASK IT

`promotedTurn`, `healedTurn` and `evolvedTurn` are all written by something that is NOT the attack,
so their read and their write could not collide. **This one is written BY the attack and read BY the
attack.** `scaledAttackDamage`'s `boardCondition` arm evaluates the clause **at declaration**
(attack.ts, D115's placement — whose own comment says it is there so *"Gyarados ex's 'already has any
damage counters on it' cannot be bootstrapped by this very attack"*), so a stamp written beside
`ATTACK_DECLARED` would overwrite LAST turn's record with THIS turn's attack **before that read**.
Neither printed bonus would then pay on any board, and every board would still look plausible.

**THE READ IS AT THE FRONT OF THE DECLARATION AND THE WRITE IS AT THE BACK OF IT.** ⚠️ **WHENEVER A
NEW FIELD IS BOTH WRITTEN AND READ BY THE SAME MECHANISM, WRITE DOWN WHICH COMES FIRST BEFORE YOU
WRITE EITHER.**

### `finishAttack` IS THIS ENGINE'S DEFINITION OF "AN ATTACK WAS USED"

The one writer, and the placement is the argument. Every exit out of `attack.ts` reaches it — the
confusion-tails failure (§12), the D125 requirement gate whose own comment already read *"a cancelled
attack is an attack that was USED"*, the cancel-on-tails flip, the no-effect-program tail — plus the
parked program's `attackEpilogue` stage; and the Checkup's poison KO and the mid-turn evolve sweep
call `collectKnockOuts` directly and never come through. That is D158's *"by an attack"* discharged
by placement, used a second time for a different verb.

⚠️ **WHICH IS WHY `PendingStage.attackEpilogue` GAINED A REQUIRED `attack`.** The parked route is the
one of the five on which `declared.name` is out of scope by the time the stamp is written — D189's
argument about `uid` with the subject changed from *which body* to *which attack*. Falinks's index 0
is a deck search and parks every time, which is why that fixture carries BOTH printed attacks and not
only the one this slice buys.

### A NAME AND NOT AN INDEX — `LockedAttack`'s ANSWER INVERTED FOR ITS OWN REASON

D154 stored an INDEX because every consumer of that record asks per index (the §8 gate compares
`action.index`; both payability projections build rows by `attacks.map`), resolving the printed proper
noun ONCE at the install. This record's one consumer is `conditionHolds`, which compares against a
printed clause key that is a **NAME** — so the same rule ("translate at the site that reads the
printed token") lands on the other side. **And an index would be the wrong FACT besides**: the record
outlives the turn it was written on, and a body that evolves in between renumbers its own attacks.

### THE PAYLOAD FIELD IS `attack`, NOT `name` — D392's RULE APPLIED TO A NEIGHBOUR

The member directly above in the union carries `name: string` and it is a POKÉMON name; this one is
an ATTACK name. Nothing in the type system separates two `string`s, so **the identifier is the whole
guard** — which is exactly why D392 named its own substring field `fragment`. D392's rule was written
about a member and its DELEGATE; this is its first use on a member and its NEIGHBOUR.

### 🛑 A REQUIRED FIELD IS NO COMPILER GUARANTEE THAT ANYBODY SET IT — THE SECOND MECHANISM

D393 found this in a **SPREAD**: `evolveOnto` builds `{...from, …}`, so deleting the stamp line still
typechecks because the pre-evolution body supplies a value. D394 finds it in a **DEFAULT**:
`makeInPlay` writes `usedAttack: null`, so deleting the write in `finishAttack` leaves a REQUIRED
field that nothing ever sets and a clause that is permanently false. Both typecheck, both are
invisible in a diff of the type, and both are bought in mutants and nowhere else (**C4**).

**THE GENERAL FORM IS NOW TWO CASES WIDE: A REQUIRED FIELD GUARANTEES A KEY, NEVER A WRITER.** Any
per-body field whose writer is not the only constructor owes this mutant.

### `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 24 → 25, WITH TWO MISSING REQUIRED FIELDS ON ONE BUMP

A v24 record's in-play Pokémon carry no `usedAttack`, so a resumed match reads the clause FALSE
forever and the printed bonus silently stops existing — D393's failure mode one field over. **The
second field is the sharper one**: a v24 record saved **PARKED MID-ATTACK** carries an
`attackEpilogue` stage with no `attack` key, so draining it would stamp the attacking body with
`undefined` as an attack name while the record went on looking healthy. **A KEY THE WRITER NEVER
WROTE IS NOT A KEY WITH A DEFAULT.**

### 🛑 THE HANDOFF UNDER-PRICED THE FIELD BY A FACTOR OF THREE — SWEEP THE CLAUSE, NOT THE SENTENCE

The handoff priced this row at **2 printings**, which is the count of sentences matching the BONUS
skeleton. The count of what the state actually answers is **six**, measured off `legalAttackCorpus()`:

| printed sentence | printings | why it is not bought here |
|---|---|---|
| the pair | **2** | bought |
| *"You can use this attack only if this Pokémon used **Rollout** during your last turn."* | **1** | ✅ **BOUGHT AT D395** — Miltank `sv08.5-081` idx 1 "Moomoo Rolling". SAME subject, SAME window, SAME field; it is an ATTACK GATE (D281/D282), not a damage bonus, and `yourActiveUsedAttackLastTurn { attack: "Rollout" }` served it **UNCHANGED and with ZERO new state**, as this row predicted |
| *"…If **1 of your Pokémon** used Angelite during your last turn, this attack can't be used."* | **3** | the biggest single row in the family. Same window, same field; the SUBJECT is Active **plus** Bench, so it needs a second member over the same field, and the consequent is a CANCEL the `NOTHING` skeleton does not spell |
| *"If 1 of your other **Ancient** Pokémon used an attack during your last turn…"* | **1** | refused at the **BANNER** (D207), not at the window — the sharpest illustration in the residue of where this family stops |

⚠️ **A HANDOFF'S PRINTING COUNT IS THE COUNT OF THE SENTENCES THAT MATCH ONE SKELETON, NOT THE COUNT
OF WHAT THE STATE YOU ARE ABOUT TO BUILD CAN ANSWER.** This measurement cost one query and doubled
the recorded value of the slice's own state.

### A DOC BLOCK ROTTED, AND NOTHING MECHANICAL WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT

`lastKoTurn`'s block called itself *"the engine's ONLY piece of turn HISTORY"*. `usedAttack` is a
second one. It is not in a mutant's `survives` reason (which reports **STALE** and fails the run) nor
even in a `what` string (which rots silently but is at least inside the corpus `precheck.ts` walks) —
it is a **comment**, with no harness looking at it at all. Found by grepping the SENTENCE. **D393's
asymmetry, one address further out: `survives` fails loudly, `what` rots silently, a doc block rots
invisibly.**

### THE CENSUS CASCADE — TWO NEW WAYS TO GET THE REPAIR WRONG

62 failures in 47 files, listed with file:line by **one** full `vitest run` captured outside the
checkout. Four classes: the `attackEpilogue` stage shape (11 sites, most of which can read the name
off their own `ATTACK_DECLARED` row — the idiom they already use for the uid), the `InPlayPokemon`
key pins (10 sites), the bonus residue 11 / 14 → 9 / 12 with its offset chains, and the reader
instruments.

⚠️ **NEW (1): THE OFFSET CHAINS ARE WRITTEN OVER TWO DIFFERENT SUBJECTS UNDER THE SAME VARIABLE
NAME.** A blind `refused.length + N → N + 2` sweep also hit the **CANCEL** residue in
`crossBoardStatus.test.ts`, `exactHandSize.test.ts` and `stadiumPresence.test.ts`, which uses the
identical local `refused` over the `NOTHING` skeleton and **did not move at all** — three files went
red on a number this slice never touched. D392 said grep the chains; D393 said they are written in two
syntaxes; **D394 adds that the name is not the subject.**

⚠️ **NEW (2): A TWO-PASS INDENTATION REPLACE DOUBLE-APPLIES.** `"        \"turnPlayed\","` CONTAINS
`"      \"turnPlayed\","`, so a 6-space pass run after an 8-space pass edits the line it just wrote.
Both defects were caught by the next full run; neither would have been caught by reading.

### WHAT DID NOT MOVE, SAID OUT LOUD

The possessive fixture-name toll was **not** paid — neither `Falinks` nor `Weezing` carries an owner
prefix — so `switchSeam.test.ts`, `inPlayTarget.test.ts`, `ownerTargetOps.test.ts` and
`ownerPrefix.test.ts` stood still for the first time in three slices, and the apostrophe census's
BEARING half stayed at 22 while its free half took both new keys. `redact.ts` and `packages/schema`
took **ZERO bytes** (`redactedInPlayOf` names its output fields one at a time and has never carried a
turn stamp). No registry row, so `registryCardIds()` is unmoved at 709. What DID move for reasons
that have nothing to do with this clause: `stage1Bonus.test.ts`'s pool-wide Stage 1 sweep **71 → 72**
and the `FIXTURE_POOL` floor **493 → 495**, while `Card.resistances` STOOD STILL at 28 because
neither printing prints one.


## D395 — THE ROLLOUT ATTACK-GATE: derived or authored, and the first board that can falsify a map key (engine 0.299.0 → **0.300.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 25**)

Miltank `sv08.5-081` "Moomoo Rolling" ({C}{C}, flat `100`, index **1** of TWO) —
*"You can use this attack only if this Pokémon used Rollout during your last turn."*, **1 legal
printing**. Its own index 0 is "Rollout" ({C}, 20, no effect text): **the attack the clause names is
printed on the same card, one index down.**

**WHAT SHIPS:** ONE registry row (a bare `CardProgram.attackGate`), ONE new `ATTACK_GATE_CLAUSES`
literal, ONE reversed branch in `splitAttackGateClause`. ZERO new state, `BoardCondition` members,
ops, events, error codes, prompt kinds, readers, regexes, `redact.ts` bytes or `packages/schema`
bytes.

### 🛑 THE SHAPE QUESTION WAS *DERIVED GATE OR REGISTRY ROW*, AND THE RULE DOES NOT NAME THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES IT

D180/D187 say *"an arm transfers across sets; a registry row does not"*. That is a claim about
**reprints**. What settles the question is **how many legal printings a deriver buys that a row does
not**, and here it is **ZERO**: the clause is 1 printing on 1 id (`legalAttackCorpus()`), and the
only other gate spellings in the catalog are the 13 that already carry rows.

Against that zero stand two costs:

- **`attackGate` HAS NO DERIVER SEAM AT ALL.** `attackGateOf` (continuous.ts) reads
  `programFor(top.id)?.attackGate?.[index]` and nothing else. Building the first deriver **is** the
  machinery D282 refused for a family of one.
- 🛑 **AND A DERIVER WOULD HAVE DISSOLVED A GUARD, NOT ONLY ADDED CODE.** `attack.ts` splits the
  printed text **only when a registry row REPRESENTS the clause at this index** — its own comment
  says *"the gate is the PRECONDITION, not the text"*. A derived gate makes that two-key check a
  tautology and re-installs the too-loose build `D282-split-fires-without-a-gate` exists to refuse.

**A TRANSFERABILITY ARGUMENT WITH A ZERO IN IT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT.**

### 🆕 AND THE ONE ARGUMENT *FOR* A DERIVER IS D394's — WHICH DOES NOT SURVIVE THE MOVE, AND THAT IS A FINDING ABOUT SCOPE

D394 refused `^this Pokémon used (.+) during your last turn$` and gave a specific reason: the
varying token is an ATTACK NAME, **and it is not checked against the card**, so a template would
resolve *"used Surf Back during your last turn"* to a predicate that answers FALSE forever and
silently — on a body that CAN use Surf Back.

That objection **does not transfer to this seam**. `attackGateOf` is handed the CARD (`topCardOf`)
and could require the parsed name to appear in `top.attacks`; D394's site (`CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_
CLAUSES`, resolved by text alone) has no card in scope and could not. **The refusal D394 wanted is
available here and is not available there.**

> **THE SAME TOKEN IS UNTEMPLATABLE IN ONE PLACE AND TEMPLATABLE IN ANOTHER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS
> WHAT IS IN SCOPE — NOT WHAT IS PRINTED.**

And the failure DIRECTION is worse here than there: D394's template would cost a damage bonus that
never pays; this one costs the DECLARATION — a mis-parsed condition is a legal attack barred
forever, on a board no suite would look wrong on. The template still loses, on population.

### 🛑 THE FIRST GATE AT A NON-ZERO INDEX — A MAP KEY WITH NO FALSIFYING BOARD IS AN UNTESTED FIELD

`CardProgram.attackGate` has been `{ [attackIndex: number]: AttackTimingGate }` since D281 and
carried **13 printings, every one of them at index 0**. D281's own field doc says so and calls it
*"an accident of today's pool and not a reason"*. The consequence nobody had written down: an
**INDEX-BLIND** read — `Object.values(attackGate)[0]`, or a per-BODY flag — was **green on every
assertion in the repo**, because every board anyone could build about that field was about index 0.

Miltank is the first board that can tell them apart, and it does so totally:

| index | attack | what an index-blind read does |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | "Rollout" ({C}, 20) — the attack the clause NAMES | inherits idx 1's gate |
| **1** | "Moomoo Rolling" ({C}{C}, 100) — the attack the clause GATES | keeps its gate |

Since "Rollout" is the **only** way to satisfy the gate, gating it locks the card out of the game
forever. `rolloutGate.test.ts` §2 therefore asserts **idx 0 is LIVE before it asserts idx 1 is
barred**, over 4 seeds × 2 seats × 2 assignments, on the engine and on the wire — D278/D279's
standing lesson at its sharpest instance, because here the too-wide direction is not a wrong refusal
but a **DEADLOCK**.

> **WHEN YOU SHIP A KEYED RECORD, WRITE DOWN WHICH BOARD MAKES THE KEY WRONG. IF THERE ISN'T ONE,
> THE KEY IS PROSE.**

### 🆕 D282's EMPTY-BODY REFUSAL NAMED ITS OWN EXPIRY DATE — AND CALLED THE WRONG DIRECTION SAFE

`splitAttackGateClause` returned `null` for a clause-only string, with this comment:

> *"No legal printing is clause-only today (all 13 carry a body), so this is a guard against a
> future one rather than a live path, **and it is the safe direction**: the whole printed string
> goes to the readers unchanged."*

Miltank is that printing. And the direction it called safe was the **unsafe** one the moment it went
live: `null` hands the WHOLE printed string to the readers, every one refuses it, and
`ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` fires **naming a sentence the §8 seam enforced in full** — which is D282's
own defect (*"half their sentence resolved and the other half invisible"*) with the resolved half
being ALL of it.

The branch now returns `{clause, body: ""}`, and `""` needed **no caller change**: the requirement
split, all four damage readers and the skip block in `attack.ts` are each already guarded
`=== null || === ""`. The worry the old comment recorded — *"it would make the caller's 'is there a
remainder' question depend on an empty string"* — was already answered by the code it was written
about.

> **A REFUSAL THAT NAMES ITS OWN TRIGGER IS NOT A DECISION TO REVERSE SILENTLY — IT IS A DECISION
> FIRING. CHECK THE CLAIMED *SAFE DIRECTION* TOO: IT WAS ARGUED ON A BOARD THAT DID NOT EXIST.**

### 🆕 A CENSUS FILTER CAN EXCLUDE A PRINTING TWICE OVER AND BE RIGHT BOTH TIMES

D282 priced its refusal against *"1,732 legal attack units, 613 multi-sentence, and of those only 16
open with `If `"*, and its clause list's doc said *"there is no fourth spelling in the catalog"*.
Both were TRUE and both were blind to this row:

- Miltank's printed text is a **SINGLE sentence**, so it cannot be in the 613;
- it opens `You can use this attack only if…`, so it could never be in the 16.

`splitOrder.test.ts` §1 now carries the arithmetic that says so: the **10 + 3 partition is UNMOVED**
while the family total goes **13 → 14**, which is what proves the new row joined from OUTSIDE both
filters rather than from inside one of them.

### ⚠️ `BUILT.attack` DOES NOT MOVE, AND THE CENSUS GAINS A THIRD CLASS

The split summand counts printings whose **BODY** a reader resolves. This one has no body, and
`resolvedByAnyReader("")` is false because every reader in `effects.ts` is `^…$` anchored on a
non-empty pattern. The printing is accounted at the **DECLARATION** seam, which that addition does
not count from.

So the gate census is now three readings where two used to do:

| reading | at this head |
|---|---|
| gated (the split claims it) | **6 sentences / 14 printings** |
| …of which it has a BODY | **5 / 13** |
| …of which the body RESOLVES once split | **5 / 13** |

Named explicitly in `censusAtHead.test.ts` and `precociousEvolution.test.ts` rather than folded into
either of the two before it — **because *"5 of 6 resolve"* would otherwise read as a reader that
stopped working, when it is really a printing with no body. The two findings look identical in the
count and are opposite in the cause.**

### CENSUS MOVEMENT

registry ids **709 → 710** (a REAL catalog id, no `fix-*` demonstrator — the suite drives a LOCAL
`cardPool`, D275's idiom, and `sv08.5` is not among `CATALOG_MANIFEST`'s six sets, so a shared-pool
body would have owed a key); `BUILT.ability` **280 → 281** and `nonAttackRegistryIds()`
**564 → 565**; whole-census `built` **1,705 → 1,706** with `units − built` **678 → 677**; the
ability triple **280/127/116 → 281/128/117** and its join **129 → 130**; the `attackGate` shortfall
**13 → 14**, with `attacksJson`/`abilitiesJson` moving **UNEVENLY for the first time since D310**
(281 / 267) because Miltank carries an `attacks_json` and **no Ability at all**. `BUILT.attack`
**1,304** and every `usedAttack`-family figure UNMOVED.

### TWO SENTENCES ROTTED, AND THE GREP WAS FOR THE SENTENCE

D394's rule, used one slice later. Neither would have reddened anything:

- *"there is no fourth shape"* (`attackIndexGate.test.ts`) was a claim about the FIRST-TURN clause
  family that read as a claim about the FIELD — the family is still 13 in three shapes; the field is
  now 14 in four;
- *"`attackGate` appears in 13"* (`benchBodySelfScaling.test.ts`) is a fact about that file's `POOL`,
  not about the registry, and stays 13 for that reason. The registry-wide count lives in
  `splitOrder.test.ts` §1 and IS 14.

### WHAT THIS SLICE HANDS ON

**The Angelite cancel — Sylveon ex `sv08-086` / `sv08.5-041` / `sv08.5-156`, 3 legal printings**,

⚠️ **AND THE SPLIT QUESTION HAS A CHEAP MEASURED ANSWER**: Angelite's gate clause is **TRAILING**,
