## D396 — THE ANGELITE CANCEL: a subject widening settled as a MEMBER, and a map key given its second falsifying board (engine 0.300.0 → **0.301.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 25**)

Sylveon ex `sv08-086` / `sv08.5-041` / `sv08.5-156` "Angelite" ({W}{L}{P}, **no printed damage**,
index **1** of TWO) —
*"Choose 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. Shuffle those Pokémon and all attached cards into
your opponent's deck. If 1 of your Pokémon used Angelite during your last turn, this attack can't be
used."*, **3 legal printings on ONE byte-identical `attacks_json`**. Its own index 0 is "Magical
Charm" ({P}{C}{C}, 160): **the attack an index-blind gate confiscates.**

**WHAT SHIPS:** ONE `BoardCondition` member (`yourPokemonUsedAttackLastTurn { attack }`), its TWO
exhaustive-switch arms, and ONE registry program shared by THREE ids. ZERO new state, ops, events,
error codes, prompt kinds, choice kinds, readers, regexes, clause-table rows, `CardFilter` members,
`redact.ts` bytes or `packages/schema` bytes.

### 🛑 THE CONSEQUENT WAS PRICED AS A THIRD SHAPE AND IS THE PASSIVE VOICE OF ONE THAT SHIPPED AT 0.195.0

D394's handoff called *"this attack can't be used"* a THIRD consequent the union does not spell.
It is D281's `barredIf`, whose seven Terapagos ex printings spell the identical rule the other way
round (*"…you can't use this attack during your first turn"*). Both bar the index **while the
condition holds**; the polarity token is the whole of it.

Measured on the committed corpus rather than argued: `"can't be used"` is **1 sentence / 3
printings** and `"you can't use this attack"` is **1 sentence / 7 printings** — two spellings, one
shape, no reader needed for either. **The row was materially cheaper than the price it was handed
on at**, and D395 had already said so; this slice re-derived it instead of inheriting the
correction.

### 🛑 MEMBER OR FIELD — THE FIRST *SUBJECT* WIDENING D391's RULE HAS BEEN ASKED ABOUT, AND THE DELEGATE CLAUSE IS WHAT DECIDES IT

D391's rule: *a comparand is a shape and takes a MEMBER; a filter the delegate already accepts is a
FIELD.* The handoff predicted **FIELD**, reasoning *"the comparand is the same and the ZONE is a
filter the walk already takes"*. **That is the error, and it is a precise one: there is no walk to
take it — the arm IS the walk.**

- **THE DELEGATE CLAUSE.** D391's field was cheap because `countAttachedEnergy` had accepted exactly
  that filter since D128, so the member became isomorphic to a call it was already making.
  `usedAttackOnYourLastTurn` (types.ts) takes ONE `InPlayPokemon` and cannot take a zone. A `zone`
  field therefore buys a **BRANCH inside the `conditionHolds` arm**, not an argument to a function.
- **SITE ARITHMETIC.** `yourActiveUsedAttackLastTurn` has **12 executable sites across 5 files** (8
  `kind:` literals + 2 exhaustive-switch arms + 2 narrowing assertions). A second member edits
  **ZERO** of them; an optional field edits **both** switch arms and rewrites the `conditionHolds`
  one **wholly** — `active !== null && used(...)` becomes a spread and a `.some`. That is D391's own
  test for a member, applied rather than quoted.
- ⚠️ **AND ONE MEASUREMENT POINTED THE OTHER WAY.** The note IS one interpolation slot here:
  *"your Active Pokémon used X during your last turn"* and *"1 of your Pokémon used X during your
  last turn"* share a skeleton, so D389's *"a second SENTENCE, not a second SLOT"* arithmetic — the
  bullet that carried D392 — **does not transfer**. It is recorded because it lost, not dropped
  because it lost. **A RULE WITH FOUR TESTS BEHIND IT IS NOT A RULE WITH FOUR AGREEING MEASUREMENTS
  BEHIND IT: SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECIDED.**

### 🛑 AN OPTIONAL FIELD IS INVISIBLE TO THE COMPILER — AND ON *THIS* FIELD IT FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE

D392 wrote down that an optional field forgotten on a row silently gets the default read. This slice
adds the sharp form: **the same forgotten default is too LOOSE and too STRICT depending on a token
the field does not control.**

- Under Angelite's **`barredIf`**, the Active-only default means the cancel does not bite on the
  board the card is printed for → **an illegal declaration is accepted**.
- Under Miltank `sv08.5-081`'s **`onlyIf`**, the identical omission would bar a legal attack.

`AttackTimingGate` reads one condition at two polarities on purpose (D281), so a condition member
whose meaning depends on a defaulted field can never have one safe default. **WHEN AN OPTIONAL FIELD
FEEDS A VALUE READ AT TWO POLARITIES, ITS DEFAULT IS WRONG SOMEWHERE BY CONSTRUCTION.**

⚠️ And the union had already settled a subject widening as a MEMBER **twice**, both times refusing
the scope parameter by name: `yourBenchHasNamed` → `yourNamedPokemonInPlay` (D279 — *"the printed
words are different, and the one printing that reads the narrow word depends on it being narrow"*)
and `yourActiveHasEnergyAttached` → `yourEnergyInPlayAtLeast` (*"folding them together behind a
`scope` parameter would put the choice between 'your Active' and 'your whole side' inside a value
the four other consumers of this vocabulary would then have to author"*). D394's own two printings
depend on the narrow reading staying narrow, for Falinks's reason exactly.

### 🛑 THE SECOND NON-ZERO GATE INDEX, ON THE OPPOSITE GEOMETRY — WHICH IS WHY IT IS A SECOND TEST

D395 gave `attackGate`'s `[attackIndex: number]` key its first falsifying board. **One board can
still be an accident.** These three are the second, and the failure they catch is a different one:

| | gate at | clause names | index-blind read does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Miltank `sv08.5-081` | 1 | index **0** ("Rollout") | **DEADLOCK** — gates the only attack that can open the gate |
| Sylveon ex ×3 | 1 | index **1** ("Angelite" bars ITSELF) | **CONFISCATION** — gates "Magical Charm" (160 dmg) and frees "Angelite" |

`splitOrder.test.ts` now reads **13 gates at index 0 / 4 at index 1**, and the registry side and the
TEXT side of that file **disagree for the first time**: 17 registry ids carry the field, 14 printings
carry a clause `splitAttackGateClause` claims. **The gap IS the measurement that no split was
authored.**

### ⚠️ NO SPLIT — AND THE INHERITED *REASON* FOR THAT WAS STALE

The gate clause is TRAILING; `splitAttackGateClause` is `^`-anchored by deliberate policy. The
handoff's cheap answer was right and its reason was not.

- **The measurement that stands**: all nine live readers were RUN over the stripped body
  (*"Choose 2 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. Shuffle those Pokémon and all attached cards into
  your opponent's deck."*) and **every one refuses it**. A trailing stripper buys **ZERO** printings.
- **The reason that did not**: the handoff said the body was *"Illumise `sv06-010`'s refusal
  verbatim — no `EffectOp` moves an OPPONENT'S benched Pokémon into the OPPONENT'S deck"*.
  **D299 BUILT THAT OP.** `returnBenched { whose: "opponent", dest: "deck" }` is exactly what
  Illumise's own body derives to today, and `censusAtHead.test.ts` has asserted since D307 that
  every gate sentence WITH A BODY resolves once split. What refuses Angelite's body is the **COUNT**
  (*"Choose **2**"* against a park of `min: 1, max: 1`) plus the two-sentence *"those Pokémon"*
  back-reference — Lickitung `sv05-124`/`-180`'s refusal, one op over.

🛑 **A REFUSAL COMMENT AGES IN TWO WAYS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MOVES A CHARACTER.** The stale bullet
sat in `effects.ts`'s `returnBenched` doc block, which the op's OWN slice (D299) had edited without
re-reading the refusal list beside it. `git grep` on any key in it finds it; nothing mechanical says
its premise expired. **RE-RUN THE READERS OVER THE SENTENCE BEFORE YOU QUOTE A REFUSAL OF IT.**

### THE FALSIFYING BOARD, AND IT IS REACHED TWO WAYS ON PURPOSE

Sylveon ex A uses "Angelite" and leaves the Active Spot; Sylveon ex B is promoted and declares
"Angelite" on the next of your turns. The printed clause bars it — A is 1 of your Pokémon and it used
Angelite during your last turn — and the ACTIVE-only read does not, because B's own `usedAttack` is
`null`. `angeliteCancel.test.ts` §3 drives it through `setActiveFromDeck` surgery **and** through a
real §11 `retreat` paying the printed cost of 2, so the board is reachable in play and not only in a
fixture. `stampAttackUse` (flow.ts) already wrote the stamp through a BENCH walk for its own reason
(an attacker can move off the Active Spot mid-attack), so the record the member reads was already
there — the slice is a walk, not new state.

### CENSUS MOVEMENT

Registry ids **710 → 713** (three REAL catalog ids, no `fix-*` demonstrator — the suite drives a
LOCAL `cardPool`, D275's idiom); `nonAttackRegistryIds()` **565 → 568**; `BUILT.ability`
**281 → 284**; whole-census `built` **1,706 → 1,709** and `units − built` **677 → 674**; the ability
instrument **281/128/117/130 → 284/129/118/131** — a **3:1:1:1** step, so sizing any of the last
three off the printing count is wrong by two; the `attackGate` shortfall **14 → 17**, its
`attacksJson`/`abilitiesJson` pair moving UNEVENLY for a **second consecutive slice** (284/267),
which only an `attackGate` row can do. **UNMOVED and that is the claim**: the gate-corpus split
(6 sentences / 14 printings), the two-split disjointness, `BUILT.attack` (**1,304**), the bonus
residue (**9 / 12**) and every `usedAttack`-family reader figure.

⚠️ **`ABILITY_NAME_TERMS` GAINS "Sylveon ex" AND NOT "Sylveon"** — the page already carries a

The `during your last turn` family is now **exhausted in Standard except for one banner refusal**:

## D397 — THE BENCHED-CUBONE FILTER: one walk with two tests on the same body, and D391's shape rule amended on its third test (engine 0.301.0 → **0.302.0**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 25**)

Marowak `sv07-073` (Stellar Crown) "Bone Vengeance" ({C}{C}, `60+`, **+120**, index **1** of TWO) —
*"If any of your Benched Cubone have any damage counters on them, this attack does 120 more
damage."*, **1 legal printing**. Its own index 0 is "Growl" ({F}, no printed damage): the control,
and — as the pool sweep found — a producer in its own right.

**WHAT SHIPS:** ONE `BoardCondition` member (`yourBenchNamedDamaged { name }`), its TWO
exhaustive-switch arms, ONE literal `CONDITIONAL_DAMAGE_CLAUSES` row, TWO fixtures and ONE dedicated
60. ZERO new state, ops, events, error codes, prompt kinds, choice kinds, readers, regexes,
templates, patterns, registry rows, `CardFilter` members, `redact.ts` bytes or `packages/schema`
bytes.

### 🛑 HAVING BOTH HALVES OF A CLAUSE IS NOT HAVING THE CLAUSE — `allOf` IS REFUTED ON A BOARD

Both halves were shipped members: `yourBenchHasNamed { name: "Cubone" }` (D118) and
`yourBenchDamaged` (D116). `allOf([…])` over the two asks *"some benched Cubone exists"* **and**
*"some benched body is damaged"* — two INDEPENDENT existentials over one array. The printed clause
runs ONE existential over the FILTERED set, so the composition is strictly WEAKER and a Bench
holding an UNDAMAGED Cubone beside a DAMAGED filler separates them. That board is built and driven
(§3), the composed reading answers TRUE on it, the member answers FALSE, and the printing deals its
unboosted 60. **THE COMPOSED READING IS NOT WRONG, IT IS WEAKER** — so the same suite shows the two
agreeing once the counters move onto the Cubone, because a guard that only showed a disagreement
could not tell "narrower" from "broken".

### 🛑 MEMBER OR FIELD — THE THIRD TEST OF D391's RULE, AND THE ONE THAT AMENDS IT

D391's rule reads *a comparand is a shape and takes a MEMBER; a filter the delegate already accepts
is a FIELD*, and D396 established that its clauses can disagree. They disagree here too, and all
four measurements were taken at this head rather than predicted:

* **DELEGATE — MEMBER, and this is the clause that was let bind.** `yourBenchDamaged`'s arm is an
  INLINE `bench.some((p) => p !== null && p.damage > 0)` with no delegate at all, and `cards.ts`
  carries no name-matching predicate to hand a filter to. **There is no walk to take the filter; the
  arm IS the walk** — D396's finding verbatim, one member over.
* **NOTE — FIELD, recorded rather than dropped.** `1 of your Benched Pokémon has damage counters on
  it` and `1 of your Benched Cubone has damage counters on it` are ONE interpolation slot apart and
  the unnarrowed spelling comes back byte-identical. This is the SECOND consecutive slice on which
  the NOTE clause dissented and lost.
* **SITES — even, so it decides nothing.** `yourBenchDamaged` has **24** executable sites (**22**
  `kind:` literals — 2 in source, 19 across four suites, 1 inside a mutant row's `replace` — plus
  its 2 exhaustive-switch arms). An optional field edits **3** of them and none of the 22; a second
  member edits **0** and adds 3.
* **POLARITY — MEMBER, and independently of the rule.** `BoardCondition` is read at two polarities
  on purpose: `AttackTimingGate.onlyIf` against `.barredIf` (D281) and `conditionGate.then` against
  `.otherwise` (D269). A forgotten optional `name` silently takes the UNNARROWED read, which is
  wrong in opposite directions under the two polarities and is never a type error. A REQUIRED field
  on a distinct member is a compile error when omitted.

### 🆕 THE AMENDMENT — THE NOTE CLAUSE IS RETIRED AS A DECIDER

Across four tests the two clauses have very different records:

| slice | DELEGATE says | NOTE says | answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| D391 (typed energy threshold) | FIELD (`countAttachedEnergy` took it since D128) | FIELD (one slot) | **FIELD** |
| D392 (substring name read) | MEMBER (no delegate) | MEMBER (a second sentence) | **MEMBER** |
| D396 (Angelite cancel) | MEMBER (the arm is the walk) | FIELD (one slot) | **MEMBER** |
| D397 (benched-Cubone filter) | MEMBER (the arm is the walk) | FIELD (one slot) | **MEMBER** |

**DELEGATE is 4/4 and NOTE is 2/4, which is chance.** So the rule is amended rather than asserted a
fourth time: **the NOTE clause is RETIRED AS A DECIDER and kept as a COST note**, and what remains
is *a filter is a FIELD only when a SHIPPED delegate already accepts it; otherwise it is a MEMBER —
and if the value is read at two polarities, MEMBER regardless, because an optional field then has no
safe default.* **A RULE TESTED THREE TIMES AND AMENDED ONCE IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE ASSERTED FIVE
TIMES.**

### ⚠️ THE FIELD IS `name`, WHICH IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM D392's NAMING RULE

D392 spelled its field `fragment` so a mistyped `kind` could not silently swap an exact read for a
substring one — there, the two members are two readings of the SAME fact and would otherwise differ
by their `kind` token alone. These two assert DIFFERENT facts (a name lookup, against a name lookup
AND a damage test), which is exactly what `yourBenchHasNamed` and `yourNamedPokemonInPlay` already
are — and those two have shared `name` since D279. **So `name` is this union's settled spelling for
a printed card name, and the kind-swap that stays typeable is bought in MUTANTS instead** (C5), which
is where D391 bought the same class of hazard.

### 🛑 THE §1.2 STACK READ IS THE MEMBER'S WHOLE BEHAVIOUR HERE, NOT HOUSEKEEPING

The attacker is a **Marowak** and the clause names **its own pre-evolution**. Damage rides a body
across an evolution and the NAME does not, so a damaged benched Cubone evolved into Marowak keeps
every counter and **stops satisfying the clause** — the one board where the two tests this member
conjoins move in opposite directions at the same instant. `yourBenchHasNamed` can lose its name that
way too; only this member can lose it while the other half of its own predicate stays true. Driven
on a real `evolve` action (§5), which is why the suite needs a board two turns in — §4/§10 bar
evolving on a seat's first turn, and the `armed` board IS that turn.

### 🛑 A LITERAL ROW AND NOT A TEMPLATE — THE CORPUS DECIDES IT, NOT THE COUNT

A pattern would have to read the token after "Benched" as a card NAME. Measured over the same
640-sentence column, that slot takes a **D207 BANNER** (*"your Benched **Ancient** Pokémon"*), two
**OWNER prefixes** (*"your Benched **Team Rocket's** Pokémon"*, *"all of your Benched **Cynthia's**
Pokémon"*) and a **BRACE CODE** (*"all of your Benched **{F}** Pokémon"*). A `(.+)` capture would
hand every one of those to an exact-name equality that succeeds against nothing — D118's rule
failing on an OPEN vocabulary, which is `yourBenchHasNamed`'s own reason for being four literal rows.
And under this skeleton the printed population is exactly ONE, so there is no second name to
generalise from either.

### 🛑 The invariant was wrong, not the card, and it had refused this member since D40

`BoardCondition`'s doc block has said since **D40**:

> a condition over hidden state (a hand's CONTENTS, a deck) would leak through the gate.

The hand half names **CONTENTS** deliberately, because a hand's SIZE is public and four shipped
members have read exactly that since D118. The deck half named the **ZONE** — and that unqualified
noun is what **four consecutive resume points** quoted forward as a reason to price a REFUSAL
first, twice in as many words.

**A CARDINALITY IS NOT A CONTENT.** `redact.ts` writes `deckCount: side.deck.length` for BOTH
sides with no viewer test, and `packages/schema`'s `RedactedSide` declares it `z.number()`, so this
member is evaluable on a projection and the P4 gap does not widen by a byte — unlike
`yourStadiumInPlay`, which really is unevaluable there. The invariant is corrected IN PLACE: the
line is **CONTENTS against CARDINALITY**, not zone against zone. A member reading a deck's ORDER or
its CARDS would still be a leak, and nothing in this union does.

⚠️ **THE GENERAL LESSON IS ABOUT DOC BLOCKS, NOT ABOUT DECKS.** An invariant written with an
UNQUALIFIED NOUN is a refusal with no expiry date on it, and this one blocked a buildable printing
through three handoffs without anyone re-deriving it. `redact.ts` answered the whole question in
one grep. **WHEN A HANDOFF SAYS "PRICE A REFUSAL FIRST", THE FIRST THING TO PRICE IS THE SENTENCE
THAT DEMANDS THE REFUSAL.**

| **POLARITY** — *independent veto* | **MEMBER** | a `BoardCondition` is read at `onlyIf`/`barredIf` and at `then`/`otherwise`, so an optional `zone?` has no safe default. |

### ⚠️ The threshold is a PARAMETER and the row is a LITERAL — one measurement decides both

Over the whole 640-sentence legal attack column, deck-CARDINALITY clauses are **2 sentences /

there is no deck FLOOR printed at any value. So:

  D118's test cannot be run on it;
- a `counts` **LIST** (`opponentPrizesRemaining`'s shape) would be reachability nobody prints —
  D377's arithmetic;
- and `count` stays a real field, because it is the axis a second printing would vary on. That is

### ⚠️ The board helper, and two failures that were observed rather than reasoned about

`endTurn` starts a turn with a §5.1 DRAW. So a deck trimmed to N **before** the pass is a deck of
N − 1 when the clause is read (the boundary case went green at the wrong value), and a deck trimmed
to **0** is a §14.3 deck-out LOSS before an attack can be declared at all (`GAME_OVER: deckOut`).
The trim now comes AFTER the draw — which is also what makes the EMPTY-deck board **ordinary**
rather than an edge: §14.3 is checked at the DRAW step and nowhere else, so a player who milled
themselves to zero attacks legally this turn and loses at the start of the next.

### ⚠️ The mechanical repair over-applied in the OPPOSITE direction to D397's

D397's lesson: key a scripted census repair on the `.toEqual([N, M])` TAIL, not on the offset chain.
That held wherever it was applied. What bit instead was a **blanket** bump of every
`refused.length + N` offset, which matched a LOCAL `refused` in three files that is not the bonus
residue at all (its tails are `[1,2]` / `[2,4]` / `[3,5]`). **A VARIABLE NAME IS NOT A POPULATION.**

And the corollary D397's rule leaves implicit, learned the hard way here: **THE TAIL IS THE THING A
SLICE MUST NOT MOVE.** Three past-head tails were bumped along with their chains — which nets to no
change at all and reddens the assertion — and were reverted. In these files a past-head figure is
FROZEN and the OFFSET is what each slice grows.

### 🛑 The shape question, and the cell that turned out to be EMPTY

The 6-printing sentence spells *those Pokémon* where Umbreon "Feint Attack"'s tail spells *that
Pokémon*. So the choice was a `th(?:at|ose)` CLASS — which resolves two sentences nobody prints —
or ENFORCED AGREEMENT between the count and the tail's number word. D399's handoff attached a
falsifiable prediction: *that* only at count 1, *those* only at count ≥ 2, at every amount.

**It holds in the direction it can be tested and is vacuous in the other.** Measured over
`legalAttackCorpus()`:

| cell | sentences | printings |
|---|---|---|
| this tail, *those*, count 2 | 1 | 6 |
| this tail, *that*, count 1 | **0** | **0** |
| the count-1 W/R sentence the column DOES print (bare tail) | 1 | 2 |

The optional *"or by any effects on that Pokémon"* clause this anchor has admitted since **0.46.0
serves no legal printing at all** — Umbreon's own legal printing carries the bare form. So the
prediction's first half could not be falsified and could not be confirmed either.

**⚠️ A PREDICTION WHOSE ANTECEDENT HAS AN EMPTY CELL IS NOT EVIDENCE, IT IS SILENCE.** Reporting it
as "held" would have been the census version of a vacuous guard — D200's shape (a flag that can
only fail if the card is deleted) arriving through a MEASUREMENT instead of through a test. **AN
EMPTY CELL IS A RESULT AND MUST BE NAMED AS EMPTY RATHER THAN COUNTED AS AGREEMENT.**

### ✅ What did decide it: the whole column, and it decided it mid-sentence

Across all 640 legal attack sentences:

- *that Pokémon* — **15 sentences / 32 printings**, referent SINGULAR every time (a "1 of", an
  Active, or a distributive "for each of").
- *those Pokémon* — **4 sentences / 12 printings**, referent PLURAL every time (a "2 of", a "3 of",
  an "up to 2 of").
- Zero counterexamples in either direction, and **one sentence spells BOTH, correctly**: the {D}
  evolve search says *"Choose up to 2 of your {D} Pokémon. For each of **those** Pokémon, search
  your deck for a card that evolves from **that** Pokémon…"*

**The column does not merely happen to agree; it SWITCHES spelling when the referent's number
switches.** That is the difference between a coincidence and a rule, and it is why enforcing
agreement is READING while the class would have been AUTHORING — D190b's *exact map or flag*, read
from the regex side.

**THE TRANSFERABLE FORM: a census that answers "no data" is asking you to change the DENOMINATOR,
not the predicate.** The anchor's own printings were the wrong population for the question.

### ⚠️ The constraint lives at the READ SITE, because a regex cannot express it

A regex cannot tie one capture to another capture's VALUE. Spelling agreement inside the pattern
would take TWO copies of the whole skeleton with the count written twice — the duplication D399's
shared fragment exists to prevent, one anchor over. So: one anchor, one count capture, one captured
number word, and one comparison in `deriveAttackEffect`'s 6d arm. A DISAGREEING sentence falls
through to the loud `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` path exactly where a printed 0 falls through.

Each refusal is driven by a **ONE-WORD FLIP** of a resolving sentence, with the unflipped twin
asserted to resolve in the same `it` — so nothing but the comparison can be blamed for either.
That is D399's *"a near-miss the fragment already refuses proves nothing about the anchor wrapped
around it"*, spent before it could cost a GAP.

### ⚠️ Inserting a capture renumbers every group after it — grep the PROSE

Four doc blocks across three files claimed *"`CHOSEN_ANY_TARGET`'s group 2"*: `effects.ts` (twice),
`index.ts` and `damageSuppression.test.ts`. All four are annotated in place with a
`🆕🆕 D400: group 3 now` rider (D178). **The grep that found them was `"group 2"`** — not a symbol
name, and not something a search for `CHOSEN_ANY_TARGET` surfaces in the same shape (D394's rule:
grep the SENTENCE, not the key).

Mutant **C6** exists for exactly this: keeping the `ignoreWR` branch on `match[2]`, which is now
the COUNT and is never `undefined`, silently gives EVERY any-target snipe the flag — and **no
census figure moves**, because every sentence still resolves. Four of D400's eight rows are silent
that way. **A reader can be right about what it ACCEPTS and wrong about what it BUILDS, and only a
board rung or an unprinted near-miss separates them.**

### ⚠️ `ignoreWR` at `count: 2` on `opponentAny` — the one genuinely unexercised combination

Team Rocket's Crobat ex ships `{opponentAny, count: 2}` without the flag; Umbreon ships the flag at
count 1. `fix-twinsnipe` and `fix-twinfeint` drive the SAME two picks — the opponent's Active and a
benched Bouffalant — under both readings, and the two answers move in OPPOSITE directions:

| pick | flat (`fix-twinsnipe`) | `ignoreWR` (`fix-twinfeint`) |
|---|---|---|
| Active (×2 Lightning) | **100** (§8.5 doubling) | **50** (Weakness nulled) |
| Bench (Bouffalant, −20 "Bouffer") | **30** | **50** (reduction nulled) |

Neither number can move without the other staying put, so a flag threaded to one `placeSnipe` arm
only cannot pass.

### ⚠️ What this slice did NOT buy, named rather than left to be discovered

Two more count-≠-1 any-target sentences are printed and both lead with a discard —
*"Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 120 damage to 2 of your opponent's
Pokémon. (…)"* (3 printings) and *"Discard all Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 110
damage to 3 of your opponent's Pokémon. (…)"* (1). They sit off the `^This attack does` anchor and
a count capture structurally cannot move them. With their count-1 siblings that is **4 sentences /
7 printings on ONE shape: a self-discard COST followed by an any-target snipe** — a
split-sentence slice, not a regex slice, and the next thing to price. Three of the five largest
remaining sentences in the whole unresolved corpus share that shape, which is why the sequencing
question is worth more than any single sentence.


## D404 — THE MANDATORY HAND WIPE AND REFILL: an arm whose whole price is an ORDER (engine 0.309.0)

The largest single sentence left in the SPLIT-AWARE residue D403 measured, and the cheapest.
*"Discard your hand and draw 6 cards."* — **1 sentence / 7 legal printings** — on ONE
whole-sentence anchor (`DISCARD_HAND_DRAW`) and ONE `deriveAttackEffect` arm returning
`[{ op: "discardHand" }, { op: "drawCards", count }]`. `BUILT.attack` 1348 → **1355**. **ZERO new
ops, ZERO new fields, ZERO readers, ZERO `BoardCondition` members, ZERO registry rows and ZERO
`attack.ts` edits.**

**THE PRINTED "and" IS AN ORDER, NOT A SET, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE CORRECTNESS CLAIM.** Swapped,
the six cards just drawn are exactly the ones discarded and the attack ends with an EMPTY hand:
every op present, every op right in isolation, and the program wrong. ⚠️ **A COUNT CANNOT SEE
IT** — a hand of three discarded and six drawn reads six under both readings — so the rung that
owns this claim captures the hand and the deck's top six **BY UID** before the attack and asserts
the two SETS end up in opposite zones. Generalised: **when a program's defect is a permutation of
correct ops, the instrument has to be identity, never cardinality.** `mutants.ts` has carried the
same defect against Larry's Skill's registry row since D336; this is the first time a DERIVER
could make it.

**BOTH HANDED-DOWN FALSIFIERS HELD, AND THE REASONS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN THE VERDICTS**
(D403's rule, sixth payment).

1. **`drawCards` ON A SHORT DECK COSTS NO RULE, AND §8 ALREADY HELD THE PRECEDENT.**
   `drawToHand` (types.ts) SLICES the deck and pushes the SHORT list, so a 6-card draw off a
   2-card deck files two and stops. **§14.3's deck-out is checked at the DRAW** (`flow.ts`
   `startTurn`), never at the moment the deck runs dry — so an attack-borne draw inside §8 cannot
   lose the game however deep it digs, and the loss stays OWED to the drawing player's next turn.
   That is not this arm's invention: `deckTopMill`'s doc block says it about a self-mill that
   empties the ATTACKER's deck mid-attack, and `ATTACK_DRAW`'s arm says it about its own short
   draw. `discardHandDraw.test.ts` §5 drives it end to end — attack on a 2-card deck, pass the
   turn back, and P1 loses at their OWN draw step with `reason: "deckOut"`.
2. **`discardHand` HAS NO TRAINER-SHAPED GATE, AND `programPlayable` NEVER SEES AN ATTACK.** The
   interpreter's case is one line, fully automatic, no park, no `sourceUid`, keyed on `ctx.seat`
   alone; `programPlayable`'s three call sites are `playTrainer` and the two ability paths. D385
   had already reached this op from ATTACK text inside `optionalCostOps`; what is new is only the
   TOP LEVEL. **The question "is this op reachable from a new site" is answered by grepping the
   op's GATES, not by reasoning about the sentence.**

⚠️ **A CAPTURE WHOSE POPULATION HAS ONE MEMBER CANNOT BE TESTED FROM THAT POPULATION.** The legal
attack column prints **6 and nothing else** for this skeleton, so a literal `6` in the anchor
could never go red off `legalAttackCorpus()` — the corpus simply cannot distinguish a capture from
a constant. The evidence had to come from where the parameter varies: `registry.ts` carries the
identical printed skeleton at **7** (Professor's Research `sv01-189`) and **5** (Carmine
`sv06-145`), both hand-authored years before this arm. §2 reads the arm's output at those two
counts **against those hand-authored programs** rather than against a re-typed literal, so one
sentence with two producers has to agree byte for byte. `ATTACK_DRAW`'s own `(\d+)` is the sibling
arrangement.

🆕 **THE SUITE FOUND A GAP THE SLICE HAD NOT PREDICTED, AND IT IS THE TWENTY-SECOND OP IN
`preventBlock.test.ts`'s §11 TABLE.** That sweep is TOTAL over what an attack in `FIXTURE_POOL`
can emit, and it went RED naming `discardHand` — arriving the way D181's three did (an op the
Trainer path has run since M4 that the deriver has just learned to reach) rather than the way
D313's did (a population gap). Classified **untouched**: the two zones are the actor's own HAND
and own DISCARD PILE and neither is a Pokémon, so there is no body for a §11 block to protect.
⚠️ **THE PROBE READS THE DISCARD PILE, NOT THE HAND** — an op that emptied the hand and dropped
the cards on the floor would satisfy *"the hand is smaller"*, and this table's whole business is
telling a landed effect from a swallowed one.

✅ **NO `attack.ts` TERM WAS OWED, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE SEAM RATHER THAN OF THE
SENTENCE.** `effectSimulated`'s FIRST disjunct is `program !== null`, and `program` is
`authored ?? derived` — so any new `deriveAttackEffect` arm answers the effect half by
construction. `programDamage` stays FALSE (neither op is a `damageDefender`), so the printed base
is KEPT and dealt by the pre-program §8.5 pipeline, which is what `fix-handdraw`'s flat `30`
exists to observe. **The three disjunction chains were not touched, so none of the seven
multi-line `find` rows that span them moved** — the first slice in eight not to pay that toll.

✅ **AND THE MUTANT BLOCK IS THE FIRST IN THIS CORPUS WITH NO `find` SPANNING A COMMENT LINE.**
The arm was WRITTEN for it: both explanatory blocks sit above the `return` rather than between the
two op literals, because the ORDER is what the rows have to name and a comment spliced between
those lines would break every one of them without a character of the code moving. D403's own
lesson, applied to a two-line array instead of a disjunction chain.


## D403 — THE ADDITIVE HALF OF THE SAME FAMILY: a fold that needed the printed base (engine 0.308.0)

The half the section below refused, taken once its **mechanism** was bought rather than argued
around. *"You may discard up to 2 [Basic] Energy from your Benched Pokémon. This attack does
{60|90} more damage for each card you discarded in this way."* — **2 sentences / 8 legal
printings**, 8 of the 10 D402 measured. `BUILT.attack` 1340 → **1348**.

**WEAKNESS CANNOT TEST A ONE-HIT-VERSUS-TWO CLAIM; ONLY A SUBTRACTION CAN.** This is the finding
to carry out of the slice, and it is a statement about algebra rather than about this family. The
claim under test is that `base + P × N` is dealt as ONE §8.5 pass. A ×2 Weakness **DISTRIBUTES**
— `(b + s) × 2` equals `b × 2 + s × 2` — so a Weakness rung returns the same number under the
correct build and under the split-hit build it exists to refuse: an identity dressed as a guard,
the vacuous shape `conventions.md` is about. **Resistance, `damageReductionAfterWR` and the §8.1
survival clamp are each paid ONCE PER HIT**, so any of them separates them. On
`fix-psychic-resist-big` (200 HP, −30 Psychic) two discards read **140** for the built shape,
**110** for two passes, **90** for a dropped base and **160** for an unsuppressed one. Generalised:
**a MULTIPLICATIVE passive cannot distinguish any reassociation of a sum; an ADDITIVE or CLAMPING
one can.** Pick the instrument from the algebra, not from what the fixture pool happens to hold.

**THE OBSTACLE WAS A SIGNATURE, NOT A SHAPE.** `deriveAttackEffect` takes only a STRING and the
printed base is a field on the attack, so a captured `more` on D402's anchor would have produced
an op whose `base` nothing could populate. The build is therefore a READER
(`deriveAttackDiscardScaledBoost`, the ELEVENTH) plus an EXPORTED assembler
(`discardScaledBoostProgram(reading, base)`) read at `attack.ts`'s own site — D163's finding on
the `SELF_COUNTER_SCALE` / `SELF_COUNTER_MULTIPLY` pair reproduced one count-source over, and the
same shape D316/D317/D318/D381 already have. **The repair on the op is an OPTIONAL `base` whose
absent value is ZERO**, which is byte-for-byte what every `per`/`count` op has meant since D96 —
so it is a widening rather than a new arm, and `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 25.

⚠️ **A `scaledBase` CLAIMANT IS OWED FOR AN *ORDERING* REASON, NOT A NESTING ONE, AND THE THREE
EXISTING DOC BLOCKS ALL SAY OTHERWISE.** D316/D317/D381 each attribute their own `scaledBase` term
to their `damageDefender` being NESTED inside a gate that `programDamage`'s top-level `.some` does
not walk. That is true of them and is **not the general rule**. This slice's hit is a bare
TOP-LEVEL op, exactly like Hail Blade's, and the term is owed anyway: `programDamage` is computed
from the registry/derived program **four hundred lines above the append**, so no reading-borne
program can reach it, nested or not. Any future reading read at that site owes the term.

🛑 **`discardEnergy.from` GAINS A COMPLEMENT.** `yourBench` is the own side MINUS the Active, so
the union's *"a spot, a side and a body"* is now four kinds. `yours` is wrong for it on every real
board of the family — the attacker's own cost Energy is attached to the ACTIVE and a cost is not
spent — and the member cost TWO literals (`discardVictimSeat`, `discardableEnergies`) plus ONE
caption arm, because `attachedEnergies` has taken a `"bench"` argument since it was written with
no producer ever asking for it. **`discardNote`'s `switch` is EXHAUSTIVE over this union**, which
is the compiler D222 said the old negated conjunction did not have: the member cannot be added
without answering the caption question.

⚠️ **TWO PROCESS FINDINGS, BOTH PAID FOR HERE.**

1. **A COVERAGE-FLAG ASSERTION AFTER A PARK IS GREEN BY CONSTRUCTION.**
   `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED` is pushed while the attack is **declared**; a parking program splits
   one attack into two actions with two event lists, and the row can never appear in the second.
   Two of this slice's fifteen mutants (the `effectSimulated` and `modifierSimulated` terms)
   SURVIVED the first probe for exactly that reason, and nothing else in the file noticed because
   every other assertion was correct about its own list. **When a program parks, say which of the
   two event lists your claim lives in.**
2. **THE RAW RESIDUE OVER-COUNTS EVERY GATE-SPLIT SENTENCE, BY EXACTLY `splitHead`.** D402's
   handed-down residue list named *"If you go second, … This attack does 30 damage for each of
   your Benched Pokémon."* (7 printings) as a head; `YOUR_BENCH_MULTIPLY` has read it since D282,
   reachable only after `splitAttackGateClause` takes the clause off the front. Eleven-reader raw
   residue **243 / 413**; split-aware **238 / 400**; difference 5 sentences / **13** printings, to
   the unit. **A residue list is a claim about a sweep, and a sweep that does not split is not the
   one `BUILT.attack` uses.**


## D402 — THE DISCARD-COUNT-SCALED ATTACK: a deriver's refusal re-priced by re-deriving its reason (engine 0.307.0)

The slice the section above handed on, taken at HALF its scope and for a measured reason:
**6 sentences / 13 legal printings** of the `"… for each card you discarded in this way."` family,
on ONE map-built whole-sentence anchor (`ENERGY_DISCARD_SCALED_DAMAGE`) and ONE
`deriveAttackEffect` arm returning the two-op pair `registry.ts` has spelled BY HAND since D96.
Zero new ops, fields, `BoardCondition` members or registry rows. `BUILT.attack` 1327 → **1340**.

### 🛑 The refusal expired because its REASON died, not because its verdict aged

D96 wrote *"a variable-count park the deriver deliberately refuses"* **on the day it invented the
vocabulary**. On that day there was no `discardEnergy.count: "any"`, no `cap`, no
`recordAs: "discarded"` and no `damageDefender` — the sentence had nothing to derive INTO, and a
registry row was the only honest producer. D97 added the last piece and did not revisit the note.
What reached this head was therefore a **verdict whose premise had been gone for three hundred
decisions**.

**THE TRANSFERABLE FORM, and it is the fifth slice this move has paid on (D396, D398, D399, D401,
D402): a refusal written at the moment a mechanism was INVENTED is the most likely kind to have
expired, because the thing it was waiting for is the thing that slice shipped.** Grep the SENTENCE,
not the key (D384): `mutants.ts` held nothing, but `registry.ts` (three doc blocks), `attack.ts`,
`testFixtures.ts`, `providesEnergy.test.ts`, `hailBlade.test.ts` and `psyPurge.test.ts` all did.

### 🛑 D187 is an argument you can MEASURE, and here it paid 13 to 0

*An arm transfers across sets; a registry row does not.* Chien-Pao ex `sv02-061` and Mewtwo VSTAR
`swsh10.5-031` have both **rotated**, so the two hand-authored rows serve **ZERO** Standard-legal
printings while the arm serves **13**.

⚠️ **The rows were KEPT rather than retired, and that is the part to copy.** A registry program wins
(`programFor(id)?.attack?.[index] ?? derive`), so no board moved; Mewtwo VSTAR's row is additionally
this engine's only index-keyed multi-attack witness, and deleting it would have deleted the proof
that "Star Raid" does not inherit index 0's program. What changed is that two
`deriveAttackEffect(...) === null` rungs became `toEqual(AUTHORED)` rungs — D361's move on Mawile,
one family over. **A null rung can only go red one way; an agreement rung goes red whenever EITHER
producer moves alone**, which is the defect a hand-authored row and a text reader can actually have.
Mutant C3 (the `cap` dropped, which is Hail Blade's row copied verbatim) is killed by
`psyPurge.test.ts` and is the evidence that the re-pointed claim is load-bearing.

### 🛑 The FOLD is the family's real split, and the other half is refused on a mechanism

| half | sentences / printings | fold | taken? |
|---|---|---|---|
| *"does N damage for each"* | **6 / 13** | MULTIPLY — printed "N×" IS the per-unit, base dropped | ✅ built |
| *"does N **more** damage for each"* | **3 / 10** | ADDITIVE — printed base KEPT | ❌ second reader |
| deck mills + a hand discard feeding a chosen target | **3 / 4** | — | ❌ different mechanism |

`damageDefender {per, count}` deals its hit through a **separate `snipeActive` pass**, and
`attack.ts` drops the printed base whenever the program owns the damage (`programDamage` →
`scaledBase`). That is exactly right for the multiply half. For the additive half a kept base would
deal the printed number in the pre-program pipeline and the scaled part inside the program:
**Weakness DISTRIBUTES over a split hit, but Resistance and `damageReductionAfterWR` are
SUBTRACTIONS paid once PER HIT and the §8.1 survival clamp is asked twice**, so `base + per×N` is
not `base` then `per×N`. D163's finding on `SELF_COUNTER_SCALE` / `SELF_COUNTER_MULTIPLY`, one
count-source over: **a fold is a reader, not a field.**

### ⚠️ The handed-down prediction was false, and its two named falsifiers were CORRELATED

The prediction said all 12 sentences were expressible with no new op and no new field, the one
widening being a Bench-only member on `discardEnergy.from`. Measured over `legalAttackCorpus()`:

* every Bench-only printing — 2 sentences / **8** printings — is on the ADDITIVE side;
* the count of Bench-only **MULTIPLY** printings is **ZERO**, asserted as zero rather than left
  unsaid (D400).

So the fold split **removed the need for the union member entirely** rather than compounding with
it. `discardEnergy.from` was not widened, and that is also why `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` stays 25.
**When a prediction names two falsifiers, test whether they are correlated before you test either
one.** Both mutants built from them (C9 admitting `more`, C10 admitting `Benched`) are silent on
every real printing for exactly that reason, and are caught only by the vary-ONE-byte rung: a
positive control, then the fold alone, then the zone alone, then the sentence as printed — which
differs in both places at once (D399's rule made mechanical).

### ⚠️ One read site moved that no census counts

`energyNoun` (interpreter.ts) grew a `basicEnergy` arm. The family's largest member — *"You may
discard any amount of **Basic** Energy from your Pokémon"*, 6 legal printings — is the first
sentence ever to reach `discardNote` with that filter, and the caption would otherwise have promised
*"any amount of Energy"* over a pick restricted to Basic Energy (D295's caption defect, one
destination over). `auraNarrowing.test.ts`'s read-site census had graded that function **ZERO** on
the ground that it *"spells two kinds and returns 'Energy' for the rest, so a filter that is not an
Energy filter was already handled"* — true of `basicPokemon` and **not** true of `basicEnergy`,
which is an Energy filter falling through to a WIDER noun than the card prints. `moveNote` had
hand-spelled the same phrase since D226 and now delegates; its bytes are unchanged on every board.

### ⚠️ The anchor's own shape questions, and how each was settled

* **The QUANTIFIER is three COUPLED literals**, not a `(?:You may )?` prefix times an
  `(any amount|all|up to N)` tail. The column prints *"You may discard any amount of"*,
  *"Discard all"* and *"Discard up to N"* and prints NEITHER crossing, so a matrix would have
  derived two sentences nobody prints (D361's refusal, re-derived).
* **The ZONE is a free parameter**, and deliberately so: `this Pokémon` and `your Pokémon` are one
  field (`from`) at two values the interpreter already resolves, the way the TYPE is one field at
  nine. Where D361's refused matrix would have made the engine INVENT a behaviour, every
  combination here is a board action it already performs.
* **The FILTER's third arm is `Basic` → `basicEnergy`, not `providesEnergy`.** "Basic Energy" names
  the CARD, not what the card provides — the distinction `TYPED_SELF_DISCARD`'s own doc draws about
  Decidueye's hand discard — so a provision reading would have offered a Special Energy.
* **`Energy(?: cards)?`** is `DECK_TOP_MILL`'s alternation: exactly one printing spells the plural
  and it means the same thing.

### ⚠️ The `count: "all"` arm is the first program to file a §9.2 record INLINE

*"Discard all {L} Energy from this Pokémon"* asks nothing, so the whole attack resolves in one
action: the board decides the count, the record carries it, and the damage reads it with no prompt
anywhere. The op's doc had said for six years that *"only the `"any"` mode records today"* — a
statement about what was AUTHORED, not about the interpreter, whose `op.count === "all"` branch has
called `recordMoved` since D96. `fix-allscale` and `fix-basicscale` are the pair that separates
*"the program parks"* from *"the OPERAND parks"*.

### ⚠️ A tooling fact paid for here

Biome's `useTemplate` and `noUnusedTemplateLiteral` together force **every concatenated piece of a
map-built regex to carry an interpolation**: a quoted string beside an interpolated template trips
the first, and a backticked string without one trips the second. `SELF_DISCARD_THEN_ANY_TARGET`
looks like a counterexample and is not — none of its pieces interpolates. So a map-built anchor has
as many source pieces as it has `${…}`s, and this one is two long lines for that reason alone.


## D401 — THE SELF-DISCARD COST IN FRONT OF AN ANY-TARGET SNIPE: a sequencing question whose answer was already in the code (engine 0.306.0)

The slice the section above handed on, taken exactly as scoped: **4 sentences / 7 legal
printings**, one whole-sentence COMPOUND anchor (`SELF_DISCARD_THEN_ANY_TARGET`) and one
`deriveAttackEffect` arm returning two already-shipped ops in printed order. Zero new ops, fields,
`BoardCondition` members or registry rows. `BUILT.attack` 1320 → **1327**.

### 🛑 The shape question was answered by a GREP OF THE READER, not by a census of the cards

The handoff asked *"one anchor or two reads"* and told the successor to look for a split
mechanism first. The grep that settled it is one line: **`deriveAttackEffect` is never called
recursively — not once, anywhere in the file.** So there is no `. `-joined composition path and
there never has been; every compound this engine reads is its own whole-sentence anchor returning
both ops in printed order (`DEFENDER_POISON_CANT_RETREAT` arm 5c, `COUNTER_PUT_ANY_THEN_SELF_LOCK`
arm 25, D147's `SELF_DISCARD_ALL_THEN_REDUCTION`, D148's `SELF_DISCARD_ONE_THEN_DEFENDER_LOCK`).

⚠️ **D382's `. Then, ` join is NOT the counterexample it looks like.** It lives in
`deriveAttackBonusConsequent`, not here, and it dispatches its captured tail over a CLOSED anchor
list *precisely because it could not delegate to this reader* — that consequent lowercases its
verb and `deriveAttackEffect` returns null for it. The transferable form: **when a handoff asks
whether a general mechanism exists, the cheapest honest answer is a grep for the CALL, not a
census of the cards.**

### 🛑 The same earlier decision reversed on one axis and upheld on the other, in one slice

D382 made two calls about widening, and this slice goes opposite ways on them.

**The JOIN call is REVERSED.** D382 refused `(?:, and |\. Then, )` because its anchor wraps a
leading `(.+)` antecedent, so an alternation would have collapsed the pair *"into a regex whose
greed nobody can read off the page"*. `SELF_DISCARD_THEN_ANY_TARGET` **contains no `.`
metacharacter at all** — every byte outside its three captures is a literal, and the captures are
`(all|\d+)` and two `(\d+)` — so `(?:\. This|, and this)` can match at exactly one offset and
there is no greed to hide. Measured over `legalAttackCorpus()`: the period join carries **3
sentences / 6 printings**, the comma join **1 / 1**, and the two derive to the IDENTICAL program.
A `. `-only reading would have taken three of the four and refused the fourth **on a conjunction
rather than on a mechanism** — D399's *"a refusal that expired on a literal"*. The CASE lives in
the join (`\. This` / `, and this`) rather than in a `[Tt]` class, on D246/D316's rule: a case
class gives up the whole-sentence discipline in both directions at once.

**The TAIL call is UPHELD.** `CHOSEN_ANY_TARGET`'s tail is a THREE-way optional (bare | the
Benched clarifier | Umbreon's W/R sentence); this anchor's is TWO-way, because a W/R tail behind a
discard cost returns **ZERO** sentences in the whole 640-sentence legal attack column. Sharing a
fragment with that anchor is otherwise **exactly D383's condition** — a second reading of one
printed clause with a lower-case leading word — and it was still declined, because sharing a
fragment is also a widening of every caller to every arm the fragment carries.

⚠️ **The discriminator is which of the two arguments is a MEASUREMENT.** *"Is the alternation
readable"* is an argument about the regex and yields to inspection; *"does the column print it"*
is a count and does not. **A rule inherited from a prior slice must be re-tested against the
reason it was written down with, not against its conclusion.**

✅ A side benefit that mattered mechanically: `CHOSEN_ANY_TARGET`'s bytes were never touched, so
D400's find surface — including its C3 row anchored on that anchor's first template line — is
intact and needed no re-transcription.

### 🛑 The first attack program in this engine that PARKS TWICE on one printed sentence pair

`discardEnergy {from: "yourActive", count: 2}` asks which Energy; `damageChosen {target:
"opponentAny", count: 2}` then asks which bodies. **The persisted question was asked of the
CONTINUATION rather than of the ops**, because a queue of two parks is exactly where a new
persisted shape would have had to appear. It does not: `EffectContinuation` has carried
`rest: EffectOp[]` since M5 and `resumeProgram` re-enters `runProgram` with it, so a program that
parks, resumes and parks again is the existing shape doing what it already did.
**`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` STAYS 25.** D342's `searchTopOrderProgram` (searchDeck then reorderTop)
is the two-park ATTACK precedent and has been live since that slice.

⚠️ **The ORDER of the two ops is invisible to every census.** Mutant C2 returns them snipe-first
— the board ends in the same place, every sentence still resolves, no figure moves — and only a
rung that drives both parks in sequence and reads the EVENT STREAM ACROSS TWO ACTIONS can see it.
That is why `anyTargetSnipe.test.ts` §6 asserts every `ENERGY_DISCARDED` lands in the first resume
and every `DAMAGE_DEALT` in the second, rather than only reading the derived op back.

### ⚠️ Four earlier refusal claims re-pointed NULL → SHAPE, found by grepping the SENTENCE

`attackPark.test.ts` and `tailsSelfCost.test.ts` each held Kyurem `sv06.5-047` "Trifrost" as a
NULL witness — the **last of D145's four compounds** to leave those lists, after D147 and D148
took Eiscue's two, leaving only Weavile `sv06.5-014`'s Paralyze compound unread.
`anyTargetSnipe.test.ts` §1 and `conditionalBenchSnipe.test.ts` §1 each asserted the count-≠-1
compounds were refused by all nine readers. Every population figure is kept and each rung gains
the strictly stronger claim: **the bare anchors STILL refuse them, and the compound derives TWO
ops where a prefix match would derive one.** A build that had merged the two anchors into a prefix
match would pass every `toBeNull` in the repo and silently drop a printed Energy cost.

### ⚠️ What this slice did NOT buy, named rather than left to be discovered

The residue is **254 sentences / 442 printings**, and its biggest *shape* is not its biggest
*sentence*: the `"… for each card you discarded in this way."` family is **12 sentences / 27
printings** unresolved, against 7 for the largest single sentence left. Its two largest members
are 6 printings each — *"You may discard any amount of Basic Energy from your Pokémon. This attack
does 70 damage for each card you discarded in this way."* and *"You may discard up to 2 Energy
from your Benched Pokémon. This attack does 60 **more** damage for each card you discarded in this
way."*

**The ops already ship, authored twice, as REGISTRY rows.** Chien-Pao ex's "Hail Blade" and Mewtwo
VSTAR's "Psy Purge" are both
`[discardEnergy {from, filter, count, recordAs: "discarded"}, damageDefender {per, count:
"discarded"}]` in `registry.ts`, and the row's own doc says the sentence is *"a variable-count park
the deriver deliberately refuses"*. **That refusal is the thing to re-price**, now that a two-op
compound behind a park is known to cost one anchor and one arm. Two things will decide it: the

that union), and the family splits on the same one-word FOLD discriminator D163 already paid for —
*"does N damage for each"* multiplies and drops the printed base, *"does N **more** damage for
each"* adds to it.


## D420 — THE HAND-ENERGY COST AND ITS CANCEL: the KO-without-damage family closed (engine 0.322.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **26**)

**3 sentences / 4 legal printings** — the 6-card compound (2), the 2-card cost (1), the 1-card cost
(1). With D414/D415/D416 this **closes the KO-without-damage family**: 7 sentences / 13 printings.

### 🛑 Why the cost and the cancel had to land together

`payFromHand` inside an ATTACK **pays what it can and refuses nothing**, and `handCostUnmet` has **no
`attack.ts` caller**. So the cost without the cancel is a **FREE KNOCK OUT** — a hand of two Grass
discards two and Knocks Out anyway, **passing every "was the cost paid" assertion**. That is not a
tidiness argument; it is the defect the slice was ordered around, and mutant C4 is it.

✅ It also discharges the decision `effects.ts` has said is owed since D46: **at the attack seam an
unpayable hand cost is a CANCEL, checked in front of §8.5, never inside the program** — with
why-not-a-`conditionGate` (D125's placement rule) and why-not-`handCostUnmet`-in-`attack.ts` (a second
reader free to disagree, inventing refusals the card does not print).

🛑 **Backed by a structural guard, not a comment**: no derived attack program may hold a `payFromHand`
at **any depth** without a cancel requirement from the same sentence — recursive, and negatively
controlled against a top-level-only scan. **The hazard is closed for the next hand-cost sentence.**

### The member

`yourBasicEnergyInHandAtLeast { energy: BasicEnergyType; count }` — a zone mirror evaluated by
`matchesFilter`'s own predicate, so **gate and payment agree by construction**: the arm asks exactly
what `handCostCandidates` is about to answer, and a hand-rolled loop would drift toward a free KO.

⚠️ It is the union's **first member reading a hidden zone's CONTENTS**, and the argument was **cited**
(D70's posture: the viewer's own hand only, server-side, shipped as a boolean) rather than invented.
The authoring hazard is named: the union is shared with `trainerPlayableIf`, which IS projected, so
the member is **attack-gate-only today**.

### 🛑 A doc block written at D417 was false, and it was a trap

It told a successor to add a table row *"and stop — no anchor, no arm"*. **True only when the head is
already claimed.** For Ogerpon it is not, and a row ALONE makes `resolvedByAnyReader` true — stepping
`BUILT.attack` while the attack still falls to the loud path. **D407's built-but-dead, introduced by a
recipe rather than by code.** Corrected in place; the rule now states its precondition. And the
correction was itself corrected — D420 does *not* make the `cancelSplit === null` conjunct live.

### ⚠️ One mutant survived, and it was the author's fault

C1's first spelling mutated a `case` **label** with a TypeScript `as` assertion — erased at runtime,
so it expressed no defect and the sweep reported a GAP that did not exist. **A row that survives
because it changes nothing is worse than no row.** Re-authored onto the zone read, KILLED.
**5 mutants / 5 killed / 0 GAPs.**

### Also closed

A `find`-uniqueness collision fixed **at the source** (locals renamed rather than re-anchoring five
rows); a stale corpus line pointer a test had copied; and **the residue's SENTENCE cardinality**,
which was guarded nowhere while its printings count was pinned.

**563**; `unbuiltAttack` 321 → **317**. `splitHead` 13, `compoundHead` 18, registry 16 unmoved.

place of a catalog. Completeness is now machine-checked: **47 collections, 0 unguarded**, and the

`clauseApostrophe.test.ts` asserted 139 where the truth is **140**. A missing reader

Every other figure in all 36 files stood still. **Proven directly**: a red-drive deleted the largest

- **Adjacency paid proactively**: readers spliced mid-list in all 36 files, never appending, reason

- **Refusal rungs re-pointed with D418's second-half question asked of each**; the answer was

## D418 — THE CENSUS INSTRUMENTS WERE STALE IN 38 OF 40 FILES (no engine change; 0.321.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **26**)

**Seventeen false assertions corrected across eleven suites**, ten of them **wrong figures** rather
than misleading prose. No behaviour moved, so no version moved.

### The measurement, and the correlation that is the whole mechanism

40 test files keep a hand-maintained `READERS` array. **38 were stale at HEAD** — 25 nine-long, 13
eleven-long, against 12 exported. **The only two that were current are exactly the two with a
module-surface guard.** Nothing else predicted correctness.

Ground truth over `legalAttackCorpus()`: 9 readers → 406 / 1,347; 11 → 411 / 1,363; **12 → 412 /
1,364, residue 228 / 368**. Five suites were off by **6 sentences / 17 printings** (stale since
**D381 — never re-pointed in 179 commits**); three by 1 / 1 (since D417).

✅ **Every frozen baseline endpoint survived byte-identical** — the proof that the baselines were
right and only the live-head term was wrong.

### 🛑 The finding that matters most is about process

**This fix had been explicitly declined**, by `exactHandSize.test.ts`: *"THE NINE-READER ARRAY IS NOT
A BUG AND IS NOT WIDENED HERE… adding a tenth reader to it would move numbers this slice has nothing
to do with."*

**That reasoning was locally correct** — and it is why the drift lasted 179 commits and grew from one
missing reader to three. **A defect every local decision is right to decline has no local fix; it
makes every slice the wrong place and leaves no place at all.**

✅ **D418 did not answer the argument. It removed the premise.** The figures now come off a
module-derived `attackReaderSurface()` / `resolvedByAnyReader()` in `censusAttackCorpus.ts` FIRST, so
widening a local array moved **zero digits** — proven by a red-drive where deleting a reader left
every figure green and reddened only the guard. The original refusal is kept word for word with the
correction marked beneath it.

⚠️ **And its workaround is the second half of the lesson**: removing one sentence from a list rather
than fixing the array is a repair that does not compound, and by D418 it had become a rung that would
go **RED if anyone fixed the array** — the repair defending the defect.

### What was built

- **Eleven module-surface rungs**, each pinning the diff **and** the count separately (a diff alone
  stays green when a reader is deleted from module and list together).
- **Refusal rungs re-pointed, not deleted.** Where a rung claimed *"no reader takes this"* about a
  family, the claim came apart: the Stadium row is now asserted RESOLVED and claimed **specifically**
  by `deriveAttackCancelRequirement`, while the hand-cost row is asserted still refused by **every**
  reader including D417's — a **sharper** rung, because D417 built the mechanism for one body and not
  for the family.
- **A mutant anchor saved without touching `mutants.ts`**: appending a reader would have moved the
  `];` that a D382 row quotes, so the entry was spliced mid-list with the reason stated. All 1,522
  anchors verified; the row re-probed by hand and still KILLED, now by the new guard.

### ⚠️ Follow-on debt

**30 files still hold an unguarded hand-kept copy.** Their figures are correct today **by luck**. The

## D417 — THE TRAILING, ANAPHORIC CANCEL: a reader for a mechanism that already existed (engine 0.321.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 26**)

*"Discard a Stadium in play. If you can't, this attack does nothing."* — Eternatus `sv08-141`,
**1 sentence / 1 legal printing**. One regex, one splitter, one head-keyed table, one reader, and
four lines at the `attack.ts` reader seam.

### The scoping inverted the plan

The handoff said to price the cancel and, if it did not exist, choose a placement. **It exists.**
`attack.ts` has cancelled whole attacks in front of the §8.5 pipeline since **D125**, with the
printed semantics in its own comment — *"no damage, no W/R, no effect ops, no triggers"*. What was
missing was a **reader**: the existing anchor is `^`-anchored and reads only sentences that OPEN with
the clause; this printing puts it TRAILING and ANAPHORIC. **D380 had already named the gap** — *"the
member was right and the reader was missing, which is a different refusal from 'no vocabulary'"*.

⚠️ An abort **op** was refused by D125's standing rule, not by preference: a program runs after the
damage pipeline, and *"a derived shape is classified by WHERE IN RESOLUTION IT LANDS"*.

**The table is keyed on the HEAD SENTENCE, and that is forced.** The clause is byte-identical across
the family and carries no referent — which is what *anaphoric* means — so the referent is the head. A
second printing costs one `Map` row: no anchor, no arm, no branch.

**The fourth head/tail stripper paid its disjointness debt**: all six pairs measured **0 / 0** over
640 sentences / 1,732 legal units, each refusal attributed to the rule that produces it, and the
converse driven rather than asserted.

### 🛑 The bigger finding: a census instrument had gone blind

`censusAtHead.test.ts` keeps a **hand-maintained local copy** of the reader list, and it held **11
entries against 12 exported** — so `BUILT.attack`, the figure most of this repo's accounting keys
off, was computed from an 11-reader view. Its sibling `precociousEvolution.test.ts` has exactly the
tripwire that would have caught it; **`censusAtHead.test.ts` had zero references to it, and had had
none since the file was written at D233.**

**The stale entry was the symptom; the missing guard was the defect.** Measured, not assumed: one
reader missing (D417's own, so the drift was one slice old), delta exactly +1/+1, checked by running
the 11- and 12-reader views side by side. The file now derives its surface from the **module** and
pins **both the diff and the count** — the count separately, because a diff alone stays green when a
reader is deleted from the module and the list together.

### ⚠️ And the same class sits in eight more suites

`benchNamedBonus`, `exOnlyActive`, `retreatCostBonus`, `sameEnergyBonus`, `sawkRequirementSplit` run
**9** readers; `inPlayTypeBonus`, `moreEnergyBonus`, `opponentBenchCount` run **11**. None has a
module-surface rung, and **every one claims its list is "the same set `censusAtHead.test.ts` uses"** —
false in all eight. Their figures are internally consistent with their own lists, **which is exactly
why none has ever reddened**. Named and left for its own slice; the resume point says how to decide
it per file (does the suite claim to measure THE HEAD, or only its own slice's delta against a frozen
baseline? — those cost very different slices, and the doc claim is false either way).

### The rule this slice earned

🛑 **An instrument with a hand-kept copy of something the module already exports cannot go red — it
can only go quiet.** The guard is not "keep the copy updated", it is "derive it from the module and
pin both the diff and the count". **And when you add that guard to one file, grep for the other
copies in the same breath.**

**CENSUS**: raw 411 → **412** / 1363 → **1364**; `BUILT.attack` 1410 → **1411**; residue 568 →
**567**; `unbuiltAttack` 322 → **321**. `splitHead` **13**, `compoundHead` **18**, registry **16**
unmoved. **5 mutants / 5 killed / 0 GAPs**; corpus 1517 → **1522**. `bun run check` **418 files /
8,881 tests, exit 0** (+1 file / +25 cases).

## D416 — THE KNOCK OUT THAT IS A *CHOICE*: one parking op for two sentences (engine 0.320.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 26**)

**2 sentences / 6 legal printings** on ONE new parking op:
`knockOutChosen { target: "opponentBench" | "opponentAny"; basicOnly?: true; damageCountersExactly?: number }`.
A is one `coinFlipGate` with both arms — its HEADS arm is D414's arm 6a byte for byte — and its TAILS
arm plus B are the two producers of the new op.

### Why they were built together

`target` is REQUIRED because the two producers genuinely **disagree** about scope (A-tails is
Bench-only, B is the whole opponent board), so no absent value is safe. Building B alone would have
shipped that field with **one inhabitant ever exercised**, which is how a persisted field turns out
to be the wrong shape after it is persisted. The comparator lives in the **field name**
(`damageCountersExactly`): only *"exactly"* is printed, so a comparator selector would be vocabulary
no card prints — but a bare name would need RENAMING the day *"at least"* prints, and **a rename on a
parking op is the one thing that costs a bump**. No bump for the park itself (D307).

### 🛑 A mutant survived, and the survivor was right

Dropping the `koByEffect` stamp from the **parked** `applyChoice` path survived. **Every marker
assertion in the suite ran on a bench of ONE**, where `parkOrForce` FORCES and the parked arm is never
entered. The park is the *point* of this op, and the marker is what keeps D414's two mechanisms
repaired — so the one path carrying both had **no witness at all while looking perfectly guarded**.
Closed with a driving two-candidate board, with the READER driven rather than the mark.
**13 mutants / 13 killed / 0 GAPs.**

### ⚠️ The refactor rotted seven rows, in two classes

Factoring `knockOutSelf`/`knockOutDefender` into a shared `doomBodyAt` moved four D345 rows
(`find occurs 0×`, ordinary adjacency rot). **But the new funnel was written by copying
`gustTargets`**, so three D331 rows matched BOTH — `find occurs 2×`, **D404's wrong-arm trap**: the
mutant would edit the NEW copy while claiming to test the old one. Re-anchored onto lines the
original uniquely owns, **and the copied filter got rows of its own**, so the repair did not move a
tested line into a file nothing pins.

### ✅ Two things verified rather than trusted

- **A declared survivor's reason was re-argued and held.** `D345-self-ko-overwrites-existing-damage`
  rests on `Math.max` being unreachable-equivalent; the factoring gave that line two new callers, so
  the declaration was re-earned on three counts — and `expectKilledBy` was **widened to all three
  callers**, because a survivor's suite list is the evidence its reason is claimed against.
- **`flow.ts` needed nothing.** `lethalRefs`, `koRecoilOf` and `byAttackFor` already scan
  `[active, ...bench]`, so a BENCHED body carrying D414's marker is classified correctly for free —
  driven (benched effect-KO: Prize taken, no promotion owed, revenge clause FALSE, Vengeful Punch
  pays **0** where a damage KO pays **40**), not asserted.

⚠️ **One deviation from the design**: the §11 ask is not a parameter of `doomBodyAt`.
`knockOutDefender` NAMES one body and refuses the op WHOLE (a guard); `knockOutChosen` PICKS from a
set and must merely not OFFER a shielded body (D259's *"a filter and not a guard"*). A boolean cannot
express both placements.

### 🛑 The two rules this slice earned

1. **A guard that only ever runs on the FORCED path does not guard the PARKED one.** When an op can
   park, count the candidates your boards actually offer — if none offers two, the park is untested
   however many cases there are.
2. **Copying a function copies its mutants' anchors, and the corpus goes quiet rather than red.**
   `precheck` catches it mechanically, but only if you run it — and the repair is **two-sided**.

**CENSUS**: raw 409 → **411** / 1357 → **1363**; `BUILT.attack` 1404 → **1410**; residue 574 →
**568**; `unbuiltAttack` 328 → **322**. `splitHead` **13**, `compoundHead` **18**, registry **16**
untouched. ⚠️ `compoundCompose` §4 moves **+1 / +4** against the census's +2 / +6, taken off the
sentences: the flip sentence is three clauses and crosses into the claimed-whole population; the
counter sentence has no internal `. ` and cannot. `bun run check` **417 files / 8,856 tests, exit 0**
(+1 file / +36 cases); corpus 1504 → **1517**.

## D415 — THE OPPONENT-SCOPED SPECIAL-ENERGY KO GATE: a seat mirror, and a slice that spent more of itself correcting false claims than building (engine 0.319.0, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 26**)

*"If your opponent's Active Pokémon has any Special Energy attached, it is Knocked Out."* (Haxorus
`sv06.5-046`) — **1 sentence / 1 legal printing**. One new `BoardCondition` member
(`opponentActiveHasEnergyAttached`), its two arms, one anchor, and a `deriveAttackEffect` arm that is
**D414's arm 6a with the `cond` swapped and nothing else**. No park, no new op, no persisted shape.

### One printing, and why D121's warrant is not the bar

D121's warrant — *two printings with one token varying* — decides whether a **parameterised
template** is earned over a **literal row**. This is neither: one member mirroring a shipped member
across the SEAT axis. The tree already builds members at one printing when the shape is inherited
(D397's `yourBenchNamedDamaged`). Written down here so a successor does not re-litigate it.

It carries the full `energy: BasicEnergyType | "special"` parameter for a sentence that only prints
`"special"`, because the parameter is **inherited, not invented**: the twin has had it since D350 for
a measured reason, `hasAttachedEnergy` takes both readings, and the `{R}` rewrite is already a
constructed refusal in `energyClause.test.ts` — a named future rather than speculation.

### 🛑 Why the mutants are unusual

**Every one of the five is a way of accidentally rebuilding the twin** — the seat, the predicate, the
gate's `cond`, the note, the apostrophe class. **Under all five the sentence still resolves, the gate
still fires and the Knock Out still happens.** Nothing a census counts moves. **Only a board where
the two seats DISAGREE tells the builds apart**, so the suite fields one and asserts the mirror as an
equivalence in both directions. 5 killed / 0 GAPs.

`energyClause.test.ts` refused this sentence for two stated reasons: *"its consequence is a KO, not a
damage bonus"* (**expired at D414**) and *"it reads the OPPONENT's Active — this member is
self-scoped by construction"* (**expired at D415**). The `deriveAttackEffect` null became a program
equality; the two damage-bonus nulls **stayed**, because a KO is still not a bonus. The rung's own
point — that this sentence *"would tempt a substring match hardest"* — is **more** true now, since a
live arm reads those exact words.

### 🛑 Three false claims in shipped work, two of them a day old

1. **D414's census note was wrong three ways**: the residue was 4 sentences / 9 printings, not three;
   *"targets are NAMED"* was never the discriminator (two residue sentences name theirs too); and one
   of them needed **no park at all**. ⚠️ It had been **replicated byte-identically into 21 sites
   across 10 suites** — all hashed, all corrected in place, wrong clause left standing.
2. The resume point priced this half at *"3 sentences / 8 printings"*. It is **7**.
3. **A member of the family was named by nothing in the repo** — no rung, no comment, no census note:
   the hand-Energy KO at `censusAttackCorpus.ts` line 93 (2 printings). **A witness that is not even
   a comment cannot go red.** Now in `UNBUILT_TEXT`, with its mechanism stated: a hand-Energy COST
   plus an *"If you can't …"* CANCEL — a whole-attack verdict, not a gated step.

### 🛑 The rule this slice earned

**A claim that is copied is a claim that rots in N places.** Before correcting a comment, `grep` for
its first distinctive clause — if it appears more than once, the correction is a **sweep** and its
cost is the sweep, not the sentence.

⚠️ **And its corollary, which this slice also paid**: `precheck` is not just for lint fixes. **Any
edit to a file the mutation corpus quotes rots a row — including a test-only edit made by an agent
you delegated to.** Paying D414's classification debt added one sentence to a set `D341`'s mutant
quotes, and it was committed without re-running `precheck`. Caught one commit late, re-pointed,
killed.
